headline: Free train travel facility extended to all trains for Chakra awardees
content: New Delhi The Ministry of Railways, in consultation with the Ministry of Defence, has extended the complimentary train travel facility for Chakra-series gallantry awardees to all trains, including the Vande Bharat Express. The government provides complimentary rail travel in First Class and AC 2-Tier to recipients of the Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra. The facility is also available to widows of posthumous award recipients, along with a companion. The initiative is aimed at recognising the courage, sacrifice, and service of gallantry awardees and honouring their contribution to the nation. The first three gallantry awards — the Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, and Vir Chakra — were instituted on January 26, 1950, with retrospective effect from August 15, 1947. Subsequently, the Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra were instituted. The order of precedence for the six awards is Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra.

headline: IIMBAA to bring 500 alumni, 115 CXOs and 21 management institutions together for sports fest in Bengaluru
content: Bengaluru The IIM Bangalore Alumni Association (IIMBAA), to bring together some of India’s management institutions on a common sporting platform, is hosting a two-day inter-institutional alumni sports festival in Bengaluru, with participation from 21 premier institutions, including alumni communities from IIM, ISB and XLRI. The event, scheduled to be held between November 28 (Saturday) and November 29 (Sunday), is expected to bring together approximately 500 alumni participants and 300 visitors, making it a significant gathering of India’s management alumni community, as per a statement. "The event is distinctive for the participation of more than 115 senior corporate leaders, founders, CXOs, partners and Vice Presidents from leading organisations, who will step away from their boardrooms and business responsibilities to compete alongside fellow alumni on the sports field,’’ IIMBAA said. The participating institutions include IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Amritsar, IIM Bangalore, IIM Bodh Gaya, IIM Calcutta, IIM Indore, IIM Jammu, IIM Kozhikode, IIM Lucknow, IIM Mumbai, IIM Raipur, IIM Ranchi, IIM Rohtak, IIM Sambalpur, IIM Shillong, IIM Sirmaur, IIM Tiruchirappalli, IIM Udaipur, IIM Visakhapatnam, the Indian School of Business (ISB) and XLRI Jamshedpur. According to the statement, the event would be part of IIMBAA’s initiatives towards building bridges across various management institutions in the country. "By leading the conceptualisation, organisation, and convening of alumni communities from 21 premier management institutions, IIMBAA is creating a distinctive platform for inter-institutional engagement through sport,’’ it said.

headline: 'Katha Won't Help You Win': Sachin Pilot Slams AAP After Hindu Preacher Dhirendra Shastri's Punjab Event
content: Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot, in charge of the state unit in poll-bound Punjab, on Wednesday attacked the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), taking a dig at its alleged political misuse of religion by organising a 'katha' by popular Hindu preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri in Pathankot earlier this week. "Elections are no longer won by organising such a 'katha' (religious storytelling)," Pilot said in a media interaction, referring to the presence of AAP leadership at the event headlined by Shastri, who heads Bageshwar Dham, a temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. The event, held by a local organisation, was overseen by AAP's candidate from Sujanpur Assembly segment, prominent businessman Swaran Singh Salaria. Pilot further said Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, a former comic artiste, was "still busy with comedy" while the state's law-and-order situation "keeps worsening". Pathankot, Punjab: At Bageshwar Dham Peethadhishwar Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's programme, AAP Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia says, "Today, I had come to meet Shastri ji. Regarding the country, the country's education- so that every child can get a good education- and so that politics moves in the right direction, uniting the country to build a Viksit Bharat, we need everyone's blessings for this. We need the blessings of all saints and the support of all people in this. On behalf of the Aam Aadmi Party, we are doing whatever we can. And in the coming times, if everyone's blessings remain with us, Punjab will prosper further. Just as the Bhagwant Mann government has worked for every household in Punjab- worked on schools, worked for hospitals, worked on jobs, worked for farmers, worked for traders, and provided an honest government with a farsighted vision- may Bhagwant Mann Sahab and the Aam Aadmi Party receive the blessings of all saints, and may we take Punjab and the country forward; that is my prayer." The three-day 'Shri Hanumant Katha' and 'Divya Darbar' were held at Lamini Stadium in Pathankot from November 22 to 24. AAP's Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia attended on the final day and welcomed Shastri on stage, sought his blessings for the Bhagwant Mann government, and passed on greetings from party boss Arvind Kejriwal and Mann. Leaders from the BJP and the Congress also attended, including Punjab BJP working president and Pathankot MLA Ashwani Sharma and former Pathankot MLA Amit Vij of the Congress.

headline: At least 30 killed in blaze after vehicle overturns in Egypt, health ministry says
content: Nov 25 (Reuters) – At least 30 people were killed and 15 injured when a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Egypt, the health ministry said on Wednesday. The ring road connects key highways across Greater Cairo, linking the governorates of Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia. The fire broke out above a tunnel in Giza’s Al-Warraq district, the ministry said. Local media reported that firefighters had brought the blaze under control. Road accidents are common in Egypt due to factors including speeding, weak enforcement of traffic regulations and poor road conditions. In recent years, Egypt has expanded its road network with new highways and bridges under a broader infrastructure programme aimed at easing congestion and accommodating rapid population growth and urban expansion. While the projects have improved traffic flow in some areas, concerns over road safety persist. (Reporting by Yomna Ehab and Enas Alashray. Editing by Timothy Heritage and Mark Potter)

headline: 31 police officers transferred in Punjab; 3 dists get new Commissioners
content: The Punjab Government has ordered a major police reshuffle, transferring and assigning new postings to 31 senior officers, including 25 IPS and six PPS officers, with immediate effect. headline: Akal Takht panel accuses Punjab govt committee of misleading people, invites it for talks
content: Amritsar: An expert committee constituted by Akal Takht to examine the Punjab govt’s ‘Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026’ has accused the govt’s coordination committee of misleading the Sikh sangat over Akal Takht’s directives and invited it for discussions at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib in Anandpur Sahib on Nov 30.The meeting has been scheduled for 11am, according to a release issued by the Akal Takht secretariat on Wednesday. Expert committee coordinator Lakhvir Singh said he had written to the nodal officer of the govt’s coordination committee.The expert committee said it had discussed the news conference held after the govt coordination committee’s Nov 23 meeting in Amritsar and subsequent statements. In its letter, it expressed concern over what it described as misleading remarks made at the news conference by two people who were not members of the govt committee, and the disregard shown towards objections raised in letters sent by the expert panel.“The expert committee has asked the Punjab government’s coordination committee not to mislead the Sikh Sangat regarding the directives of Akal Takht Sahib,” Lakhvir Singh alleged.The expert committee said the proposed meeting was in the interest of Panthic unity and to prevent the public from being misled on the issue. It said discussions would be held in the light of Akal Takht’s directives.The letter stated that only nominated members of the two committees would be allowed to attend the joint meeting. The expert committee meeting was attended by Justice (retd) Rupinder Singh Sodhi, Justice (retd) Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, Dr Kehar Singh, Prof Jagmohan Singh and coordinator Lakhvir Singh.

headline: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
content: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab, the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress, and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ NDA-SAD reunion: Why the Akali Dal severed ties with BJP 6 years ago storyline 1 https://www.thehindu.com/topic/aam-aadmi-party/ After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election storyline 1 The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance, with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least. headline: GAIL’s Faridabad Data Centre Plan Explained
content: GAIL is proposing to enter India’s data-centre market through an equal joint venture with an established operator, beginning with a facility of at least 5 MW in Faridabad, Haryana. The plan would use a GAIL-owned land parcel and its optical-fibre network, while the proposed joint venture would arrange power and water and develop, operate and commercialise the facility, according to an expression of interest reported by Economic Times. The state-run gas transporter is also evaluating the possibility of developing additional data centres in Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra. Any expansion would depend on the performance of the Faridabad facility and techno-economic assessments of other sites, the report said. GAIL’s proposal reflects the growing importance of land, connectivity and energy in data-centre development. The company operates around 15,800 km of optical-fibre cable along its cross-country natural-gas and LPG pipelines, connecting more than 100 towns and cities. It also has land parcels at pipeline terminals and compressor stations across several states, which could be considered for future facilities. For the first project, GAIL would contribute the land and access to its fibre network. The selected partner would be responsible for arranging the remaining infrastructure and for establishing and running the centre. The prospective partner must have at least one operational data centre with a capacity of 1 MW to qualify for the bid. The selection process will assign weight to an applicant’s data-centre portfolio, the capacity of its largest facility, its commitment to book capacity in the proposed Faridabad centre and its revenue over the previous three financial years, according to the report. Data centres are power-intensive facilities, making electricity supply a central consideration in their planning and operation. GAIL’s access to natural gas is identified in the proposal as another potential asset because gas could fuel generators supplying electricity to the facilities. However, the proposed joint venture, rather than GAIL alone, would be responsible for arranging the power and water needed for the Faridabad unit.

headline: Forteasia Group to develop Industrial Township in Rohtak
content: Faridabad-based real estate firm Forteasia Group is developing a commercial project named Forteasia Industrial Township in Kalanaur, Rohtak, Haryana. Spread over 138 acres, the RERA-approved (Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority approved) ecosystem is designed to bring together industrial, residential, and commercial opportunities within a planned environment supported by modern infrastructure and lifestyle amenities. The project will feature a golf course, clubhouse, gymnasium, landscaped parks, a kids’ play area, wide internal roads, and a gated environment designed to support convenience, recreation, and contemporary living. The project will be developed in phases. In the first phase, 22.2375 acres will be developed as an initial industrial plotted colony. Phases 2 & 3 will develop 915 plots covering 78.425 acres. The township is strategically located on the Rohtak-Bhiwani Highway, offering connectivity to key regional routes, including the KMP Expressway and the Delhi-Hisar Highway. headline: HP to get 50% free power royalty from central PSUs after 40 years
content: Shimla: To augment the state’s revenue, the Himachal Pradesh govt has amended the Swaran Jayanti Energy Policy-2021 to increase free power royalty from hydroelectric projects operated by central public sector undertakings (CPSUs) to 50% after completion of 40 years of commissioning.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said hydropower was a major source of revenue for Himachal Pradesh and the state must receive its rightful share from projects utilising its water resources.He said the enhanced royalty would strengthen the state’s financial position and generate additional resources for development and welfare activities.Govt is committed to protecting the state’s interests and ensuring that its natural resources generate equitable returns for its people, Sukhu added.Under the amended provisions, projects operated by the NHPC, SJVN and the NTPC will have to provide 50% of their power generation to the state as free power royalty for the first 10 years after completing 40 years of commissioning.After 50 years, these projects will revert to the state govt. Separate agreements will be signed with the concerned CPSUs to implement the provisions. Currently, Himachal receives free power royalty at 12% for the first 12 years, 18% for the next 18 years and 30% for the remaining 10 years of the agreement period.The amendment will cover major hydropower projects, including Baira Siul, Chamera-I, II and III, Parbati Stage-II and III of NHPC; Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur projects of SJVN; and Kol Dam of NTPC.Baira Siul, commissioned in 1982, has already operated for more than four decades. The state govt recognises water as one of Himachal’s most valuable natural resources and seeks to secure greater economic benefits from long-operational hydropower projects.

headline: Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal Pradesh recommended as Tripura chief justice
content: Shimla: The Supreme Court collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal Pradesh high court as the chief justice of Tripura high court.The elevation, recommended on Tuesday, will be consequent upon the transfer of the incumbent chief justice of Tripura , Justice MS Ramachandra Rao, as chief justice of Karnataka.Justice Rao had also earlier served as the chief justice of Himachal Pradesh from May 30, 2023 to Sept 25, 2024. Justice Thakur took oath as a judge of Himachal Pradesh high court on April 12, 2016.A native of Lanjata village in Ghumarwin tehsil of Bilaspur district, Justice Thakur completed his schooling and BSc from Bilaspur before pursuing LLB and BJMC from Himachal Pradesh University, Shimla. He enrolled as an advocate with Himachal Pradesh Bar Council in 1990 and practised before various legal forums, including Himachal Pradesh high court.His areas of practice included revenue, civil, criminal, constitutional, service, arbitration and taxation matters. He also served as legal adviser to several organisations.Before his elevation to the high court, he served as assistant advocate general of Himachal Pradesh from 1998 to 2003 and additional advocate general from 2008 to 2013. He also served as senior panel counsel for central govt. During his tenure as a high court judge, Justice Thakur was entrusted with administrative and guardian judge responsibilities for several sessions divisions, including Sirmaur, Una, Chamba, Kullu, Solan, Mandi, Kangra and Shimla.

headline: Chandigarh: Admission schedule for entry-level classes out
content: The UT Education Department has announced the admission schedule for entry-level classes in private unaided recognised schools for the 2027-28 academic session, with the application process set to begin on December 9.As per the public notice issued by the District Education Officer, schools have been directed to display admission-related information, including the total number of seats, age criteria, fee structure, admission criteria and documents required, on their notice boards and websites by December 7.Admission forms will be available free of cost from December 9 to December 22. Schools will display the list of eligible candidates on January 18, 2027, while the final list of selected candidates and the waiting list must be published by February 2. The last date for depositing admission fees is February 12.In a separate notice, the department clarified that parents applying under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and Disadvantaged Group (DG) categories must submit valid certificates. Acknowledgement receipts for applications seeking income or DG certificates will not be accepted as substitutes.The centralised online admission process for EWS/DG candidates will be conducted under Section 12(1) of the Right to Education Act. Detailed guidelines will be notified separately.

headline: Delhi to get 2 new hospitals, 40 Arogya clinics as CM pushes health infra expansion
content: New Delhi: Delhi will get two hospitals, one in Siraspur (north) and the other in Hastal (west), next year, which will add 1,815 beds to the capital’s total bed capacity.Several existing hospitals will also get specialised treatment blocks.Next month, 40 more Ayushman Arogya Mandirs will become operational, chief minister Rekha Gupta said after reviewing health department projects at the Delhi secretariat Wednesday. The expansion is aimed at easing the growing patient load on existing hospitals, reducing the distance people have to travel for routine treatment and strengthening specialised medical care.Delhi govt is also planning two medical colleges, an increase in MBBS and dental seats, and the integrated redevelopment of major hospital campuses under its plans to expand healthcare capacity and the availability of trained medical professionals in the capital.The two hospitals in Siraspur and Hastal will “significantly strengthen healthcare facilities in the capital. Govt is also targeting the opening of 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, on the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee,” Gupta said.The Siraspur hospital with 1,164 beds is ready. The procurement of medical equipment is under way. The completion deadline is the end of Jan. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal is also nearing completion.CM Gupta said that govt is also developing hospitals with 691 beds each in Madipur and Jwalapuri. Both projects are scheduled for completion by 2028. The Madipur hospital is being built at a cost of Rs 466.5 crore, while the Jwalapuri hospital has an estimated cost about Rs 484 crore.Govt is also expanding maternal and child healthcare facilities in the existing hospitals. A 463-bed maternal and child healthcare block is being developed at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini. Its OPD block is ready for inauguration. A 270-bed maternal and child healthcare block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are also nearing completion. These facilities will be operational shortly.Work is also under way on a plan for the integrated redevelopment of Lok Nayak Hospital and the Maulana Azad Medical College campus. The project has a stipulated timeline of approximately 30 months, including planning and construction. Efforts are also under way to bring Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi State Cancer Institute and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS) in the Trans-Yamuna region under a common institutional framework.The objective is to strengthen specialised medical services and the functioning of these institutions.The CM said govt has plans to establish medical colleges at Indira Gandhi Hospital in Dwarka and Guru Gobind Singh Govt Hospital. Each of the two proposed colleges will have 150 MBBS seats. The process is also under way to increase the number of seats at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and at the Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70.“A total of 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are being developed across Delhi, of which 415 are operational. Plans are also under way to introduce services in two shifts at Arogya Mandirs receiving a higher number of patients, ensuring timely treatment at the local level,” Gupta said.At the meeting, the CM directed officials to ensure that all projects related to hospitals and healthcare facilities are completed within the stipulated timelines and that there are no unnecessary delays.Health minister Pankaj Singh said all the projects are being monitored regularly.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Misraa Live In Saket: ₹3 Passes, Free Food & Secret Venue
content: An intimate evening of spoken word poetry, chiffon drapes, floor seating, and a complimentary rooftop North Indian feast awaits just three lucky ticket holders in South Delhi on Saturday, November 28, 2026. Listed under the PVR Anupam Saket hub on District, Misraa Live—curated and performed by Pranav Kirti Misra—flips the conventional Delhi open-mic script on its head by offering entry for a nominal ₹3 alongside a strict lottery selection system that keeps the exact indoor room under wraps until 24 hours before showtime. For Delhiites tired of overcrowded auditoriums and overpriced event F&B, this hyper-exclusive gathering blends literary storytelling with old-school hospitality. Whether you are trying to beat the registration deadline or figure out the logistics around Saket Community Centre on a Saturday evening, here is everything you need to know before the gates open at 5:30 PM. Unlike commercial poetry slams or stand-up specials held at standard basement venues, Misraa Live: An Evening of Poetry and Plates is designed as an ultra-intimate, living-room-style salon. Rather than rows of plastic chairs and stage spotlights, Pranav Kirti Misra performs his newest verses in an all-white home setting styled with floor seating, soft chiffon drapes, and a close circle of guests. Once the poetry reading concludes, the evening transitions upstairs to a rooftop space for a curated North Indian dinner spread and drinks. The catch—and the reason the event has sparked immediate buzz across South Delhi’s cultural circles—is the capacity: only three ticket holders are selected to sit inside the room and stay on for dinner with the artist. While technically priced at ₹3 rather than ₹0 on the District app, Misraa Live functions essentially as a free-entry, invite-style experience where the nominal fee filters out bots and casual clickers. Because demand far outstrips the three available seats, securing a spot follows a strict three-step timeline: If you are looking for other budget-friendly cultural experiences around the capital without the lottery suspense, check out our curated roundup of free events in Delhi NCR this weekend for open-access gigs and exhibitions.

headline: Manesar civic body told to conduct 24-hour monitoring to curb air pollution
content: With Manesar’s air pollution levels frequently placing it among India’s most polluted cities, the Municipal Corporation of Manesar (MCM) has been directed to conduct mandatory 24-hour monitoring to improve the area’s air quality index (AQI).Manesar figured among the country’s 10 most polluted cities on 16 days in September and again featured in the top 10 in October, based on monthly PM2.5 levels, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.Neighbouring Panchgaon topped the national pollution chart at least three times in November, according to reports citing Central Pollution Control Board data.Ashima Brar, Commissioner and Secretary of the Excise and Taxation and Energy Departments, who is also the nodal officer for air pollution control in Manesar, reviewed the measures at the MCM office on Thursday.She directed officials to take action against those violating the directions of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM). Teams deployed in all wards would be monitored weekly. Even in wards where teams were strictly enforcing the norms, the number of challans and other enforcement actions should be doubled, she said, adding that such seriousness would help bring down pollution levels.Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh said all departments in the district were working in coordination. Pollution control was not the responsibility of any single department and required a joint effort, he said.Municipal Commissioner Pradeep Singh said teams were active in all wards and taking action against those dumping garbage in the open or setting it on fire. The corporation has issued challans to 1,692 persons so far this year.He said roads were being cleaned at night using sweeping machines, while around 600 employees had been deployed to clean roads and streets. Nine anti-smog guns were sprinkling water on roads, and more would be added soon.Brar asked officials to share the routes and timings of the sweeping machines and anti-smog guns with resident welfare associations (RWAs) and other stakeholders, and revise the schedules based on their feedback.Ravinder Singh, Additional Chief Executive Officer of Gurugram Metropolitan City Bus Limited (GMCBL), said CNG buses operating in Manesar would be replaced with electric buses. As many as 100 electric buses have been inducted into the GMCBL fleet and would hit the roads soon.Officials of the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) said a proposal for a flyover at the congested Dadi Sati Chowk had been sent to the state government for approval.The Commissioner also briefed the nodal officer on pollution hotspots. After the meeting, Brar inspected several sites in the municipal area and issued directions to officials.

headline: 'Offering flowers to Babasaheb crime in UP?' CJP's Saurav Das stopped at UP border
content: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das on Thursday alleged that he was stopped at the Uttar Pradesh border while travelling to Meerut to pay homage to BR Ambedkar on Constitution Day.Das shared the claim on X, questioning why he was being prevented from visiting the city to offer flowers at Ambedkar's statue."I was on my way to Meerut to pay homage to Babasaheb Ambedkar ji's statue on Constitution Day. But I am stopped at the border and being disallowed," he said."Is offering flowers to Babasaheb a crime in UP today?" he added.The alleged incident comes days after Das was stopped at the immigration counter at Delhi airport while preparing to board a London-bound flight. He was scheduled to attend an event at the University of Oxford.Das moved the Delhi high court on Wednesday, challenging the action. In his petition, he alleged that immigration authorities prevented him from boarding the flight over discrepancies in his passport details, particularly his place of birth. He also said no order or travel restriction was shown to him.During Thursday's hearing, the Centre informed the court that Mumbai Police had issued a look out circular (LOC) against Das on November 23. The submission came after the court sought the Centre's response to his petition.Das's lawyer told the court that he had not been informed about the LOC or its purpose. The court also issued notices to the regional passport officer and the ministry of external affairs, seeking their responses by the next hearing. The matter has been listed for further hearing on December 9.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also questioned the decision to stop Das from travelling, drawing comparisons with the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Himachal Pradesh Government
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta today released two recently published books authored by K. R. Bharti, a retired IAS officer and noted author from Himachal Pradesh at Lok Bhavan. The first book, Fairs and Festivals of Himachal Pradesh is an extensively researched account of the traditional fairs and festivals of the state. It explores their historical origins, folklore, rituals, religious significance and vibrant community traditions, offering readers an insight into the rich and diverse cultural heritage of Himachal Pradesh. The second book presents a critical review and literary analysis of Hindi short stories written by authors associated with Himachal Pradesh. It pays tribute to the literary contributions of eminent writers such as Chandradhar Sharma Guleri and Yashpal, whose works have left an enduring imprint on Hindi literature. Bridging the literary past with the present, the book also critically examines the works of 19 prominent contemporary Himachali story writers. Speaking on the occasion, the Governor appreciated K. R. Bharti's efforts in documenting Himachal Pradesh's cultural heritage and promoting literary appreciation of regional writing. He observed that such works play an important role in preserving the state's rich traditions, literary legacy and cultural identity. He said that the books would be useful for researchers, students appearing in competitive examinations, cultural enthusiasts and general readers. K. R. Bharti is a noted Himachali author who has authored 11 books in Hindi and English so far. headline: Health ministry mandates insurance, bans fees for autism stem cell trials; sets 90-day approval deadline
content: NEW DELHI: The Union health ministry has tightened controls on stem cell treatment for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), barring clinics from offering the experimental procedure as routine care and introducing safeguards for patients in clinical trials. Under two regulatory notices issued on 20 November, institutions must insure participants against research-related harm, researchers cannot charge for treatment or other study-related costs, and trials must follow defined approval timelines.

headline: 'Excellent trade deal with US': MEA official says India tariffs will be lower than most others
content: Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said on Thursday that the tariffs faced by India after a trade deal with the US will be lower when compared to duties on countries such as Vietnam and Bangladesh. He also praised India's negotiations with the US, stating that New Delhi had negotiated an "excellent trade deal" with Washington on tariffs.This comes after the US on Wednesday proposed a tariff of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, following an investigation into what Washington described as "structural excess capacity" in 16 major economies.Also Read | US proposes up to 25% ‘excess capacity’ tariff on India, 17% if trade deal is signed Speaking to news agency ANI about the USTR proposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods and 17 per cent under a reciprocal trade agreement, Singh said, “The tariff that the US is currently imposing on India stands at 25%; however, following further negotiations, this will be reduced to 17%—a rate that will even be 1% lower than what applies to Vietnam, Bangladesh, and various other South Asian nations.”Singh credited the government for negotiating “an excellent trade deal” with the US, calling the deal a major achievement for India."Credit for this should go to our government, as it has successfully negotiated an excellent trade deal with the US regarding these tariffs. This is a significant achievement for us." Also Read | What the US tariff proposal means for Indian exportsAn interim trade deal between India and the US is yet to be signed. Furthermore, the 17 per cent is lower than the 18 per cent the two nations agreed on in a framework for the deal in February.Meanwhile, Bangladesh, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia and Indonesia face 18 per cent. Vietnam, on the other hand, faces up to 35 per cent, or 20 per cent if a deal is reached.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the findings of the investigations, identifying India, China, Bangladesh, the European Union (EU), Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Vietnam among the economies under scrutiny.India on US excess capacity claimsMinistry of commerce and industry on Wednesday issued a statement on the USTR Section 301 determination concerning structural excess capacity in manufacturing across 14 economies, including India.The official statement noted that the notice is “currently under examination.”"India engaged constructively throughout this investigation. In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," the ministry added.It further emphasised that India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement.Also Read | India rejects US excess capacity claims, says no structural overcapacity in any sector"It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations. Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026," it further said.(with inputs from ANI)

Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court. headline: Tukaram Mundhe effect? Gym removes protein powder display after FDA warning on unlicensed sales
content: A gym has reportedly removed its entire protein powder display following a warning by Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe against the sale of health supplements without the required licences.The development was shared by an X user, Kanan Bahl, who claimed that the gym owner cleared the shelf after watching a video of Mundhe explaining the licensing requirements.Posting on X on Thursday, Bahl wrote, "My gym used to have a showcase full of protein powders. Someone showed the owner a reel of @Tukaram_IndIAS saying that gyms selling protein without license is illegal and they'll take action."He added: “Overnight, the shelf is empty! We honestly need just 100 Nayaks like him across the country!”The post has drawn attention to the regulatory requirements governing the sale of protein powders and other health supplements through gyms and fitness centres.What did Tukaram Mundhe warn gyms about?Mundhe has warned gyms and fitness centres against selling health supplements without the required licences. He has also cautioned manufacturers against printing misleading health claims on nutraceutical labels.He has questioned claims suggesting that consuming protein powder alone builds muscle, describing such advertising as misleading.The warning covers gyms, health clubs, pharmacies and retailers involved in selling supplements without the necessary authorisation.Why do gyms need an FSSAI licence to sell protein powder?A statewide Maharashtra FDA order makes it mandatory for gyms and fitness centres selling health supplements to obtain an FSSAI food licence or registration, even if they already hold licences under other laws.The order also addresses misleading claims by manufacturers, pharmacies, influencers and online sellers. It seeks to tighten compliance across the health supplement supply chain.The requirement does not mean that selling protein powder is prohibited. It means businesses selling these products must comply with the applicable food safety licensing and regulatory requirements.Social media reacts to the gym clearing its shelvesBahl's post prompted reactions from other X users, with some questioning how the licensing requirement would be enforced.One user wrote, “Is selling it really illegal? Even if it's how is it enforced?”Another user commented, “We need some 10 @Tukaram_IndIAS in namma Bengaluru.”Maharashtra FDA's wider enforcement driveMundhe, a 2005-batch IAS officer, took charge as Maharashtra FDA Commissioner in May 2026. The department had reportedly conducted more than 3,000 raids since then.The enforcement drive has covered restaurants, dairies and quick-commerce facilities and has led to licence suspensions.The sale of protein supplements through gyms has also attracted regulatory scrutiny in other states. In 2023, checks in Karnataka found that two-thirds of protein powder samples collected from gyms were misbranded.

headline: Accredited vs self-proclaimed: SC to examine protection for journalists
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday referred allegations of police assault, manhandling and wrongful detention of seven journalists covering protests in Delhi in October to a high-powered inquiry committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit relevant material before the five-member committee, which will examine the allegations and establish whether the journalists were subjected to police excesses.The petitions were filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) and the Delhi Union of Journalists over alleged police action against media personnel covering protests on October 10 and 11, 2026. The demonstrations were reportedly demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Justice Bagchi said the committee would ascertain whether the journalists were present at the protest sites, whether force was used against them and, if so, whether it was excessive in the circumstances."You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there. If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force," he observed, as quoted by PTI.The judge added that the committee should examine whether the force used was disproportionate to what was necessary for maintaining public order.The bench also indicated that it would consider broader constitutional questions concerning the protection available to journalists covering protests and public events, including whether accredited journalists are entitled to greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters.Justice Bagchi observed that self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection as accredited media persons.Appearing for the journalists, senior advocate PV Dinesh said the seven media personnel worked for established news organisations and were not social media reel-makers."We are just journalists, recognised journalists. Allow us to do our work," he submitted.He also questioned whether journalists working for established media organisations could be taken into custody while performing their professional duties."The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" Dinesh asked, as quoted by PTI.The court indicated that it would examine the constitutional safeguards available to journalists, including their freedom of movement and right to practise their profession. It would also consider whether forcibly removing a journalist from a location amounts to custody and the legal consequences of such action.The petitioners alleged that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting locations, prevented from recording events and subjected to physical force despite displaying their press credentials. The allegations also include an attempt to snatch a photographer's camera and the physical assault of a woman journalist while she was reporting live.The seven journalists named in the petition are Suhail Muhammed and VS Rahul of 24 News, Sajin of Asianet News, Roshni Rajan and Farsana of Reporter TV, Vishnuprasad of Mathrubhumi and Miji P Jose of Manorama News.The Delhi Police had earlier told the Supreme Court that social media influencers and reel-makers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests.In an affidavit, the police described journalists as a "distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain. It argued that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections available to the press while reporting from protest sites.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: P.V. Sindhu named international event ambassador for Pink City Half Marathon
content: Jaipur Two-time Olympic medallist P.V. Sindhu has been named international event ambassador for the 11th edition of the Vedanta Pink City Half Marathon, scheduled to be held here on November 29. The badminton star will lend her support to the Anil Agarwal Foundation's 'Run for Zero Hunger' campaign, under which Vedanta has pledged to provide one meal to a child or an animal in need for every kilometre covered by participants. Organised by Anybody Can Run (ABCR), the event will feature three race categories: the 21.1-km half marathon, the 10-km Cool Run and the 5-km Dream Run. According to a company release, the campaign supports the foundation's nutrition and early childhood development initiatives through Nand Ghar, a network of modernised anganwadi centres, as well as its animal welfare programme, The Animal Care Organisation (TACO). Vedanta also organises the Zinc City Half Marathon in Udaipur, whose third edition witnessed participation from more than 9,700 runners representing 27 states and six countries, the company said. The organisers said the Jaipur event aims to promote fitness and greater public participation in sporting activities while raising awareness about hunger and animal welfare.

headline: Infra projects see cost overrun of ₹3.28 trillion in October: MoSPI
content: Infrastructure projects worth more than ₹0.0015 trillion each recorded a cumulative cost overrun of approximately ₹3.28 trillion, according to a monthly government report for October 2026. About 1,862 ongoing infrastructure projects across 17 central ministries and departments were monitored. The total revised cost was ₹38.11 trillion, compared with the original cost of ₹34.83 trillion. However, the report did not specify the actual number of projects that faced cost overruns. The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stood at ₹17.87 trillion, accounting for approximately 46.88 per cent of the project cost and indicating steady progress in project implementation, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) said in its monthly report for October on Wednesday. A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 649 projects (35 per cent) having achieved over 80 per cent physical progress, while 326 (18 per cent) have crossed 80 per cent financial completion. The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation. Of the 1,862 ongoing infrastructure projects, 790 are mega projects, with a project cost of ₹0.01 trillion or more, and 1,072 are major projects, with a cost below ₹0.01 trillion. The transport and logistics sector accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1,324), with a cumulative cost of ₹20.37 trillion, underscoring the priority given to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth. The report said physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0-20 per cent) and advanced (81-100 per cent) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly started projects alongside many nearing completion. While physical progress exceeds financial advancement in the 81-100 per cent range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, at 972 (52 per cent of the total 1,862), and a share of the total revised project cost of ₹9.55 trillion (25 per cent of the total project cost of ₹38.11 trillion), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development. The Ministry of Railways has 288 ongoing projects (15 per cent), with a total revised project cost of ₹7.38 trillion (19 per cent). The Coal Ministry accounts for 121 ongoing projects (7 per cent), with a total revised project cost of ₹2.22 trillion (6 per cent). The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 117, 108, 50 and 33 projects, respectively, with associated project costs of ₹4.42 trillion, ₹6.55 trillion, ₹3.44 trillion and ₹1.93 trillion. The remaining 173 projects (9 per cent), with a total project cost of ₹2.63 trillion (7 per cent), are distributed across various ministries and departments, including Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour and Employment, Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Health and Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT and Sports.

headline: ED attaches Ozone Group properties worth ₹702.70 crore in homebuyers’ fraud case
content: Bengaluru The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Bengaluru Zonal Office, has provisionally attached immovable properties, including flats and land, valued at ₹702.70 crore belonging to the Ozone Group and others in connection with an alleged ₹1,305-crore homebuyers’ fraud. The investigation further revealed that substantial amounts were collected from buyers, while housing loans were also disbursed directly to the builder entities. However, the projects remained incomplete and the promised apartments were not delivered. ED raids on promoters of defaulting realty project Ozone Urbana in Bengaluru, Mumbai ED raids on promoters of defaulting realty project Ozone Urbana in Bengaluru, Mumbai The project, Ozone Urbana Housing Township in Devanahalli taluk, is one of the biggest defaulters of Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA-K) revenue recovery orders ED raids on promoters of defaulting realty project Ozone Urbana in Bengaluru, Mumbai storyline 1 The ED alleged that funds collected for specific projects were diverted through various Ozone Group entities by way of inter-corporate deposits and other financial transactions. Instead of being used for construction and completion of the projects, the funds were allegedly utilised to repay or refinance loans, meet interest and finance costs, repay investors and meet corporate expenses and other liabilities. The latest attachment is in addition to properties worth ₹423.37 crore provisionally attached by the ED through PAO No. 29/2025 dated October 4, 2025. The agency said the fresh attachment followed further investigation and identification of additional properties allegedly linked to the proceeds of crime. headline: 78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave
content: CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) signed 78 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) involving investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors and districts of the State. The MoUs were exchanged in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Industries Minister S. Keerthana and Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and CEO of Guidance at the second edition of the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave held in Chennai. The Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for 15 projects involving investments worth ₹7,925 crore, which are expected to generate 19,965 jobs. He also inaugurated six projects involving investments to the tune of ₹1,430 crore, creating employment opportunities for 1,710 people. Mr. Vijay handed over appointment letters to 18 candidates selected for various positions for companies including UPS, Autoliv, Stylcove, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Omron. With this, the total number of MoUs signed by the TVK government has risen to 190, involving investments worth over ₹1.73 lakh crore within 200 days of assuming office. The conversion rate is 74.1% (the MoUs signed on August 13, 2026). Our competition is with world’s leading manufacturing economies, not other States: T.N. Minister Keerthana Industries Minister S. Keerthana said: “There has been considerable discussion about which State is attracting the most investment. Tamil Nadu welcomes competition. But for us, investment must translate into productive employment, better incomes and opportunities for our people. We are not chasing jobless growth.” She went on to add, “Our real competition is not another State. It is the world’s leading manufacturing economies.” The Minister also said that two out of every five women working in India’s factories are employed in Tamil Nadu. “That is why we launched the ‘Vetri Magalir Thozhilmunaivor Membattu Thittam’, which offers loans of up to ₹5 crore to women entrepreneurs. We have received thousands of applications, and 19 women entrepreneurs have already been sanctioned loans totalling ₹13.26 crore,” she said. On Global Capability Centres (GCCs), the Minister said the government would work with the Greater Chennai Corporation to strengthen social infrastructure. S. Vijayakumar, Additional Chief Secretary to the Government for the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department said that Tamil Nadu Single Window Portal 3.0 is under development and is expected to be ready by January 2027. The New Industrial Policy is also being prepared and is expected to be ready by January 2027, he added. Mr. Vijayakumar also said that the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission has approved that industries may self execute their HT/EHT power connections by procuring the equipment, accessories and installations on their own. The Energy Department will share the specifications for self execution. Our Budget Estimates for the incentives to the industries for this current year is ₹2000 crore. We have distributed this amount in 200 days and have requested the government of Tamil Nadu for another ₹1600 crore,” he pointed out. Key MoUs inked Royal Enfield is set to establish an electric motorcycle manufacturing facility with an investment of ₹1,000 crore, creating 500 jobs. The company also unveiled its C6 model at the conclave. Sweden-based PMC Hydraulics is shifting a part of its manufacturing operations from Bengaluru to Tamil Nadu and will establish its first manufacturing facility in Krishnagiri, with an investment to the tune of ₹300 crore. The project is expected to generate 300 jobs. JK Fenner is set to invest ₹900 crore to establish a massive new manufacturing plant in Sivaganga, creating employment opportunities for 1,650 persons. Brazil-based WEG is set to make a new greenfield investment of ₹2,000 crore in Dharmapuri district, generating employment for 3,000 persons, as part of the expansion of its integrated manufacturing plant. This will serve as an integrated manufacturing project for electric motors, automation systems, and control devices, making it the company’s largest integrated facility outside Brazil.

headline: CJP’s Saurav Das ‘stopped’ at UP border while on way to pay tribute to Ambedkar
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das on Thursday alleged that he was stopped at the Uttar Pradesh border while on the way to Meerut to pay homage to B R Ambedkar on Constitution Day."I was on my way to Meerut to pay homage to Babasaheb Ambedkar ji's statue on Constitution Day. But I am stopped at the border and being disallowed," he said on X."Is offering flowers to Babasaheb a crime in UP today?" he said.The incident comes days after Das was stopped at the immigration counter at Delhi airport, before he could board his London-bound flight to attend an event at the University of Oxford.He has approached the Delhi High Court challenging the restriction on his foreign travel.The Centre informed the court on Thursday that Mumbai Police had issued a Look Out Circular against Das on November 23.The court listed the matter for hearing on December 9.

headline: 'Single-digit parties': Punjab Congress president takes a dig at BJP-SAD alliance
content: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Thursday took a swipe at the newly announced Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance, predicting that the two parties would together win only single-digit seats in the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.Reacting to the SAD-BJP alliance, Pargat Singh said, "These are strictly single-digit parties; even together, both will end up in single digits."He further said that people in Punjab were still unhappy with the BJP and SAD over their role during the farmers' protest against the now-repealed farm laws, ANI reported.Referring to the farmers' agitation, Pargat Singh claimed that around 750 farmers had lost their lives during the protest.He also targeted the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling it the "East India Company" and ruling out any possibility of the Congress joining hands with the party."They (AAP) are the East India Company, and the Congress never shakes hands with any East India Company," Singh said.Launching a further attack on AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and his associates, he said, "These are thugs, Kejriwal and company."The Congress leader's remarks came amid renewed political activity in Punjab ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The SAD and BJP, which ended their alliance in 2020 over the Centre's farm laws, have now joined hands again.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Prayed for death every night': Azam Khan gets emotional about his time in jail
content: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan got emotional while recalling his five-and-a-half years in jail at the launch of the party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on Thursday. He spoke about the fear of being killed during a jail transfer with his son, Abdullah Azam, and said he had wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav could spend six months behind bars to understand what imprisonment was like.Recalling the incident, Khan said he and his son were made to travel in separate vehicles during a jail transfer, leaving them fearing it could be their last meeting."They made me stand on one side and my son on the other, taking us in separate vehicles. When I asked why he was being taken separately, there was no answer. I told my son, 'Son, today might be our last meeting. If we don't meet here, we will meet in the hereafter,'" Khan said, adding that he prayed for death every nightHe also recalled how his son would ask whether they would ever get out of jail. Khan said he wished Akhilesh could spend six months in prison to understand the hardships faced by inmates.Describing himself as a "half-broken man", Khan said the treatment he and his family had faced could have destroyed someone less resilient. He also referred to the hardships endured by his wife and son during their imprisonment."The strictness, hatred and disgust I faced should have killed me, but I proved to be tough. Now we feel, we'll die but die after achieving something," he said.Khan accused the government, jail authorities and enforcement agencies, including the Enforcement Directorate (ED), of subjecting him and his family to severe harassment. Comparing his treatment with that during British rule, he said his five-and-a-half years in a "dark cell" had taken a toll on his body, heart and mind. He also questioned the cases registered against him, alleging that charges relating to chicken theft were framed under provisions meant for dacoity, and said his legal fight to prove his innocence was continuing.The senior SP leader also recalled his five-decade association with the party and its founder Mulayam Singh Yadav, reaffirming his support for Akhilesh ahead of the 2027 polls.With Akhilesh present on the stage, Khan said, "He will be chief minister again and again, and perhaps even much more. He won't be just here; he will go much further."Khan described the newly released PDA manifesto as a blueprint for the country's future, saying the party would be willing to deliver beyond its written promises if required. The SP's PDA formulation refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).Khan also took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, without naming him directly, accusing him of trying to prevent governments from being formed rather than seeking to play the role of a kingmaker.Owaisi had recently spoken about Muslims moving beyond organising rallies to occupying positions of political power, including that of deputy chief minister. Responding to the remark, Khan had sarcastically said, "Declare my name too, make me the Prime Minister. Only the word 'Wazir' needs to be added to my name; I am already 'Azam' (Wazir-e-Azam)."Taking another veiled dig at Owaisi during Thursday's address, Khan said those troubling the SP had been given an inflated stature by their own supporters and needed to be brought back to their "original stature"."He cannot be the kingmaker, but he can spoil others' play. This is a petty and shameful goal," Khan said.Azam Khan was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in November 2025 in a money laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, founded by him, and was lodged in Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad. The case relates to alleged financial irregularities and the acquisition of land for the university. The Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail on November 25, 2026, observing that mandatory legal provisions governing his arrest had prima facie not been followed. He was released from Dasna jail on November 26 and is headed to Rampur.His wife, former Rajya Sabha MP Tanzeen Fatima, and their son Abdullah Azam Khan were also jailed along with him in October 2023 after the three were convicted in a case involving two birth certificates issued to Abdullah. The court sentenced all three to seven years in prison. Fatima was released on bail on May 29, 2024, after spending over seven months in jail. Abdullah, a former MLA, was also granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in January 2024.Azam Khan's remarks came at the event where Akhilesh unveiled the Samajwadi Party's PDA manifesto, titled Sattais ka Sankalp: PDA ka Prannpatra, on Constitution Day. The party's PDA formulation refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).The SP has brought forward its manifesto launch early compared with the previous two assembly elections, when it released its poll document shortly before voting. The party has said the early announcement will give it more time to take its proposals to different sections of the electorate.Read more: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts - Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifestoGet the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Medchal PoCSO Court summons Bandi Bageerath to appear after two months
content: HYDERABAD The Medchal PoCSO court has issued summons to Bandi Bageerath, son of Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, directing him to appear before it on January 28 in connection with a case involving the alleged sexual assault and physical abuse of a 17-year-old girl. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/telangana-high-court-grants-conditional-bail-to-bandi-sai-bageerath-in-pocso-case/article71202203.ece The case was registered at Petbasheerabad police station on May 8, 2026, following a complaint by the girl’s mother. She alleged that Bageerath had sexually assaulted and physically abused her daughter after making her consume alcohol. The complaint also referred to emotional manipulation of the girl over several months. Following the registration of the case, Cyberabad Police launched a search for Bageerath. In May, police said he was absconding and that his mobile phone had been switched off for three days. Investigators analysed his call detail records and formed five special teams to trace him. Searches were conducted at Maitri Residency in Banjara Hills and at a residence linked to Bandi Sanjay Kumar in Karimnagar. A lookout circular was also issued. The Telangana High Court had rejected his anticipatory bail plea. Police had said Bageerath failed to appear for questioning on May 13 despite being served notices and had sought two additional days. Bageerath was arrested by Cyberabad Police near Telangana Police Academy junction in the night on May 16. The victim’s statement was recorded by police, with investigators indicating that it would be recorded again to gather further details. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/bandi-bageerath-arrested-near-narsingi-after-week-long-manhunt/article70988035.ece The latest summons direct Bageerath to appear before the Medchal PoCSO court on January 28.

headline: Eighteen years after 26/11, Ajmal Kasab's lawyers still await fees
content: Mumbai Eighteen years after the 26/11 terror attacks, two lawyers who set aside their other cases to represent the lone captured Pakistani terrorist Ajmal Kasab continue to await their remuneration. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/2611-The-first-few-hours-at-the-Taj/article16893280.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/I-was-shot-at-in-police-custody-Kasab/article16854598.ece 2008 Mumbai terror attacks: Tributes paid to martyrs on 18th anniversary 2008 Mumbai terror attacks: Tributes paid to martyrs on 18th anniversary Ten LeT terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea on November 26, 2008, and killed 166 people, including 18 security personnel, during a 60-hour siege of Mumbai 2008 Mumbai terror attacks: Tributes paid to martyrs on 18th anniversary storyline 1 Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah represented Kasab before the Bombay High Court for nine months following their appointment by the Maharashtra government in 2010. The two were nominated by the High Court and appointed by the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) via a notification on June 8, 2010, to defend Kasab in his appeal against the death penalty awarded to him by a trial court. According to the notification, signed by the then secretary A.K. Sonawane, Solkar was to be paid on a par with a special public prosecutor and Mr. Shah was to receive remuneration equivalent to that of an additional public prosecutor conducting a death penalty confirmation case. Beyond 26/11: Other major terror attacks in Mumbai over the years Beyond 26/11: Other major terror attacks in Mumbai over the years Here is a look at some of the other major terror attacks that have struck Mumbai city over the years, apart from the 26/11 attacks Beyond 26/11: Other major terror attacks in Mumbai over the years storyline 1 Official sources pegged this amount between ₹1,500 and ₹2,000 per day. However, more than 15 years after the High Court proceedings concluded, both advocates say they are yet to receive their dues. "We have still not received our fees for representing Kasab. I have been corresponding with the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority time and again, but there seems to be no positive headway," Mr. Solkar told PTI. According to both lawyers, whenever they raise the matter with the MSLSA, they are asked to submit detailed bills and memos specifying the exact number of dates and hours they appeared for the accused, a demand termed by them as "unreasonable" after so many years, and also pointing out that nobody would retain granular records of daily court hours over a decade later. Ajmal Kasab was hanged on November 21, 2012, at the Yerwada Central Jail in Pune. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/I-am-innocent-acquit-me-Kasab/article16627869.ece Mr. Solkar said that their appointment letters explicitly linked their pay scale to that of the prosecution. "What is stopping the Government from using the same pay scale and clearing our dues?" Mr. Solkar questioned. Chasing a name in jihadi heartland Chasing a name in jihadi heartland The reporter who established to the world that Ajmal Kasab was a Pakistani from Faridkot in Okara district looks back on the challenge of those crucial days opinion Chasing a name in jihadi heartland Ajmal Kasab. File photo Echoing his concern, Mr. Shah questioned the insistence on itemised memos when both the Government notification and the order passed by the then Chief Justice of the High Court clearly defined their fee structure. "We gave our entire day for nine months to argue this case. We had to keep all our other cases on the backburner so that there was no hurdle caused to the proceedings," Mr. Shah said, adding that the notification stipulated their fees were to be cleared as soon as the High Court delivered its verdict. An official from the state legal services authority maintained that, as per standard practice, advocates are required to submit formal bills and memos for the clearance of fees. In contrast, advocate Abbas Kazmi, who defended Kasab during the trial before special judge M.L. Tahaliyani, said his dues were settled promptly. "My remuneration was cleared by the government soon after the completion of the trial," Kazmi said. Under legal provisions, if an accused fails to engage a counsel, the court nominates a lawyer from the legal services authority to ensure a fair trial. Also Read : The hangman’s justice https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/The-hangman’s-justice/article12515854.ece The Bombay High Court commenced hearing the confirmation of Kasab's death sentence and his appeal in June 2010, upholding the capital punishment in February 2011. The Supreme Court subsequently affirmed the verdict, and Kasab, who was lodged at the Arthur Road prison following his capture, was hanged at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune on November 21, 2012. A total of 166 people, including six Americans, were killed in the November 26, 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, during which 10 heavily armed Pakistani terrorists laid siege to key locations across the city for over 60 hours.

headline: Defence, Aerospace Growing Faster than IT and Pharma in Telangana: Minister Uttam
content: Hyderabad; Telangana’s defence and aerospace sector is growing faster than its traditionally dominant Information Technology (IT) and pharmaceutical sectors, with both production and exports registering a 100 per cent year-on-year increase, Telangana irrigation and civil supplies minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy said. He called upon industry leaders to take advantage of the state’s strong manufacturing ecosystem and emerging opportunities in global defence and aerospace markets.Delivering the inaugural address at the CII Telangana defence and aerospace conclave 2026, organised on the theme “Telangana to Global Markets – Building Defence and Aerospace Supply Chains,” the minister said Telangana was well positioned to emerge as a major partner in global defence and aerospace manufacturing networks.Uttam Kumar Reddy said Hyderabad and Telangana had traditionally been known for their strengths in the IT and pharmaceutical sectors. However, defence and aerospace manufacturing had emerged as a rapidly growing sector with immense potential for investment, exports and employment generation.“India’s gradual transition from dependence on defence imports to developing indigenous manufacturing capabilities, technologies and products had opened up considerable opportunities for both public and private sector enterprises. The changing global environment and the growing need for reliable and resilient supply chains had also created an opportunity for India to emerge as a trusted manufacturing partner for countries seeking to diversify their defence and aerospace supply networks,” he said.Uttam said Hyderabad’s long association with defence research and aerospace manufacturing gave Telangana a distinct advantage in attracting further investments.“The presence of premier defence research institutions, public sector undertakings, leading private companies, MSMEs and a large pool of skilled professionals had helped build a strong industrial ecosystem over the years. Our focus must now be on taking this ecosystem to the next level,” he said.There were significant opportunities for Telangana industries in aircraft components, defence electronics, precision engineering, aerospace systems, drones, robotics, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, the minister said.On the participation of micro, small and medium enterprises, Uttam said large companies and international manufacturers should work closely with smaller domestic suppliers and help them meet international quality and manufacturing standards. Telangana-based companies should not confine themselves to meeting India’s domestic defence requirements but should aspire to become suppliers to leading aerospace and defence companies across the world, he said.Uttam Kumar Reddy, who is also chairperson of the executive council for Raksha Expo 2026, extended an invitation to national and international industry leaders to participate in the prestigious event being organised as part of the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026.The expo would bring together leading defence and aerospace manufacturers, technology providers, investors, startups and other stakeholders from India and abroad. It would showcase advancements in defence manufacturing, aerospace, drones, robotics, space technologies and other emerging areas through exhibitions, displays and live demonstrations, Uttam Kumar Reddy said.“More importantly, we want Raksha Expo to be a platform for business,” the minister said, emphasising that the event should facilitate investments, technology collaborations, industrial partnerships and long-term business relationships.ends/You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
