headline: Mumbai Police issued Look Out Circular against CJP's Saurav Das: Centre tells Delhi HC
content: New Delhi The Centre informed the Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) that a Look Out Circular (LOC) had been issued against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das by the Mumbai Police. The submission was made before Justice Amit Mahajan, who had issued notice and sought the Centre’s response on Mr. Das’s petition challenging the authorities’ decision to prevent him from travelling abroad. The court listed the matter for further hearing on December 9. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre along with standing counsel Ashish Dixit, told the court that the LOC was issued on the intervening night of November 22 and 23. He added that Mr. Das was yet to respond to a show-cause notice issued in connection with alleged discrepancies in his passport details. CJP’s Saurav Das to file criminal complaints against social media handles over passport leak CJP’s Saurav Das to file criminal complaints against social media handles over passport leak The CJP co-convenor alleged targeted harassment as his passport details were circulated online after he was stopped from boarding London-bound flight over discrepancies flagged by Chennai passport office CJP’s Saurav Das to file criminal complaints against social media handles over passport leak storyline 1 The Centre’s counsel said an inquiry was initiated in Puducherry on August 20 to verify Mr. Das’s place of birth, address and parentage because he left the father’s name column blank in his passport. The ASG submitted that the alleged discrepancies could have a bearing on determining Das’s citizenship. Mr. Sharma also informed the court that the Madras High Court had issued notice on October 30 on a separate plea seeking an inquiry into Mr. Das’s antecedents. The ASG further argued that the travel advisory issued to Mr. Das was in his own interest, as he could face serious complications if the passport authorities subsequently found his explanation unsatisfactory. “There is no order today which either invalidates or suspends the passport. It is only a show-cause notice he has to reply,” Mr. Sharma told the court. Why was Saurav Das stopped from flying to London? Delhi HC to hear case Why was Saurav Das stopped from flying to London? Delhi HC to hear case CJP co-convenor Saurav Das has approached the Delhi High Court after being stopped from boarding a London-bound flight, arguing that authorities prevented his travel without showing any formal order. Why was Saurav Das stopped from flying to London? Delhi HC to hear case video 1 Opposing the Centre’s submissions, senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Mr. Das, argued that the mere pendency of a show-cause notice concerning his passport could not be a ground to prevent him from travelling abroad, particularly when the right to travel is a fundamental right. Mr. Sibal told the court that his client had not been informed about the existence of any LOC, the reasons for its issuance or its purpose. He sought a copy of the circular to enable Mr. Das to challenge it, but the Centre’s counsel said it could not be furnished. Mr. Das had approached the High Court after officials stopped him at the immigration counter at Delhi airport on November 23. He was not allowed to travel to the United Kingdom to attend an event at the Oxford Union on December 1, where he was scheduled to speak about the “Cockroach Movement”.

headline: Keralam Home department mulls action against Madhusoodanan’s controversial speech, says Chennithala
content: KOCHI Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has strongly criticised former MLA and Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] leader T.I. Madhusoodanan’s controversial remarks following the verdict in the Dhanraj murder case, stating that the Home department has taken the matter very seriously. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/cpim-activist-dhanraj-murder-case-3-bjp-workers-get-life-imprisonment-in-keralam/article71741332.ece CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan faces flak over ‘threatening’ speech after Dhanraj murder verdict CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan faces flak over ‘threatening’ speech after Dhanraj murder verdict CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan faces flak over ‘threatening’ speech after Dhanraj murder verdict storyline 1 Talking to reporters in Kochi on Thursday (November 26, 2026), Mr. Chennithala said that the police are collecting the full text of the speech, on the basis of which strict action will be taken. A person who has served as a people’s representative should never have made such a speech “calling for murder,” he said. “Justifying murders taking place in the State and calling for the killing of others are actions unbecoming of a people’s representative. Neither the police nor the government will accept such conduct. We are examining the full text of the speech and will consider what legal action can be taken,” the Minister said. Political leaders and former MLAs are not expected to incite violence or create unrest in the State. They are expected to take the lead in maintaining peace and ensuring that murders and violent incidents do not occur. It is wrong for them to engage in such conduct. Therefore, the statement should be withdrawn. It is unacceptable. The CPI(M) leadership should also intervene seriously in the matter, Mr. Chennithala said. In Kannur During an event organised by the Democratic Youth Federation of India at Payyannur in Kannur, Mr. Madhusoodanan reportedly warned that the party would settle scores and had no hesitation in doing so, while referring to the Cheemeni case of 1987, in which CPI(M) workers were burnt to death. He said that although no court had punished anyone in the case, none of those accused were alive today. His remarks came in the wake of the verdict acquitting the accused in the C.V. Dhanraj murder case. Allegedly, the former MLA did not even spare the judge who delivered the judgment.

headline: Non-veg food ban extended in Somnath Temple vicinity
content: The Gujarat High Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) extended the ban imposed by local authorities on the sale of non-vegetarian food in the vicinity of the famous Somnath Temple until December 16. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai said its interim order of October 30 shall remain in force till the next hearing on December 16. The Gujarat government has filed an appeal against a single Bench’s order of the High Court striking down the Gir Somnath District Collector’s notification banning non-vegetarian food.

headline: 'To clean-shaven face & head': Owaisi's 'moustache' challenge to Yogi, Akhilesh over CM fight in UP
content: NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Thursday took a swipe at Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, saying neither would become the chief minister after the 2027 assembly elections.Addressing the Samajik Parivartan Morcha's first joint rally in Lucknow, he said the next chief minister would be someone with a moustache, in an apparent reference to alliance partner Chandrashekhar Azad."Someone remarked that this is an alliance between the bearded and the moustachioed. And, in truth, it is. Now, I wish to address that clean-shaven face and the other clean-shaved head, you will not become the CM anymore; it will be someone with a moustache..," he said.Owaisi accused the BJP and the Samajwadi Party of failing to protect the Constitution and ensure adequate political representation for Muslims.Invoking Dr BR Ambedkar, he said the Constitution guaranteed liberty, fraternity, justice and equality. He accused the RSS and the Sangh Parivar of working against these principles."Justice will not come through bulldozers or encounters. Justice will come through Babasaheb Ambedkar's Constitution. The rule of law will be restored," he said, targeting the BJP government.He also criticised the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that it was being used to weaken the Constitution.Targeting the Samajwadi Party, Owaisi accused its leadership of practising caste-based politics and seeking Muslim votes without ensuring adequate representation to the community."How many times will we be betrayed? Akhilesh Yadav, will you give a ticket to a Muslim from Karhal?" he asked. Yadav had won the Karhal seat in the 2022 Assembly elections.Owaisi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adityanath of promoting communal divisions while failing to address unemployment and concerns over education.He said the Morcha, if voted to power, would focus on education and employment for young people."We will ensure education for young people and jobs after they complete their education. We will make doctors and engineers, and ensure that our students get opportunity to study in IITs," he said.Referring to the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, Owaisi urged people to support the Morcha's candidates in the 2027 elections."The historic opportunity before us is that we should support neither the red cap (of Samajwadi Party) nor the RSS-BJP," he said.Praising Azad, Owaisi said he could represent the poor, oppressed and deprived sections of society."If there can be a chief minister in Uttar Pradesh who represents the poor, the oppressed and the deprived, and whose government will be of the people rather than only a particular section, his name will be Chandrashekhar Azad," he said."I am confident that with our unity, prayers and hard work, we will make Chandrashekhar Azad the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh. Together, we will prevent the BJP from forming the government for a third time," Owaisi said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Supreme Court directs tightening of front-of-package nutrition labelling
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) directed that front-of-package nutrition labelling should treat "total sugars" and "saturated fat" rather than "added sugar" and "added fat" as the nutrients of concern alongside "salt". Front-of-package nutrition labelling (FoPNL) is a nutritional information graphic on food packaging that can assist consumers in making an informed decision about food purchases and healthier dietary choices. Supreme Court questions FSSAI for delay in roll-out of warning labels on packaged foods storyline 1 A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran also asked the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to ensure that each hexagon in the FoPNL carries a standardised pictorial representation of the nutrient of concern, together with the corresponding words "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt", as the case may be. Front-of-pack nutrition labelling to be rolled out in single phase, FSSAI tells Supreme Court Front-of-pack nutrition labelling to be rolled out in single phase, FSSAI tells Supreme Court The regulator sought a four-month period for issuing and finalising the draft regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act Front-of-pack nutrition labelling to be rolled out in single phase, FSSAI tells Supreme Court storyline 1 "The FSSAI shall ensure that the FoPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern, each containing the words 'High Fat', 'High Sugar', 'High Salt', respectively, alongside their corresponding pictograms, rather than a single combined hexagon," the Bench said. "The FSSAI shall ensure that the FoPNL treats 'total sugars' and 'saturated fat', rather than 'added sugar' and 'added fat', as the nutrients of concern, alongside 'salt', in alignment with its own long-standing consensus existing prior to the DGI, 2024 (Dietary Guidelines for Indians)," it said. The Bench said the FSSAI shall revisit and reformulate the threshold levels for each nutrient-of-concern. Supreme Court questions FSSAI on thresholds for ‘high’ sugar, salt, fat warnings Supreme Court questions FSSAI on thresholds for ‘high’ sugar, salt, fat warnings Bench emphasises that food safety is a cause of “national interest” Supreme Court questions FSSAI on thresholds for ‘high’ sugar, salt, fat warnings storyline 1 It said as regards sweetened beverages that do not exceed the threshold limits for the relevant nutrient of concern, the FSSAI shall ensure that no front-of-pack label which is identical or deceptively similar, in appearance, form or shape, to the warning label required for beverages that exceed the threshold limits, is displayed for the purpose of denoting its food category. The Bench directed that as regards artificial preservatives and other additives, the FSSAI shall closely monitor the reformulation of products following the introduction of the FoPNL. It noted that the FSSAI, in its affidavit, had stated that it proposes to adopt a single-phase approach for the implementation of the FoPNL regime. "The FSSAI shall bring the regulations into force within the timeline proposed by it and shall take all necessary steps, including pre-emptive steps, to ensure that this timeline is strictly adhered to," the Bench said. Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained Why has FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? What made the water sample unsafe? What are the health risks of bromate and PAHs? How is packaged drinking water regulated in India? What safety checks must bottled water manufacturers follow? What risks do plastic bottles pose to consumers? Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained storyline 1 The Supreme Court delivered its verdict on an application filed in a petition by public charitable trust '3S and Our Health Society' which sought directions to the Centre, States and Union Territories to implement mandatory FoPNL on packaged foods. While hearing the matter on September 28, the top court had questioned the FSSAI over its proposed timeline for implementation of front-of-package labelling on packaged foods. The food regulator had told the top court that it would require approximately four months to issue and finalise the draft regulations. FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO The regulator has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO storyline 1 It had told the Supreme Court that the draft amendment regulations would be published for 60 days to invite comments from stakeholders through domestic consultation and the WTO platform. The Supreme Court had earlier asked the FSSAI, which has proposed phased implementation of front-of-package labelling on packaged foods, to come up with more clarifications on the planned labels of "nutrients of concern", fat, sugar and salt.

headline: Kalaburagi seeks over ₹375 crore in interim crop insurance relief for farmers
content: KALABURAGI The Kalaburagi district administration has submitted a proposal to the State Government seeking interim crop insurance compensation of more than ₹375 crore for farmers who have suffered crop losses due to deficit rainfall during the 2026-27 kharif season. Deputy Commissioner Ikram Shariff said the proposal had been submitted under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) to mitigate the financial losses suffered by farmers and provide them with timely assistance. The district had experienced a severe rainfall deficit, adversely affecting agricultural activities and crop growth, resulting in a considerable decline in expected yields. ₹243.52 crore interim crop insurance relief released to 2.9 lakh farmers in Kalaburagi ₹243.52 crore interim crop insurance relief released to 2.9 lakh farmers in Kalaburagi Minister Priyank Kharge inaugurated district-level Millet Fair-2026 in Kalaburagi city on Saturday ₹243.52 crore interim crop insurance relief released to 2.9 lakh farmers in Kalaburagi storyline 1 The State Government has already declared all 11 taluks of the district drought-affected. Taking into account the rainfall deficit, the extent of damage and the prevailing condition of major crops, including green gram, black gram, soybean, tur, cotton and other crops, the administration has sought interim compensation under the crop insurance scheme. Declare entire Kalaburagi district drought-hit, KPRS demands storyline 1 Mr. Shariff said the insurance company, IndusInd General Insurance Company, had also agreed to the proposal. If the government approves the proposal and sanctions the compensation, eligible farmers in the district are expected to receive more than ₹375 crore against the premium contribution of ₹67.82 crore paid by them. The proposed relief would be nearly six times the farmers’ premium contribution and is expected to provide substantial financial support to those who suffered crop losses during the kharif season, besides helping them continue their agricultural activities. Kalaburagi tops State in crop insurance enrolment Kalaburagi district has secured the first position in Karnataka in crop insurance enrolment for the 2026-27 kharif season, with 4,52,609 farmers insuring a total area of 5,35,820.48 hectares and paying a premium of ₹67.82 crore. Mr. Shariff attributed the achievement to the sustained efforts of officers and staff of the Agriculture Department and the awareness programmes conducted to encourage farmers to enrol under the scheme. November 30 last date for rabi crop insurance The Deputy Commissioner said November 30 was the last date for farmers to enrol under the Karnataka Raitha Suraksha Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for the 2026-27 rabi and summer seasons. Farmers growing Bengal gram, jowar, wheat, safflower and other notified crops have been urged not to wait until the last date and to complete their enrolment at the nearest bank, Grama One or Common Service Centre (CSC). Farmers who have availed themselves of crop loans have been advised to contact the respective banks from which they obtained the loans to complete the enrolment process, he added. headline: ‘Are we alliance partners or your servants?’: Imran Masood to Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing
content: It is no alliance if one partner "leaves" seats for the other after announcing its candidates, Congress MP Imran Masood said on Thursday, doubling down on his criticism of ally Samajwadi Party (SP), which declared five names for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, while the seat-sharing talks were still underway.The SP on Tuesday announced five candidates, four of whom sitting MLAs, attracting the ire of several Congress leaders.Masood, who asserted he will be with the Congress no matter what, said his party is not there to do the SP's bidding."What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us? We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.The MP, who was present during the seat-sharing discussions, said there was little point in holding talks if the seat allocation list was to be released unilaterally afterwards.The Congress lawmaker declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, which is to be released later in the day."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.Masood said the Congress contested 107 seats when SP president Akhilesh Yadav was the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister. "Now, he is yet to become the Chief Minister," he said.Masood also criticised the denial of permission for the Congress's Samvidhaan Raksha March. "What can I say? The Constitution that gives you power is the same Constitution that you want to trample upon," he said.Asked about permission being granted to a conference organised by AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Bhim Army chief Chandra Shekhar Azad, Masood said, "That is precisely the irony. This is the game, and people should understand it … People can draw their own conclusions."BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary said that SP-Congress friendship has "reached the ICU" even before the elections. The Samajwadi Party's "false promises" would ensure its defeat, he said in a statement.Chaudhary said the public witnessed the SP's "misleading manifesto" in the past, and would reject it again.The BJP leader claimed that the Congress submitted a list of 181 seats to the SP, but the latter announced that it would give the ally only 26 seats.

headline: Mumbai Police issues LOCs against CJP's Saurav Das, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka over Dadar protest last month
content: Mumbai Police has issued look-out circulars against Cockroach Janta Party leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, seven weeks after the organisation's protest in Shivaji Park on October 2.According to Mumbai Police officials, the circulars were issued over an FIR registered against Dipke, Das, Ranka, as well as other CJP members and their supporters on October 3 for allegedly gathering illegally and sloganeering in Dadar.The police had denied permission to the CJP’s representative Ajinkya Shinde for organising the protest on Gandhi Jayanti at Shivaji Park, saying they were not empowered to grant permission for any gathering at Shivaji Park. An LoC is an alert sent to Indian immigration checkpoints at international airports, seaports, and land borders to track or stop the person named from entering or leaving the country. Also Read | CJP’s Saurav Das claims his passport leaked, blames ‘BJP-aligned’ social media handlesThe LoC against CJP spokesperson Saurav Das came to light earlier on Thursday after the Centre informed the Delhi High Court about it, stating that it had been done at the request of the Maharashtra Police. Das had moved the HC on Monday (November 23), alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at Oxford University. The CJP had condemned the LoC against Das, saying the outfit spokesperson had not been informed about this when he was stopped at the airport, PTI reported. There was no immediate reaction from the CJP on the LoCs against Dipke and Ranka.Mumbai Police's FIR against CJP leaders, supportersThe Shivaji Park police had registered a case against Abhijeet Dipke, Pranav Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, Saurabh Das, Afreen Nawaz, Saumya Korde, Ankit Bharadwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingle over the protest at Shivaji Park last month. The FIR also mentioned 400 CJP supporters, HT reported earlier.“We have registered a case against the organisers of CJP protests on October 2 at Shivaji Park. The case has been registered under sections 189 (unlawful assembly) and 223 (disobedience to a public servant’s lawful order) of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and section 37 (power to prohibit certain acts for prevention of disorder) and 135 (disobeying or breaking official orders issued by the police) of the Maharashtra Police Act,” a police personnel from the Shivaji Park Police Station had said.The cops had denied permission for CJP's October 2 protest citing a judgment of the Bombay High Court in PIL 116/2009 dated January 4, 2013, and a subsequent order of the Maharashtra government dated January 20, 2016. The HC order had restricted the use of Shivaji Park for purposes other than sports. Police had also said that the organisers had not submitted the required BMC permission for using the ground.Also Read | Passport row: CJP leader asked to explain birthplace discrepancy, says MEACentre informs Delhi HC of LoC against Saurav DasIn a separate development this morning, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, submitted before Justice Amit Mahajan that an LoC had been opened against him.The development came days after Saurav Das claimed he was stopped from flying to London.Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, who was representing Das, told the court that he had not been informed about the LoC and sought details of the circular from the Centre. Sharma argued that Das's legal team could obtain the details independently and challenge the LoC, issued on November 22 and 23. The court has listed the matter for December 9, when Das's counsel is expected to respond to the circular.

headline: KTR calls Rahul Gandhi’s Ashok Nagar interaction with job aspirants ‘PR stunt’, accuses Congress of betraying unemployed youth
content: Hyderabad: BRS working president KTR criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the party’s unfulfilled employment promises to Telangana’s youth, alleging that assurances made ahead of the assembly elections had remained largely on paper. Recalling Gandhi’s interaction with unemployed youth at Ashok Nagar in Hyderabad nearly three years ago, KTR described the visit, during which the Congress leader had Irani chai and spoke to job aspirants, as a “PR stunt”.In a statement, KTR said the Congress’s promise of providing two lakh jobs had proved to be a “myth”, while its Yuva Vikasam initiative remained a “mirage”. He also described the govt’s job calendar as a “mockery” of the trust Telangana’s youth had placed in the party.“Creating jobs is not a photoshoot. It is not a chai-sipping PR stunt. It takes vision and unwavering commitment to create even one job,” the statement said.Accusing Gandhi and the Congress leadership of betraying the expectations of unemployed youth, the BRS leader said the party had failed to deliver on the promises it had made before coming to power. He also invoked the sentiment associated with the Telangana statehood movement, warning that the youth could launch another agitation against the Congress govt.“The youth who fought for a separate Telangana can fight again,” the party leader said, describing the proposed struggle as a fight for the “re-liberation of Telangana” from Congress rule.Invoking former chief minister K Chandrashekar Rao, the BRS working president said Telangana was “the land of KCR” and “the land of fighters”, adding that its youth would not forget what he termed to be a betrayal by the Congress.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Telangana CM Revanth meets new AICC in-charge Sandeep
content: HYDERABAD Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy held a lengthy meeting with the newly appointed All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge for Telangana, Sandeep, with the State Congress government completing nearly three years in office and the party preparing for the next phase of its political activity. The meeting at the Praja Bhavan Guest House in Hyderabad on Thursday (November 26, 2026) lasted nearly two hours. The Chief Minister visited the guest house before joining the Samvidhan Raksha March from the Ambedkar statue at Tank Bund to the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road. He is scheduled to attend a public meeting in Achampet later in the evening. The duration of the Chief Minister’s meeting with the AICC in-charge has assumed significance, particularly as Mr. Reddy had two important public engagements lined up for the day. His decision to set aside nearly two hours for discussions with the newly appointed AICC in-charge indicated the importance the Congress leadership was attaching to consultations on the party’s affairs in Telangana. Though the details of the discussions were not officially disclosed, sources said the meeting covered a wide range of political and organisational issues, including the functioning of the Congress government, the political situation in Telangana and the party’s prospects in the next elections. Mr. Revanth Reddy is learnt to have briefed Mr. Sandeep on the State’s political dynamics and the government’s assessment of its electoral prospects. The issue of indiscipline among party leaders and the need to enforce greater discipline in the organisation also figured in the discussions. Pending appointments of chairpersons to various government corporations and the constitution of their respective teams, besides the party’s future organisational strategy, are understood to have been among the subjects taken up. The meeting assumes importance also in the backdrop of Mr. Sandeep’s recent appointment as the AICC in-charge of Telangana and the need for the new in-charge to familiarise himself with the State’s political and organisational situation. TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud is scheduled to meet Mr. Sandeep separately on Thursday night, indicating a series of consultations by the new AICC in-charge with the State’s top Congress leadership. Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy makes his stand clear Meanwhile, Congress MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy is learnt to have clarified to Mr. Sandeep during a meeting a couple of days ago that his grievances were not directed against Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. Sources said Mr. Rajgopal Reddy reminded Mr. Sandeep that the Congress leadership had promised him a Cabinet berth when he was persuaded to leave the BJP and join the Congress, but the assurance had not been honoured. At the very least, he wanted adequate funds to be released for the development of his constituency, he is understood to have conveyed. Mr. Rajagopal Reddy is understood to have told the AICC in-charge that his concern was over the alleged concentration of development funds with a handful of Ministers, leaving other MLAs struggling to secure allocations for their constituencies.

headline: ICAR-NDRI develops two high-yielding goat strains, eyes national breed recognition
content: Scientists at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research–National Dairy Research Institute (ICAR-NDRI) have achieved another milestone by standardising two high-milk-producing crossbred goat strains — Alpine x Beetal (AB) and Saanen x Beetal (SB).The institute is now working towards registering these strains as breeds to secure national recognition. This could help farmers gain access to improved genetic resources and enhance their income through goat farming.Here is what you need to know about the research and its significance for the future.Why did ICAR-NDRI develop these crossbred goats?The indigenous Beetal goat breed is well adapted to local climatic conditions and can survive on locally available feed. These are hardy animals, but their milk production potential is relatively limited compared with that of specialised dairy goat breeds.On the other hand, Alpine and Saanen goats, originating in North America/France and Switzerland, respectively, are known for their high milk-producing capacity but may not adapt as easily to Indian environmental conditions.Scientists, therefore, decided to cross these exotic dairy breeds with Beetal goats to combine the desirable characteristics of both, particularly higher milk production and better adaptability to Indian conditions.What exactly has ICAR-NDRI developed?Scientists have developed two crossbred goat strains — AB and SB. The AB strain is a cross between Alpine, a dairy goat breed originating in North America/France, and Beetal, an indigenous breed of Punjab.Similarly, the SB strain combines Saanen, a high-milk-producing goat breed originating in Switzerland’s Saanen Valley, with the Beetal goat.Both strains have been developed to improve milk productivity while retaining adaptability to Indian farming conditions. The SB goats also have distinctive physical characteristics, including a predominantly white coat with small brown spots, pale blue eyes and pink skin, which help identify them in the field.How long did it take to develop and standardise these strains?The achievement is the result of long-term scientific research and multiple breeding experiments spanning several decades.The work began in 1971 under the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Goat Improvement, with focused efforts gaining momentum around 2006, when NDRI developed these two strains.A more intensive phase of breeding and improvement began in 2016 and continued thereafter. During this period, scientists focused on systematic breeding, stabilising desirable characteristics, maintaining records of milk production and other performance parameters, selecting superior breeding animals and controlling inbreeding.The standardisation of these strains is, therefore, the outcome of sustained scientific efforts rather than a recent development.What benefits will these goats offer to farmers?According to scientists, the biggest advantage of these crossbred strains is their higher milk production potential. Both strains reportedly produce a maximum of 450 litres of milk per lactation, which lasts around 150 days.Compared with indigenous Beetal goats, these strains reportedly produce nearly twice the total milk yield and have an approximately 20 per cent longer lactation period.This could help farmers increase their daily milk sales and earn an income over a longer period. The strains may be particularly beneficial for small and marginal farmers, landless families and women involved in livestock rearing, as goat farming requires relatively little land and investment.What benefits could these goats offer to the meat industry?Although the primary objective behind developing these crossbred strains is to improve milk production, their offspring, particularly male kids, can also contribute to meat production.Crossbreeding and selective breeding may improve growth and production performance, potentially helping animals reach market weight earlier. This could benefit livestock farmers, meat traders and small-scale producers by reducing the time required to raise animals for sale and improving the economic value of surplus male kids.However, the actual benefits in terms of growth rate, meat yield and market weight would need to be established through comparative performance studies, which are currently underway.How can these goats contribute to better milk quality?Goat milk is valued for its nutritional composition and contains proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals. Its fat globules are generally smaller than those found in cow milk, and its composition makes it an attractive alternative for certain consumers.Crossbreeding can also influence milk composition, including fat and protein content. However, higher milk production does not automatically translate into better milk quality.The nutritional quality of milk depends on the animal’s genetics, feeding, health and hygienic milking practices. By combining improved productivity with appropriate feeding and management, farmers may be able to produce milk that meets the requirements of consumers and organised dairy markets.Will these crossbred goats be easy for ordinary farmers to manage?Scientists claim that these goats can be reared by smallholder farmers without any extra effort.However, since they carry genetic characteristics from exotic dairy breeds, they may require better nutritional and healthcare management than some indigenous goats.Farmers need to ensure balanced feeding, clean and well-ventilated housing, regular vaccination and deworming, adequate drinking water and timely veterinary attention.What does national registration mean, and why is it important?National registration would give these standardised goat strains formal recognition within India’s livestock breeding framework and help prevent bio-piracy.It would establish their identity as recognised genetic resources and provide documented information about their breeding characteristics and performance.

headline: BPSC Issues Notification For 935 Assistant Education Development Officer Vacancies
content: BPSC AEDO Recruitment 2026:The Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) has issued a recruitment notification for 935 posts of Assistant Education Development Officer (AEDO). The application window will open on December 1, and the last date for fee payment is December 30. The deadline for submitting applications is December 31. The Commission stated that the previously published advertisement has been cancelled. Interested and eligible individuals can submit their applications through the official website,bpsconline.bihar.gov.in. Candidates must hold a graduate degree or an equivalent qualification from a recognised university or institution. The minimum age limit is 21 years as on August 1, 2025. The upper age limit is 37 years for unreserved male candidates, 40 years for unreserved female candidates and candidates belonging to backward and extremely backward classes, and 42 years for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe candidates. विज्ञापन सं.-16/2026, शिक्षा विभाग, बिहार के अन्तर्गत सहायक शिक्षा विकास पदाधिकारी के कुल-935 रिक्त पदों पर नियुक्ति हेतु (पूर्व में दिनांक-22.08.2025 को प्रकाशित विज्ञापन संख्या-87/2025 को रद्द करते हुए) सुयोग्य भारतीय उम्मीदवारों से विहित प्रपत्र में ऑनलाइन आवेदन आमंत्रित किए जाते हैं। BPSC BPSCExam BPSCNotice BPSCUpdates AEDO ExamUpdate BPSCAEDO AEDOExam AEDONotification Age relaxation will be applicable to eligible candidates as per Bihar government rules.

headline: Jonty Rhodes adds star attraction to police sports meet in Bidar
content: KALABURAGI Former South African cricketer Jonty Rhodes added a touch of glamour to the three-day annual sports meet of the Bidar District Police Department, which began at the District Police Parade Ground here on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Mr. Rhodes inaugurated the 2026 sports meet by releasing balloons and pigeons into the air, drawing enthusiastic applause from police personnel, sports enthusiasts and members of the public who had gathered in large numbers to catch a glimpse of the former international cricketer. The police department had publicised his participation extensively, putting up large cut-outs and posters at the venue. As he arrived at the ground, the crowd welcomed him with loud applause and cheers. Superintendent of Police Pradeep Gunti felicitated him by presenting a Mysore Peta, shawl and garland. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Rhodes said police personnel worked in a demanding and stressful environment and deserved appreciation for their patience and commitment. “Sports are an excellent way to relieve stress, remain active and improve one’s health. This sports meet should not remain merely an annual event. Everyone should make sports and physical activities a regular part of life,” he advised. Mr. Rhodes said it was his first visit to the city and expressed happiness at being there. He spoke warmly about his association with India, saying that he had travelled extensively across the country for playing and watching cricket and had visited India more often than his home country, South Africa. He also recalled that his daughter, born in Mumbai in 2015, was named ‘India’. His remarks drew loud applause from the audience. Thanking the children who had waited patiently to see him, he described India as a beautiful country and urged people to appreciate the services rendered by the police. For physical, mental fitness Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj and Bidar district in-charge Eshwar B. Khandre said sports were an integral part of life and played an important role in maintaining physical fitness and providing recreation. He noted that Indian sportspersons had brought laurels to the country at State, national and international levels. Emphasising the importance of physical and mental fitness among police personnel, Mr. Khandre said they carried enormous responsibilities, including maintaining law and order, protecting women and children and preventing communal disturbances. “Unlike employees of many other government departments, police personnel had no fixed working hours and had to remain on duty round the clock, responding to accidents, law and order situations, VIP visits, festivals and traffic congestion. Their demanding responsibilities often left them with little time for their families, making their profession particularly challenging. Organising sports meets is essential for the health and well-being of police personnel,” he said. Bidar MLA and former Minister Rahim Khan, Karnataka State Cricket Association’s Raichur Zone member Kushal Patil Gadagi, Superintendnet of Police Pradeep Gunti and others were present. headline: Sam Dalrymple’s ‘Shattered Lands’ wins Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize 2026
content: Author Sam Dalrymple has won the Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay New India Foundation (NIF) Book Prize 2026 for his book “Shattered Lands: Five Partitions and the Making of Modern Asia”, a statement by NIF said.The statement said the jury recognised the book for its “illuminating exploration of the historical and political forces that shaped the Indian subcontinent.”“With remarkable depth of research and compelling storytelling, Sam Dalrymple brings to life the intertwined histories of a region divided by borders, yet bound by shared pasts. An ambitious and compelling work of history, the book offers fresh perspectives on Partition and its enduring legacies.”Dalrymple’s book was selected from a shortlist of five titles. It was recognised for examining lesser-known partitions of British India, tracing the dissolution of the empire across five fractures—from Burma to Aden—rather than limiting its account of Partition to 1947.The other shortlisted books were “A Man for All Seasons: The Life of K.M. Panikkar” by Narayani Basu; “Assembling India’s Constitution: A New Democratic History” by Rohit De and Ornit Shani; “The Secret Master: Arun Kashalkar and a Journey to the Edge of Music” by Sumana Ramanan, and “A Sixth of Humanity: Independent India’s Development Odyssey” by Arvind Subramanian and Devesh Kapur.The NIF Book Prize carries a cash prize of ₹15 lakh, a trophy and a citation. Dalrymple will receive the award at the 15th edition of the Bangalore Literature Festival on December 12.The jury for the award comprised Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran, political scientist Niraja Gopal Jayal, Trilegal partner Rahul Matthan, historian of science Jahnavi Phalkey, historian Srinath Raghavan, former foreign secretary Nirupama Rao and entrepreneur Manish Sabharwal.The New India Foundation supports non-fiction writing on modern India through its Book Fellowship, Translation Fellowship and Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize. Over the past two decades, its book fellowship has supported more than 40 nonfiction books exploring post-1947 India.

headline: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking ASHA workers not to ‘blackmail’ government
content: MYSURU Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said striking ASHA workers could not ‘blackmail’ the government with their demands and urged them to call off their strike and resume duty, assuring them that the government would look into their demands. Speaking to reporters at Mysuru airport, Mr. Shivakumar, who was in the city to inaugurate the State-level Constitution Day celebrations, said he had spoken to the ASHA workers over phone during his Japan tour and appealed to them to withdraw their strike. He urged them to have faith in the government and its assurance against their demands. Karnataka Chief Minister speaks to protesting ASHAs from Japan, urges them to call off stir storyline 1 Expressing dissatisfaction over the workers’ decision to continue their agitation, he said, “They cannot blackmail my government. No government should be blackmailed. I once again appeal to them to end their strike and return to their duties.” Rain or shine, ASHAs continue their protest seeking better pay Rain or shine, ASHAs continue their protest seeking better pay As the protests enter their 10th day today, the sit-in at Freedom Park continues despite a sudden spell of rain Rain or shine, ASHAs continue their protest seeking better pay storyline 1 No written assurance The Chief Minister rejected the demand for a written assurance, saying that accepting such a condition would encourage similar demands from other organisations. “If I give this in writing, everyone will come up with similar demands. There are demands from 17 such organisations. The government has its limitations. I cannot give anything in writing, but they must have faith in the government and in the word of the Chief Minister. Otherwise, I cannot do anything,” he said. Questioning why the ASHA workers were not seeking written assurances from the Union Government, Mr. Shivakumar said there was no provision requiring him to give a written commitment on the matter. “There cannot be an agreement when it comes to meeting demands. However, as I have assured them, I will look into the matter. I am not saying their demands are unjustified. Everyone will make demands, but they must have faith. The country runs on faith. I understand their pain,” he said. He added that a decision on their demands would be taken at the Cabinet and during the Legislature session.

headline: Airline employee arrested for attacking ex-girlfriend’s new partner near Hyderabad airport
content: Hyderabad: A 26-year-old security officer working for an Indian airline at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) was allegedly attacked with a baseball bat by his girlfriend’s ex-boyfriend on Wednesday morning. The accused, who works for a foreign airline at the airport, allegedly rammed the victim’s bike with his car before assaulting him near the airport.RGIA police registered an attempt-to-murder case against the accused and arrested him on Wednesday.According to the complaint, the incident occurred around 5.30 am at Rotary-I Junction on the airport approach road when the victim was riding to work.“He rammed into my bike with a car. I fell on the road. He got down from the car with a baseball bat and attacked me on the head with an intention to kill me,” the complainant alleged, adding that he suffered severe bleeding injuries in the assault.“Cab drivers nearby came to help and took me to a nearby hospital and called the police,” the victim stated in his complaint.The victim told police that the attack stemmed from a relationship dispute. “I have been in a relationship with a co-worker for three months. She was earlier in a relationship with the accused. He could not come to terms with their break-up and her new relationship, and sent our photographs to the woman’s family. Due to his act, family members took her home,” the victim alleged.RGIA police booked a case under section 109(1) (attempt to murder) of the BNS against the accused, who works for a foreign airline at the airport, on Wednesday. “The victim is out of danger. We have arrested the accused on Wednesday. headline: Kharif food grain production for the 2026-27 crop year at 167.14 million tonnes: Union government
content: New Delhi: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Thursday projected Kharif foodgrain production for the 2026-27 crop year at 167.14 million tonnes, 9.77 million tonnes above the average of the previous five years, despite El Niño conditions and a delayed monsoon.“Despite severe weather challenges due to El Niño and a delayed monsoon, kharif food grain production is projected to be 167.14 million tonnes,” Chouhan said while releasing the first advance estimates. The figure remains below the 196.21 million tonnes Kharif target set in September, when the government revised its full-year foodgrain production goal for 2026-27 downward to 373.93 million tonnes, citing El Niño risks. Advance estimates are typically revised as the season progresses..Govt projects Kharif foodgrain production at 167.14 million tonnes despite El Nino; 2025-26 crop output a record.Nutri-cereals (millets) output is estimated at 38.11 million tonnes and oilseeds at 23.95 million tonnes for the 2026 Kharif season. Kharif crops have been harvested, and farmers have begun sowing rabi crops such as wheat.Releasing the final estimates for 2025-26, Chouhan told reporters that a record foodgrain production of 378.54 million tonnes, up about 5.8 per cent or 20.81 million tonnes from 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25.Rice output hit a record 155.15 million tonnes (up 3.3 per cent), while wheat reached a record 122.06 million tonnes (up 3.5 per cent). India, the world’s top rice producer, saw rice exports rise 5 per cent, including premium Basmati shipments to the United States, Canada and the Middle East.Maize production surged nearly 27 per cent to 55.03 million tonnes. Total pulses rose 6.1 per cent to 27.24 million tonnes, led by record moong at 4.40 million tonnes, chana at 12.51 million tonnes and tur at 3.60 million tonnes. Oilseed output touched a record 43.26 million tonnes, with groundnut at 13.17 million tonnes and rapeseed-mustard at 13.77 million tonnes. Sugarcane production was a record 503.73 million tonnes.With comfortable rice and wheat stocks, Chouhan said the government is prioritising pulses and oilseeds — where India remains import-dependent — through national missions aimed at achieving self-reliance.

headline: Owaisi, Azad target Akhilesh Yadav over ‘betrayal’ of Muslims, silence on atrocities against Dalits
content: Parliamentarians Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad, whose parties have allied for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections under the banner of Samajik Parivartan Morcha, on Thursday attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Samajwadi Party (SP). They accused the SP of betraying Muslims after securing their votes and remaining silent on atrocities against Dalits and Muslims as they addressed a gathering at Lucknow’s Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan on Constitution Day in a show of strength.Owaisi, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief, accused SP leader Akhilesh Yadav of treating Muslims as a vote bank while denying them adequate representation. He alleged Yadav took seats away from Muslims despite repeatedly seeking their electoral support.Owaisi accused Yadav of adopting Hindutva politics and questioned the community’s poor representation in educational institutions. He referred to Yadav’s visit to the Ram temple in Ayodhya on December 12. Owaisi said Yadav’s political choices reflected an ideological shift.Owaisi described the alliance with Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) as a partnership beyond electoral calculations. “This is an alliance of hearts, not merely an alliance of political parties,” he said. He added that the alliance would work to prevent the BJP from securing a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh.Owaisi attacked the Yogi Adityanath government’s law-and-order approach, arguing that justice could not be delivered through bulldozer action, “police encounters and half-encounters”. He said 110 Muslims were among 316 people killed in police “encounters” between March 2017 and October 2026. Owaisi said the “encounter policy” disproportionately affected Muslims, Dalits and backward communities.Owaisi questioned the demolition of mosques in the name of encroachment, alleging that such actions reflected the targeting of Muslims. He accused the BJP’s ideological fount, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, of being opposed to the Constitution. Owaisi said protecting constitutional rights requires political empowerment of marginalised communities.Owaisi described voting rights as the most powerful weapon available to disadvantaged sections and urged Muslims and Dalits to use their electoral strength to challenge the BJP and the SP.Azad targeted the government over atrocities against Dalits and Muslims and questioned the SP’s silence on such incidents. He referred to the killings of Vinod Sahni and Ram Lagan Maurya and the 2020 gang-rape and death of a 19-year-old Dalit woman. Azad said their alliance would fight for the dignity, security and political rights of marginalised communities.Azad questioned the government’s “encounter” policy and alleged that Muslims, Dalits and backward communities were its principal victims. He promised there would be no “encounters” if they are voted to power. Azad said that criminals would not be spared and the rule of law would prevail.Azad promised employment opportunities for disadvantaged sections in the first Cabinet meeting if their alliance forms the government. He promised a 15% reservation for the poor and promised two deputy chief ministers, one from the Muslim community and another from a backward caste.He said Muslims should not remain confined to “spreading carpets” at political gatherings but should occupy positions of power, including that of deputy chief minister.Azad questioned the deletion of voters, asking why the BJP had raised concerns over the removal of Hindu votes without disclosing how many Dalit and backward class voters were affected.The AIMIM-Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) alliance has announced plans to contest all 403 assembly seats, projecting Azad as the chief ministerial face. Their Thursday rally was its first major mobilisation.Owaisi urged Muslims to support the alliance, asking whether they wanted to remain supporters or occupy positions of authority.Azad called upon supporters to protect their voting rights and use them judiciously. “If the BJP gives ₹20,000, we will give ₹25,000.”

headline: M Kharge Schools MP Imran Masood Amid Samajwadi Seat Talks: "Let's Not Be Arrogant"
content: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday had a pointed direction for party MP Imran Masood, who's been combative against ally Samajwadi Party, as the seat-sharing talks for the UP Assembly elections become a battleground within the INDIA bloc. Kharge mentioned Masood by name in his speech in Lucknow as he spoke of state leaders one by one. "[There's] Imran Masood, whom I frequently hear on television, where he often speaks with great passion. content: KOCHI “Why do Home and Vigilance departments exist if the court has to compel every action in cases against powerful people?” the Kerala High Court has asked orally in the microfinance scam case involving Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan Microfinance fraud case: first chargesheet filed against Vellappally Natesan Microfinance fraud case: first chargesheet filed against Vellappally Natesan Microfinance fraud case: first chargesheet filed against Vellappally Natesan storyline 1 Justice A. Badharudeen on Thursday (November 26, 2026) noted that the agency had filed final report only in one of the eight cases it had informed the court. headline: ‘Modi is sitting quietly today’: Kharge hints at BJP top brass rift, jibes at Yogi over PM ambitions
content: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday credited the people of Uttar Pradesh with checking the BJP's electoral ambitions in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying their verdict had forced Prime Minister Narendra Modi to go quiet on his '400 paar' slogan.Addressing a 'Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan' at the Congress office in Lucknow on Constitution Day, Kharge also accused the BJP of allowing its funds to swell while inflation, unemployment and the prices of cooking gas and essential food items continued to rise."I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, 'Abki Baar, 400 Paar' (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today," Kharge said.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won 36 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections.Kharge also claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah had reduced his public statements, adding, "I do not know whether the two (Modi and Shah) are getting along or not."In a veiled reference to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, the Congress chief said another leader in Lucknow also had his eyes on the prime minister's chair.Kharge questions BJP's Rs 10,000 crore fundsTargeting the BJP over its finances, Kharge questioned the source of nearly Rs 10,000 crore in party funds, alleging that the ruling party was benefiting from the use of central investigative agencies to intimidate people and collect money."Everything has become expensive. But the BJP's coffers are filling up. Where has the BJP got Rs 10,000 crore in its party funds from? You question us, but we want to ask you where this Rs 10,000 crore came from," he said.The BJP has cash and deposits worth nearly Rs 10,000 crore, according to its annual audit report recently submitted to the Election Commission.Kharge alleged that the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Income Tax Department and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were being used to threaten people and extract money."By deploying the ED, Income Tax Department and CBI to threaten people and extract money, the BJP is filling its coffers. This is nothing short of robbery," he said.Congress holds Constitution Day march in LucknowThe Congress organised a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Lucknow on Thursday to mark Constitution Day. However, the march did not reach its intended destination, with Kharge alleging that the state government was afraid of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.Kharge said the government had begun fearing even the party's shadows and asserted that Congress workers would take out the march whenever an opportunity arose.Kharge also recalled the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, and highlighted Uttar Pradesh's contribution to the process. He referred to a resolution passed by the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly in October 1937 calling for the repeal of the Government of India Act, 1935, and the framing of India's Constitution by an elected Constituent Assembly.Earlier, Kharge paid tribute to the ashes of BR Ambedkar at the Ambedkar Mahasabha in Lucknow before heading to the Congress office. Congress state president Aradhana Misra Mona, MP Imran Masood and the party's state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam were among those present.Meanwhile, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused the Modi government of undermining parliamentary democracy and disregarding parliamentary conventions. Addressing reporters during the march, he said the party was holding protests at state headquarters across the country over concerns about Parliament's functioning and the protection of the Constitution."They have turned Parliament into a complete mockery; even after 106 days, they haven't even prorogued Parliament," Venugopal said, questioning the delay in convening the Winter Session.He also alleged that the government had denied people an opportunity to observe Constitution Day through parliamentary proceedings, and asked why there was no indication of when the Winter Session would begin.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: After Delhi, INDIA bloc to hold next anti-CEC rallies in BJP-ruled Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Bengal
content: The INDIA bloc has decided to take its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to three BJP-ruled states — Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and West Bengal — in the next phase, people aware of the matter said on Thursday.Leaders of the Opposition grouping plan to hold a rally in Bhopal on December 12, in Ahmedabad on December 19 and in Kolkata in January, according to the people.“It is a well-thought-out plan. After Delhi, we are going to BJP-ruled states. Holding a rally in Madhya Pradesh holds significance for north India,” Derek O’Brien, Trinamool Congress’s leader in the Rajya Sabha, told HT.The proposed rallies will follow a series of marches in Delhi and a gathering at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, where Opposition parties demanded Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise. The choice of Bhopal as a site of the rally also carries political significance for the alliance. When the INDIA bloc was formed in Patna in June 2023, one of its early decisions was to organise a rally in the Madhya Pradesh capital. At the first meeting of its 14-member coordination committee, held at Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar’s residence on September 13, 2023, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal announced that the rally would take place in the first week of October. The proposed agenda included rising prices, unemployment and alleged corruption by the BJP government in the state.ALSO READ | Delhi police files FIR against 22 people from INDIA bloc rally who went near Jantar MantarHowever, the rally was called off amid a controversy over remarks by Udhayanidhi Stalin, son of then Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK leader MK Stalin, on Sanatan Dharma. The cancellation was announced by then Madhya Pradesh Congress chief Kamal Nath.The political context in Madhya Pradesh has since changed, with the Congress registering a few electoral victories in the state. It won the Vijaypur assembly bypoll in November 2024 and three of the nine urban local body polls in July 2025. In August this year, Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh also defeated BJP’s Ashutosh Tiwari in the Datia assembly bypoll.The INDIA bloc’s campaign against the SIR has included marches by leaders and workers of more than 19 Opposition parties in central Delhi. The parties also submitted a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu and approached the Supreme Court over the revision exercise.At the November 1 Ramlila Maidan rally, Opposition leaders demanded Kumar’s resignation. Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also warned that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah would be the next targets of the Opposition’s campaign after the chief election commissioner.At a rally in Lucknow on Thursday, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the BJP of attempting to disenfranchise people through “vote chori”, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “Gyanesh alliance” was taking away their voting rights, in an apparent reference to CEC Kumar.ALSO READ | INDIA bloc's protest keeps shoppers away, Connaught Place bears the brunt before Diwali“A conspiracy is being hatched through SIR to disenfranchise Dalits and backward classes in Uttar Pradesh. Today, Modi ji’s ‘Gyanesh alliance’ is stripping people of their voting rights under the guise of ‘SIR’. They have forgotten that the vote is the power of the people, not the private property of any government,” Kharge said.He also accused the BJP of selectively raising concerns over deleted votes, saying that the people most affected were Dalits, extremely backward classes and other marginalised communities.“A few days ago, the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh suddenly realised that votes were being deleted. He raised a huge hue and cry, claiming that the votes of Hindus had been deleted! Yes, votes have indeed been deleted — specifically those of Dalits, the extremely backward classes and the marginalised — the very people who defeated Modi ji in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections,” Kharge said.There was no immediate reaction from the BJP to his allegations.

headline: HC to hear Tata Trusts' plea against Chandra's reappointment on Friday
content: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT) on Thursday filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.The court will hear the matter on Friday. ALSO READ: Tata Trusts moves Bombay HC against Chandrasekaran's 3rd term at Tata SonsThe SDTT has sought ₹50 crore, while the RDTT has sought ₹15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest.As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA). Senior counsel Janak Dwarkadas, appearing for the two trusts, mentioned the suits on Thursday before a single bench of Justice Arif Doctor, seeking an urgent hearing.Justice Doctor, however, recused himself without assigning any reasons, following which the suits were mentioned before Justice Abhay Ahuja, who was sitting on the alternate bench.Dwarkadas told the court that a hearing was required before the November 30 board meeting of Tata Sons.Justice Ahuja then said the pleas shall be heard on Friday.The immediate relief sought is to prevent the chairman of Tata Sons from exercising his casting vote during the November 30 board meeting in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors.In the suits, the trusts have not sought a stay on the board meeting but a direction that Chandrasekaran does not cast his vote.The suits said Article 121 of Tata Sons' AoA does not permit the chairman of a board meeting to exercise a casting vote in cases where the articles require the affirmative vote of a majority of the trustees.The dispute follows N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman for five more years at the September 17 board meeting.The suits have said the decision was "ultra vires the Articles of Association and is invalid, illegal, null and void".The two trusts voted on Wednesday night to pass the resolutions to move HC as there was a lack of any satisfactory replies to the communications sent by them since September 17.Tata Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata, holds around 66 per cent of Tata Sons and has sought a permanent order and injunction restraining Tata Sons, its directors, officers and other agents from acting upon in any manner or giving effect to the September 17 resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran.In a statement on September 20, the Trusts had said the resolution was not validly passed and had no legal effect.At the centre of the dispute are Tata Sons' AoA and special rights given to Trusts-nominated directors. It has two nominee directors on its board -- Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan. On September 17, Noel Tata had voted against Chandrasekaran's reappointment, while Venu Srinivasan supported it.As per Trusts, both nominated directors were required to support the decision.In its statement issued in September, the Trusts said the AoA of Tata Sons provide that no decision can be taken unless it has the affirmative support of at least a majority of the Directors nominated by the Tata Trusts. This is a separate condition under the AoA, it said, pointing out that the AoA does not leave any decision of the board to a mere head count of directors.
