headline: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts: Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifesto
content: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday released his party's "PDA manifesto" ahead of the UP assembly polls. The announcement comes on Constitution Day.The PDA, a political formulation promoted by Akhilesh Yadav, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities). The SP has indicated that releasing its manifesto months before the polls will allow it to take its proposals to the public ahead of the election campaign.Here's what Akhliesh Yadav announcedPDA youth will be provided access to higher education through a special state education policy. The issue of paper leaks will be addressed, all examinations will be conducted on schedule, and results will be declared with complete transparency.Graduate students will be provided employment opportunities. Those who remain unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of Rs 5,000.The party will provide government jobs to 25 lakh youths and create employment opportunities across other sectors.Will begin caste-survey across the state to frame policies for the targeted upliftment.Samajwadi canteens will be set up, where meals will be available for Rs 5 per plate.Elderly women will receive Rs 40,000 as pension, with the amount transferred directly to their bank accounts.Women workers above a certain age will also be provided Rs 40,000.For government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore, 50% reservation will be provided to members of the PDA community.The party is expected to announce three more detailed manifesto, including district, city and women-centric.In the party's election manifesto release, Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the rival BJP, saying: "When a few dominant, supremacists and selfish people want to keep their thousands of years of power intact and in that attempt want to not only amend and change but also erase the Constitution - all of us those who love the Constitution should take it up as our national and social duty to unite and thwart all conspiracies to amend the Constitution".He further said: "Our country will be governed by 'Samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'Manvidhan' (arbitrariness). There are a few powers who want to do this through 'Manvidhan' and not 'Samvidhan'. There is an ongoing war over Constitution. On one hand, there are those who want to misue the Constitution to come to power. One the other hand is PDA, who wants the rule of social justice of the Constitution, we want to erase all differences, uphold reservation and equality..."Akhilesh Yadav's annoucement comes as relations between Congress and his party appeared to sour after the SP jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming polls.The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties. To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.Later, SP offered 26 seats to the Congress, which triggered unease on the second day of the seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls between the two alliance partners in Delhi on Tuesday.According to reports, SP’s offer of 26 seats came after the Congress tabled a list of 120 seats of its choice.Unease was noticeable in the Congress camp over SP’s 26-seat offer as Saharanpur MP and member of Congress’s negotiating team Imran Masood objected to media claims of SP’s 36-seat offer.The SP is expected to contest the 2027 assembly elections in alliance with the Congress against the BJP-led govt in UP. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, while the SP governed under Akhilesh from 2012 to 2017. The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), led by Mayawati, was in power from 2007 to 2012.The 403-member UP assembly is expected to witness a major contest between the BJP and the SP-led opposition, with alliances and the mobilisation of different social groups likely to play an important role in the campaign. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while its ally Apna Dal (Sonelal) secured 12.The SP won 111 seats, while its allies also won seats. The Congress secured two seats, and the BSP one. The SP received approximately 32% of the vote in the 2022 polls, emerging as the principal opposition party in the state.By choosing to release its manifesto on the Constitution Day, the SP has linked the launch of its electoral programme to a day associated with constitutional values and democratic institutions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Judicial Member Must Hear Probe Agency Property Attachment Cases: Supreme Court
content: In a significant verdict, the Supreme Court on Thursday held that the adjudicating authority confirming provisional attachment of properties by the Enforcement Directorate under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member. Observing that even a single-member bench can adjudicate such matters if its sole member is from the judicial field, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant held that adjudication under Sections 8(2) and 8(3) of the PMLA involves interpretation of statutory provisions and appreciation of evidence, and hence the presence of a judicial member is essential to ensure legal objectivity and fairness. The CJI, however, clarified that a judicial member is not required while issuing a show-cause notice under Section 8(1) of the Act. The requirement applies to subsequent hearing and determination of whether the attached property is involved in money laundering. Referring to the serious consequences of property attachment, the verdict said that confirmation of provisional attachment can lead to the government taking possession of the property, potentially depriving its owner of its use until the trial concludes. "If the adjudicating authority finds that the property is involved in money laundering, the provisions of Sections 8(3) and 8(4) are attracted, and the property is taken over by the Government of India. Such dispossession may well endure until the conclusion of the trial for the offence of money laundering, depriving the person of the use of the property for a considerable period before the offence is proved," the verdict said.

headline: Colombo Security Conclave adopts 2026-27 roadmap to boost maritime security, counter terror
content: The members of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) have adopted a roadmap of cooperation for 2026-2027, with deliverables and activities in areas such as maritime security and countering terrorism and radicalisation.A meeting of national security advisers of the CSC was hosted by the Maldives at Villa Nautica Paradise Island on Wednesday. India was represented at the meeting by a delegation led by National Security Adviser Ajit Doval.The CSC includes India, the Maldives, Mauritius and Sri Lanka and has emerged in recent years as a key platform for countering terrorism and ensuring maritime security in the Indian Ocean.The external affairs ministry said on Thursday that the CSC member states adopted the roadmap of cooperation, which sets out key deliverables and planned activities under the five pillars of cooperation – maritime security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational crime, cybersecurity, protection of critical infrastructure and technology, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.In addition to delegations from the Maldives, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, Australia and Malaysia participated in the meeting as guests. Australia was represented by Sarah Storey, head of the office of Southeast Asia in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and Malaysia by Khairul Azhar bin Abu Bakar, director of the maritime security division at the National Security Council.During the meeting, the CSC’s first secretary general, Vice Admiral SN Ghormade (retired), presented a review of the actions taken to implement the decisions of the last meeting of the national security advisers in New Delhi in November 2025.The member states also reaffirmed their collective commitment to promoting regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. They emphasised the need to strengthen collaboration across the five pillars of cooperation, especially through training and capacity-building initiatives, and underlined the importance of collective efforts to advance the objectives of the CSC.

headline: AI safety debate intensifies as researchers warn of risks, UN seeks rules
content: Concerns over the safety of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models are growing, with researchers at leading AI companies reportedly questioning whether some systems under development can be released safely, given the risks that existing safeguards may not be able to contain. Recent incidents involving AI agents bypassing security controls, accessing real-world systems and acting beyond their assigned tasks have added to these concerns. The debate has also exposed differences among leading AI companies over how much autonomy should be given to AI systems and how much control humans should retain over their decisions. The developments have prompted fresh calls for stronger safeguards, with the United Nations (UN) urging countries to work towards a common framework for managing AI risks.Why are AI researchers worried about unreleased modelsAccording to a report by Axios, employees at Anthropic and OpenAI have been raising concerns that their most advanced internal AI models could become too capable to release safely. Researchers have reported advances in reasoning across mathematics, science, cybersecurity and AI research. Some unreleased models are said to be far more capable than those available to the public. Researchers are also questioning whether they can reliably monitor their behaviour and prevent them from acting against instructions.ALSO READ: India Inc built websites for people. AI bots are struggling to read themOne concern relates to reinforcement learning, a training method in which AI models learn through trial and error, receiving rewards for completing tasks or meeting specific objectives. As models become more capable, they may also become better at finding ways to exploit the reward system. A model could learn to bypass safety restrictions if doing so helps it achieve a higher score. Another concern relates to how researchers monitor an AI model's reasoning. Developers have traditionally relied on written explanations of models' thought processes, often referred to as chain of thought, to understand how they arrive at an answer or decide on an action. However, sources cited by Axios said some advanced internal models have shown signs of concealing their reasoning or producing misleading explanations that satisfy human monitors. These developments have led to discussions within the companies about whether the most capable models should be made publicly available. Some researchers believe companies may need to restrict access to advanced systems, while others have questioned whether training even more capable models should continue until better safety methods are available.Is AI moving towards developing its own successorsAnother concern highlighted in the Axios report is the possibility of recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems become capable of designing and developing more capable versions of themselves with limited human involvement. AI companies already use their models to assist with software development and research. Anthropic said more than 80 per cent of the code it merged into its codebase was written by Claude as of May 2026. Its engineers were also producing around eight times as much code a day in the second quarter of 2026 as they did in 2024.ALSO READ: No violation of AI scheme in Sarvam's Chinese offerings: Meity secyFully autonomous recursive self-improvement has not been achieved. The concern is that as AI takes on more of the development process, it could accelerate the creation of successor models and leave researchers with less time to evaluate their capabilities and establish safeguards.Rival AI leaders question Anthropic's approachThe discussion around AI safety has also exposed a disagreement over the future relationship between humans and increasingly capable AI systems. Anthropic has faced criticism from rival AI leaders over its position on how much decision-making authority should eventually be delegated to AI. The disagreement centres on the possibility that AI systems could outperform humans in several areas, including scientific research, software development and complex decision-making. One argument within the industry is that if these systems become more capable than human experts, allowing them to take on greater responsibility could produce better results. OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman and Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang have been among those arguing that humans must retain control over the direction of AI development. Their criticism of Anthropic reflects concerns that the company is too willing to accept a future in which AI systems exercise authority over decisions that should remain with people. Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei rejected the suggestion that his company supports surrendering human agency to AI. In a post on X on November 25, he called the allegation "absurd" and said handing governance over to AI systems would be a terrible idea. Amodei argued that the criticism conflates two separate questions: allowing AI to govern human affairs and allowing it to perform specific tasks with greater autonomy. He said he supports humans retaining control over political decisions and governance through legitimate democratic processes. However, he acknowledged that greater AI autonomy could be useful in specific areas, including driving, drug discovery and software development. In these cases, allowing systems to carry out tasks with limited human intervention could save time and potentially lives. Amodei also identified areas where AI autonomy may need to be restricted. These include systems that can contribute to developing more capable versions of themselves, deployments that could cause significant job disruption and AI systems used in research into AI alignment, which focuses on ensuring that a model's behaviour remains consistent with human intentions. He also criticised rival executives for publicly arguing in favour of human control while releasing products that automate more tasks. Amodei described some of their messaging as "vibes-based commercial and political positioning", arguing that companies should demonstrate their commitment to human agency through their products and safety measures.UN calls for global framework as AI risks outpace safeguardsThe concerns raised by researchers and the disagreement among AI companies come as governments face pressure to establish common rules for the development and deployment of advanced AI systems. On November 23, UN Secretary-General António Guterres called on member states to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing AI risks. Speaking at the close of the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety in Barbados, he warned that AI was driving "the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind". Guterres said this transfer was taking place from states and governing institutions to a small number of companies and individuals. He also warned that existing protections against AI risks remained fragmented, with governments often struggling to keep pace with developments in the technology. He called on member states to develop a globally inclusive, principles-based multilateral framework for AI risk management within a year. The proposed framework would establish shared safety measures, common approaches to testing, clear safeguards and transparency requirements. It would also provide for independent and credible oversight of advanced AI models. The proposal seeks to establish a common foundation for AI safety while helping countries develop the capacity to assess and manage risks. Guterres said support would be needed to ensure that all countries could implement the framework, given differences in their technical and financial resources. The UN chief also warned that the risks were not limited to the behaviour of individual AI models. Recent cyberattacks and technology outages have exposed vulnerabilities in digital infrastructure, while AI systems have begun behaving in ways that their developers did not always anticipate. The proposal also addresses concerns about the concentration of AI capabilities among a small number of companies and countries. Most advanced models require large-scale computing infrastructure, specialised chips, data and research teams — resources that remain concentrated among a limited group of technology developers. This leaves many governments dependent on companies for access to AI systems and information about their capabilities. Independent testing and oversight could help address this imbalance, although putting such a framework into practice would require countries to agree on common standards and how they should be implemented.

headline: ‘Tears of Anger’: South Korean anchor breaks down on live TV after Samsung, KOSPI crash on Nov 25 | Viral video
content: A sharp sell-off in South Korean stocks took an emotional turn on Tuesday when financial television anchor Kim Ah-hyun struggled to hold back tears during a live broadcast, as she watched a Samsung Electronics-linked leveraged investment product plunge more than 15% in a single session.The moment, which has since spread across social media, came as South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index suffered one of its steepest single-day declines this year. The index fell 6.16%, shedding 308.52 points to close at 4,697.51 on November 25, wiping out the previous session's gains and marking its lowest closing level since January 13.Kim, who hosts Seoul Economic TV's financial programme 'Kim Ah-hyun's Golden Stocks', was discussing the difficult conditions facing investors when a chart showing a 15.21% fall in a single-stock leveraged product linked to Samsung Electronics appeared on screen.She fell silent for several seconds, lowered her head and appeared visibly emotional before looking towards the production team for assistance. The broadcast subsequently cut away from the chart.WATCH THE VIRAL VIDEO HERESouth Korean stock market crash leaves retail investors under pressure The sharp fall in the KOSPI came after a strong rally a day earlier, when the index had gained 4.79% amid renewed enthusiasm for artificial intelligence stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to his position. However, the mood changed sharply on November 25. Falling US chip stocks and reports that Washington could impose fresh tariffs on 16 economies added to investor anxiety, triggering heavy selling across Seoul's markets. The KOSPI opened nearly 4% lower, briefly triggering a temporary halt in programme trading sell orders. It later touched an intraday low of 4,672.55 before recovering slightly towards the close. South Korea's two biggest semiconductor companies bore much of the damage. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.87%, while SK Hynix plunged 11.05%. Foreign investors sold a net 1.8993 trillion won, worth approximately $1.4 billion, in South Korean shares. 'Tears of anger': What the South Korean anchor said after going emotional on air In a subsequent livestream, Kim explained that her reaction came after hearing repeated accounts of retail investors suffering substantial losses. She described her emotions as 'tears of anger' and urged investors not to lose hope despite the difficult market conditions. The incident struck a chord online, with footage of the broadcast circulating widely on overseas social media platforms. South Korea considers market support as KOSPI rebounds The sharp sell-off has also prompted South Korean authorities to consider additional support for the stock market. According to reports, the South Korean government is examining an expansion of its securities market stabilisation fund, which currently stands at 10.76 trillion won, or around $8 billion. The Korea Development Bank has reportedly approached 25 financial institutions to assess their capacity to contribute more funds. No final decision on the expansion has been announced. There was some relief on November 26, when the KOSPI recovered after the previous day's steep losses. The index rose 0.3% to close at 4,711.21, while Samsung Electronics gained 0.4% and SK Hynix advanced 2.2%. Investors also kept an eye on the Bank of Korea's interest rate decision, looking for signals on the direction of monetary policy amid the market turbulence.

headline: From film boycotts to OTT: A timeline of India's curbs on Pakistani content
content: Over the years, India has taken several steps to restrict Pakistani entertainment content. These include cancelling concerts, calls to boycott films, stopping television shows and streaming content, and blocking social media accounts. On Thursday, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting asked Netflix to ensure that content originating in Pakistan is not streamed in India. The ministry’s move followed complaints about the possible release in India of the Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, which is scheduled to premiere globally on December 4. This action is the latest in a series of measures the government has taken over the years to restrict Pakistani entertainment content. Here is a look at the major developments over the years. 2016: Uri attack leads to calls to ban Pakistani artistes The September 18, 2016, terror attack on an Army camp in Uri, Jammu and Kashmir, in which 19 soldiers were killed, led to demands to stop Pakistani artistes from working in India. The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) asked Pakistani actors, including Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, to leave the country within 48 hours. It also warned that film shoots involving Pakistani artistes would be disrupted. The Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association (IMPPA) subsequently passed a resolution barring Pakistani actors, technicians and performers from working in India on fresh assignments. The association said the restriction would apply to new projects, while films already completed or under production would not be affected. ALSO READ: 18 years since 26/11: Remembering the horrors of Mumbai terror attack The controversy also affected television. Zee's Zindagi channel stopped airing Pakistani shows after the Uri attack and replaced them with other content. One of the films caught in the debate was Karan Johar's Ae Dil Hai Mushkil, which featured Fawad Khan. The film faced calls for a boycott, but was eventually released in October 2016 after discussions and assurances from the filmmaker. 2019: Pulwama attack triggers fresh boycott calls The February 14, 2019, Pulwama terror attack, in which 40 Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel were killed, led to renewed demands for a ban on Pakistani artistes. The MNS asked Indian music companies, including T-Series, Sony Music, Venus and Tips, to stop working with Pakistani singers. T-Series removed songs by Atif Aslam and Rahat Fateh Ali Khan from its YouTube channels and stopped promoting them on radio and television. The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) also announced a blanket ban on Pakistani actors and artistes working in the Indian film industry. It warned that action would be taken against production houses that continued to work with them. The controversy extended to films as well. Salman Khan's Bharat, which had songs recorded by Pakistani singers, faced demands to remove their contributions. The songs were subsequently re-recorded with Indian voices. 2023: Courts reject calls for a blanket ban In October 2023, the Bombay High Court rejected a petition seeking a ban on Pakistani artistes working in India. The petitioner had asked the court to direct the Centre to prevent Indian citizens and companies from engaging Pakistani actors, singers, musicians and other film workers. The matter reached the Supreme Court, which dismissed the appeal in November 2023. The court advised the petitioner against taking a narrow view of cultural exchanges. The ruling did not amount to a government policy allowing all Pakistani artistes to work in India. However, it rejected the demand for a blanket legal ban through the court. 2025: Pahalgam attack leads to restrictions on social media accounts The April 22, 2025, attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed, led to another round of restrictions on Pakistani entertainment and media content in India. On April 30 and May 1 last year, Instagram accounts of several Pakistani actors and celebrities became inaccessible to users in India. These included Hania Aamir, Mahira Khan, Ali Zafar, Sanam Saeed, Bilal Abbas, Iqra Aziz, Imran Abbas and Sajal Aly. Users trying to access the accounts saw a message stating: "Account not available in India. This is because we complied with a legal request to restrict this content". The restrictions applied to access from India. Other Pakistani artistes, including singers and actors, were also affected. Some Pakistani social media accounts briefly became accessible again in July. However, officials said this was due to a technical error, and several accounts were blocked once more. Restrictions were also reported on X, formerly Twitter, against some Pakistani public figures. These included accounts of political leaders and other personalities. April-May 2025: Pakistani YouTube channels blocked The government also blocked 16 Pakistani YouTube channels in April 2025 following the Pahalgam attack. The channels included those run by Dawn News, Samaa TV, ARY News and Geo News. The government said the channels were spreading provocative and communally sensitive content, as well as false and misleading information about India, its Army and security agencies. On May 2, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's YouTube channel was also blocked in India. May 2025: Govt asks OTT platforms to stop streaming Pakistani content On May 8, 2025, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued an advisory to online curated content publishers, OTT platforms, media streaming services and intermediaries. It asked them to discontinue access to web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming content originating in Pakistan. The ministry referred to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. These rules require platforms to exercise caution while carrying content that could affect India's sovereignty and integrity, national security, relations with foreign countries or public order. The advisory came after the Pahalgam attack and referred to concerns over cross-border links to terror activities. June 2025: Netflix tells govt it has no Pakistani shows in India In June 2025, Netflix informed the government that it had not made any film or series originating in Pakistan available to subscribers in India. The assurance became relevant again in November 2026, when the proposed India release of a Pakistani series on the platform led to fresh complaints. November 2026: Centre asks Netflix to keep Pakistani content off its India platform On November 26, 2026, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting asked Netflix to adhere to its May 8, 2025, advisory and ensure that Pakistani-origin content was not streamed in India. The move followed complaints about the possible release of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo. The series is based on a novel by Pakistani author Farhat Ishtiaq and features Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir, Sanam Saeed and Ahad Raza Mir, among others. Its trailer was released on November 24, and it is scheduled to premiere globally on December 4. The AICWA and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) had also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene and stop the series from being streamed in India. AICWA sought a permanent ban on Pakistani content across television, cinema and OTT platforms. The ministry reminded Netflix of the commitment it had given in June 2025 that it was not making Pakistani films or series available to Indian subscribers. It asked the platform to maintain that position.

headline: Who is Vardhaman Jain? Chennai entrepreneur donates 121 kg gold worth up to  ₹206 crore to Tirupati temple
content: A donation of 121 kg of gold ornaments to Lord Venkateswara at the Tirumala temple has brought attention to Chennai-based entrepreneur Vardhaman Jain. The offering, made on November 26, 2026, is among the major individual contributions reported in the history of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and his wife, Nara Bhuvaneswari, were present when Jain presented the gold ornaments at Tirumala. The value of the donation has been estimated differently across reports, with figures ranging from ₹150 crore to ₹206 crore.Who is Vardhaman Jain?Vardhaman Jain is a Chennai-based entrepreneur known for his work in healthcare technology, business process outsourcing (BPO) and automation. He is the founder and former vice-chairman of Access Healthcare, a company that provides technology-enabled services to the healthcare industry, The Times of India reported.Jain studied Statistics at Loyola College in Chennai before moving to the US to pursue a master's degree in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Austin.His professional expertise includes healthcare technology, medical coding, image processing and robotic process automation (RPA). He also holds several patents related to image processing and medical coding, according to reports.Before establishing his entrepreneurial ventures, Jain held senior corporate positions. He also co-founded Vision HealthSource and served as managing director of the BPO division at Dell Services.He has also been associated with Asia Chennai Engineering and other business ventures, according to the supplied reports.What does Vardhaman Jain's 121 kg gold donation include?The gold offering comprises an elaborate collection of ornaments designed for Lord Venkateswara. These include a crown, armlets, shoulder ornaments, a waist belt and ornaments for the deity's feet. According to TOI, the collection consists of dozens of specially designed pieces intended to adorn the deity from head to toe. The ornaments are expected to be used during daily rituals and special occasions. Reports said the deity would be adorned with the new ornaments on November 27.The estimated value of the offering has varied across reports. Initial estimates placed it at around ₹150-160 crore, while a subsequent report cited a valuation of approximately ₹206 crore.Vardhaman Jain's earlier donations to Tirumala templeThe 121 kg gold offering is not Jain's first contribution to the Tirumala temple. He has reportedly supported several TTD initiatives since 2019. His earlier contributions include: ₹7 crore for SVBC: Jain contributed ₹7 crore towards the development of Sri Venkateswara Bhakti Channel, the devotional television channel operated by TTD. ₹5 crore cattle feed plant: He established a fodder mixing plant worth ₹5 crore at the TTD Goshala to support cattle care. ₹1 crore coin-sorting machine: He donated a machine to help the temple administration sort and count coins received through devotees' offerings.Electric buses: In May 2026, he also contributed electric buses to support TTD's transportation requirements.Vardhaman Jain's philanthropic work beyond religious donationsJain has also reportedly been associated with initiatives in healthcare, education and skill development.He serves as the managing trustee of Kanchi Kamakoti CHILDS Trust Hospital, which works in paediatric healthcare, TOI reported. Through the Sarita Jain Foundation, he reportedly supports educational and medical assistance programmes, including Vidya Seva and Vaidya Seva. He has also established Aavishkaar, an initiative aimed at providing skill development opportunities to young people from underprivileged backgrounds.His reported philanthropic activities therefore extend beyond contributions to religious institutions, covering healthcare access, education and social development.

headline: Nitin Gadkari's big infrastructure push for Kolkata: 250-km ring road approved at ₹14,000 crore; here's what he said
content: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari on Thursday gave the go-ahead to a 250-km ring road project in Kolkata, which is expected to cost ₹14,000 crore and help tackle the city's traffic congestion.The announcement came during an event at Kolaghat in Purba Medinipur district, where Gadkari inaugurated 22 development projects with an investment of ₹8,700 crore. He said the proposal was taken up after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and his ministerial colleagues approached him over the city's traffic woes, following which he directed officials to work out a plan."I want to make Kolkata a better city. I had told your minister and officials to prepare a plan to free Kolkata from traffic congestion. I am announcing approval for a 250-km ring road for Kolkata at a cost of ₹14,000 crore," he said, with Adhikari present on the stage, according to PTI.Gadkari said the proposed ring road was the first step in a larger initiative to upgrade Kolkata's road network and instructed officials to evaluate the city's infrastructure needs.He also advocated the use of contemporary urban road engineering techniques, under which roads, flyovers and metro rail corridors can be accommodated on a common pillar-based structure. Such an approach, he said, could maximise the use of limited urban space while improving traffic movement.Referring to similar infrastructure projects undertaken in Pune and Nagpur, he highlighted their potential as models for Kolkata."This is just the beginning. The real picture is yet to unfold," he said, adding that "We have developed Mumbai and Delhi; now we will develop Kolkata."Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh refers to Gadkari as ‘Vishwakarma’State minister Dilip Ghosh on Thursday voiced optimism about new infrastructure projects and progress on pending highway proposals. He praised Gadkari, referring to him as "Vishwakarma" and expressing confidence that the minister would deliver on expectations, as per ANI.Addressing reporters in Kolkata, Ghosh recalled that Gadkari had earlier approved funding and announced several infrastructure initiatives for the state, including major highway projects and greenfield roads. However, he alleged that these proposals failed to advance because the previous state government did not provide the necessary support.Highlighting Gadkari's contribution to infrastructure development, Ghosh said, “Respected Nitin Gadkari ji, whom we consider Vishwakarma. Wherever he lays his hands, he transforms it.”He further said that despite the Union minister extending considerable financial assistance and introducing schemes for West Bengal, implementation remained slow because of the lack of cooperation from the government at the time."However, the government at that time did not extend cooperation," he said.Ghosh added that the BJP government in the state was committed to speeding up development work and described Gadkari's visit as an important opportunity to advance West Bengal's infrastructure projects."Now we have a double-engine government, and we also want development to happen day and night. Receiving Gadkari ji's blessings and having him visit personally is a very big achievement for us. It will bring substantial benefits in the future. The second bridge at Farakka is also going to be inaugurated, and several other projects will be inaugurated as well as announced," he stated.

headline: GST registration cancellations to go automatic from 1 December
content: New Delhi: To reduce administrative intervention and ease compliance, the government has amended the goods and services tax (GST) rules to allow automatic processing of registration cancellation through the common portal for taxpayers who have filed the prescribed returns and cleared all outstanding dues.The amendment, notified by the finance ministry late Wednesday, will take effect from 1 December. It provides for electronic processing of cancellation applications where taxpayers have met the prescribed return-filing requirements and paid all outstanding tax, interest, fees, penalties and other liabilities.The move could reduce the time it takes businesses to exit the GST system by eliminating the need for tax officials to manually review routine cancellation applications. Under the earlier rules, tax officers were required to issue cancellation orders within 30 days of receiving an application. A CAG audit report released in December 2025 found delays in 3,022 cases across 46 ranges in 25 Central Tax Commissionerates. As per the CAG report, in Dehradun, 378 of 622 taxpayers' requests for cancellation applications were approved with delays of up to 227 days.Reducing procedural delaysThe automated process is also expected to reduce procedural delays for businesses that have discontinued operations but must complete their tax-related formalities before closing their GST registrations, experts said."It’s a positive step towards reducing procedural delays in GST administration. Businesses that have discontinued operations should not have to go through prolonged manual processes to cancel their registration when they have filed the prescribed returns and cleared all outstanding liabilities," said Vivek Jalan, partner at Tax Connect Advisory Services, a multi-disciplinary consulting firm. “Automating such applications will reduce the compliance burden on businesses and allow tax officers to focus on cases involving pending dues or other compliance issues.”The amendment is part of the broader procedural reforms recommended by the GST Council at its 57th meeting on 8 October. The Council had proposed a series of changes to make GST administration more predictable and technology-driven, including faster refunds to businesses, safeguards against arbitrary enforcement action, and a shift from discretionary scrutiny by tax officials to system-based, risk-led verification.Electronically communicatedUnder the amended Rule 20 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017, registrations covered by the automated process will be cancelled with effect from the date sought by the applicant. The cancellation will be communicated electronically to the taxpayer through the prescribed form.Applications will, however, continue to be referred to tax officials for examination if taxpayers have not filed the prescribed returns or statements or have outstanding tax, interest, fees or penalties. This means that applications involving pending compliance requirements or dues will remain subject to official scrutiny.It effectively shifts routine, compliant cases to an automated process while retaining manual scrutiny for applications that require further examination.The move comes amid an increase in GST collections. Gross GST revenue rose 22.9% year-on-year to ₹2.31 trillion in October, driven by a 42.2% surge in import-related revenue and a recovery from subdued consumption in the same month last year, ahead of the GST rate rationalisation.

headline: Man gets life imprisonment for raping 13-year-old daughter in 2024, POCSO court says act was betrayal of trust
content: A special POCSO court here has sentenced a man to life imprisonment for raping his 13-year-old daughter in 2024, observing that it was a shameful act and amounted to a betrayal of trust.Special POCSO court judge Narendra Prakash pronounced the verdict on Wednesday and also imposed a fine of ₹40,000 on the convict.Also Read: Manipur court sentences man, 48, to life imprisonment for raping minor daughterSpecial Public Prosecutor Sarnam Singh said the incident took place on the evening of March 14, 2024, when the girl was alone at home.According to the prosecution, the accused threatened to kill the girl before sexually assaulting her. The girl managed to escape and sought help from a woman in the neighbourhood.Also Read: Ghaziabad man gets life term for daughter’s rapeThe girl later narrated the incident to her grandfather and aunt. She also told them that her father had sexually assaulted her on earlier occasions.The girl's mother had left the house due to the behaviour of the accused and his drinking habits.Based on the girl's statement recorded before a magistrate, medical examination and age-related documents, a chargesheet was filed before the court on April 29, 2024.Also Read: 114 days after FIR, Sitapur man convicted of raping 13-year-old daughterDuring the trial, the prosecution examined seven witnesses. The court denied bail to the accused during the proceedings.The court observed that the crime was not merely a sexual offence but a grave and shameful act committed by a father against his own child, amounting to a betrayal of trust.The court also directed that the fine amount be spent on the rehabilitation of the survivor.

headline: ‘Self-proclaimed journalists may not get same protection as accredited ones’: SC on anti-CEC protest pleas
content: Self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection which is given to accredited reporters, the Supreme Court noted on Thursday while hearing pleas over ill-treatment of media personnel during anti-CEC protests in Delhi.The top court was hearing pleas filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists, who had submitted that their reporters were forcibly removed from protest sites and prevented from recording events, with some also being subjected to physical force, news agency PTI reported.These petitions were filed by journalist organisations and associations over complaints of police excesses and misconduct by police personnel during the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the Capital last month.The top court, in context of the pleas, noted that the status as a journalist “is not self-conferred,” adding that reporters are accredited according to their medium.Also Read | Supreme Court tightens food labelling norms, gives FSSAI four months to finalise them“Status [as a journalist] is not self-conferred. If you're a journalist from a newspaper/print media, you're under [Press Council] accredited journalist...if you are a TV channel of that newspaper you are accredited accordingly...you can also be an online journalist and you can also have registration. These things we have to...we are in the realm of atomized individuals claiming to be journalists. Self proclaimed journalists may not have same protection as accredited journalists,” Justice Joymala Bagchi noted, according to Live Law.The bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also relegated to a high-powered committee the pleas over the alleged detention of seven journalists, and the alleged assault and obstruction of reporters who were covering protests in Delhi on October 10 and October 11, PTI reported. The committee is headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy.This comes a week after the Delhi Police, in an affidavit filed in response to petitions by journalist organisations and associations, said there was a need to scertain if “reel makers” and “content creators” can be considered journalists, HT reported earlier.“In the present era of evolving digital media, several individuals, whether creative or otherwise, make reels, upload them and commercially exploit the content created by them. While there can be no objection to such activities, the question as to whether such reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters is yet to be determined,” the affidavit, filed by Joint Commissioner of Police Surender Kumar, said.‘First we have to define a journalist’: SC to consider questionThe Supreme Court, while hearing the pleas, said it would first have to “define” who a journalist is. ""Please appreciate - first we have to define a journalist. Is it a journalist in the category of a profession where someone is registered under the Press Council? Or is employed with a registered newspaper/TV channel? Or a person who seeks to be a (spokesperson) to the citizens, like in social media who are making reels," Live Law cited Justice Bagchi as saying.Also Read | ‘Don’t act like Robin Hood or Bahubali’: SC rebukes Bihar judge for convicting copJustice Bagchi further said the issues raised before the court would constitute balancing journalistic freedom with the administration of public order and law. CJI Surya Kant indicated that in regards to laying down a standard operating procedure (SOP) on how to deal with journalists who are covering protests, the court would intervene when it came to grey areas or wherever clarification is needed.One of the counsels said that the categorisation of people between “journalists” and “reel-makers” could not be done during the protest when people are being removed for the site. Justice Bagchi, in response to this, said, “Even if we lay down an SOP, the SOP's graded stance of law enforcement agencies would also depend upon the status and character of the person claiming to be a journalist.”

headline: Modi, Shah conspiring to remove votes to regain power fourth time: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
content: HYDERABAD Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that the country had reached a situation where instead of the Constitution determining who should govern, those in power were attempting to decide who should be allowed to vote. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/bjp-aiming-to-amend-constitution-and-scrap-reservations-telangana-cm-revanth-reddy/article70877573.ece Addressing a public meeting after participating in the ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’ organised by the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) on Constitution Day on Thursday (November 26, 2026), he alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah were conspiring to secure a fourth consecutive term for the Bharatiiya Janata Party (BJP) at the Centre by deleting voters’ names. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/congress-to-hold-samvidhan-raksha-marches-across-states-on-constitution-day-kharge-to-join-programme-in-lucknow/article71741430.ece The march, organised on the call of the All India Congress Committee (AICC), began at the Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund and proceeded to the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road in Hyderabad. Mr. Revanth Reddy, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, TPCC president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud, AICC in-charge B.M. Sandeep, Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and senior Congress leaders participated. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/new-aicc-in-charge-bm-sandeep-to-face-challenges-in-telangana-congress-on-his-maiden-visit/article71727835.ece Mr. Revanth Reddy said the Constitution, shaped by the vision of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and B.R. Ambedkar, had provided equal voting right to all. He reminded that women in the United States were denied voting rights for several decades despite the country gaining independence much earlier, while Dr. Ambedkar had ensured universal adult franchise in India. Ideological battle Mr. Revanth Reddy said the country was witnessing an ideological battle between the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi and that of Nathuram Godse. While the Gandhi family — including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra — were fighting to protect the country and its Constitution, the BJP was following the legacy of Godse, he alleged. Calling upon people to stand with the Gandhi family and the Congress, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the party that had fought for India’s independence would continue to exist for another 100 years. The BJP, which he described as a party formed for power, had no comparable history, he said. Mr. Mahesh Kumar Goud alleged that the BJP was organising counter-rallies because it could not tolerate the public response to the Congress’s Constitution protection campaigns. He said the Congress would continue to enjoy the support of people despite such counter-mobilisations. AICC incharge for Telangana B.M. Sandeep said the history of the Congress and that of independent India were inseparable. He alleged that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had played no role in the freedom struggle and that constitutional values had come under pressure over the past 13 years.

headline: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
content: New Delhi The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts. U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest in the 14 countries against which action has been taken storyline 1 An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries. The tariffs are not final yet, with the U.S. government opening a window for written comments and requests to testify by January 5, 2027. Public hearings will begin on January 25, 2027, following which the final action will be communicated. Back to square one The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries. As temporary tariffs expire, U.S. imposes 10% ‘forced labour’ tariffs on India As temporary tariffs expire, U.S. imposes 10% ‘forced labour’ tariffs on India The new tariffs are a result of the findings of its investigations on whether the U.S.’ trade partners were doing enough to prevent the import of goods made using forced labour. A separate investigation on excess capacity is pending and could attract further tariffs As temporary tariffs expire, U.S. imposes 10% ‘forced labour’ tariffs on India storyline 1 In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%. During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty. In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued. In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors So far, Indian government officials have been maintaining that India would move ahead with a trade deal with the U.S. only if such a comparative advantage is assured In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors storyline 1 As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations. Experts recommend waiting Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests. “FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.” The president of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Anil Gupta, pointed out that the tariffs will have a limited impact on Indian exports due to the nature of the commodities that India predominantly exports to the U.S. “India’s top exports to the U.S. include electronic goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, and textiles and apparel,” Mr. Gupta said. “As these products account for more than 50% of Indian exports to the U.S. and are price-sticky, there will be limited impact in the short to medium term.” Threats and opportunities Manoj Mishra, partner and tax controversy management leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, acknowledged that the proposed tariffs could weaken India’s export competitiveness, put pressure on profit margins, and dampen manufacturing investments. However, he was also of the view that India should not rush into a deal. “While the possibility of a lower tariff rate of 17% underscores the need to expedite bilateral trade negotiations, India could also leverage its expanding Free Trade Agreement (FTA) network, and diversify export markets and global supply chains to reduce dependence on the U.S. and mitigate the impact of evolving tariff measures.” Meanwhile, Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), a think tank, pointed out that the 100% tariffs applicable under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 persist, even though they have been temporarily paused. “Because these manipulated rates are a deliberate bait to extract one-sided concessions — and with the threat of Graham tariffs of up to 100% still hanging over it — India must reject the trade deal and instead answer the allegations [on excess capacity made by the USTR] sector by sector, showing that its investment serves domestic buyers, overseas customers, and future demand rather than letting exports alone be treated as proof of excess capacity,” Mr. Srivastava argued.

headline: Vellappally Natesan says he has ‘no differences’ with Keralam CM Satheesan
content: Alappuzha Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan on Thursday said he had “no differences” with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, signalling a softening of his stand towards the Congress leader after a series of public exchanges between them. The SNDP Yogam represents the numerically strong Ezhava community in Keralam. Speaking to reporters, Mr. Natesan said there had been no differences between him and Mr. Satheesan. “There are no differences with me in the first place. So, why should we talk about reconciliation,” he asked. The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Mr. Natesan and Mr. Satheesan before the UDF came to power following the Assembly election earlier this year. Asked about his past criticism of Mr. Satheesan, Mr. Natesan said there was no difference in his assessment of the Congress leader “then and now.” “I have only expressed my views on specific issues,” he said. Mr. Natesan said he had criticised Mr. Satheesan for “an immature stand” and for not respecting the Opposition when the latter was the Leader of the Opposition during the previous government. When asked whether Mr. Satheesan has matured since becoming the Chief Minister, he said: “It is only six months. Let’s wait and see.” Mr. Natesan said it was Nair Service Society (NSS) general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair who had earlier announced that Mr. Satheesan would not be allowed into the organisation’s office, adding that he had never objected to the Chief Minister visiting the SNDP premises. “I have never objected to anyone coming here. It was the NSS leadership that announced such a restriction,” he said. Mr. Satheesan is scheduled to inaugurate the Mannam Jayanthi celebrations at the NSS headquarters in Perunna, Kottayam, on January 2, 2027, marking the 150th birth anniversary of the organisation’s founder, Mannathu Padmanabhan. Asked about the differences between Mr. Nair and Mr. Satheesan and reports that they had since been resolved, Mr. Natesan said it was “their own matter.” “They fell out and they reconciled on their own. It is their way of doing things. They fall out, come together and resolve their differences. What opinion should I offer on that,” he asked. Asked whether his criticism of Mr. Satheesan had been personal, Mr. Natesan said he did not make personal remarks and that there were good and bad people everywhere. Referring to reported differences within the Congress over the functioning of the government, he said disagreements among leaders were not unusual and would eventually be resolved. “Differences within the Congress are nothing new. Such disagreements happen when people exchange criticism, but they eventually come together,” he said. He said the leaders concerned had themselves indicated that any disputes would be settled among them and that he did not want to comment on matters that did not concern him.

headline: Plea seeks guidelines to govern protests; Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, CJP leaders
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) agreed to examine a plea by a lawyers’ body seeking directions for formulation of uniform guidelines and a standard operating procedure governing public demonstrations and protests. Supreme Court directs Centre to file comprehensive response on pleas against detention of political leaders during Delhi protests Supreme Court directs Centre to file comprehensive response on pleas against detention of political leaders during Delhi protests Supreme Court directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file the response within 10 days and asked the petitioners to file their rejoinders, if any, within a week thereafter Supreme Court directs Centre to file comprehensive response on pleas against detention of political leaders during Delhi protests storyline 1 A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others. Justice Surya Kant: Striking a balance in a divided nation storyline 1 https://www.thehindu.com/topic/cockroach-janta-party/ Who is Abhijeet Dipke? Inside the viral Cockroach Janta Party movement storyline 1 https://frontline.thehindu.com/profile/author/saurav-das-26102/ Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani appeared for the lawyers’ body. The Supreme Court was hearing a plea by Lawyers Voice seeking directions for framing comprehensive, uniform and effective guidelines defining the responsibilities of organisers and participants at public protests. Police ‘handling’ of women protesters: What law says about crowd control, use of force Police ‘handling’ of women protesters: What law says about crowd control, use of force The women’s journalists’ group, NWMI said the freedom to gather and report news is not dependent on State accreditation, formal employment with a recognised media organisation or possession of an employer-issued identity card Explained Police ‘handling’ of women protesters: What law says about crowd control, use of force storyline 1 The petition argued that while dissent is part of democracy, protests must stay within legal bounds and avoid paralysing the capital or disrupting lawyers’ livelihoods. “Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents to review, modify, formulate and implement a standard operating procedure [SOP] for dealing with public protests conducted in violation of applicable law, lawful restrictions or valid directions of the competent authorities, ensuring timely, coordinated action to ensure normal public life,” the plea said. The petition referred to the protests organised by CJP during July and October, 2026. Referring to media reports, the petition said the Delhi Police, by way of a “one-time exemption”, permitted the CJP to hold a Dharna at Jantar Mantar on June 6, 2026, strictly between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. on the strength of the undertaking furnished by its organisers. Permission was sought and granted for a single day on June 20, 2026 again, confined to the hours between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m., but the demonstration was not discontinued at the expiry of the permitted hours, it said. SC backs right to protest, says blanket transit ban in Delhi ‘over-reaching’ SC backs right to protest, says blanket transit ban in Delhi ‘over-reaching’ Supreme Court’s remarks came in an oral mention by senior lawyers against the ‘complete shutdown’ of Delhi ahead of Oct 10 protests SC backs right to protest, says blanket transit ban in Delhi ‘over-reaching’ storyline 1 “No extension was ever granted, and that the organisers unilaterally announced an indefinite sit-in in the absence of any permission. The sit-in is reported to have continued until July 25, 2026, a period of about thirty-five days, during which a march towards Parliament was also undertaken on July 20, 2026 without the permission of the authorities,” the plea said. The plea further said a letter was received on October 7 from Mr. Das seeking permission for a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, with the organisers indicating that thousands of persons were expected to participate. “The Delhi Police is reported to have refused permission on October 9 on the ground that the intimation had been furnished merely three days before the proposed event, as against the 10 days prescribed. “It was further stated that the organisers had previously failed to adhere to lawful directions and to their own undertakings, and that the refusal was founded on considerations of public order, public safety and regulation of traffic,” the plea said. Notwithstanding the refusal, the organisers are reported to have persisted in their call for assembly, it added. “About 1,500 persons had to be detained by the forenoon of October 10 in order to prevent a breach of public order, while other media houses reported that a larger number was detained. “The grievances arising therefrom are linked by a common feature, namely that demonstrations are reported to have been continued, or sought to be held, in disregard of the conditions imposed by the competent authorities or in the absence of their sanction,” the plea said.

headline: Rajasthan chief secy asks officials to fast-track operationalising mines
content: Rajasthan Chief Secretary V Srinivas called for greater focus on mineral exploration and developing mining blocks outside the Aravalli region. With 24 major mineral blocks auctioned in 2026-27 (FY27) alone, Rajasthan has emerged as the country’s leading state in auctioning such blocks. The Mines Department has also recorded revenue collection of approximately ₹809 crore more than in the corresponding period of the previous financial year, up to October, representing growth of 12.98 per cent. It has set a revenue target of ₹14,000 crore for FY27. Srinivas urged the departments concerned to strengthen coordination and dialogue to resolve inter-departmental issues, noting that this would create new opportunities for investment, employment and revenue generation — both directly and indirectly — within the state’s mineral sector. On Wednesday, Srinivas chaired a meeting in Jaipur of the state-level coordination committee, comprising senior officials, to discuss inter-departmental matters concerning the Mines Department. At the meeting, he said the state should also aim to become a national leader in bringing auctioned mines into operation. To achieve this, the departments concerned must move into “action mode” to expedite issuing necessary clearances and commencing mining activities. Aparna Arora, additional chief secretary for mines and petroleum, said a roadmap for auctioning 55 major mineral blocks, along with several minor mineral blocks, is being implemented for FY27. A post-auction facilitation cell has been established at the departmental level to coordinate with, assist and guide mine leaseholders and the departments concerned. Regular reviews are also being conducted, she said. Arora said the department was currently focused on bringing auctioned mines into operation. The operationalisation of major mineral mines had been accelerated, while 716 minor mineral mines had already become operational. She said the process of obtaining environmental clearances for auctioned mines had gained momentum but needed to be expedited further. Arora suggested that inviting the relevant mine leaseholders to attend deliberations by the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority on their proposals would streamline and expedite necessary formalities, thereby avoiding delays in issuing clearances. She also emphasised the need to expedite mining clearances for blocks in urban areas, including Jodhpur, Jaipur-Sanganer and Kota, to curb illegal mining in these regions.

headline: Doctor, Entrepreneur and Health Educator: Dr. Kumar Gaurav Jha Takes Preventive Wellness to Indian Families Through Rayhope Global and Social Media
content: VMPLGhaziabad (Uttar Pradesh) [India], November 26: Dr. Kumar Gaurav Jha, CMD of Rayhope Global, is on a mission to make health awareness simple, reliable and reachable for every Indian household. By combining his medical experience, an ethical direct selling business and regular health education on social media, he is helping families take charge of their wellness before illness takes charge of them.From Treating Patients to Educating MillionsDr. Jha began his career as an allopathic medical practitioner. While treating patients with chronic lifestyle diseases, he saw a pattern: most people reach a doctor only after a problem becomes serious. He realised that awareness about diet, daily routine and early warning signs could prevent much of this suffering. He also observed that financial stress quietly affects the health of many households.Rayhope Global: Wellness With IntegrityTo address both challenges, Dr. Jha founded Rayhope Global in 2022. The company offers Ayurvedic wellness and personal care products and a transparent direct selling model, and delivers across India. Its approach rests on three pillars: preventive wellness that brings together traditional Ayurvedic wisdom and modern health understanding; continuous health awareness; and an ethical business opportunity built on structured training, mentorship and a fair plan, with no false promises.Spreading Health Awareness Through Social MediaDr. Jha believes that correct health information should not be limited to a clinic. He regularly creates short Hindi health education videos on his facebook page, Dr. Kumar Gaurav Jha (@Dr.KumarGauravJha), and on his social media pages. In simple, everyday language, these videos explain common health concerns, healthy habits, the right diet, the value of early check-ups and when to see a doctor. His aim is to counter health myths and misleading claims online with responsible, doctor-led guidance that ordinary families can understand and use."Today, people search for health answers on their phones before they visit a doctor," says Dr. Kumar Gaurav Jha. "If the information they find is wrong, it can harm them. That is why I use social media to share simple, honest health knowledge in Hindi. When people understand their bodies, they make better choices, and prevention becomes a habit."Building Awareness Along With OpportunityThrough regular online training sessions, Dr. Jha also guides Rayhope Global's network on product knowledge, responsible communication and ethical selling, so that every member becomes a source of correct health awareness in their own community."Most people struggle with health and finances not because they lack effort, but because they lack the right awareness and a trustworthy platform," he adds. "When you educate people on true wellness and give them an honest platform to grow, you build a healthier, self-reliant nation."About Rayhope GlobalRayhope Global is an Indian wellness and direct selling company founded in 2022, offering Ayurvedic wellness and personal care products with delivery across India.Website: www.rayhopeglobal.com (ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. headline: G’Day Namaste festival to showcase Australia-India ties across six Indian cities from December 7-12
content: G’Day Namaste, the Australian government’s flagship festival to present the country as a trusted partner for trade and investment and a leading destination for education and tourism, will take place across six cities in India from December 7 to 12.The festival will bring together business leaders, innovators, artists, athletes and communities for a week-long programme of diverse events, from the arrival of Australia’s Big Bash League (BBL) in India to the India-Australia Business Summit in New Delhi, as well as a Business Council of Australia investment roundtable and a Sports Summit in Mumbai.G’Day Namaste is being organised in partnership with the Australian government’s Centre for Australia-India Relations and Cricket Australia, alongside government, business and education partners. It will include events in New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Kohima.Announced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Australia in July, G’Day Namaste will showcase the creativity, diversity and dynamism of modern Australia and build greater understanding of the country among Indian audiences.Australian high commissioner Philip Green said G’day Namaste reflects the breadth of engagement between the two sides. “Australia and India have never been closer. Our partnership is powered by the connections between our people, and by a shared ambition for a more prosperous future,” he said.“G’Day Namaste is our invitation to Indians to discover Australia, understand our national story and see the breadth of opportunities that exist between our two countries,” he added.The CEO of the Centre for Australia-India Relations, Ryan Neelam, said, “The Australia-India relationship is ultimately about people. Whether through business, education, culture, sport or family, the connections between Australians and Indians are stronger and more diverse than ever.”A highlight of the festival will be the arrival of Australia’s Big Bash League (BBL) in India. On December 12, the Melbourne Renegades and Perth Scorchers will face off at Chennai’s MA Chidambaram Stadium in the opening match of the Australian Men’s Big Bash League season.The game will be the first BBL regular-season match played outside Australia and the first foreign cricket league game to be staged in India.“Australians and Indians speak a common language when it comes to cricket. Bringing the Big Bash League to India for the first time is something truly special, reflecting our shared passion for the game and the way in which we can use sport to grow the connections in many other fields of our thriving partnership,” Green said.Cricket Australia Executive General Manager (Big Bash Leagues), Alistair Dobson, said, “Chennai is home to some of the most passionate cricket fans on the planet and we can’t wait to bring the BBL to the MA Chidambaram Stadium.”G’Day Namaste will also span business, education, clean technology, film, music and culture. Highlights include education and clean technology showcases in Chennai, and Australian film, music and cultural programming across India. Australia will be an official partner country at this year’s Hornbill Festival in Nagaland.The festival will bring Australian stories to Indian audiences, showcasing First Nations culture, Australia’s multicultural identity and creative industries, and the Indian diaspora’s contribution to modern Australia.

headline: Stock Market Today: This Smallcap Stock Plans AI Health App Launch. Do You Own It?
content: Stock Market News: A smallcap stock that has caught the market's attention with a sharp rally is preparing to enter a new business. SC Agrotech Limited (BSE: 526081) is set to launch its digital healthcare platform, SC Health Suite, on November 27. The company plans to offer 15 wellness and self-monitoring tools through a smartphone browser. Users will get three months of introductory free access.
