headline: SIT files charge sheet over alleged irregularities in Karnataka Public Service Commission exam
content: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing alleged irregularities in the recruitment of veterinary officers through the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) filed its chargesheet on Wednesday, detailing alleged paper leaks and financial deals involving 15 candidates, officials aware of the development said.Former KPSC Controller of Examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and intermediary Basavaraj Kannale have been named in the chargesheet, which was filed before the 23rd City Civil and Sessions Court, in connection with the alleged manipulation of the recruitment process, where candidates were allegedly asked to pay between ₹40 lakh and ₹80 lakh to secure selection. There was no immediate comments from the two accused at the time of filing this report."The investigation findings centre on the alleged circulation of confidential examination material before the recruitment test. The question papers and answers were allegedly made available to selected candidates, who were also trained to help them clear the examination," one of the officers cited above said, seeking anonymity.The alleged involvement of an intermediary in arranging the deals and facilitating access to examination material is among the aspects detailed in the chargesheet. The SIT said it has investigated the role of those involved in obtaining confidential papers and making them available to candidates in return for money.The recruitment was conducted to fill 400 veterinary officer posts in the state government's animal husbandry and fisheries department. The alleged irregularities in the selection process led to an investigation into the role of KPSC officials and intermediaries.The Enforcement Directorate is conducting a separate investigation into alleged financial transactions linked to the recruitment.In its prosecution complaint filed earlier this month, ED alleged that the paper leak network extended to three other recruitment examinations conducted by the KPSC. Gangwar allegedly supplied answer keys to candidates recommended by him for panchayat development officer, junior engineer and agriculture officer posts in exchange for payments, it said.Kannale, the agency added, said he handled between ₹12 crore and ₹15 crore in cash belonging to Gangwar since 2023, including money linked to recruitment examinations.In the veterinary officers' recruitment, Kannale told ED that he received the question paper along with the answers from Gangwar on January 7 and distributed it among the candidates at Orchid Nirvana Villas the following day, ahead of the examination on January 9, officials said.In statements to the agency, Kannale said he collected between ₹1.35 crore and ₹1.50 crore from candidates, including ₹70 lakh through banking channels and ₹65 lakh in cash, which was handed over to Gangwar.

headline: IT sector employees seek national AI layoff policy as automation threatens jobs; unions and experts want
content: Amid the ongoing job uncertainty with regards to adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in the IT sector, workers are now seeking protection. India’s information technology industry needs a common policy for reporting job losses caused by artificial intelligence and protecting workers affected by automation.Employee representatives and workforce experts are seeking minimum standards for advance notice, severance pay, internal redeployment and reskilling, rather than leaving these decisions entirely to individual employers.Policy for AI layoffsNascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has approached government authorities over concerns about mass layoffs, forced resignations and unfair employment practices.It is now seeking a separate policy framework specifically addressing job losses linked to AI.The proposed framework would require companies to record and disclose the number of positions eliminated because of AI, employees shifted to different roles within the organisation and workers retrained for new jobs, according to an ET report.It would also establish minimum expectations for employers to explore internal transfers before making employees redundant, offer fair compensation and help those affected find alternative employment.Harpreet Singh Saluja, president of NITES said companies should be able to adopt new technologies but must also account for the impact on employees’ livelihoods. He said technological progress should not come at the cost of leaving workers without adequate support.Saluja told the financial daily that employees and the government should have access to clear information on the number of workers affected, the reasons for eliminating positions and the extent to which technology is directly replacing jobs.He said employers should make genuine efforts to retrain employees or move them into other positions within the organisation before eliminating roles because of AI or automation. Saluja also called for adequate advance notice, fair severance packages and the settlement of outstanding dues. Reskilling, he stressed, should provide employees with meaningful opportunities to take up new work, rather than being limited to a handful of online courses.Need for reliable dataTeamLease Digital estimates that over the next 18-24 months, 30% of jobs in the technology sector could face compression, while AI could significantly augment another 45% of roles. The remaining 25% could move towards higher-value work involving AI, data, cloud computing and cybersecurity.Employees are looking for exit packages similar to those provided by Microsoft and Canva. Under Microsoft's voluntary exit programme in India, eligible employees received one month's base salary for every completed year of service, along with health insurance and career transition assistance.Neeti Sharma, chief executive of staffing firm TeamLease Digital, told ET that the IT industry currently has no clearly defined, common policy setting minimum requirements for severance, redeployment or reskilling when employees lose their jobs because of AI.She called for baseline safeguards covering advance communication, fair exit compensation, opportunities to move into other roles within the company and employer-funded reskilling. Sharma also said companies should maintain data on positions eliminated due to AI, employees transferred internally and workers trained for different roles.Ravi Venkatesan, founder of the Institute for Human Flourishing (IHF), said the matter required a national-level response instead of separate approaches by individual companies. He suggested that an industry association such as NASSCOM should consult its members and prioritise disclosure of workforce reductions.Venkatesan said society needed reliable data and evidence on these developments to determine the appropriate policy response. He also called for a national safety net that defines employers’ responsibilities towards workers who lose their jobs and clarifies the government's role in helping them transition to new employment.He argued that fair severance should be governed by a national policy rather than left solely to individual company rules. He also stressed the need to establish what responsibilities employers and the government should share in helping displaced workers acquire the skills required for new jobs.Canva, which announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, equivalent to 22% of its workforce, offered those leaving the company at least six months' salary, healthcare coverage where applicable and career support. The company maintained that the positions being eliminated were not being replaced by AI.ET had earlier reported that employees affected by Qualcomm's workforce reduction in India were offered two months' notice pay, an additional month's salary for every year of service, continued insurance coverage for a year, stock awards and placement assistance, among other benefits. These details were provided by employees familiar with the exit arrangements and were not publicly confirmed by the company.However, despite growing demands for common industry-wide safeguards, there is little indication that companies are jointly developing such a framework.Pareekh Jain, chief executive of EIIRTrend, said companies had not begun discussions on a common policy, even as employees were raising the issue. He said workers wanted fair exit packages comparable to those offered by Microsoft and Canva. Some were also approaching the government for tax relief on their final settlements.The absence of transparent data is another obstacle to determining the actual extent of AI-driven job losses, said Kamal Karanth, co-founder of Xpheno. He observed that the last period when the industry had some visibility into workforce reductions was during the pandemic-related layoffs between late 2020 and 2022.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

headline: The Reserve Bank of India has luck on its side—here's why
content: Napoleon is often quoted as having said about one of his leading generals, “I know he’s a good general but is he lucky?” I am reminded of this when reflecting on the challenges Governor Sanjay Malhotra has had to deal with at the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lately. headline: 10 years and doubled cost: The four-laning saga of Mangaluru-Bengaluru NH 75 in Dakshina Kannada and Hassan
content: MANGALURU In the decadal saga of widening about 115 km stretch of Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and B.C. Road in Dakshina Kannada district (excluding the 26-km Shiradi Ghat stretch), the total project cost has close to doubled, from about ₹1,220 crore estimated in the year 2017 to about ₹2,220 crore when the project was almost complete by 2026-end. While the travel time (by a car) has reduced to about three-four hours between Hassan and Mangaluru from about five hours, road users endured tremendous ordeal during the past decade when the construction was underway, with the project witnessing an almost complete halt between 2018 and 2021. Driving from Mangaluru to Hassan had become a nightmarish experience during this period. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Mangalore/four-laning-of-hassanbc-road-highway-stretch-comes-to-a-halt/article25489177.ece Unending work on NH 75 in Karnataka spells misery for people Unending work on NH 75 in Karnataka spells misery for people The National Highway 75 connects Karnataka’s capital with the only port city in the State. But with work on a stretch of this highway, between Sakleshpur and Maranahalli, going on for years with no end in sight, this key connecting road either gets completely unusable or turns unsafe every monsoon, report Anil Kumar Sastry and G.T. Sathish SPOTLIGHT Unending work on NH 75 in Karnataka spells misery for people storyline 1 Initial contracts While the Union Road Transport Ministry handed over the highway stretch to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in July 2016 to widen the stretch into a four-lane road, contracts were awarded to M/s Isolux Corson for the Hassan-Maranahalli stretch (about 50 km) at an estimated cost of ₹400 crore and M/s Larsen and Tubro for the Addahole-B C Road stretch (about 65 km) for ₹821 crore in 2017. Within about 20 months, M/s Isolux declared insolvency and left the Hassan project while M/s Larsen submitted a letter of foreclosure as the NHAI wanted to change the scope of the project and refused to revise the project cost by about ₹140 crore for the changed scope. The Authority spent a good about two years in choosing new contractors for the Dakshina Kannada stretch and arranging the sub-contractor M/s Rajkamal Builders, to continue the Hassan district work. A long-winding decadal construction saga July 8, 2016: Union Road Transport Ministry hands over 47.5 km of NH 75 between Hassan and Maranahalli in Hassan District and 65 km of NH 75 between Addahole and B C Road in Dakshina Kannada district to National Highways Authority of India to widen it into four-lane. 2017: Hassan-Maranahalli Package awarded to M/s Isolux Corson at ₹400 crore and Addahole-B C Road to M/s Larsen Tubro at ₹821 crore cost on EPC (engineering, procurement and construction mode). 2018: M/s Isolux declares insolvency and exits the project, while M/s Larsen forecloses the contract as the NHAI wants to change project scope. 2018-2021: Time spent in inviting fresh tenders for Dakshina Kannada package and asking subcontractor M/s Rajkamal Builders to continue Hassan package. 2021: Dakshina Kannada package further subdivided into two — Addahole-Periyashanthi (15 km) to M/s Autade Engineering Pvt., Ltd. at ₹400 crore; Periyashanthi-B C Road (about 50 km) to M/s KNR Constructions at ₹1,100 crore. 2021: Hassan-Maranahalli four-laning project cost revised to ₹1,021 crore December 2024: Chowlagere Toll Plaza between Hassan and Maranahalli becomes functional. November 26, 2026: Valalu Toll Plaza in Dakshina Kannada district commissioned. Slow construction pace The abnormally slow pace of construction, notwithstanding Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari’s claim of constructing about 40 km highway in a day, irritated road users as well as general public in the vicinity of the project highway. With the contractors seldom following proper construction methods, including providing motorable alternative roads during the construction period, road users struggled to negotiate pothole and crater-ridden highway for years. While clouds of dust engulfed the highway during summer, the stretch was riddled with slush during the rainy season for years. Kalladka Town near B.C. Road where the NHAI built a 3 km elevated road (flyover) due to public demand, suffered massively for almost five years during the construction period. Mangaluru | Woes of Kalladka residents continue as flyover work on NH 75 leaves little space for rainwater drainage storyline 1 NHAI yet to act despite 300 complaints of inordinate delay at Chowlagere toll plaza on NH 75 Hassan-Sakleshpur section NHAI yet to act despite 300 complaints of inordinate delay at Chowlagere toll plaza on NH 75 Hassan-Sakleshpur section The Authority says it will raise the issue with Indian Highways Management Company that handles FASTag of vehicles NHAI yet to act despite 300 complaints of inordinate delay at Chowlagere toll plaza on NH 75 Hassan-Sakleshpur section storyline 1 Much remains to be done While the project highway is almost complete except for about 1 km at two places in Dakshina Kannada district, the NHAI needs to take measures to ensure pedestrian safety at many places, including Mani, Uppinangady, Melkar, and other places as the vehicles move at high speed on the newly built wide carriageways. headline: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Kerala case reveal about the health risks of skin-lightening creams? | Explained
content: The story so far The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Kerala. Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online How does mercury in face creams lead to kidney injury

headline: SC asks HDFC, ICICI bank to grant prosecution sanction in subvention fraud
content: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of their officials within a week in alleged subvention scheme frauds involving real estate developers, banks and financial institutions.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these financial institutions would have to personally appear before it in case of non-compliance."We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them," the bench said in its order.Under the subvention scheme, banks disburse the sanctioned amount directly to the accounts of builders, who are then required to pay the EMIs until the flats are handed over to homebuyers.However, when builders default on the EMI payments to banks in violation of tripartite agreements, banks demand repayment from homebuyers.The top court was hearing a batch of petitions relating to subvention schemes under which homebuyers were subjected to loan recovery proceedings despite builders' failing to honour their financial commitments.During the hearing, Additional Solicitor General Aishwaya Bhati, appearing for the CBI, informed the court that the agency was facing difficulties in securing prosecution sanctions under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, including in cases where HDFC Bank had granted conditional sanctions.Bhati told the apex court that the CBI had filed its sixth supplementary status report, stating that investigations had been completed in 25 of the 55 registered cases.The agency informed the court that it had filed 22 chargesheets and submitted closure reports in three cases.The CJI orally observed that it was the bounden duty of the banking authorities to grant prosecution sanction.The top court directed the CBI to complete the remaining investigations within two weeks. It also said timelines would be prescribed for the completion of trials and that it would not allow delaying tactics.While hearing a batch of separate petitions, the top court had, in July last year, allowed the CBI to register 22 cases over the "unholy nexus" between the banks and developers to dupe homebuyers in the National Capital Region (NCR).

headline: Employee leaders detained ahead of AAP rally in Moga, released after protest
content: The detention of several employee union leaders and the house arrest of some others by the Faridkot police ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party's rally in Moga on Thursday triggered resentment among various employee organisations.Representatives of several unions reached the City police station and staged a protest against the police action. Following nearly two hours of confrontation, the police released the detained leaders this morning.Employee representatives said no protest or other programme had been planned by the unions during the AAP rally in Moga. Despite this, the police detained several of their colleagues and placed some leaders under house arrest.They said the police picked up Karan Jain, district president of the DC Office Employees Union, from his residence early Thursday morning and lodged him at the City police station. Sukhwinder Singh Sukhi, district president of the Democratic Teachers' Front, was also placed under house arrest.On learning about the action, employees from various organisations, led by Gurnam Singh Virk, a state-level leader of the Ministerial Employees Union, gathered at the police station and raised slogans against the police. The police subsequently released Karan Jain and other detained employees.Addressing the protesters, Virk alleged that the AAP government had failed to fulfil even a single promise made to employees and pensioners. He said several rounds of meetings had been held with the government after prolonged protests, but none of the major demands had been addressed.Even demands accepted by the government had not been implemented, he alleged.Virk said detaining employee leaders and placing them under house arrest despite there being no planned protest during the Moga rally amounted to a violation of their democratic rights.He said employee organisations had decided to intensify their agitation against the government and asserted that the employee community would oppose AAP in the forthcoming Assembly elections.The police authorities declined arresting any union leader. There was a formal request to the employee union leaders to not disturb law and order situation with road blockage during the rally, said a senior police officer, preferring anonymity.

headline: 'Jeopardises safety in train operations': North Central Railway warns staff against making reels
content: NEW DELHI: The North Central Railway (NCR) has warned its employees against making and posting social media reels during duty hours, saying the activity distracts staff and jeopardises train operations.In an advisory issued on November 17, 2027, the railway zone cautioned that employees could face disciplinary action for violating safety protocols or engaging in unauthorised commercial activities through content creation.The communication was addressed to senior officials of its three divisions, Prayagraj, Jhansi and Agra, and its workshops. The zone said some railway employees were creating and posting reels on their social media accounts while on duty, which could compromise operational safety."Performing such activities during duty hours poses a severe distraction, jeopardises safety in train operations, and compromises administrative integrity," the NCR zone said as quoted by PTI.Reels could amount to unauthorised businessThe railway zone also flagged the possibility of employees earning money through social media content, saying this could amount to running an unauthorised commercial enterprise or side business."Moreover, there is a strong likelihood that some staff are deriving monetary advantage through their (social media) content creation, which amounts to running an unauthorised commercial enterprise/side business, which is a direct violation of Rule 15 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966," it said.The zone warned that filming on railway premises or equipment for commercial purposes without formal permission or payment of prescribed fees was prohibited."Filming on Railway premises or equipment for commercial gain without formal permission or without payment of prescribed film shooting/commercial fees is prohibited."It added that if social media posts were found to be generating commercial benefits, the prescribed fees would have to be paid. Failure to do so could invite penal action.Prior approval required for railway-related contentThe NCR zone also clarified that employees creating educational or awareness-related content about the Railways would need prior approval from the competent authority."Posts intended for educational or socio-awareness generation regarding Railways may only be published with the prior approval of the Competent Authority," it said.It further directed employees who frequently post content on social media to submit a formal undertaking to the railway administration."Staff who frequently post content on social media must submit a formal undertaking to the Railway Administration confirming that they derive no monetary advantage from such posts and that their activities do not compromise Railway safety or security."Divisional and workshop authorities have been directed to closely monitor the active social media accounts of railway personnel. The zone warned that employees found violating safety protocols or engaging in social media activities during duty hours would face strict disciplinary action.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: 'Elected to work, not gossip': Supriya Sule rejects NDA buzz, CM post speculation
content: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule on Thursday dismissed speculation about her party joining the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and claims that Sharad Pawar was seeking the Maharashtra chief minister's post for her, saying she was elected to serve the people of Baramati and not "indulge in political gossip"."I am a serious politician and a serious policymaker. I do not waste my time on gossip. The people of the Baramati Lok Sabha constituency sent me to Delhi not to indulge in gossip. They sent me there to work and serve the state and the country," she told news agency PTSule questions political speculationResponding to questions about the speculation surrounding her political future, Sule urged journalists to focus on policy, accountability and governance rather than unsubstantiated reports.On claims that Sharad Pawar, who is admitted in Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital with suspected dehydration, wanted her to become chief minister, she recalled that her late cousin Ajit Pawar had consistently maintained over the past 40 years that anyone commanding the required numbers in the state legislature could occupy the post.She also asked journalists to question her about her parliamentary work, including her contributions to four Joint Parliamentary Committees (JPCs) and the Finance Committee."Ask me what I have achieved through the four JPCs I have served on. I am on the Finance Committee. What is my position on the issues before it? What impact will US President Donald Trump's tariffs have on people's daily lives? These are the questions that matter," she said.On reports of internal differences within the NCP (SP), Sule said everyone in a democracy had the right to express their views while also being willing to listen."In a strong democracy, everyone has the right to express their views. Just as I have the strength to speak, I must also have the strength to listen," she said.She maintained that Sharad Pawar, who founded the NCP, continued to be its president and alleged that injustice had been done to him in the dispute over the party's name and election symbol."We submitted all documents and evidence before the Election Commission, but injustice was still done to Pawar saheb. Our fight for the party continued yesterday, continues today and will continue tomorrow," she said."Until Sharad Pawar gets justice and regains the party that he founded, our fight will continue," she added.Sule flags Pune's law and order situationOn Maharashtra's law and order situation, Sule said she had urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the Home portfolio, to take the matter seriously.Citing Union home ministry data, she said Pune had the highest crime figures in Maharashtra and expressed concern over the city's reputation as a safe educational hub."I have no personal issue with the Pune Police Commissioner. The accountability must be fixed on the administration and the system overseeing the police," she said.While expressing confidence in Maharashtra Police personnel, she called for accountability within the administration overseeing the force."We are not interested in allegations and counter-allegations. Public safety is important, and we must discuss the issue and find a solution," she said.Sule added that the NCP (SP), which represents two Lok Sabha constituencies in Pune district through her and Amol Kolhe, would cooperate with the government on public safety.On the party's organisational activities, she said all NCP (SP) MPs had submitted details about the implementation of the VB-G RAM G scheme and the disbursement of funds to farmers following requests from Sharad Pawar and Maharashtra unit chief Shashikant Shinde.The party plans to discuss the information with its office-bearers at the district, taluka and village levels over the next one-and-a-half to two months.Sule also said the party would work constructively with the government on farmers' issues and development rather than oppose it merely for the sake of opposition.On Constitution Day, she stressed that laws must apply equally to political parties and private companies."If companies such as Colgate or Godrej put up advertisements or hoardings, they have to pay the required charges. Political parties should also be subject to the same rules. Those in power must practise what they preach," she said.Recalling the November 26, 2008, Mumbai terror attacks, Sule said she had lost three to four friends in the incident."I remember that day as if it happened yesterday," she said, recalling how she had rushed out with family members and friends after hearing about the attacks. Their vehicle was stopped near Wilson College, and they initially thought it was an accident or a smaller emergency."It was a huge personal loss for all of us," she said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Saviour or Devil, India Must Engage With AI: Industry, Government, and Global Experts at the Ahmedabad Dialogue Call for Impact Over Pilots
content: Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India (NewsVoir)Twenty years. That is how long it once took to develop a new grade of aircraft-engine material. The goal was to bring it down to five, with artificial intelligence at the heart of the effort. The story, shared by Gopichand Katragadda, CEO of Myelin Foundry and former Group CTO of Tata Sons, captured the spirit of the third Ahmedabad Dialogue hosted by Ahmedabad University: AI matters when it changes what is possible, not when it is bolted on to business as usual.https://www.newsvoir.com/images/article/image1/37515_ahmdabad-image.jpgHeld on the theme “AI for Productivity, Public Value and Resilience,” this day-long Ahmedabad Dialogue brought together leaders from industry, government, academia and public health to ask a pressing question: if AI is so powerful and pervasive, why are so few Indian businesses and public systems getting real value from it—and what will it take to change that?Manufacturing, Skilling, and Supply ChainsFor P. Bharathi, Secretary, Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat, the question is no longer whether to adopt AI. “AI is compulsory. I mean, we have to live with it,” she said. The missing link, she emphasised, is talent and skilling. The Government of Gujarat is targeting 500,000 young people for AI skilling this year, offering support of up to Rs 50,000 per student, establishing a dedicated Taiwan desk to learn from its semiconductor ecosystem, and preparing a state AI governance policy.Punit Lalbhai, Vice Chairman, Arvind Limited, described the work required to make AI productive in an industrial setting. Arvind is midway through a 24-month effort involving what he called “very grinding” work on data quality and enterprise-system reconfiguration, so that its data is ready for inference and productivity gains. “Whether it be saviour or devil, one has to be engaged with it, because not engaging with it is a huge risk of being left behind,” he said.Lalbhai said talent is available, but bringing AI specialists and manufacturing teams together remains a challenge. “It is a Mars and Venus challenge. This AI talent that comes in is a different species from the manufacturing talent that we have.” He predicted that organisations would move from valuing knowledge to valuing ideas, and then to thinking big and collaborating.Moderating the plenary on manufacturing, technology, supply chains and skilling, Ahmedabad University Vice Chancellor Professor Pankaj Chandra highlighted the gap between AI’s promise and its adoption. AI adoption in Indian manufacturing stands at around 15 per cent; only about 5 per cent of MSMEs have integrated AI into core operations, while 71 per cent identify a lack of employee training as their biggest barrier. “Most businesses buy AI licences probably out of FOMO and without having a digitised shop floor, clean data, or even standardised workflows,” he said. The deeper issue, Chandra argued, is cultural, “We have become too accustomed to throwing people at problems… It is more of a mindset shift than a size-of-prize or cost-consciousness issue.”Katragadda, founder of Myelin Foundry and former Group CTO of Tata Sons, urged companies to stop treating AI as a showcase. Pilots, he said, are often “a way of saying that we also do AI” and rarely target the areas that matter most. “If you do business as usual and use AI to improve productivity… that is only going to give you ten per cent impact. You need to restructure your business.” He cautioned organisations against waiting for perfect data: “You will not get clean data; you will not get more data. And with the present generation of AI, we can do without that.”On India’s position, Katragadda said the constraint was not talent but funding, particularly early-stage funding. He urged India to “go ahead of the world in the applications” and proposed a “seventy-twenty-ten” division of horizons: industry looks three years ahead, academia five or more, and government funds what will matter seven years from now.Professor Pao-Ann Hsiung, Dean, College of Engineering, National Chung Cheng University, Taiwan, traced TSMC’s success to the combined strength of its supply chain, education, and government. AI, he said, is now extending that advantage to smaller firms: “The high-end, or the precise machines that TSMC employs, can now be done by medium and small enterprises because of AI.” He also cautioned against expecting AI to solve every problem. A gap between 72 per cent and 92 per cent, he noted, “is not solvable by AI. So, we need expertise in the field.” For countries building semiconductor capacity, he added, fabrication plants are only part of the task; the supply chain is the bigger challenge.Health and SustainabilityThe plenary on AI for health and sustainability, moderated by Minal Pathak, Academic Director of The Climate Institute at Ahmedabad University, examined both the opportunities and the responsibilities involved in applying AI to people and the planet.Dr Anunaya Jain of Ahmedabad-based Jhpiego, who leads health-sector AI implementation across more than 30 countries, reported a four-fold reduction in treatment interruptions among HIV patients in Nigeria following the deployment of a predictive model.Dr Arindam Ray of the Gates Foundation described India’s eVIN network, which tracks vaccine stock and cold-chain temperatures at nearly 30,000 points in fifteen-minute intervals. Dr Shweta Agarwala of Ahmedabad University shared how she used AI to discover a skin-compatible electrode material for a textile-based muscle-atrophy treatment for ICU patients. The panel also addressed AI’s energy and water footprint, data bias, unclear accountability, and the fragility of “human in the loop” safeguards.Dr Arunabha Ghosh, former CEO of the Council on Energy, Environment and Water Ghosh cautioned that progress depends on how society defines it: “It’s not AI’s problem, it’s our own thinking of what progress means that will be fundamentally holding us back.” Jain recalled a first deployment in which the model’s predictions were accepted 99 per cent of the time and warned that human oversight “succeeds only if humans have the time, the required skill, and the required authority” to disagree. The greatest health gains, he said, come not from the model itself but from the intervention that follows it. Agarwala called for an “AI life assessment,” modelled on product life-cycle assessment, so that each new use of AI is weighed against the resources it consumes.The Ahmedabad Dialogue’s central message was that meaningful AI value will come from tackling important problems and having the courage to restructure how work is done—not from a scattering of pilots designed to show that an organisation “also does AI.” The groundwork is often unglamorous: clean data, digitised workflows, and disciplined change management. India’s advantage will depend on people who can bridge AI skills with deep knowledge of the factory floor, the hospital ward, and the climate system. As adoption grows, governance must keep pace with questions of accountability, transparency, intellectual property and explainability. The next test is to take promising health and climate solutions that currently work as pilots and make them work across entire systems and, ultimately, across the country.The Ahmedabad Dialogue is an annual forum hosted by Ahmedabad University, bringing together researchers, policymakers, industry leaders, and practitioners from India and across the world to examine questions shaping India and the region’s development. This year’s edition focused on harnessing AI for productivity, public value, and resilience.About Ahmedabad UniversityAhmedabad University is a leading private, non-profit research university offering students a liberal education focused on interdisciplinary learning, practice orientation, and research thinking.The University has been • Recognised by the Government of Gujarat as a Centre of Excellence.• Accredited with 'A' grade by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC).• Awarded Leadership and Management Team of the Year at the Times Higher Education Awards Asia 2025.• Awarded a 5-star rating, the highest awarded in the Gujarat State Institutional Rating Framework (GSIRF) for 2021-22 and 2023-24, by the Knowledge Consortium of Gujarat (KCG), Department of Education, Government of Gujarat.• Awarded the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) International Award for Excellence 2024 for its University Centre.• Awarded a 'Platinum Rating' by the Indian Green Building Council for sustainability and green practices.• Recognised by the UGC under Section 12(B) of the UGC Act, becoming one of the very few private research universities to have been awarded this recognition for select research universities.• Recognised as a Highly Commended University for Teaching and Learning Strategy of the Year in the Times Higher Education (THE) Awards Asia 2023.• Awarded the AACSB’s Innovations That Inspire Award 2023 for its Foundation Programme.• Awarded Gold Rating by the Indian Green Building Council for achieving the Green Building Standards at its University Centre.The University, established in 2009, is rooted in the vision of one of India’s finest educational foundations, the Ahmedabad Education Society, which was founded in 1935 by nationalist leaders. Programmes at the University range from bachelors to doctoral levels in humanities and social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, and management through its 4 Schools and 10 Centres: Amrut Mody School of Management | Bagchi School of Public Health | School of Arts and Sciences | School of Engineering and Applied Science | Ahmedabad Design Lab | Centre for Heritage Management | Centre for Learning Futures | Global Centre for Environment and Energy | International Centre for Space and Cosmology | Sahyog: Centre for Promoting Health | Stepwell Centre for Asian Futures | The Climate Institute | The Institute of Manufacturing and Economy | VentureStudio.An urban university, Ahmedabad promotes independent-mindedness and diversity across all dimensions of its activity and helps students mature into critical thinkers who are analytically equipped, practically oriented, and contextually aware global citizens. The University provides a contemporary educational framework that brings liberal arts, sciences, and the professions to engage together in creating new knowledge for addressing complex challenges of the society and in offering majors that merge the boundaries of disciplines to prepare students for the new economy.(Disclaimer: The above press release comes to you under an arrangement with Newsvoir and PTI takes no editorial responsibility for the same.).
