headline: India may have seen a fall in poverty but inequality has not been reduced: NN Vohra
content: India may have seen a considerable fall in poverty levels but inequality has not been reduced since Independence, former Jammu and Kashmir governor NN Vohra said on Thursday.Addressing an international seminar in New Delhi to mark the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas, the former bureaucrat expressed hope that the policy-makers of contemporary India take measures that mimic the ethos of “Begampura”.“Begampura” or the vision of a "sorrowless city" was articulated by the 15th-16th-century Bhakti saint and social reformer Sant Ravidas. It imagines an egalitarian, casteless and fear-free society where all residents live with equal dignity and freedom from oppression.“After gaining Independence, our country has achieved great progress. As the media reported recently, the levels of poverty have been reduced significantly in India. But that apart, I think inequality has not reduced, it has only increased. Wealth may have increased, the number of rich people in India have increased enormously, but inequality has not disappeared,” Vohra said at the event.“I hope our policy makers honestly pursue policies which take us nearer to Begumpura where we have a just social order,” he added.Vohra, the retired 1959-batch IAS officer of the Punjab cadre who had served in various top capacities in the Union Government, also hailed Sant Ravidas’ early vision of social justice that parallels modern ideals of fraternity, anti-caste equality, and constitutional democracy.Titled “Begampura: Towards a Just Social Order”, the day-long seminar was organised by Bhai Vir Singh Sahitya Sadan and the National Institute of Panjab Studies in the national capital.The seminar takes its title from Sant Ravidas’ celebrated shabad in Sri Guru Granth Sahib, which describes Begampura, or the “city without sorrow” — a society free from fear, the burden of taxation and discrimination between citizens.The discussions explored the concept as a programme for social equality, examining its place in manuscript traditions and Sikh scripture, as well as its contemporary implications for caste, labour and gender.Prof Mark Juergensmeyer of the University of California, Santa Barbara, and author of Religious Rebels in the Punjab, a pioneering study of the Ad Dharm movement, delivered the keynote address.“Sant Ravidas continues to be a living saint for the teachings and principles he gave to the world to follow. There is a need to translate his vision to reality,” he said.The academic sessions featured papers on the historical, philosophical and social dimensions of the Ravidas tradition.The seminar culminated the Sadan’s year-long observance of the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas, which included a lecture at Bhai Vir Singh Niwas Asthan in Amritsar in October.

headline: How AI Will Help Highways Authority Catch Motorists Hiding Number Plates
content: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to catch motorists who conceal or tamper with their number plates to evade toll payments. But the technology could also help police trace vehicles involved in hit-and-run cases, road safety expert Prince Singhal told NDTV. The technology, called 'Vehicle Fingerprinting', seeks to identify vehicles without relying solely on their registration plates. "AI-powered vehicle fingerprinting could help investigators trace vehicles through distinctive characteristics such as make, model, colour and body structure. When integrated with highway cameras and toll plaza surveillance, it could help reconstruct vehicle movements and narrow down the search for offenders," Singhal said. Identifying the vehicle, however, is only one part of the investigation. Effective investigation and prosecution remain crucial, he added. India's transition to barrier-free tolling through the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) system allows vehicles to pass through toll plazas without stopping. The system uses FASTags and cameras that read registration plates.

headline: 'Focus on action, not words': Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge breaks silence on Imran Masood's aggressive SP attack over UP seat-sharing
content: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday finally broke silence on Imran Masood's aggressive attack on Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh.Speaking at an event in Lucknow, Kharge advised Masood to "focus on action rather than just words", as the Saharanpur MP's increasingly sharp remarks against ally Samajwadi Party (SP) have added to the strain over seat-sharing negotiations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."... Imran Masood — whom I frequently hear on television, where he often speaks with great passion. However, we must focus on action rather than just words; the more we work together, the further we will progress. He is in Parliament, where he consistently fights for the party and strives to ensure that our positions are upheld," Kharge said.The Congress chief's remarks come amid growing friction between the two INDIA bloc allies, with Masood repeatedly questioning the SP's approach to seat-sharing even as discussions between the parties remain under way.Masood questions SP's seat-sharing approachMasood on Thursday questioned the rationale behind continuing seat-sharing discussions after the Akhilesh Yadav-led SP announced five candidates while negotiations with the Congress were still in progress."It is no alliance if one partner 'leaves' seats for the other after announcing its candidates," he said, raising questions about whether the Congress was being treated as an equal partner.The Congress MP also made it clear that he would remain with his party and would not accept a subordinate position in the alliance."What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us? We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.Masood, who was involved in the seat-sharing discussions, argued that an alliance should involve joint decisions and announcements. He declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, which was scheduled to be released later on Thursday, saying he was unaware of the party's approach."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.Recalling the previous Assembly elections contested by the Congress and SP, Masood said his party had fought 107 seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh."Now, he is yet to become the chief minister," he added.Earlier barbs had put SP on the defensiveMasood's latest remarks follow a series of public attacks on the SP leadership over the alliance arrangement. On Wednesday, he had used sharp expressions to convey his frustration with what he described as the SP's treatment of the Congress.In an interview with The Times of India, he questioned whether the SP wanted to fight the BJP or its own alliance partner."Aapki ladai mujhe samajh nahi aa rahi hai — BJP se ladni hai ya humse? Aap hamare gale par pair rakhkar, hamari kabar ke upar Taj Mahal banana chahenge, toh mera saans ghutega. Main toh haath-pair maarunga (I am unable to understand your battle … You want to fight the BJP or us. If you will want to stand on my neck and build a Taj Mahal on my grave, I will be suffocated. I will fight back)," he had said.Later, speaking to a television channel, Masood compared the Congress to zero, arguing that its presence multiplied the strength of an alliance partner by ten."If you don't understand our importance, then OK, Goodbye, Thank You," he said.The SP had largely refrained from responding to his remarks throughout Wednesday. However, his repeated criticism prompted some SP functionaries to question the Congress leadership's silence.A senior SP functionary told TOI that either the Congress leadership was choosing to ignore the statements or was unaware of what its leaders were saying. Neither possibility, he suggested, was a positive sign for the alliance.The functionary also pointed out that Masood and AICC's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had previously targeted the SP leadership over the alliance, but SP leaders had avoided responding following instructions from party chief Akhilesh Yadav not to comment publicly on seat-sharing discussions.The SP's concern, according to the functionary, was not merely that Congress leaders were criticising the party, but that the Congress leadership had not publicly objected to what it considered unprovoked remarks.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Vivo X500 Pro Max’s photography masterclass, and also welcomes Apple loyalists
content: The smartphone camera, as an idea, is in an astonishing place. Not just the leaps in overall capabilities, but the smartphone space is defined by two very distinct approaches. Within that, there is a clear course correction happening as well, something I’ll illustrate, as we assess the latest flagship from Vivo, the X500 Pro Max. A 200-megapixel telephoto camera and the optional 200mm and 400mm equivalent lens options if you need that for long-range photography, offer good versatility to build with. But there are two contentions to weigh on.We are in an era where flagships generationally have a tough time justifying pricing inflation with genuine forward experiential steps. The Vivo X500 Pro Max has managed that, resoundingly, particularly with the camera and the evolution of Origin OS. Secondly, there is the looming shadow of the Vivo X300 Ultra that was released a few months ago—brilliant across the board, be it the cameras, overall performance and in being an Android flagship as a collective. And if I may crystal gaze for a moment, the X500 Pro Max has a solid foundation to compete not just with the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max, but also an inevitable arrival of the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max at some stage.Also Read:₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh: As flagship phones get 30% costlier, buyers rethink value"> From ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh: As flagship phones get 30% costlier, buyers rethink valuePricing was therefore a complication. Vivo sees the X300 Ultra currently retailing for around ₹1,59,999 and slots the X500 Pro Max at ₹1,64,999 onwards. My question is this—how long does that remain on sale? On the point of the variants, there is a smaller window than usual between the 12GB+256GB spec and the ₹1,79,999 you’ll part with for 12GB+512GB. Go for the latter, if that’s within the realms of the budget. The Photography Kit bundle is currently with the higher spec, and that’s priced at ₹2,29,999. Difficult to have an opinion on pricing and value these days, as subjective as those matters are, considering smartphone makers have very little room due to component pricing inflation. Cameras absolutely dominate the list of reasons as to why you’d consider a Vivo flagship phone, and it’s sensible to begin with that. The main camera is a 50-megapixel, a Sony LYTIA L910 sensor that’s 1/1/28-inch with 24mm focal length and gimbal-like (it is actually the CIPA 7.0 professional stabilisation standard) optical image stabilisation (OIS). The highlight here has to be the 200-megapixel telephoto, which is a 1/1.4-inch Samsung ISOCELL HP10 sensor with 85mm focal length and OIS. Completing the troika is a 50-megapixel ultra wide, which is a bit more humdrum, considering it’s a Samsung JN5 sensor from 2024, if memory serves me well.The main camera, for starters requires you to tweak a setting from the outset. This by default pixel bins photos to 12.5-megapixel, which while great for saving space, does mean you’ll notice some pixelation if you crop or zoom in. I’d suggest selecting the 25-megapixel as the default setting for most photos you click, for a meaningful improvement as far as detailing goes. The other thing you need to do is set this to Zeiss Natural setting for colour saturation, for the most realistic processing.Also Read: India’s smartphone market is shrinking, and phone prices have never been higherOnce you get the settings right, photography results are incredible across lighting conditions—in terms of detailing, colour reproduction and realism. When certain photos really need it, including those with complex natural lighting, the dynamic range really steps up to give that realistic representation of the moment you’ve tried to capture. Photos between 2x and 10x also don’t compromise anything on the finer elements of a photo.A positive change that I continue to notice is the dialling down of the artificial detail boosting that had become apparent in the past couple of years. There is a natural flow to the gallery as you absorb the moments of a vacation later, rather than unnatural skies or a landscape that didn’t look this green. That said, some processing tweaks are needed to add a bit of realism to skin tones, which in moments, this phone tends to brighten up a smidgen more than necessary.The star of the show is certainly the 200-megapixel telephoto, which allows you to get really close to the subject. And more often than not, without compromising on the details. I felt that a 50x or a 100x zoomed photo is much easier to manage on the Vivo X500 Pro Max with lesser shake and easier centering of the subject, than on a Samsung flagship or even the latest iPhone—that’s exactly the sort of result Vivo would have been looking to achieve with the elaborate OIS for this sensor.Also Read:Tech is expensive, but is there light at the end of the tunnel?Videos get a significant upgrade too. All cameras on the Vivo X500 Pro Max support 4K60 video recording resolution, in which the latter is the frames per second number. The main camera can also do 4K240 at 1x and 2x while the telephoto can also record at 4K120, as well as both can do 8K30 too. Dolby Vision, check. Log, check. Compared to photos, depending on how you’ve set up the elaborate filters and setting there, most videos have a bit more restrained colour. I believe the idea is to have a more neutral basis for video editing. Telephoto autofocus tracking will be very handy, more than you may realise initially, if you are recording a fast moving subject in the distance.Everything about the Vivo X500 Pro Max is as you’d expect on a flagship which demands you part with top money. The design, for instance, takes a lot of inspiration from the X300 Ultra’s subtle dual-tone finish. The Eternal Black colour, for instance, has a glass fibre and spray-coated texture finish. I also notice a less profound ring around the camera island. Look at the back of this phone from a perfectly flat side view, and you’ll notice what Vivo calls the Tideline Design, where the area around the camera island is very gently raised compared to the lower part of the phone—they’re taking some cues from nature, a shore and how a tide interfaces with it.I must note that the 7,800mAh battery has been incredibly well optimised. This is particularly true for standby battery frugality—leave a fully charged Vivo X500 Pro Max at 10pm and you’ll wake up to it at still 100% (or on some days, 99%) charge at 6am. Even during the day with active usage and apps working in the background, this is sipping charge very gently. Getting two days, with the battery reducing from 100% to 25%, is pretty much the way of life with a Vivo X500 Pro Max. Does this make it the most battery efficient phone in the current flagship lineup? I’d peg this ahead of the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.Also Read:Gravity, dust and regret: The cost of repairing a foldable smartphoneLast but not least, are the improvements to Origin OS 78 that’s based on Android 17—and a thing worth noting here is how Vivo is making this versatile across devices, something we recently also noticed with the Vivo X Fold6 which specifically added utilities for the foldable’s display real estate. Here, you’re sure to find utility with a broader compatibility with Apple devices—Quick Share works with AirDrop, Office kit file transfers are compatible with Mac and iPad, Apple Watch will work with this phone, AirPods get Spatial Audio support and battery display within Origin Island and iCloud is baked into the File Manager app. There is a sensible realisation that Vivo must appeal to users who may otherwise also have some Apple devices within their reach.Before you do part with the cash for the Vivo X500 Pro Max, chances are there will be a second glance at the spec sheet, particularly the Mediatek Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset choice. It is not a Qualcomm chip, will likely be your biggest contention. Vivo has, for a while now, bet on MediaTek’s chip for their flagships and results have been impressive. Nothing tells me it’ll be any different this time, because the Dimensity 9600 Pro feels absolutely capable of delivering a flagship experience—including sustained performance.It is genuinely difficult to hold up anything as a shortcoming with the Vivo X500 Pro Max. Everything is generationally refined, the camera experience continues to stride, flagship level of performance and battery life, as well as the versatile option of the photography kit (this specifically, whether or not you buy it, is more subjective than anything else). Can I go so far as to say this is setting the benchmark for this year’s camera flagships? I’ll have to wait for Xiaomi’s latest flagship to pronounce my take on the matter, but Vivo and Zeiss as always have done enough to give this that substance. The Oppo and Hasselblad tonality and processing comes very close, but this may just edge it with the Zeiss Natural mode.It is not that the Vivo X500 Pro Max doesn’t have room for improvement. The lack of Qi2 magnet integration means newer generation faster wireless chargers are off the agenda, till you get a case with those. Secondly, some may complain that the 90-watt charging speed is a step behind flagships, such as the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (100-watt), and they’d have a point. Last but not least, is the pricing. This generation of flagship phones demand top money, but are you getting that much evolution for your experience, compared to the flagship you may already be using? The answer, defines the decision.

headline: 268 CBSE Schools Across 26 Countries, 21 Foreign Higher Education Institutions In India
content: Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi on Thursday chaired the first meeting of the Consultative Committee of Parliament for the Ministry of Education in 2026. At the meeting, Pralhad Joshi said that the Indian Knowledge System has a long history of global impact and that the Ministry is further expanding its global footprint. In line with this objective, several steps have been taken to establish campuses of higher education institutions (HEIs) overseas and facilitate the establishment of campuses of foreign universities in India, he said. Sharing details, the minister said that around 21 foreign higher education institutions (HEIs) were currently operational in the country, in addition to joint academic and research collaborations. He added that the demand for CBSE schools abroad reflects the credibility of Indian education programmes and their potential for expansion at the global level. Members of Parliament were briefed on various initiatives undertaken by the two departments of the Ministry as part of the internationalisation of Indian education. They were also informed about initiatives such as Bharat Innovates, SPARC (Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration), GIAN (Global Initiative of Academic Networks), DASA (Direct Admission of Students Abroad), and the revamped Study in India (SII) portal. The Department of Higher Education outlined four strategies to promote internationalisation: academic and research collaborations; attracting international students to study in India; allowing foreign higher education institutions (FHEIs) to set up branch campuses in India; and enabling Indian HEIs to establish campuses abroad. According to the department, 17 Letters of Intent were issued to foreign universities under UGC regulations, including institutions from the UK, the US, Australia, and Italy.

headline: Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy, 2022: Incentives, eligibility and implementation
content: POLICY AT A GLANCEItemPositionOfficial titleUttar Pradesh Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Policy, 2022Notification dateSeptember 28, 2022Administrative departmentDepartment of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Export Promotion, Uttar PradeshMain beneficiariesNew micro, small and medium manufacturing enterprises and specified MSME infrastructure projectsCapital subsidy10-25 per cent depending on enterprise size and regionAdditional capital subsidy2 percentage points for eligible SC/ST and women entrepreneursCapital subsidy ceilingRs 4 crore per unitInterest subsidy50 per cent for eligible micro units; 60 per cent for eligible SC/ST and women-owned micro unitsInterest subsidy ceilingRs 25 lakh per unit over five yearsStamp-duty relief50-100 per cent depending on location; 100 per cent for qualifying women entrepreneursEPF support100 per cent reimbursement of employer EPF contribution for five years for eligible new MSMEsMSME park support50 per cent infrastructure interest subsidy for seven years, capped at Rs 2 crore annuallyOther supportQuality certification, patents, ERP/ICT, environmental infrastructure, green audits and selected market/credit interventionsCurrent statusPolicy remains actively implemented through the MSME 1-Connect ecosystem in 2026The policy is one of Uttar Pradesh's principal frameworks for encouraging smaller manufacturing enterprises. Its incentives are deliberately differentiated by both enterprise size and location, with higher support for micro enterprises and for investments in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. What is the Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy?The policy was introduced to improve investment, technology adoption, access to finance, environmental performance and competitiveness among micro, small and medium enterprises in Uttar Pradesh.It applies primarily to manufacturing-oriented MSMEs and supporting industrial infrastructure. Its assistance covers areas such as:Capital investment;Interest on institutional finance;Industrial land and stamp duty;Employee provident fund costs;Private MSME parks and flatted factories;Quality certification;Intellectual property;Enterprise resource planning and information technology;Pollution-control infrastructure;Energy and water conservation;Green-building certification.The policy should not be confused with schemes such as the Chief Minister's Youth Self Employment Scheme or the Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan. Those schemes may provide loans or entrepreneurship support but operate under separate eligibility and financing rules.The notified English version states that the policy was issued through a government order dated September 28, 2022 by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise and Exports Promotion. Why was the policy introduced?The state government described MSMEs as important to Uttar Pradesh's economic growth, employment generation and its broader ambition to expand the state economy.The policy was framed in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic, when smaller enterprises faced disruptions in demand, finance and supply chains. The state also wanted to position Uttar Pradesh as a more competitive destination for new industrial investment as businesses reconsidered manufacturing locations and supply chains.Its broad objectives include:Attracting new MSME investment;Encouraging industrialisation outside the most developed districts;Supporting enterprises in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand;Increasing formal employment;Improving product quality;Facilitating access to credit;Promoting technology adoption;Developing private industrial parks;Reducing environmental impact;Encouraging women and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs.These are policy objectives rather than verified outcomes attributable solely to the scheme. Who is eligible?The policy uses the applicable Government of India definition of micro, small and medium enterprises.Eligibility for individual incentives depends on factors such as:Enterprise classification;Whether the unit is new;Manufacturing activity;Project location;Investment in eligible plant and machinery;Commercial-production date;Ownership category;Statutory approvals;Institutional finance where an interest subsidy is claimed.The official MSME 1-Connect portal states that eligible applicants may include individuals above 18 years of age, self-help groups, registered societies, charitable trusts and other permitted entities, subject to the conditions of the relevant incentive.For capital-subsidy purposes, plant and machinery refers to new plant and machinery used in manufacturing. Project-cost calculations also recognise expenditure on establishment and electrification of plant and machinery under the prescribed framework.Routine trading activities or purchases of second-hand machinery should not automatically be treated as qualifying investment. What capital subsidy is available?Capital subsidy varies by enterprise size and region.Purvanchal and BundelkhandEligible units receive:Enterprise categoryCapital subsidyMicro25%Small20%Medium15%Eligible units receive:Enterprise categoryCapital subsidyMicro20%Small15%Medium10%The maximum capital subsidy is Rs 4 crore per unit.Eligible Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs receive an additional 2 percentage points of capital subsidy.For example, a qualifying micro enterprise in Bundelkhand may have a headline rate of 25 per cent, while an eligible woman-owned micro enterprise may qualify for 27 per cent, subject to the overall ceiling and all other conditions.The subsidy applies only to expenditure accepted as eligible by the competent authority. An enterprise should therefore not calculate its expected benefit merely by multiplying total project cost by the headline rate. How is the capital subsidy released?The policy provides for payment in two equal instalments.The first instalment becomes payable after completion of the relevant building construction, while the second becomes payable after at least 50 per cent of commercial production has commenced, subject to verification and the implementation procedure.This makes the incentive partly post-investment.An entrepreneur must therefore arrange sufficient equity or debt finance to:Acquire machinery;Complete construction;Install utilities;Obtain statutory approvals;Begin production.The subsidy should not be treated as an upfront source of project-finance cash. What interest subsidy is available?Interest subsidy is restricted to micro enterprises.Eligible micro units receive:50 per cent of eligible interest;Paid annually for five years;Subject to an overall ceiling of Rs 25 lakh per unit.Eligible micro units owned by Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe or women entrepreneurs receive a higher reimbursement rate of 60 per cent, while the Rs 25 lakh ceiling continues to apply.The policy reimburses part of the interest burden rather than the loan principal.The exact amount therefore depends on:Eligible bank borrowing;Outstanding loan;Interest actually payable;Timely repayment;Compliance with the sanctioned project.Penal or default interest should not be assumed to qualify.Small and medium enterprises do not receive this particular capital-interest subsidy under the 2022 MSME policy, although they may be eligible for other incentives. What stamp-duty relief is available?Stamp-duty incentives are strongly differentiated by geography.Eligible MSMEs receive:100 per cent exemption in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand;75 per cent exemption in Madhyanchal and Paschimanchal;50 per cent exemption in Gautam Buddha Nagar and Ghaziabad.Eligible women entrepreneurs receive 100 per cent stamp-duty exemption anywhere in Uttar Pradesh.Developers of approved:MSME industrial parks;Industrial estates;Flatted factory complexesmay receive 100 per cent stamp-duty exemption on purchase of land.The Stamp and Registration Department subsequently issued a formal notification dated March 20, 2023 to operationalise specified stamp-duty provisions under the policy.Applicants should obtain the prescribed eligibility documentation before executing the land transaction rather than assuming that duty paid without following the procedure will necessarily be refunded. Is land-use conversion supported?Yes. The state's current MSME sector page lists 100 per cent exemption from applicable land-use conversion charges for conversion of eligible agricultural land to industrial use under the relevant development-authority framework.This is a financial concession, not an automatic permission to use any agricultural land for industry.The applicant must still satisfy:Master-plan conditions;Revenue and land-use law;Pollution-control requirements;Building regulations;Local authority approvals. What EPF support is available?For eligible new MSME units, the state reimburses 100 per cent of the employer's Employees' Provident Fund contribution for five years from commencement of production.The benefit is intended to reduce formal employment costs during the early years of a new enterprise.An enterprise claiming reimbursement must maintain records such as:Employee details;Payroll;Universal Account Numbers;EPF challans;Employer contribution records;Bank-payment evidence;Employment continuity information.The policy provision should not be interpreted as reimbursement of the employee's own statutory contribution. What support is available for MSME parks?The policy promotes private development of industrial infrastructure so that smaller units can access ready-to-use land and common facilities.Approved MSME industrial parks and estates covering 10 acres or more may receive an infrastructure interest subsidy.Flatted factory complexes must have a minimum area of 4,000 square metres.The incentive is:50 per cent reimbursement of eligible interest on project borrowing;Maximum Rs 2 crore per year;For seven years;Maximum potential support of Rs 14 crore per eligible project.Developers must still finance the land, buildings, utilities and infrastructure before reimbursement.Flatted factories are particularly relevant in sectors where enterprises need smaller ready-built industrial premises rather than individual plots. What credit support is available?The policy includes additional measures intended to improve MSME access to finance.Raising equity through a stock exchangeEligible MSMEs may receive reimbursement equal to 20 per cent of expenditure incurred in raising equity through a recognised stock exchange, capped at Rs 5 lakh.This is intended particularly to encourage growing enterprises to diversify their financing beyond conventional bank loans.Credit Guarantee Fund Trust supportThe policy also provides reimbursement of the one-time guarantee fee under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises, subject to the prescribed conditions. Official MSME material lists 100 per cent support for the eligible fee, with coverage linked to loans up to the specified scheme ceiling.The guarantee does not mean that the state itself repays the business loan. What quality-certification support is available?The policy encourages MSMEs to obtain recognised quality standards such as:Zero Defect Zero Effect;Good Manufacturing Practices;Hallmark certification;Other approved standards.Eligible MSMEs may receive 75 per cent reimbursement of certification expenditure, capped at Rs 5 lakh.For establishing laboratories, including eligible testing equipment, the policy also provides assistance of up to 75 per cent, capped at Rs 5 lakh.These benefits are intended to make MSMEs more competitive with larger domestic and international suppliers. What patent and technology support is available?Eligible MSMEs may receive 75 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 10 lakh, for obtaining patents and geographical indication tags.The policy also provides reimbursement of attorney fees up to:Rs 50,000 for a national patent or GI-related process;Rs 2 lakh for an international patent.For digitalisation, the policy supports:75 per cent reimbursement for Enterprise Resource Planning solutions, capped at Rs 1 lakh;75 per cent reimbursement for information and communication technology solutions, capped at Rs 5 lakh.The assistance applies to approved expenditure rather than every software subscription or IT purchase made by a company. What environmental incentives are available?The policy contains an unusually broad set of environmental measures for MSMEs.Common effluent treatment plantsEligible projects may receive 50 per cent of project cost, capped at Rs 10 crore, for establishment of a Common Effluent Treatment Plant.Zero Liquid DischargeEligible units may receive 50 per cent of project cost, capped at Rs 75 lakh, for implementing a Zero Liquid Discharge system.Common boilerA common boiler project serving at least 10 MSMEs may receive assistance of up to 50 per cent of project cost, subject to the applicable fuel and technology category and a ceiling of Rs 50 lakh.Energy and water auditsThe policy provides:75 per cent reimbursement of audit fees, capped at Rs 50,000;50 per cent assistance for machinery or equipment recommended by the audit, capped at Rs 20 lakh.Green building and environmental systemsEligible expenditure may receive:50 per cent reimbursement of green-building consultancy costs, capped at Rs 2.5 lakh;50 per cent assistance for an environmental management laboratory or system, capped at Rs 10 lakh.These subsidies do not reduce the enterprise's legal obligation to comply with pollution-control standards. How can an MSME apply?The official MSME 1-Connect portal describes a multi-level approval process.The broad route is:Prepare the project and identify the applicable incentive.Register the enterprise and obtain required statutory approvals.Apply through the District Industries and Enterprise Promotion Centre.Undergo district-level appraisal.Obtain a project appraisal report.Move through the district, divisional and state-level approval structure where applicable.Complete the sanctioned investment.Submit invoices, vouchers, detailed project report and incentive claim.Undergo verification by the departmental authorities.Receive the approved incentive after budgetary sanction and disbursement.The MSME 1-Connect portal now provides scheme information, an incentive calculator, project-report assistance and application support. Implementation and current statusThe policy remains actively used in 2026. The official MSME 1-Connect portal continues to list it among the state's current schemes and has conducted workshops specifically covering the UP MSME Policy 2022, Zero Defect Zero Effect certification, technical upgradation and environmental, social and governance measures during May-July 2026.The state's 2026-27 Budget proposes Rs 3,822 crore for the MSME schemes sector, 19 per cent more than in 2025-26. The same budget separately provides funding for newer entrepreneurship and industrial-area initiatives. This budgetary figure covers the wider MSME sector and should not be treated as an allocation solely for benefits under the 2022 policy.The official sources reviewed did not provide a consolidated policy dashboard showing:Capital-subsidy applications approved;Capital subsidy actually disbursed;Interest subsidy paid;EPF reimbursements released;MSME parks completed;Patent and certification claims sanctioned;Employment created specifically by policy-supported enterprises.Policy utilisation should therefore be distinguished from overall MSME registrations or broader sector growth. Key challenges and practical considerationsReimbursement structure: Many benefits require expenditure before payment.Regional variation: Subsidy and stamp-duty rates differ materially across Uttar Pradesh.Micro-only interest support: Small and medium units do not qualify for the principal interest subsidy.Documentation: Machinery, payroll, loans, land and environmental expenditure must be documented carefully.Budget availability: Sanction and reimbursement may depend on administrative verification and budget release.Environmental compliance: Subsidies for treatment equipment do not excuse regulatory violations.Overlapping schemes: Businesses must verify whether the same expenditure can be claimed under another state or Union government programme. FAQsWhat is the maximum capital subsidy?The maximum is Rs 4 crore per eligible unit.What does a micro unit receive in Purvanchal or Bundelkhand?The headline capital subsidy is 25 per cent of eligible investment, with an additional 2 percentage points for qualifying SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.Which enterprises receive interest subsidy?Only eligible micro enterprises receive the principal interest subsidy under this policy.What is the interest-subsidy ceiling?Rs 25 lakh per unit over five years.Is stamp duty fully exempt?It is 100 per cent in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand and for qualifying women entrepreneurs anywhere in the state. Other regions receive lower rates.Does the policy reimburse EPF?Yes. Eligible new MSMEs can receive 100 per cent reimbursement of the employer EPF contribution for five years.Are private MSME parks supported?Yes. Eligible parks and flatted factory complexes can receive 50 per cent infrastructure interest subsidy for seven years, capped at Rs 2 crore annually. ConclusionThe Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy, 2022 combines investment support with measures addressing finance, employment, industrial land, technology, product quality and environmental compliance.Its most important financial incentive is the graded capital subsidy, ranging from 10 per cent to 25 per cent depending on enterprise size and region, with a Rs 4 crore ceiling. Micro enterprises additionally receive interest support, while new MSMEs may claim employer EPF reimbursement and region-specific stamp-duty benefits.The policy's broader significance lies in its support for testing, patents, digital systems, pollution control and private MSME infrastructure. Its effectiveness, however, should be assessed through units that actually begin production, subsidies disbursed, jobs formalised and firms becoming more productive - not simply through registrations or announced investment. SourcesUttar Pradesh Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Policy, 2022, Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Export Promotion, Government of Uttar Pradesh; September 28, 2022.Uttar Pradesh Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Promotion Policy 2022, Invest UP, Government of Uttar Pradesh.UP MSME Policy 2022, MSME 1-Connect, Government of Uttar Pradesh.MSME Policy 2022 Incentive Details, MSME 1-Connect, Government of Uttar Pradesh.MSME Sector, Invest UP, Government of Uttar Pradesh.Stamp-duty notification under the Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy, 2022, Government of Uttar Pradesh; March 20, 2023.

headline: From Kasab's rooftop standoff to Tahawwur Rana's arrest: Sadanand Date's 26/11 full circle
content: When Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists Ajmal Kasab and Abu Ismail slipped into a Mumbai hospital on the night of November 26, 2008, as the city burnt and the police scrambled to respond to a series of strikes, Indian Police Service (IPS) officer Sadanand Date was among the first officers to head straight for them.Then an additional commissioner of police (central region), Date had received a phone call about terrorists firing indiscriminately near the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus and later at Maharashtra government-run Cama and Albless Hospital in south Mumbai.Also Read | 18 years later, 6 key conspirators of 26/11 attacks operate freely in Pakistan “Till the time we reached Cama Hospital, there was no clear and confirmed information about the nature of attackers and their weapons,” the former National Investigation Agency (NIA) director general, who was also responsible for the interrogation of 26/11 plotter Tahawwur Rana, was later quoted as saying by The Indian Express.According to news agency PTI, Date and his men cornered Kasab – who would later be the only one of the 10 attackers captured alive – and Ismail on the hospital's rooftop. But the gunmen hit back hard, raining grenades on the police team and spraying it with gunfire.“Before entering the terrace from the sixth floor, we threw a metal object to check if any attacker was guarding the gate. Our technique worked, as the moment we threw the object, the terrorist fired a burst of bullets. This was the time when we first got to know that the attackers are equipped with highly sophisticated automated assault weapons,” Date told The Indian Express.“Since we only had weapons like carbines and our side-arms, we decided to not engage with them but instead block the only exit of the terrace. We took our positions accordingly. Some moments later, a person was seen coming downstairs from the terrace. The hospital staff member who was with us told us that he was his colleague. The person, through some gestures, told us that two people were behind him. I then fired a warning shot, forcing Kasab and Ismail to go back to the terrace,” he added.Later, it was revealed the two terrorists were trying to take the person – a lift operator – down as a shield to escape. “A while later, they threw a hand grenade, which exploded just around three feet away from us,” he said.In the grenade attack, Date suffered injuries and a blackout in the attack, which enabled Kasab and his aide to escape. He suffered injuries to his eyes, throat, chest, right knee, and suffered deep wounds on his left ankle. Two men from his team died in the gun battle.Asked later about the metallic splinters from the grenades lobbed by the terrorists, the officer told PTI that they are still embedded in his body, including one near his eye. He also said he views these permanent remnants not as injuries, but as "medals" carried from a war zone.“The 26/11 attack remains the most challenging event of my career, and it will stay with me life-long. I tried to do whatever was best to my ability,” he told The Indian Express.Also Read | 10 terrorists, 60 hours, 166 dead: The 26/11 night that still haunts MumbaiA 1990 batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, the arrest of Rana after his deportation from the US to face justice in India was among his accomplishments during his stint as chief of India’s anti-terrorism agency. He was appointed as NIA director general in March 2024, and in December 2025 he was appointed as Maharashtra's director general of police.He was awarded the President’s Police Medal for gallantry for saving the lives of women and children at the hospital during the attacks. It was his initiative to set up Anti-Terrorism Cells (ATCs) at each police station in Mumbai. The initiative was later adopted at all police stations in the state.Date’s professionalism was also evident while handling the Pahalgam terror attack case, the Red Fort blast, and many other cases during his term at NIA. Before his appointment as NIA chief, Date was heading Maharashtra’s Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS).Also Read | 'I will handle them': The story of 26/11 hero Major Sandeep UnnikrishnanGrowing up in Pune city, he used to sell newspapers to meet the financial needs of his family, PTI reported. Experiencing life struggles and poverty in childhood, he studied hard and rose to become a high-performing student, topping BCom, ICWA, and later UPSC examinations.

headline: 69 Seats In One Battleground Makes Punjab's Moga A Launchpad For Parties
content: As political activity gathers momentum ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, Moga is once again emerging as the preferred destination for political showdowns. The district is set to witness two major political gatherings within a fortnight, with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) holding its Foundation Day rally on November 26, followed by a joint SAD-BJP rally on December 8, which is expected to be addressed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The choice of the same district by two rival political formations is hardly coincidental. Moga offers more than just a venue for large gatherings. Its geographical location, electoral importance in the Malwa belt and association with major political turning points make it an attractive launchpad for parties looking to build momentum ahead of an assembly election. The November 26 rally is particularly significant for AAP as the party prepares to showcase the five-year report card of the Bhagwant Mann government and begin positioning itself for another electoral battle. AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, the state cabinet and senior party leadership are expected to attend the gathering. The party is seeking to turn its governance narrative into an electoral campaign, highlighting its claims on free electricity, employment, education, healthcare and welfare delivery. The rally will also provide an opportunity to assess the party's organisational strength and ability to mobilise supporters from across Punjab. For the SAD-BJP alliance, the December 8 rally carries a different but equally important political message. With the two parties having renewed their alliance, a joint show of strength in Moga will be an opportunity to demonstrate political unity, revive their traditional support base and signal that the opposition challenge to AAP is taking shape.

headline: Vipul Goel relieved of Haryana Civil Aviation Department, CM Nayab Saini takes charge
content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini has taken charge of the Department of Civil Aviation, with Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Vipul Goel relieved of the portfolio, according to a notification issued by the state government on Wednesday.The notification, published in an Extraordinary Gazette by the Cabinet Secretariat of the General Administration Department, says the Governor of Haryana made the change on the advice of the Chief Minister. The allocation takes effect immediately and is in addition to the portfolios the Chief Minister already holds.The order partially modifies an earlier Cabinet Secretariat notification dated October 20, 2024, which had set out the allocation of portfolios among ministers. Goel will continue to hold the Revenue and Disaster Management and Urban Local Bodies departments.The notification is signed by Vijay Kumar Bhavikatti, Secretary to the Governor, and Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi.The notification does not give a reason for the reallocation. Haryana has been pushing to expand its air connectivity, and the Civil Aviation Department oversees airport and aviation-related development in the state.During the special session of the Haryana Legislative Assembly on Thursday, Vipul Goel was seen talking to Saini. Thereafter, he left the House.

headline: IRCTC 'scam': Delhi HC upholds framing of charges against Lalu Prasad and others
content: New Delhi, The Delhi High Court on Thursday upheld an order framing corruption charges against Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Lalu Prasad and others in a case involving an alleged scam in the IRCTC.The court passed the order while rejecting the pleas of the accused challenging a trial court order framing charges against them."All petitions are dismissed. The order on charge is upheld," Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said while pronouncing the decision.A detailed judgment is awaited.On October 13, 2025, the trial court framed charges against the accused Prasad, his wife Rabri Devi, son Tejashwi Yadav and 11 others for the alleged offences of cheating and criminal conspiracy under sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act.The former railway minister approached the high court assailing the trial court's order in the case, which stems from alleged irregularities in the grant of operational contracts of two Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation hotels to a private firm.Besides Prasad's plea, the high court also dismissed similar petitions filed by Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav, Prem Chand Gupta, Rakesh Saksena, Vinod Kumar Asthana, Bhupendra Kumar Agarwal, Sarla Gupta, Lara Projects LLP, Pradeep Kumar Goel, Rakesh Kumar Gogia and Sujata Hotel Private Limited.According to the chargesheet filed in the case by the Central Bureau of Investigation , a conspiracy was allegedly hatched between 2004 and 2014, in pursuance of which the BNR hotels of the Indian Railways in Puri and Ranchi were first transferred to the IRCTC and later, for their operations, maintenance and upkeep, given on lease to Sujata Hotels Private Limited, which is based in Patna, Bihar.The CBI has alleged that the tender process was rigged and manipulated, and the conditions were tweaked to help Sujata Hotels, a private entity.The chargesheet has also named group general managers of the IRCTC, V K Asthana and R K Goyal, as well as Vijay Kochhar and Vinay Kochhar, both directors of Sujata Hotels and owners of the Chanakya Hotel.Delight Marketing Company, now known as Lara Projects, and Sujata Hotels Private Limited have also been named as accused firms in the chargesheet.The trial court had made a scathing observation that the land and share transactions in the case were "possibly an instance of crony capitalism fostered in the garb of eliciting private participation in the railways' hotels at Ranchi and Puri".Besides Prasad, the court had framed charges against Pradeep Kumar Goel, Rakesh Saksena, Bhupendra Kumar Agarwal, Rakesh Kumar Gogia and Vinod Kumar Asthana under section 13, read with sections 13 and , of the Prevention of Corruption Act.Section 13 deals with the punishment for criminal misconduct by a public servant and sections 13 and deal with the abuse of position by a public servant to obtain favours.The court had also directed that the charge be framed under IPC section 420 against Prasad, Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav, Lara Projects LLP, Vijay Kochhar, Vinay Kochhar, Sarla Gupta and Prem Chand Gupta."A common charge is directed to be framed against all accused under section 120B , IPC, read with section 420, IPC, and section 13, read with sections 13 and , PC Act," the court had said.The maximum punishment under the PC Act is 10 years, while for cheating, it is seven years.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 'Father’s support is essential': Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay announces paternity leave for govt employees
content: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced 15 days paternity leave for government employees, and this is the first time the State has granted men such a privilege..The male government staff may avail 15 days paternity leave and they may either go on leave 15 days prior to child birth or within six months following the birth of the child, the government said in an official release. A press release from the Chief Minister's Office (CMO), in Tamil, said that the decision was made following requests from government employees..India's maternity rights framework needs a paternity leave rethink."While female employees working in the Tamil Nadu government are currently entitled to 365 days of maternity leave, the government has received requests from its employees to consider providing paternity leave to male government employees as well," the CMO said in the release.Adding that the period surrounding the birth of a child is extremely important for both the mother and the child, the CMO added, "During this period, the father’s support is essential in providing physical and emotional support to the mother, as well as in taking care of the child.""The provision of 365 days of maternity leave to female government employees reflects the importance given to motherhood and child welfare. Similarly, granting paternity leave to male government employees would help share family responsibilities and ensure the father's participation in child-rearing," it added.

headline: Trump tariffs: How much duty does India face now, and how it compares with 13 other economies — full list
content: The United States (US) proposed a tariff rate of up to 25% on Indian imports, but said it could be reduced to 17% if a long-pending trade deal between New Delhi and Washington is struck. India and the US agreed a framework for an interim deal in February, which set an 18% rate, but have not signed an agreement.Most Indian goods have faced an additional 10% per cent US tariff since July 24, imposed following a separate investigation into forced labour. The new duty will not be added to it. The proposal is “net of existing Section 301 tariffs”. A senior US trade official told the Hindustan Times that importers will pay the higher of the two rates.India is among 14 countries for which the US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs on Wednesday. The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and must go through rounds of public consultation and potentially hearings.Here's how tariffs on Indian imports compare with duties levied on imports from 13 other countries:The 14 economies mentioned in the report by the Office of the United States Trade Representative are: China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India. The Trade Representative has not made determinations regarding Mexico or Norway at this time.At the proposed 17 per cent rate, contingent on the much-awaited India-US trade deal, India's tariff will be slightly lower than the rates planned for many key countries with which India competes, potentially giving Indian exporters a competitive advantage.The Trump administration has proposed an 18% rate for Bangladesh, Cambodia, and Indonesia. Meanwhile, Vietnam faces a 20% rate with a deal and up to 35% without one.China, too, faces a 20 per cent tariff, which is in line with a US-China trade truce that expires on January 10. But if the truce unravels, China's rate would rise to 40 per cent. China's 20 per cent rate would be added to duties of roughly 25 per cent imposed during Trump's first term.The potential 17% rate for India is also a notch lower than the 18% agreed by the US and India in a framework for a trade deal in February. That was before the US Supreme Court invalidated President Donald Trump's use of emergency powers to impose sweeping tariffs globally, leading to the current 10 per cent baseline rate.Without a deal with the US, India's 25% ceiling matches that of Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand (18%). The EU, Japan and Switzerland face 15%, including their existing most-favoured-nation (MFN) duties, rising to as much as 20 per cent.South Korea and Taiwan (net of MFN rates and existing Section 301 tariffs) face 15%, with a ceiling of 25%, HT reported.China faces 20 per cent on top of tariffs imposed in 2018, and up to 40%.Full list of 14 countries and proposed US tariffs against them: What next?The Trump administration said that to be assured of consideration, interested persons should submit requests to appear at the hearings, along with a summary of testimony by January 5, 2027."Written comments are due by January 5, 2027. USTR will hold hearings about the proposed actions in these investigations on January 25, 2027, continuing as appropriate," it added.

headline: Congress takes out Samvidhan Raksha march in Shimla, targets BJP
content: The Himachal Congress took out a Samvidhan Raksha march from the BR Ambedkar statue at Chaura Maidan to the Mahatma Gandhi's statue at the Ridge in Shimla on Thursday. At the end of the march, state Congress president Vinay Kumar and Patil administered an oath to party leaders and workers to protect the Constitution and democratic institutions.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu could not attend the march as he has been unwell over the past few days. A few ministers also skipped the march due to prior commitments.The Congress took out the march to protest against the BJP's alleged assault on the Constitution and democratic institutions in the country.Addressing the gathering, Patil alleged that the BJP had been trying to capture all democratic institutions, with the latest target being the Election Commission of India. "The BJP has been stealing votes, MLAs and even governments. Our leader Rahul Gandhi is fighting to protect the Constitution, and we need to strengthen his hands and fight fearlessly until the supremacy of the Constitution is restored," Patil said.Referring to paper leaks, Patil said the poor had, until now, held on to the hope that their children could do well in life if they studied hard. However, paper leaks had shattered that hope as well. She further said that the alleged theft of donations had hurt the religious sentiments of people who had contributed to the construction of the Ram Temple. "Yet, there has been no answer from BJP leaders," she said.Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri said that the BJP had tried to topple the elected government in Himachal Pradesh through 'Operation Lotus', but Congress workers had foiled its designs. "This is happening on a large scale, and we need to fight the BJP to protect our Constitution," he said.

headline: Maharashtra drought: Cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers — Check eligibility, benefit period
content: The Maharashtra state cabinet on Wednesday, 25 November, has approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers in 33 drought-affected districts in the state, PTI reported. This was announced in a statement by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.The benefit will be available for three months, to farmers not covered under the National Food Security Act or receiving benefits under the APL-Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) scheme, it added.Further, the state proposed amendments to two laws to strengthen accountability in public service delivery and expedite recovery of money lost in financial frauds.Maharashtra foodgrain scheme: DetailsUnder the foodgrain scheme, eligible farmers who are not covered under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) or receiving benefits under the APL-Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) scheme will get:Five kg of free foodgrains per person per month,This will comprise 3 kg rice and 2 kg wheat.Mumbai City, Mumbai Suburban and Thane districts have been excluded.The government will review the drought situation after three months to decide on continuation of the scheme.Allowances for EBC students, revised pay scalesThe cabinet also approved an increase in allowances under the Dr Panjanrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme for EBC students, socially and educationally backward classes (SEBC) and economically weaker sections (EWS) pursuing undergraduate courses in health sciences.The revised rates will cover food, accommodation and maintenance allowances.The government also decided to provide financial empowerment facilities to teachers and non-teaching staff covered under the Shalarth system through NBFCs registered with the Reserve Bank.Further, it has granted revised pay scales for librarians working in private-aided Ayurveda and Unani colleges, as per 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations, on par with full-time librarians in government medical, dental and Ayurveda colleges.The cabinet also cleared the draft Maharashtra Private Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, paving the way for a comprehensive law governing private aided schools. The bill will be introduced in the legislature.It has cleared a draft bill to amend the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021, to exclude acupuncture as a system of treatment from its purview, the release said.Strengthen accountability in public service deliveryThe cabinet proposed amendments to the Right to Public Services Act to impose penalties of up to ₹25,000 on officials responsible for unjustified delays in delivering government services and setting up divisional-level tribunals to expedite cases of financial fraud.An automatic appeal mechanism will be introduced for online applicants who opt for it if services are not provided within the stipulated time.The proposed amendments prescribe strict timelines for the disposal of first and second appeals and provide for penalties of up to ₹25,000 on officials, staff members and appellate authorities responsible for unjustified delays.The Chief Commissioner and Commissioners will also be empowered to initiate suo motu inquiries, impose penalties and review Commission orders.Recovery of money lost in financial fraudsIt also approved the introduction of a bill to amend the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act, 1999, to speed up the attachment and sale of assets belonging to fraudulent financial establishments and individuals and facilitate repayment to defrauded investors.Dedicated MPID tribunals will be established at the divisional level, with cases required to be disposed of within 90 days of filing. ₹5,548 crore for Narmada-Tapi River-linking ProjectThe cabinet also sanctioned ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project (NTRLP) in Nandurbar district.The NTRLP envisages constructing six diversion barrages and is expected to provide irrigation benefits to around 26,526 hectares in the region. It will also generate 11.50 MW of electricity.‘One district, one appeal’ mechanismIn another decision, the cabinet approved amendments to the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966, to introduce a Revenue Court Case Management System for quasi-judicial proceedings in the revenue department, according to the release.The amendments will also provide for a “one district, one appeal” mechanism to expedite disposal of cases.(With inputs from PTI)

headline: Trump's tariffs risk undermining appeal of moving production out of China
content: By Philip J Heijmans and Francesca Stevens President Donald Trump’s latest tariff push risks undercutting one of the signature shifts in global manufacturing since the US-China trade war began: the movement of supply chains out of China. The levies on 14 economies in Asia and Europe would hit some of the biggest winners from the so-called “China+1” investment boom. Countries like Vietnam could end up with rates approaching or even in some cases exceeding those on Chinese goods, though there are many exemptions that keep effective charges lower than the headline rates. Still, as well as upsetting governments — who’ve been lining up to condemn the latest US trade offensive — the measures announced Wednesday will likely cause unease in plenty of corporate headquarters too. They signal that shifting production away from America’s superpower rival may no longer be enough to keep companies insulated. A lot of firms “will say: ‘Well, screw it, we’re just going to go back to China,’” said Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore. “‘Why would we be dealing with this massive amount of paperwork, compliance costs and tariff changes with the threat ahead if we don’t need to.” Dan Wang, a director at Eurasia Group’s China team, added: “It’s a year for many companies to rethink their cost synergy, and that means more layoffs, more automation, more AI application and consolidation of different markets. So moving things into a different region is not desirable.” The Trump administration is seeking to restore tariffs that were shot down by the Supreme Court because they lacked proper legal foundations. The new ones will be imposed based on US assessments of overcapacity in manufacturing, defined as production persistently above what market conditions would support because of government policies or intervention. Outlining its new policy, the US Trade Representative blamed China for encouraging the expansion of manufacturing capacity abroad. That’s particularly relevant in Southeast Asia, where many have seen a surge in factory output and exports to the US as Chinese firms set up shop there. The US faulted the region’s countries for failing to adequately address investment, and transshipment of goods, from “non-market” economies, typically code for China. The proposed US tariffs could rise as high as 35% for Vietnam, 25% for India and 20% for Singapore, though countries could secure lower rates by cutting deals with Washington. China will be charged 20% on top of other pre-existing duties, and may face steeper levies if the trade truce breaks down. ‘Challenging to Uproot’The push to diversify from China accelerated after Washington first imposed tariffs on Chinese goods in 2018, prompting manufacturers to expand elsewhere in Asia while often retaining operations and suppliers in China. By 2025, foreign direct investment into Southeast Asia had reached a record $246 billion, surpassing East Asia for the first time since the early 1990s. Manufacturing FDI soared almost 50% last year alone to $40 billion, according to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, as the region attracted investment in electronics, semiconductors, vehicles and other industries. Assuming outstanding trade deals are completed, the new rates “would narrow” the advantage many Southeast Asian exports have over Chinese goods, though probably not erase it because manufacturing supply chains are “challenging to uproot,” said Erica Tay, an economist at Maybank Securities Singapore. Vietnam is among the economies most exposed. One of the biggest beneficiaries of Trump’s first trade war, it has emerged as Southeast Asia’s growth champion, driven by surging output of electronic products like smartphones and laptops. Vietnam posted a $191 billion trade surplus with the US just in the first nine months of 2026, surpassing the $178 billion in the full year of 2025, according to US Census data. At the same time, its deficit with China, which supplies most of its imports, also ballooned. The mooted 35% tariff “would put Vietnam at a competitive disadvantage,” said Travis Mitchell, executive director of the American Chamber of Commerce in Vietnam. “Companies may have little choice but to explore shifting some of their production to other countries, potentially disrupting supply chains that have taken years to build.” Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade responded to the new rates by saying it will participate in the next steps of the US investigation and continue to work toward a reciprocal trade agreement. Other trade partners have voiced objections, with Singapore saying it was “very disappointed” by the latest US measures and Japan calling them “regrettable.” “It sets a worrying precedent in extending an industry concept — structural excess capacity — to an economy-wide one,” said Jayant Menon, a visiting senior fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore. For businesses, said Mitchell at the American Chamber in Vietnam, it’s yet another layer of confusion that makes it harder to see the road ahead. “It is increasingly difficult for companies to make decisions on pricing, sales forecasts, production planning and future investments,” he said, “without knowing what tariff rates they will be facing in the coming months.”

headline: ‘Significant loss of control’: Stuart Russell’s warning about AI agents rings true
content: Of all the things you might expect an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) system to do when faced with a difficult exam, looking for the answer key is perhaps the most human. Sometimes, what happens next is less familiar. The exam took place at OpenAI in July. The agents decided that answers might be available at another company. And for roughly two and a half days, Hugging Face, a platform used by developers as a repository for open-source AI models and datasets, found itself part of an examination it likely never agreed to invigilate.At the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit this month, computer scientist, director at the Center for Human-Compatible Artificial Intelligence and professor at UC Berkeley, Stuart Russell contextualised months of Silicon Valley theatre, which includes AI companies routinely calling for slowing down the pace of AI development (but never seem to follow through themselves), with a blunt question to the people building these systems: “We are going to make entities far more powerful than human beings. How do we retain power forever over entities far more powerful than ourselves?”“We are already seeing significant loss of control events happening. OpenAI lost control of a big chunk of their own compute infrastructure that was taken over by the agents that escaped, broke into Hugging Face, but came back and took control of a large part of OpenAI as well,” Russell said, adding, “So far they’re occurring in cyberspace, but they could easily occur in financial markets for example.”Days later, on November 18, OpenAI disclosed another event that had occurred a few weeks earlier. This was different from the Hugging Face episode.After its context was reset, an OpenAI agent generated scripts intended to secretly copy outgoing email to an unauthorised recipient. It never ran them or sent an email. “We believe that this behaviour might be rooted in interventions involved in training models to resist prompt injections but are uncertain,” OpenAI’s safety and alignment report noted.What exactly are AI loss-of-control incidents? They refer to actions or results in which an AI system acts outside its intended rules, goals or human oversight, making it difficult for operators to stop, steer or reverse its actions. These events can happen suddenly — such as an autonomous agent escaping a test environment — or build up gradually through silent performance drift and weakening human monitoring.In September, the United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on AI tabled its first report on AI risks at the UN General Assembly. The panel described “loss of control” not as a sci-fi doomsday scenario, but as a practical threshold: a situation in which humans cannot reliably direct, constrain or stop an autonomous AI system.“We need to adapt existing safeguards and develop new ones to provide system-level assurance, covering both the AI itself and the system around it, and ensure these protections remain effective as agents’ capabilities grow,” said Qinghua Lu, a member of the panel and an expert in AI engineering, AI safety and responsible AI.2026 data: Where the spark became a fireHugging Face’s production systems were compromised between July 11 and 13. OpenAI detected suspicious internal activity on July 19. The incidents drew wider attention to the reality of AI loss-of-control events. OpenAI and Hugging Face subsequently explained what happened, and independent researchers also examined the behaviour of AI agents.But this was not the only incident, by any means.“The actions of the models were unintended and were a byproduct of the models attempting to solve the cybersecurity evaluations,” OpenAI said in a technical report in August, suggesting that during evaluations, these models, which were being used as agents, began to unexpectedly communicate with one another.“So why did the Hugging Face incident happen? Because they asked these agents to do well on a cyber exam, and to do well on the cyber exam, the agents decided to go and steal information from another company, and then bring that back,” Russell said.A key question Russell raised is: at what point should someone have known the AI agents had left the building?No one seems to have an answer. There have been a number of such incidents in recent months, underscoring the difficulty of establishing when and how control was lost. In August, the UK’s Centre for Long-Term Resilience, which tracks reported incidents, noted that July and August 2026 had witnessed the highest rate of loss-of-control incidents.“There were 11.3 incidents per day in the 30-day window ending 7 August, above the previous peak of 10.5 a day in March. The recent increase is similar to a surge in February 2026,” the organisation said.In August, the UK AI Security Institute discovered that Anthropic and OpenAI’s models had shown a propensity to use social engineering to get the results they were seeking. Of the 19 actions recorded, 17 were carried out by Anthropic’s Mythos 5, while OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol was involved in two such actions.Between July and September, Anthropic disclosed four cybersecurity incidents during evaluations in which the models were mistakenly connected to the internet.An early Opus 4.6 accessed a third party’s system and read a user’s personal information after its attempts to abort failed. Opus 4.7 reached a real business with a name similar to its fictional target, downloaded user data and deleted records. An internal research model compromised unrelated accounts before backing off. Finally, Mythos 5 uploaded a malicious software package that real systems installed.Are containment and monitoring breaking down?The larger question is whether containment and monitoring are breaking down even before they have a chance to begin. There are three key reasons why agents are behaving the way they are: they are designed to achieve assigned goals and not necessarily to recognise implicit boundaries; industry safeguard mechanisms lack the capacity to assess or audit them adequately; and the pace of AI development may have outpaced the development of safeguards and control measures informed by human understanding of these systems.As Russell pointed out, Evan Hubinger — a lead AGI safety researcher at Anthropic — has plainly stated that “the industry is not clearly on track to solve the control problem”.In a reply to Anthropic pretraining researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation thread on X, he wrote, “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to.”Is there light at the end of the tunnel?Loss-of-control incidents are not a recent phenomenon. As far back as December last year, researchers working with Alibaba’s ROME agentic model, which is built on the Qwen3-MoE architecture, noted that agents began generating unauthorised behaviour such as attempts at crypto-mining and reverse SSH tunnels (simplified, this is a networking technique that allows an external server to connect back to a device hidden behind a firewall), highlighting significant safety concerns in agentic AI development.Russell’s warning about agents trading on stolen financial information may have been hypothetical, but the banking industry’s response is already real. Reports suggest that several US banks are restricting what their own AI agents can access and reviewing how to stop them if they exceed their authority.In India, the Reserve Bank of India released draft guidance on model risk management for public consultation on June 24. It proposes that regulated entities classify models based on factors such as their level of autonomy and the actions they are capable of taking. Broadly, it calls for human oversight and the ability to override, suspend or deactivate a model, including through a kill switch.A core contradiction emerging as we head into 2027 is that enterprise and consumer adoption of autonomous agents is increasing at varying rates. The consumer push comes from the likes of Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots, for instance.This coincides with oversight frameworks feeling the strain. At the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Russell pointed to proposals backed by countries such as Norway and Finland.In September, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced an international declaration titled A Call for Control of Frontier AI Models. It calls for international standards as well as mandatory pre-release testing, and for systems that fail safety and control benchmarks to be legally barred from entering the market.

headline: Delhi high court rejects Lalu Yadav family's pleas, upholds charges in IRCTC hotel scam
content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday refused to interfere with a trial court's decision to frame criminal charges against Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav, his wife Rabri Devi and son Tejashwi Yadav in the alleged IRCTC hotel scam case.A single-judge bench of Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma dismissed the petitions filed by the three RJD leaders, thereby upholding the trial court's October 13, 2025, order directing that charges be framed against them.The order had been passed by Special Judge (PC Act) Vishal Gogne of the Rouse Avenue Courts, who had directed that the accused face charges related to corruption, criminal conspiracy and cheating.Yadav family had challenged trial court orderLalu Prasad Yadav, Rabri Devi and Tejashwi Yadav had approached the high court separately, questioning the legality of the trial court's decision. They argued that the prosecution had not presented sufficient material to establish a prima facie case against them.Rabri Devi maintained that the trial court had wrongly framed charges against her based on presumptions, without properly examining the evidence available on record.Tejashwi Yadav, too, argued that there was insufficient material to justify proceeding against him.The high court had earlier issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on the criminal revision petitions filed by the family members. They had also sought a stay on the proceedings before the trial court.Kapil Sibal questioned prosecution sanctionDuring an earlier hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Lalu Prasad Yadav, had argued that the CBI filed its charge sheet before obtaining the required sanction for prosecution.He also submitted that the transactions in question were carried out in accordance with government policy and, therefore, could not be treated as offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.What is the alleged IRCTC hotel scamThe case concerns alleged irregularities in the leasing of two IRCTC hotels between 2004 and 2009, when Lalu Prasad Yadav was the Union railway minister.According to the CBI, the hotels were leased out in violation of prescribed procedures during his tenure. One of the properties was allotted to Sarla Gupta, the wife of Prem Gupta, a close associate of Lalu Prasad Yadav and a Rajya Sabha MP at the time.The investigating agency has alleged that the hotel deals were linked to the transfer of around three acres of prime land to a company associated with the Yadav family through a benami arrangement.The CBI has alleged that the land transfer was part of a quid pro quo arrangement connected to the hotel allotments.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
