headline: 20 Rohtak’s MD University candidates recommended for various entries in Defence Services in 2026
content: Maharshi Dayanand University (MDU), Rohtak, has added another achievement to its record, with 20 candidates being recommended/ selected for various entries in the Defence Services in 2026.The candidates have qualified through prestigious entry schemes, including the National Defence Academy (NDA), Combined Defence Services (CDS), Air Force Common Admission Test (AFCAT), NCC Special Entry, Technical Entry Scheme (TES) and Short Service Commission (SSC) Technical Entry, said Pankaj Nain, Public Relations Officer, MDU.He maintained that the achievement had been recorded by the University's Youth Centre for Skill Development for Defence Services (YCSDS), functioning under the Department of Student Welfare (DSW). The centre has been providing focused guidance and training to young aspirants preparing for careers in the Armed Forces.Congratulating the successful candidates, Vice-Chancellor Prof Milap Punia said that the achievement reflected the university's commitment to nurturing disciplined, confident and responsible young citizens. He observed that joining the armed forces was not merely a career choice but an opportunity to serve the nation with dedication, courage and a sense of responsibility. He also appreciated the efforts of the centre in guiding students towards their aspirations and wished the candidates success in their future endeavours.Project Director, YCSDS, Prof Shalini Singh, said that the selection of 20 candidates in 2026 was a matter of pride for the university and reflected the dedication and hard work of the aspirants. She highlighted the centre's role in providing systematic guidance, motivation and preparation for various defence selection processes. She encouraged students to remain focused, disciplined and committed to their goal of serving the nation."Among the successful candidates, Rakshit Jangra, Neha, Bharat Hooda, Jayesh and Deepali have been recommended for NDA-156, while Shivam has qualified for NDA-156 and TES Entry. Aprajeet Singh has been selected through CDS IMA Entry, while Sanjeet and Abhishek Suhag have qualified through NCC Special Entry. Ayush Kumar Tanwar, Jigyasa, Avinash, Sneha Hooda and Mansi Deswal have been recommended through AFCAT Entry," said the PRO.Nain maintained that Gaurav and Arpit have qualified for NDA-157, while Renu and Chaitanya have been recommended through SSC Technical Entry for Women and Men, respectively. Punit has qualified through AFCAT and ICG Entry, while Akash Deswal has been selected through CDS-OTA Entry, he added.

headline: Vijay govt announces 15-day paternity leave for govt employees for first time
content: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay has announced 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees for the first time in the state.Male government employees can avail themselves of the leave either 15 days before the expected date of childbirth or within six months after the birth of the child.The state government said it had received requests from male employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave.Explaining the decision, the government said the period surrounding childbirth was important for both the mother and the newborn. It said a father's support was essential in providing physical and emotional support to the mother and caring for the child.Currently, female government employees in Tamil Nadu are entitled to 365 days of maternity leave.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: SC asks Centre to submit census SOPs on caste data collection within a week
content: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the directorate of census operations to submit within a week the standard operating procedures (SOPs) governing the census, including the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information.The direction came after the Centre agreed to place the relevant SOPs on record before the court, news agency PTI reported.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant procedures.The bench asked her to provide the details within a week.What the petition soughtThe direction came in response to a plea by Aakash Goel raising concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying caste-related information under a notification issued on August 14 concerning the census.The petition sought disclosure of the methodology, applicable household schedule and instructions governing the recording and verification of caste particulars, while ensuring the confidentiality of individual information.The plea also sought a transparent mechanism to record identifying particulars of government-issued caste certificates, wherever available, and verify their authenticity through the competent authorities.The petitioner also sought a direction that caste data collected during Census 2027 should not be treated as the sole basis for formulating or revising reservation policies or determining caste-based allocation of welfare resources unless a transparent and verifiable verification protocol is put in place.It also pressed for authorities to submit an affidavit detailing the proposed protocol and steps taken to implement it.In an order dated October 12, the bench had asked the solicitor general to place on record the SOPs being followed for the census. It had also directed that a complete set of the paper book be provided to the advocate-on-record for the Centre and the office of the solicitor general.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: In a first, Tamil Nadu govt approves 15-day paternity leave for govt staff
content: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced the introduction of paternity leave for male employees working in the state government for the first time. The male government staff may avail 15 days paternity leave and they may either go on leave 15 days prior to child birth or within six months following the birth of the child.The move comes after the government received requests from male government employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave.Noting that the period surrounding child birth is crucial for both the mother and the child, the state government said it had sympathetically considered the request and issued an order granting 15 days of 'paternity leave' to married male government employees to be with their wives during child birth."This leave may be availed starting up to 15 days prior to the birth of the child or within six months from the date of child birth", the government said an official release on Thursday.Observing that 365 days of maternity leave to women government employees reflects the importance accorded to motherhood and child welfare, the government said, extending paternity leave to male government employees would share family responsibilities and ensure the father's active participation. ALSO READ: Karthigai Deepam row: VHP slams Vijay’s TVK government over Deepam lighting, says it ‘insulted judiciary’In August, the state government had announced that it would extend the maternity leave window from 12 weeks to 365 days for its women employees having their third child.In 2011, the original 90-day maternity leave window was increased to six months, which was further boosted to nine months in 2016, and extended to one year (365 days) in July 2021 by the respective state governments at the time, led by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK).ALSO READ: Tamil Nadu governor asks CM Vijay to explain why temple lamp wasn’t lit at SC-ordered siteThe 365-day benefit is applicable to regular women employees with less than two surviving children as per the standard eligibility framework, news agency PTI reported, citing a government source.However, as per the directives of the Supreme Court and subsequent state amendments, women employed by the state government with two or more surviving children are entitled to 12 weeks of maternity leave with full pay.

headline: Exporters seek early trade deal with US, cite 17% tariff advantage
content: Indian exporters on Thursday urged the government to seal a trade pact with the US at the earliest, saying the proposed 17 per cent tariff, as outlined in the USTR report, would give India an advantage over competing nations.They said that this is the right time to finalise the deal as exporters are getting good orders from the US buyers."India should do the trade deal as soon as possible. We are getting a lot of orders from the US, and further opening of the market will help increase exports," Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) President S C Ralhan said.He added that the absence of a trade deal with the US could hurt India's exports by putting domestic exporters at a disadvantage compared with competitors from countries that enjoy lower tariff rates.This could affect the price competitiveness of Indian goods in the US market, making it difficult for exporters to retain existing buyers and secure new orders, Ralhan said.He added that the agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India's long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level playing field with suppliers from other countries in the US market."While the industry is concerned with these developments as it raises uncertainty, there is no panic amongst exporters," he said.Ralhan also called for clarity on how the proposed measures would interact with existing duties under Sections 301 and 232 and how the product-specific exemptions in the USTR notice would apply."Clear rules on the duties payable on each product would help exporters quote prices with confidence and avoid overlapping tariff burdens," he said.FIEO urged negotiators to secure competitive tariff treatment for Indian products, address non-tariff barriers and improve market access.It called for particular attention to MSMEs, which have less room to absorb sudden increases in duties and compliance costs.The Federation also urged close consultations between the government and industry to assess the impact on each sector and prepare submissions for the USTR's public consultation process.Sharing similar views, Ramesh Kumar Juneja, Chairman, Council for Leather Exports (CLE), said that the proposed 17 per cent tariff will be the "best deal" for India."We would urge for early finalisation of the deal. The proposed tariffs on India is lower than its competitors," Juneja said, adding that India is in a better position than Bangladesh and Vietnam.Rafeeq Ahmed, chairman of leading leather and footwear products, Farida group, too said that the deal is "very" important for India."The key takeaway from the USTR report is that the proposed tariff on Indian goods is lower than that on Vietnamese goods. This will make Indian products more competitive in the US market," he said.The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.The proposed tariffs followed investigations by the US Trade Representative into 16 economic jurisdictions -- China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, Norway, Mexico and India -- relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.Under the proposed USTR tariffs, Indian imports face a 17 per cent tariff if a trade pact is finalised, offering a calculated one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a three per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate).On Wednesday, the USTR unveiled tariff proposals targeting 14 economic jurisdictions with two distinct rates, a higher one proposed as part of the Sec 301 probe, and a lower deal rate if the countries agree to a trade pact with the US.India, in its negotiations with the US on the trade deal, has been insisting on a competitive advantage over its Asian rivals, a demand that Washington has addressed in the tariff proposals. However, it was not immediately clear whether the one percentage point differential addresses the concerns flagged by India.The EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland face 15 per cent tariff rates, inclusive of standard import duties. Vietnam would face tariffs of 20 per cent if the trade deal is finalised.The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.The investigation began last March, after the Supreme Court overturned the indiscriminate trade levies imposed by the Donald Trump administration invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA).After that reversal, the USTR opened two investigations based on Article 301: one directed at 60 jurisdictions (about a hundred countries) for violating export regulations on forced labour; and the other against 16 jurisdictions for promoting surplus production.India and the US are negotiating an interim bilateral trade agreement after the framework they finalised in February went back to the discussion board, with the Supreme Court striking down the IEEPA tariffs imposed last year.India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitors such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia.

headline: Hexagons for nutrients: Supreme court asks FSSAI to tighten front packet labelling
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to use "total sugars" and "saturated fat", instead of "added sugar" and "added fat", as nutrients of concern in front-of-package nutrition labelling on packaged foods, alongside salt.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed the food regulator to ensure that each nutrient of concern is represented through a separate standardised hexagon carrying the corresponding pictogram and warning words, "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt", PTI reported."The FSSAI shall ensure that the FoPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern, each containing the words 'High Fat', 'High Sugar', 'High Salt', respectively, alongside their corresponding pictograms, rather than a single combined hexagon," the bench said.The court further asked the FSSAI to revisit and reformulate the threshold levels for each nutrient of concern.It also directed the regulator to ensure that sweetened beverages which do not exceed the prescribed nutrient thresholds are not displayed with front-of-package labels identical or deceptively similar to the warning labels prescribed for beverages exceeding those limits.On artificial preservatives and other additives, the bench directed the FSSAI to closely monitor product reformulation following the introduction of front-of-package nutrition labelling (FoPNL).The court noted that the FSSAI had stated in its affidavit that it proposed to adopt a single-phase approach to implementing the labelling regime. It directed the regulator to bring the regulations into force within its proposed timeline and take all necessary steps to ensure that it is strictly followed.FoPNL refers to nutritional information displayed graphically on food packaging to help consumers make informed purchasing decisions and choose healthier food options.The Supreme Court delivered its verdict on an application filed in a petition by public charitable trust 3S and Our Health Society, which sought directions to the Centre, states and Union territories to make front-of-package nutrition labelling mandatory on packaged foods.During an earlier hearing on September 28, the court had questioned the FSSAI over its proposed implementation timeline. The food regulator had told the court that it would need approximately four months to issue and finalise the draft regulations.It had also said the draft amendment regulations would be published for 60 days to invite comments from stakeholders through domestic consultation and the World Trade Organisation platform.The apex court had previously sought further clarity from the FSSAI on its proposed warning labels for nutrients of concern, including fat, sugar and salt.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Punjab and Haryana HC quashes 2 FIRs against social activist Nirmal Gorana
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has quashed two FIRs registered by the Faridabad Police in June 2021 against Nirmal Gorana, a social worker and activist who has been working for many years on housing rights and the rehabilitation of slum dwellers.The FIRs arose out of the demolition drive carried out at Khori village, Faridabad, after the Supreme Court directed the removal of unauthorised structures within six weeks.The FIRs were registered under Sections 109, 114, 117, 147, 149, 180, 188, 189, 269, 505(1)(b) and 506 of the IPC and Section 51 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, alleging that Gorana had addressed residents in breach of prohibitory orders under Section 144 CrPC and COVID-19 restrictions and had incited resistance to the demolition.Arjun Sheoran, advocate appearing for Gorana, argued that both FIRs were registered on the statements of police head constables, although the prohibitory orders allegedly violated had been issued by the District Magistrate, Faridabad.Section 195(1)(a) CrPC bars a court from taking cognisance of offences under Sections 172 to 188 of the IPC except on a written complaint by the public servant concerned.He said that the petitioner is a social worker and had been working for housing rights and rehabilitation of slum dwellers since long. He had never violated any law and was simply helping the residents of Khori village to relocate, after the orders of the Supreme Court for demolition of unauthorised structures in the vicinity within a period of six weeks.After hearing the arguments, Justice N S Shekhawat quashed FIR dated June 14, 2021, and FIR dated June 15, 2021, both registered at Police Station Surajkund, along with all consequential proceedings.Relying on the Supreme Court's decision in Devendra Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2025, the court held that where the other offences form an integral part of the same transaction as the offence under Section 188 IPC, they too fall within the bar of Section 195, and the prosecution cannot be split up to proceed on them alone.The FIRs were therefore quashed in their entirety, and not merely to the extent of Section 188.

headline: Six years after Delhi march, Punjab farmers’ movement grapples with divisions, fading momentum
content: Six years after thousands of farmers marched towards Delhi to oppose the three contentious farm laws, the farmers’ movement in Punjab is facing a crisis of unity, political differences and dwindling mobilisation.Several of the key demands that sustained the year-long agitation remain unaddressed. The historic march, which began on November 26, 2020, brought together farmers from across the country to protest against the Farmers’ Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020; the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020; and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020.The farmers had argued that the laws would weaken the regulated mandi system, undermine the minimum support price (MSP) regime, expose them to corporate exploitation and dilute safeguards against hoarding of essential commodities. Following a year-long agitation at Delhi’s borders, the Centre repealed the three laws in November 2021.However, six years on, farmers’ organisations say there has been little progress on their other major demands, including a legal guarantee for MSP for all crops, a farm loan waiver covering farmers and agricultural labourers, and a comprehensive crop insurance scheme.The movement, which brought several farmer unions together under a common umbrella, has since fragmented. The Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), which spearheaded the Delhi agitation, has split into the SKM and the SKM (Non-Political). Differences over political engagement and the electoral choices of constituent unions in the run-up to the 2022 Punjab Vidhan Sabha elections further complicated efforts to maintain a united platform.The movement has also struggled to sustain its momentum. A rare instance of wider mobilisation, albeit much smaller in scale and intensity than the Delhi agitation, was witnessed recently when the Punjab Government announced its land pooling policy.The political landscape has also changed. The pressure generated by the farmers’ agitation had contributed to the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) walking out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020. The two parties have now reunited, even as sections of the farmers’ movement continue to oppose the BJP.The divisions within the SKM have come into sharper focus, with some constituent unions making independent political choices. Harinder Singh Lakhowal of the BKU (Lakhowal), who recently extended support to the SAD, said the SKM’s rules had been amended to allow constituent unions to make independent electoral choices, provided they did not contest elections themselves.“In six years, the momentum built in 2020-21 is getting lost. There is no word on an MSP guarantee for all crops, farm loan waiver for farmers and farm labourers, or crop insurance. We have supported the SAD, not the BJP. Our support is to a regional party so that it can take our demands to the Centre,” he told The Tribune.He said the SAD had assured the union that it would take up two important issues concerning Punjab with the Centre — the release of Bandi Singhs and a legal guarantee for MSP.“We have not even been heard in the five years since the protest ended in 2021,” he said, while criticising both the AAP and the Congress over their handling of farmers’ issues.However, other farmer organisations have strongly opposed any political alignment with parties they consider responsible for implementing policies detrimental to farmers. Kirti Kisan Union general secretary Rajinder Singh Deepsinghwala said his organisation would oppose any political alliance involving the BJP.“The farmers’ movement has slowed down. When the protest was called off, nearly 70 per cent of farmers in the country did not know about MSP. It was decided that unions from all states would return and build a movement for a legal guarantee for MSP. In most states, this did not happen,” he said, adding that the lack of political engagement on farmers’ demands had also contributed to the absence of progress.Meanwhile, the state committee of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Ekta Dakaunda) has condemned what it described as indirect support extended to the BJP by certain farmer organisations. State president Manjit Singh Dhaner said that while all political parties were responsible for implementing policies favouring corporate interests, the BJP, being in power at the Centre, was the principal adversary of farmers and labourers.He maintained that farmers’ and labourers’ issues could not be resolved by aligning with political parties implementing such policies. The union said the collective strength of people had been instrumental in the success of the Delhi agitation and expressed concern that some farmer organisations were moving away from that approach.

headline: Family of slain DM Krishnaiah hails Supreme Court order quashing Anand Mohan’s remission
content: The family of slain IAS officer and former Gopalganj magistrate magistrate G Krishnaiah on Thursday welcomed the Supreme Court's order quashing the remission granted to Bihar’s former member of Parliament Anand Mohan in Krishnaiah's murder case, describing it as a moment of great relief and happiness.Both his daughter, Padma, and wife, Uma Krishnaiah expressed satisfaction with the verdict, while underlining that no judgment could undo the family’s irreparable loss.“We have got justice in the end. Mohan had come out of jail, but we knew he would again have to go back. The remission was wrong,” Padma told news channel News 18. She thanked the Indian Administrative Service fraternity and those who supported her in the legal battle against the remission the Bihar government granted in 2023Asked whether her petition in the court was based on how the remission was granted by tweaking rules, Padma replied yes, one hundred percent. “We were opposing the tweaking of jail rules,” she said. Welcoming the verdict, Uma Krishnaiah said that while it could never compensate for the loss she had to bear and the long battle she had to fight to secure justice.In a phone conversation with HT from her residence in Jubilee Hills in Hyderabad, on Thursday afternoon, she expressed gratitude to the people, particularly the officers, who stood by her throughout the difficult journey, saying their support had been crucial in helping the family fight the case this far.Mohan was convicted and sentenced to life in the 1994 murder case.The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal called the remission another example of how the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-Janata Dal (United) or JD(U) use power to tweak rules to either frame people or get them released from jail as per their own political convenience. “ It is now proven how former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar and BJP had tweaked the jail rules for granting release to Anand Mohan for their own political interests. The BJP-JD (U) always uses people with muscle power for their own needs, as it did with Anant Singh, who faced a case of possessing an AK-47 and then was given relief, when the trust vote happened a few years back for the new government in January 2024,” said RJD leader Tejashwi YadavJD(U) leader Rajiv Ranjan Singh said he was not aware of the Supreme Court and would not comment.BJP spokesperson Sumit Shashank said the RJD had become totally frustrated by its poll debacles and was making all baseless allegations against JD(U)- BJP about tweaking jail rules to give relief to Mohan. “ RJD has totally become directionless and does not have anything substantive to offer.”

headline: Same units, different electricity bill? When you use power could matter soon as Centre plans to introduce new rules
content: Electricity charges could vary by time of day for most consumers by April 2029. The Ministry of Power has proposed changes to encourage electricity use when supply is plentiful. Consumers could also be encouraged to shift usage to periods of lower demand. The draft rules are proposed to take effect on April 1, 2027, according to Saur Energy International Magazine.Consumers with maximum demand above 10 kW would move to Time-of-Day tariffs first. Their deadline is April 1, 2028. Other consumers would switch by April 1, 2029, with agricultural consumers exempt. The rates would vary across time slots and apply to the energy charge on bills.State electricity commissions would consider demand patterns and renewable power generation when setting those slots. They would look at both the state and the electricity supplier. The cost of buying power varies throughout the day and across seasons. Commissions would consider those costs, power exchange prices and what existing meters can measure.Consumers who also generate renewable power could face a storage requirement from April 1, 2028. State commissions could require storage equal to at least 20% of the system’s daily generation. A commission could set a different share. Without a specified threshold, the requirement would apply to systems above 10 kW.The draft sets deadlines for new connections and changes to existing ones. Suppliers would have three days in metropolitan and municipal corporation areas.How will it work?The limit is seven days in other municipal areas and 15 days in rural areas. Rural areas in hilly states and Union Territories would have a 30-day limit.These deadlines apply after consumers submit complete applications. Suppliers could take up to 90 days if they must extend mains or commission substations. They would have to connect the premises immediately after completing that work.Suppliers would have to flag unusually high or low electricity use in their billing systems. This applies when usage exceeds five times the average of the previous six billing cycles. Bills showing consumption below one-fifth of that average would also be flagged. State commissions could set other limits for identifying such cases.Suppliers would have 30 days from the date the electric bill is generated to resolve flagged cases. Consumers could avoid disconnection by paying for average usage over the previous six billing cycles.Those payments would continue until the supplier resolves the issue. The billing safeguards would take effect within six months of the amended rules. They could begin earlier if the supplier is ready.
