headline: NGT flags high BOD in Ashwani Khad catchment in Himachal
content: Shimla: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) flagged high organic pollution at two locations in the Ashwani Khad catchment after a Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) report recorded a biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) level of 22.4 mg/l at Combermere.The observation came during a November 25 hearing in a suo motu case over media reports calling Ashwani Khad—a key water supply source for Shimla—one of the state’s most polluted rivers.Of the 25 monitoring sites, two stretches recorded high BOD levels: Lift Nullah near the waste-processing site (16mg/l) and Lift Nullah at Combermere (22.4 mg/l), pointing to heavy organic pollution loads. The report also found relatively high faecal coliform levels at some spots, which remained within prescribed limits but still warranted scrutiny.The NGT had taken suo motu cognizance of reports alleging that unregulated industrial effluents, untreated sewage, and agricultural runoff were polluting Himachal rivers, with Ashwani Khad among the worst hit.Formed by Churat Nallah and Jagroti Nallah, Ashwani Khad runs about 16km through Shimla district before entering Solan district at Sadhupul. While there is no industrial estate along the Shimla stretch, hotels, boarding schools and colleges, automobile workshops, a slaughterhouse, fruit and pickle units, and town drains and nallahs feed into the catchment across Shimla, Dhalli, Kasumpti, Vikasnagar, and nearby areas.In a November 16 report, the HPSPCB mapped potential pollution sources, wastewater pathways, and 25 monitoring locations. During the hearing, its Shimla regional office acknowledged the report did not clarify whether the identified discharges were treated sewage or trade effluent, and sought time to clarify.The tribunal gave the Jal Shakti department two weeks to report progress on sewerage network construction and gave Shimla Jal Prabandhan Nigam Limited (SJPNL) two weeks to file its reply. It also ordered the HPSPCB to continue tracing sources—especially where BOD and faecal coliform levels are elevated—by checking discharge pathways and treatment plants, and to act against violations.The next hearing is set for March 5, 2027.STPs mostly satisfactorySamples from the Dhalli, Lalpani, and Malyana sewage treatment plants (STPs) generally met norms for pH, BOD, COD, TSS, and faecal coliform, but total nitrogen at most plants failed NGT standards. A sample from the municipal corporation slaughterhouse at Krishna Nagar—linked to STP Lalpani—recorded a pH of 9.8, above the 5.5–9.0 limit.Catchment checksThe HPSPCB listed facilities for verification, including STPs at Dhalli, Malyana, and Lalpani, captive STPs of SJVNL and Himachal Estate, the Krishna Nagar slaughterhouse, APG University, AIIMS Chamiana, and automobile workshops. Monitoring covers 25 points across Jagroti, Bhattakufer, Churath, Lift, Kasumpti, and Koti nullahs and stretches of Ashwani Khad.Meanwhile, SJPNL’s 3.1 MLD common STP at Dogra Bridge (Panthaghatti) was only about 10% complete as of a September 14, 2026 SJPNL letter, with completion targeted for March 2027.

headline: Church on ‘government land’ vandalised in Odisha village, peace committee formed
content: Koraput, Odisha Residents of a village in Odisha's Koraput district protested against the construction of a church-cum-prayer hall allegedly on government land and vandalised the structure, prompting the local administration to form a peace committee to maintain communal harmony in the area, police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026). https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/ The incident occurred at Patraguda village under the Kotpad block, where tribal people objected to the construction of the church, following which a district administration team visited the site and issued a show-cause notice to the man who had built the structure, a senior officer said. ALSO READ | Christians increasingly under attack in Odisha, claim activists https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/christians-increasingly-under-attack-in-odisha-claim-activists/article70943547.ece The incident came to light after Durjyadhan Harijan, belonging to the only Christian family in the tribal village, lodged a police complaint on November 21, alleging that a group of locals had vandalised the Beersheba Pentecostal Church. The villagers were also accused of damaging the cross and parts of the prayer hall, the officer said. "The villagers alleged that the church was established on government land which was meant for community use and not for one family. The person had failed to produce any land documents to establish his ownership of the site. He demolished the structure as he failed to reply to the show-cause notice," Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra said. A peace committee had been formed, and a meeting was held in the presence of senior police officers and villagers to maintain communal harmony, he said. ALSO READ | Church vandalised in Odisha over allegations of sexual assault https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/church-vandalised-in-odisha-over-allegations-of-sexual-assault/article70830673.ece "I have also asked the revenue inspector concerned to submit a status report on the plot and the demolished structure. Further action will be taken based on the report," Mr. Bhatra said. The police registered a case against seven people named in Mr. Harijan's complaint, the officer said. Kotpad Inspector-In-Charge Runu Majhi said the case was under investigation and no arrest had been made so far. “Attacking someone based on their religious attire is a violation of constitutional rights, human dignity” “Attacking someone based on their religious attire is a violation of constitutional rights, human dignity” Sr. Sujata Jena, a lawyer and nun of the Congregation of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary in Odisha, refutes allegations of religious conversion by nuns in tribal areas, terms them unfounded and politically motivated. “Attacking someone based on their religious attire is a violation of constitutional rights, human dignity” storyline 1 Mr. Bhatra said the only Christian family in the 250-household village has six members. Mr. Harijan, however, claimed that the plot belongs to his father and that the structure had been built for his family to hold church services every Sunday. The man also alleged that some villagers had opposed the construction of the church, and accused his family of being involved in religious conversions, a charge he denied.

headline: Sundarbans sees simultaneous erosion and land accretion, Ghoramara loses 55% of land in 50 yrs: Panel
content: The Sundarbans is not simply losing land to the sea: while some islands are shrinking, new sedimentary landforms are emerging elsewhere in the estuarine landscape. A joint committee examining coastal erosion has found that Ghoramara island in West Bengal lost 55.4% of its mapped area between 1969 and 2019, but has cautioned against trying to hold back the sea with hard-engineering structures along its entire shoreline. Instead, it has recommended targeted protection for vulnerable settlements and infrastructure, alongside mangrove conservation.The report, dated November 25, was submitted by the Union environment ministry to the National Green Tribunal (NGT), which had taken suo motu cognisance of a news report in August last year highlighting the shrinking landmass of Ghoramara island.In an order dated February 17, 2026, the tribunal constituted a joint committee comprising the deputy director general of forests (Central), representing the environment ministry’s regional office in Bhubaneswar, and the principal chief conservator of forests, West Bengal, to examine coastal erosion in the Sundarbans and prepare a comprehensive plan for mangrove protection and coastal erosion management. The environment ministry’s regional office in Bhubaneswar was designated as the coordinating agency. HT has seen the report.“The available evidence establishes substantial historical and spatial changes in Ghoramara Island and the surrounding estuarine landscape, involving erosion, sediment deposition, channel migration and landform development,” the report said.It said erosion at Ghoramara was occurring alongside accretion and the formation or expansion of landforms elsewhere in the estuarine system. “Shoreline change is therefore spatially variable and influenced by the evolving configuration of channels, sedimentary landforms and hydrodynamic conditions.”The committee cited Geological Survey of India (GSI) data showing that Ghoramara’s area declined from 8.59 sq km in 1969 to 3.83 sq km in 2019.A separate assessment by the National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), also cited in the report, found that the island’s mapped area contracted from 458.23 hectares in 2011 to 326.25 hectares in 2026, a reduction of nearly 29%.The NCSCM assessment also classified 93% of the island’s shoreline as experiencing high erosion during the pre-monsoon period, with the figure rising to 95% post-monsoon. The shoreline perimeter shrank by nearly 25% over 36 years, from 10.09 km in 1990 to 7.53 km in 2026.The committee said the available studies did not establish the relative contribution of individual processes, including tidal currents, sediment transport, cyclones, storm surges, sea-level rise and possible land subsidence, to erosion along specific stretches. It also found no evidence to attribute the island’s erosion to any single human intervention.The report noted that the West Bengal forest department had said earlier paved and bank-protection structures had not yielded the desired results in controlling erosion. The state’s irrigation and waterways department had reported protection, restoration and strengthening works covering 12.24 km, at an expenditure of ₹6.25 crore.“The management approach should focus on reducing risks to settlements, essential infrastructure, agricultural areas and other vulnerable assets, rather than attempting to arrest the natural evolution of the entire island,” the committee said.It recommended maintaining and strengthening existing embankments wherever necessary, undertaking localised protection measures at critical erosion-prone locations and conserving existing mangroves. It also cautioned against indiscriminate mangrove plantation along actively eroding banks, saying plantations should be undertaken only at suitable locations.The report further recommended setting up a state-level coordination committee, with the West Bengal Coastal Zone Management Authority as the nodal agency, to oversee the implementation of the proposed measures.

headline: ‘Politics could not change us, we changed politics’: Kejriwal on AAP foundation day
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday said his party had "changed politics" in the country, as it marked its foundation day.Listing the party's achievements, including forming governments in Delhi and Punjab, Kejriwal said that despite doubts being raised about its political future, AAP had persevered and earned people's trust."In a very short time, we have come a long way. When the party was formed, many questions were raised about us. Would we be able to achieve anything? How long would this party last? What do these people know about politics, anyway?" Kejriwal said in a post on X in Hindi."But we not only endured, we also won the hearts of the entire country. We formed a government in Delhi, we formed a government in Punjab, and from Jammu and Kashmir to Goa and Gujarat, we earned the trust and love of the people of India," he added."We focused on getting things done and talked about education and healthcare. Politics could not change us; instead, we changed politics," he said.The former Delhi Chief Minister said a lot remained to be done for the country and asserted that the party would neither be afraid nor back down.AAP celebrates its foundation day on November 26, marking its formation in 2012.

headline: ₹125.69-crore project for 540 chargers across 180 locations: Delhi govt's big EV push for school bus fleets
content: Delhi education minister Ashish Sood said on Wednesday said that the government has rolled out a project worth ₹125.69 crore project to install 540 electric vehicle (EV) chargers across 180 locations, primarily along key school bus routes, to help schools transition 30% of their private bus fleets to electric vehicles under the Delhi EV Policy.“There’s a push for schools to transition towards EV. It is rather a gradual process as we are also simultaneously building charging infrastructure on the routes where school buses ply,”Sood said as he attended the roll out of EV buses of South Delhi-based Vasant Valley School. More schools have signed up to switch from conventional vehicles to EVs while more schools have signed up for the move at reducing environmental pollution .The Vasant Valley school has so far replaced its CNG and diesel buses with 14 electric buses, catering to over 400 students.“We have completely transitioned to EV buses with 14 in the fleet. The transition has been largely smooth except that we added new routes as the capacity of the buses are a little less than the CNG buses,” said Vasant Valley school principal, Sharmila Bakshi.The 2026 policy on EVs for school bus fleets, which came into effect on July 1 and will remain in force until March 31, 2030, mandates that at least 30% of a school’s total bus fleet be converted to electric vehicles. It sets phased targets, requiring schools to achieve 10% EV adoption within two years of the notification, 20% by the third year and 30% by March 31, 2030. The education department is the nodal authority for the implementation of the planned transition for schools operating buses in any of the following manner—owned, leased or hired.Vasant Valley School’s entire electric bus fleet is hired from fleet-as-a-service provider Juleh Mobility, which oversees the day-to-day operations, including drivers, vehicle maintenance and charging infrastructure. More private schools have signed up.

headline: Temporary vegetable market for Tikkan in Mandi likely within a month as APMC inspects sites
content: The long-pending demand for a vegetable market at Tikkan in Mandi district’s Chauhar Valley has gained momentum, with the Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) exploring the possibility of setting up a temporary facility within a month while efforts continue to secure land and clearances for a permanent market.APMC Chairman Sanjeev Guleria visited Tikkan in Damchyan panchayat on Wednesday and inspected two potential sites for the proposed market. During the visit, two to three local landowners expressed willingness to offer around two to three bighas of private land for setting up a temporary facility.Guleria, accompanied by APMC officials and local representatives, held discussions with residents to explore ways to expedite the project and provide immediate relief to farmers and horticulturists of the region.The vegetable market project has been pending for several years. Its foundation stone was laid in 2017, after which the process to transfer around 10 bighas of forest land for the project and obtain the necessary approvals was initiated. However, the project hit a roadblock in 2024 after around 20 objections were raised at the departmental level, delaying the land transfer formalities.The issue was recently taken up with the APMC chairman by Mandi Press Club president Subhash Thakur, who has been highlighting the problems faced by farmers and horticulturists in Chauhar Valley.Guleria said the committee's priority was to facilitate the transfer of the proposed 10 bighas of forest land in the APMC's name and obtain the necessary clearance from the Forest Department for constructing a permanent, modern vegetable market.In the meantime, private land could provide an interim solution. During a meeting with local residents, revenue officials and panchayat representatives, Guleria urged landowners to complete the necessary formalities, including preparation of land records and passage of a panchayat resolution.He said the APMC was committed to ensuring that the market was established during the tenure of the Congress government led by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Assuring that funds would not be a constraint, he said work on the temporary facility could begin within a month once the land-related formalities were completed.The move is aimed at making the facility operational before the upcoming agricultural season.The proposed market is expected to provide growers in Chauhar Valley with better access to buyers, reduce transportation-related difficulties and help them secure better prices for their cash crops.Subhash Thakur expressed hope that the renewed efforts would finally translate into the establishment of the long-awaited market.APMC Executive Secretary Bhupender Thakur, District Superintendent Hari Singh Thakur, panchayat representatives, former elected members and several local residents were also present during the visit.

headline: Could a humans-only policy become a competitive edge for companies in the AI age?
content: When Mukesh and Anil Ambani were together in launching Reliance Telecom, one brother wanted every customer interaction to be tech-driven (interactive voice response) and the other wanted every call to be attended to by a human. The management sought our advice and we (Patty Seybold and I) were against the first. History showed us how it ended.

headline: Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to ponder question of protection for scribes
content: New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Thursday said it will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited media persons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that journalistic freedom has to be balanced with the administration of public order and law.The top court relegated to the high-powered committee headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy to examine pleas over the alleged detention of seven journalists, assault, and obstruction of journalists covering protests in Delhi on 10 and 11 October 2026.It asked the petitioners to submit material before the five-member committee."You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there. If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force."Whether they were subjected to force and, if subjected, whether such force was excessive in relation to the proportion necessary for maintenance of public order," Justice Bagchi observed.Self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists, he then added.The Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists, in their plea, submitted that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting sites, prevented from recording events, and subjected to physical force.According to the plea, accredited journalists documenting the protests were restrained, dragged away, manhandled and detained despite displaying their press credentials.Senior advocate PV Dinesh said seven journalists working with established organisations, not reel-makers, were taken into custody."The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" the lawyer submitted.The Delhi Police earlier told the top court that social media "reel-makers" and influencers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests.In an affidavit, the city police submitted that journalists "constitute a distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain, arguing that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections afforded to the press while covering protests.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Delhi Congress protests against SIR 'irregularities', demands protection of voting rights
content: The Delhi Congress on Thursday stepped up its campaign against alleged irregularities in the ongoing SIR of electoral rolls, with party leaders and workers taking to the streets on Constitution Day to demand protection of voting rights.The march began at around 12.15 pm from Chandgi Ram Akhara, opposite the Trauma Centre in Civil Lines, with participants carrying placards and posters, and raising slogans against the BJP and the Election Commission.Led by Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav, it is planned to culminate at the Dr Ambedkar National Memorial.Also Read I 331k Form 6 applications filed as Delhi SIR claims phase ends Congress alleges exclusion of genuine votersThe protest comes amid allegations by the Congress that genuine voters were being excluded from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, with Yadav accusing the BJP and the Election Commission of attempting to deprive people of their voting rights."Deleting the names of living voters by showing them as dead is anti-democratic and a direct assault on the voting rights of the people," Yadav said.He further said the SIR exercise raised serious concerns over the exclusion of genuine voters from electoral rolls, with 47.56 lakh names missing from Delhi's draft roll. He demanded transparency in the deletion process and sought details of voters removed on account of death, migration or other reasons. Protesters said that the exercise could disproportionately affect tenants, migrant workers and residents of unauthorised colonies and slum clusters, many of whom could face difficulties in establishing their eligibility because of documentation requirements.The Congress earlier cited the case of Nehru Vihar ward in the Mustafabad assembly constituency, where it alleged that 75 living voters were declared dead through Form 7 applications.‘Officials should do their job honestly’Protesters demanded an impartial probe into the alleged irregularities, special hearings for affected voters and action against officials found responsible for wrongful deletions.Several party workers also questioned the requirement for voters to produce birth certificates to establish their eligibility, saying the process could disadvantage people born in Delhi's villages who may not possess such documents."Governments will come and go, but officials should do their job honestly," Yadav said, urging electoral officials to work impartially and without political pressure.Also Read I Deleted voters’ appeals to get priority, Supreme Court tells Bengal SIR tribunalsThe march is also aimed at supporting Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's campaign against alleged vote theft.AICC general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal, treasurer Ajay Maken, Delhi Congress in-charge Qazi Nizamuddin and co-in-charge Danish Abrar were among the leaders participating in the march.AICC observers and Congress Working Committee members N Raghuveera Reddy, Rudra Raju and Akhilesh Prasad Singh were also present.

headline: 'Are we your servants?' Congress MP Imran Masood continues tirade against ally SP over seat-sharing
content: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Thursday questioned ally Samajwadi Party's approach to seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying there was little meaning in holding alliance talks if SP went ahead and announced candidates before finalising the arrangement.His remarks came a day after the Akhilesh Yadav-led party announced five candidates while discussions over seat-sharing with the Congress were still under way."It is no alliance if one partner 'leaves' seats for the other after announcing its candidates," Masood said, questioning whether the two parties were being treated as equal partners. He also asserted that he would remain with the Congress and said his party was not there to do the SP's bidding."What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us? We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.Masood, who was part of the seat-sharing discussions, said the exercise made little sense if the SP was going to announce its candidates unilaterally. He declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, scheduled to be released later in the day, saying the functioning of an alliance should involve joint announcements and press conferences."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.The Congress MP from Saharanpur also recalled that his party had contested 107 seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, adding, "Now, he is yet to become the chief minister."Separately, Masood criticised the denial of permission for the Congress's Samvidhaan Raksha March, questioning the authorities' decision."What can I say? The Constitution that gives you power is the same Constitution that you want to trample upon," he said.Asked why permission was granted to a conference organised by AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi and Bhim Army chief Chandra Shekhar Azad, he said, "That is precisely the irony. This is the game, and people should understand it… People can draw their own conclusions."Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has continued to express his displeasure with INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing arrangements for poll-bound UP.Masood stepped up his criticism after the Akhilesh's party announced its first list of candidates.Questioning the SP's decision to offer the Congress only 26 "winnable" seats, Masood asked earlier, "Are we beggars?" and objected to the ally's "unilateral" approach to the negotiations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Call for detailed report on L&O, woman collector harassment from CM, DMK urges Guv
content: Chennai, The Opposition DMK on Thursday urged Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to invoke his constitutional powers under Article 167 of the Constitution and seek a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on the law and order situation in the state since June 2026, and the action taken thereon.Also, the Dravidian major sought the Governor to demand an explanation from the state government as to why the complaint submitted on July 31, 2026, concerning the alleged sexual harassment of a woman district Collector by a ruling-party MLA was referred to the ruling party's leadership instead of being forwarded to the police or placed before an Internal Committee.It also demanded that the Kallakurichi legislator C Arul Vignesh be arrested, and also to safeguard all digital evidence and transfer the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation for an independent and time-bound investigation. In a significant constitutional move, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin formally urged the Governor to invoke his powers under Article 167 of the Constitution to compel the chief minister to submit a comprehensive report on the state's law and order situation over the past six months.According to the representation submitted during his meeting with the Governor at Lok Bhavan here on Thursday, the DMK leader specifically asked the Governor to direct the chief minister to account for every major incident cited by the Opposition since July, as well as furnish comparative data on narcotics cases registered by the Tamil Nadu Police since May 2026 against seizures made by central agencies.In the petition, the DMK leader accused the state machinery of failing to act against ruling-party legislators and functionaries, raising grave concerns over the safety of civil servants and ordinary citizens. He urged the Governor to discharge his constitutional responsibilities and keep the Union Government informed if the state fails to take corrective action.A primary focus of the representation is the alleged sexual harassment of a woman District Collector by ruling-party MLA Arul Vignesh.Udhayanidhi pointed out that despite the officer submitting a formal complaint to the Chief Secretary on July 31, 2026, no action was taken for nearly four months, and an FIR was registered only after the matter reached the High Court.He also flagged the Law Minister's public remarks characterising the incident as a "personal matter".Also, he sought action over the alleged assault by the Deputy Speaker on a citizen who approached him with a petition for drinking water and civic amenities in Thuraiyur, followed by allegations that the Samayapuram Police Inspector coerced the victim into recording a video retracting his complaint.Noting that at least nine reported deaths involving police detention or judicial custody occurred, he expressed concern over the rising cases of missing children, crimes against women and children, and specific allegations involving ruling-party functionaries in Ayanavaram, Karamadai, and Alandur.Major drug busts by central agencies including 137 kg of methamphetamine in Nagapattinam and 71.24 kg of heroin in Chennai and the reported arrests of ruling-party functionaries in narcotics cases, action against officials, advising the government to register an FIR naming the Deputy Speaker and others in the assault case, and order an independent inquiry into the Samayapuram Police Inspector's alleged coercion of the victim besides recommending the Enforcement Directorate to register money laundering cases under the PMLA regarding the Nagapattinam and Madhavaram seizures to attach proceeds of crime were among the other demands.The DMK leader also sought a coordinated probe by the DRI, NCB, and NIA to investigate financiers, maritime routes, and any protection offered by elected representatives or officials.The Governor should advise the state to establish a dedicated cell with a statewide alert mechanism for missing children, report all custodial deaths to the NHRC within 24 hours with mandatory magisterial inquiries and videographed post-mortems, and operationalise the State Security Commission and Police Complaints Authority in line with Supreme Court directives, he stressed.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: LOC issued against CJP's Saurav Das, discrepancies in passport: Centre tells Delhi HC
content: New Delhi, The Centre on Thursday informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular has been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das, who was stopped at the airport from travelling to the United Kingdom.The submission was made before Justice Amit Mahajan, who issued notice and sought a response from the Centre on Das's plea challenging the government's move to stop him from travelling.The court listed the matter for further hearing on December 9.Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, representing Das, submitted that he was not made aware of any Look Out Circular , the reason for its issuance or its purpose.He sought a copy of the LOC. However, the Centre's counsel said it cannot be furnished to him.The court was hearing a plea by Das, who was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University, where he was slated to speak on the "cockroach movement".Das has alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London on the night of November 23.During the hearing, the Centre's counsel said a request was made by the Maharashtra Police to open an LOC against Das, and it was issued on the intervening night of November 22-23.Now, Das has to challenge the LOC before an appropriate forum, he said.Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma and standing counsel Ashish Dixit, representing the Centre, said a show-cause notice was also issued to Das on November 23, and he is yet to respond to it.The law officer said there are multiple objections to the maintainability of the petition, its premise, and the factual and legal aspects of the petition.He said Das has only been advised not to travel and the advisory was "in his favour". The ASG was referring to the show-cause notice, which asks Das not to travel due to an ongoing inquiry linked to alleged discrepancies in his passport.Sharma said there were certain discrepancies in the details given in his passport and on August 20, an inquiry was initiated in Puducherry to ascertain the veracity of his place of birth, address and parentage because he has left the column of father blank.He further submitted that the Bureau of Immigration is only the executing agency, and it cannot form a judgment on its own."There is no order today which either invalidates the passport, suspends the passport. It is only a show-cause notice he has to reply," the ASG said.He said Das had to respond to the notice on November 24, but he chose to first file a petition in the high court, and now he has to respond on November 30.The Centre's counsel contended that the alleged discrepancies highlighted in the passport may have a bearing on Das' citizenship.He also said, assuming that the passport officer concludes that Das's explanation is inadequate, he will be stuck in a no-man's land, and thus the advisory issued to him is in his favour.The ASG also informed the court that the Madras High Court on October 30 issued notice on a plea seeking inquiry into the antecedents of Das.Sibal said that the pendency of a show-cause notice does not mean that Das will be stopped from travelling, which is a fundamental right.He submitted that the show-cause notice states that inputs were received that Das's place of birth was incorrect and the passport was obtained by suppressing material facts, thus requiring clarification along with supporting documents, failing which his passport may be suspended or impounded.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: India steps up push to take higher education global; 21 foreign universities now operational in country
content: Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi on Wednesday chaired the first meeting of the Consultative Committee of the Parliament for the Ministry of Education for 2026.Union Minister of State for Education, Jayant Chaudhary; Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Deepti Gaur Mukerjee; Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, T. K. Anil Kumar and other senior officials from the Ministry attended the meeting.Addressing the meeting, Pralhad Joshi said that the Indian Knowledge System had a long history of global impact. The objective of the Ministry was to further expand the global footprint of this system.With this aim, he stated that several steps were being taken to set up campuses of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) overseas and also facilitate the setting up of campuses of foreign universities in India.The Minister informed that around 21 foreign HEIs were currently operational in the country, in addition to joint academic and research collaborations.He added that the demand for CBSE schools abroad demonstrated the credibility of Indian education programmes and their potential for scalability at the global level.The Members of the Parliament were briefed on the various initiatives undertaken by both the Departments of the Ministry as part of the internationalisation of Indian education.The Department of Higher Education outlined the four strategies adopted to promote internationalisation - academic and research collaborations; attracting international students to study in India; allowing Foreign HEIs (FHEIs) to set up branch campuses in India; and allowing Indian HEIs to set up campuses abroad. 17 Letters of Intent were issued to Foreign Universities, under UGC Regulations, including those from the UK, the USA, Australia and Italy.The Members were also briefed on initiatives including Bharat Innovates, SPARC (Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration), GIAN (Global Initiative of Academic Networks) and DASA (Direct Admission of Students Abroad) and the revamped Study in India (SII) portal.The Department of School Education and Literacy informed the Members that the National Education Policy 2020 and the aspiration of Viksit Bharat 2047 were guiding a transformative shift in the Indian education system.The alignment of the curriculum with global standards, multilingual education, exchange programmes for students and teachers and the PARAKH National Assessment Centre for academic equivalence and quality alignment were among the key factors driving internationalisation. 268 CBSE schools were functional across 26 countries and an overseas regional office was also established in Dubai.A standardised assessment framework had also been implemented across affiliated schools globally to ensure uniformity.The Members appreciated the efforts taken by the Departments in the direction of internationalisation and gave their suggestions on various matters, including vocational education and expanding the network of Indian educational institutions abroad. (with ANI inputs)Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Amitabh Bachchan's Jalsa named in threat email to Mumbai mayor, civic chief
content: The offices of Mumbai mayor Ritu Tawde and municipal commissioner Ashwini Bhide on Thursday received a fresh e-mail threatening bomb blasts and drone and grenade attacks all over the city, including actor Amitabh Bachhan’s bungalow Jalsa.The email was received at around 10.00 am. Written in Punjabi, Hindi and English, the e-mail allegedly threatened to blow up the Mayor's office at 1:11 pm on November 26 and the court at 3.00 pm.The email also threatened to carry out an attack on Jalsa with drones between November 27 and December 31. It also threatened singer Diljit Dosanjh who is scheduled to perform in Mumbai on Friday at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse.The senders of the email demanded an apology from the singer and told “Marathi brothers” to protect their children, cautioning attendees against picking up any iPhones lying on the ground at Dosanjh's November 27 show. It also threatened grenade attacks across Mumbai over the next 30 days unless Diljit's three-hour concert was stopped.The sender claimed bags containing Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) have been kept at various metro trains warning commuters to avoid the metro between November 27 and December 31.“The email also has pro-Khalistan slogans and references to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. At the bottom, the sender listed the names of two organizations—Khalistan National Army and Babbar Khalsa (Parmar-Canada),” said a police officer.The police said that such hoax emails have increased over the last few days, especially considering Diljit Dosanjh is performing on Friday at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse. The police teams have already increased security for his concert.

headline: Public confidence in judicial authority must be continuously earned through independence: CJI
content: New Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday said a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority, underlining that disagreement is not a weakness of a constitutional democracy.Addressing a Constitution Day function organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association at the apex court lawns, the CJI also said that the Constitution is not tested only during extraordinary political or institutional crises, but it is tested every day."It is tested every day, in the ordinary exercise of power. The manner in which an authority treats a vulnerable citizen, the willingness of an institution to acknowledge its limitations, and the readiness to correct an error are all expressions of constitutional commitment," the CJI said. The CJI said a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority."What matters is that such engagement must remain guided by reasons, professional integrity and respect for institutional processes," he said.As pointed out by Attorney General R Venkataramani, "it must not be motivated by political agendas or personal gains to attack the institution only because it does not suit you in a particular situation," he said.He said one often understands the Constitution through its provisions, institutions and distribution of powers."These are its essential foundations, but the Constitution must ultimately be judged by what it means to the people whom it governs," the CJI said.He said constitutional governance requires every institution to remain conscious not only of the authority it possesses, but also of the limits within which that authority must operate."Institutional restraint, mutual respect and accountability are therefore essential to the proper functioning of our constitutional democracy. Each institution must discharge its responsibilities with due regard for the constitutional space within which other institutions are expected to function," he said.The CJI said ultimately, the strength of the Constitution will be measured not simply by the institutions it establishes, but by the confidence it inspires in the citizen."Judicial authority is an essential feature of our constitutional system, but public confidence in that authority must be continuously earned through independence, fairness, and consistency. We must also recognise that disagreement is not a weakness of constitutional democracy," he said.While referring to the challenges facing the justice delivery system, the CJI said pendency, delays and unequal access to legal representation continue to affect the experience of the judiciary for many citizens."Behind every case number is a person awaiting the resolution of a dispute, the protection of a right, or the vindication of a claim. The responsibility for improving this situation is shared," he said.The CJI said courts must continue to strengthen their processes and make justice more accessible, and the Bar must contribute through focused and honest advocacy, responsible case management, and professional discipline.He said the true tribute to the framers lies not merely in remembering their work, it lies in carrying forward the constitutional responsibilities they entrusted to us."Citizens may not remember every judgment or be familiar with every constitutional provision, but they will remember whether they were heard, whether they were treated fairly, and whether the justice system stood by them when they needed it most. That ultimately is the measure of our constitutional commitment," he said."Let us continue to work towards a justice system that is independent in its functioning, accessible in its reach, and humane in its approach.The Constitution has given us the framework. Giving life to its promises remains our collective responsibility," the CJI said.Besides the CJI, the Attorney General, SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Kumar Rai and others also addressed the gathering.Referring to certain issues pointed out by the SCBA president, the CJI said he thinks that periodical training of members of the Bar is a very significant issue.The CJI said he can assure the Bar members that some structured training program will be introduced in a very short time.In his address, Venkataramani said it is one matter that we talk of improving administration of justice and ease of justice."It is an entirely different matter that we denigrate our justice institutions, our judges, and the supreme value of independence by mindlessly or deliberately challenging it," he said."The lawns of the Supreme Court where we have assembled are part of the court and meant to be valued to celebrate the Constitution, not to demean the court. This is not Hyde Park," Venkataramani said.He said any attempt to devalue the court on any assumed count or to malign the judges must be strongly discouraged and stopped."Let no partisan considerations assume self-importance of freedom. Seemingly being independent can invisibly impact the court's ability to be without fear or favour," he said.Constitution Day, also known as 'Samvidhan Divas', is celebrated in the country on November 26 every year to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India.PTI ABA ABA DVDVThis article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: BJP MP Tarun Chugh’s nephew’s wedding turns Gobindgarh Fort into Punjab’s political melting pot
content: The battle lines may soon be drawn for the Punjab Assembly elections, but at Gobindgarh Fort, politics took a back seat to wedding celebrations — and old rivalries gave way to familiar smiles.The wedding of BJP MP Tarun Chugh’s nephew turned into a political melting pot, bringing together leaders from the BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal under the historic fort’s roof. For one evening, electoral opponents were guests, not rivals.SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, BJP leader Sunil Jakhar, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia and Amritsar MP and senior Congress leader Gurjeet Singh Aujla, Congress district president Amritsar Saurabh Madaan were among the prominent faces at the gathering. Senior Congress leaders from Amritsar and Tarn Taran also joined the celebrations. Prominent leaders including Prem Singh Chandumajra, BJP Punjab president Kewal Dhillon, Manpreet Badal were present as well.Haryana CM Nayab Saini with MP Tarun Chugh at the wedding.Tarun Chugh and BJP former state chief Sunil Jakhar.BJP state president Kewal Dhillon (right) and BJP senior leader Rana Gurmit Singh Sodhi.But beyond the wedding festivities, the political optics were hard to miss. The gathering offered a glimpse of the old warmth returning between Akali and BJP leaders, whose political partnership had remained on ice for years. There were warm hugs, camera-friendly smiles and some off-the-camera discussions.With the election season approaching, the fort witnessed a different kind of alliance-building — no speeches, no slogans, just greetings, conversations and bonhomie.It was a reminder that in Punjab, where politics and personal relationships often share a long history, even a wedding guest list can become a talking point.

headline: One killed as coffee machine explodes ahead of AAP rally in Moga
content: Moga: A hospitality worker died on Thursday morning after a coffee-making machine exploded at the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) rally site in Punjab’s Moga district, officials said.The victim, yet to be identified by the authorities, was employed by a private contractor on hospitality duty at the venue.According to local reports, the machine’s compressor exploded near the media/VVIP marquee area before the leaders arrived, with flying debris fatally striking the worker and triggering panic at the site.Police cordoned off the spot and launched security checks and technical inspections across the venue as a precaution.Official confirmation of the blast’s cause is awaited.The incident occurred ahead of AAP’s Khushaal Punjab rally in Moga, scheduled to feature party national convener Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann as the party pushes its outreach ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.

headline: Sebi appoints auditor to probe Coffee Day Enterprises' fund diversion
content: Markets regulator Sebi has appointed a forensic auditor to assist in a probe into the affairs of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd, following directions from the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT).The SAT had on November 5 directed the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to conduct a fresh, independent and comprehensive investigation into the alleged diversion of ₹3,535 crore from seven subsidiaries of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd (CDEL) to Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates Ltd (MACEL), an entity linked to the company's promoters.Pursuant to the order dated November 5, 2026 passed by the appellate tribunal, CDEL, in a regulatory filing on Thursday, said "Sebi has, vide its letter dated November 25, 2026, informed the company that CLA Indus Value Consulting has been appointed as the forensic auditor to assist the investigating authority." The company said its board of directors would take further steps as may be necessary in the matter.On November 5, SAT set aside an order passed by Sebi's Whole Time Member (WTM) and directed the regulator to complete further investigation within six months and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.The SAT order came over an appeal filed by CDEL, challenging the order passed by Sebi, which imposed a penalty of ₹26 crore under Sections 15HA and 15HB of the Sebi Act, 1992, in connection with alleged securities law violations.In its order, SAT had said it would be "in the interest of justice" for Sebi to undertake an "independent and comprehensive" investigation into the scheme of diversion of funds from the CDEL group and its promoters.The tribunal also asked the regulator to determine the roles of various stakeholders and consider appropriate action, particularly with a view to "adequately restituting the public shareholders" of the company.As part of the investigation, the tribunal asked Sebi to consider recording statements on oath of concerned persons, including legal representatives of late V G Siddhartha, to ascertain the ultimate beneficiaries of the allegedly siphoned-off funds.Further, SAT asked Sebi to examine bank accounts of all concerned entities, including conduit entities and beneficiaries of funds transferred from the bank accounts of late Siddhartha, his wife and parents."Sebi is directed to carry out further investigation as early as possible and in any case within the upper limit of 6 months, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law," it said.SAT has asked Sebi for "recording statements on oath of the concerned persons, including legal representatives of (Late) VGS, to ascertain the ultimate beneficiaries of siphoned-off funds and examining on oath various officials of the CDEL and its subsidiaries and banks to verify how huge transactions to the tune of ₹3,535 crores did not generate an alert by the bank nor noted by officials whose mobile numbers were linked with the bank accounts...

headline: Punjab raises sugarcane price to ₹431 per quintal for 2026-27
content: Punjab has raised the sugarcane price to ₹431 per quintal for the 2026-27 crushing season, with Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann describing it as the highest rate in the country. The announcement, made after a high-level meeting on Wednesday, November 25, sets the price for growers supplying cane to mills across the state. Mann said the revised rate was intended to improve returns for cultivators and provide financial support to thousands of sugarcane-growing farmers. He also said sugar mills across Punjab would commence operations from November 25, 2026, allowing growers to bring their produce to mills from the start of the season. In a post on X, the chief minister said the government was committed to ensuring that farmers received the rightful value for their crops. He reiterated the position at the meeting, calling the increase a major initiative for sugarcane farmers. Price and farmer incomes The government has presented the ₹431 per quintal rate as the highest sugarcane price nationally. The announcement did not state the previous season’s price or quantify the increase over the earlier rate, so a year-on-year comparison is not available from the details released so far. Mann said farmers worked day and night to feed the country and strengthen its economy, and argued that the government had a responsibility to ensure their labour received its due value. He said farmer prosperity was essential to Punjab’s progress and economic well-being. “Farmers are the backbone of our economy, and their prosperity is essential for the overall progress and economic well-being of Punjab,” Mann said. He added that the state government was committed to safeguarding farmers’ interests, strengthening their financial position and ensuring remunerative prices. The revised price is expected by the government to provide financial relief to thousands of sugarcane cultivators. Mills begin operations Mann said sugar mills across Punjab would start functioning on November 25, 2026, so farmers could supply their cane in a timely and convenient manner. He said the move would support the rural economy and help secure a prosperous future for the farming community. The chief minister described remunerative prices for agricultural produce and assistance to farmers as key priorities. The announcement links the price decision with the start of the crushing season, although details on mill-wise schedules, procurement arrangements and payment timelines were not provided. For growers, the announced rate establishes the price at ₹431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season. The government’s claim that it is the country’s highest rate is based on its announcement; no comparative state-wise price data was included in the release.

headline: Firozpur Division Observes Constitution Day; Railway Officials Take Pledge
content: Firozpur Division Observes Constitution Day; Railway Officials Take Pledge Ferozepur, November 26: Constitution Day was observed at the Divisional Railway Manager’s Office, Firozpur, on Wednesday, with railway officials and employees collectively reading the Preamble to the Constitution and pledging their commitment to its principles under the leadership of Divisional Railway Manager Sanjeev Kumar. The collective reading of the Preamble was also organised at railway stations across the division. On the occasion, passengers and railway employees were sensitised about constitutional values through awareness activities at stations and offices. Among those present were Additional Divisional Railway Manager Nitin Garg, Chief Medical Superintendent Dr Ranjana Sehgal, Senior Divisional Security Commissioner Rishi Pandey, Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Paramdeep Singh Saini, Divisional Personnel Officer Vijender Kumar and other senior officials and railway employees.

headline: 'Politics could not change us, we changed politics': Arvind Kejriwal on AAP foundation day
content: New Delhi: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday said his party had “changed politics” in the country, as it marked its foundation day..Listing the party’s achievements, including forming governments in Delhi and Punjab, Kejriwal said that despite doubts being raised about its political future, AAP had persevered and earned people’s trust..“In a very short time, we have come a long way. When the party was formed, many questions were raised about us. Would we be able to achieve anything? How long would this party last? What do these people know about politics, anyway?” Kejriwal said in a post on X in Hindi..“But we not only endured, we also won the hearts of the entire country. We formed a government in Delhi, we formed a government in Punjab, and from Jammu and Kashmir to Goa and Gujarat, we earned the trust and love of the people of India,” he added..Arvind Kejriwal slams BJP-SAD alliance for Punjab elections, says AAP's ties are with state's people.“We focused on getting things done and talked about education and healthcare. Politics could not change us; instead, we changed politics,” he said..The former Delhi chief minister said a lot remained to be done for the country and asserted that the party would neither be afraid nor back down..AAP celebrates its foundation day on November 26, marking its formation in 2012.

headline: Punjab farmers are selling paddy stubble to biomass firms, reducing burning
content: New Delhi: For years, 60-year-old farmer Rajinder Singh burned his paddy stubble after the harvest, one of thousands of fires across India’s Punjab state each autumn. Now, his crop waste is trucked to a biomass plant, generating power and village incomes instead of smoke. The shift offers a potential solution to stubble burning, which has persisted despite years of government efforts to stamp it out. Such fires have contributed to the toxic smog that blankets the capital Delhi and much of northern India each winter, making it one of the most polluted areas in the world. “Our earnings have improved considerably through this work,” Singh said, speaking in his Sedha Singh Wala village in Punjab. “Earlier we used to burn the stubble. Now many families are getting employment from it.” More Punjab farmers are finding that straw once treated as waste can generate income, reducing the incentive to burn it. Punjab recorded 5,114 farm fires during the 2025 paddy-harvesting season, down 53% from 2024 and 86% from 2023, according to government estimates. But the dramatic fall has yet to translate into noticeably cleaner air in Delhi. The capital’s air quality again reached hazardous levels in mid-November this year, underscoring both the multiple sources of its pollution and the limited scale of the biomass industry.

headline: ₹125 coin to commemorate artist Sobha Singh’s 125th birth anniversary
content: Dharamshala: The Union government has notified the issuance of a ₹125 commemorative coin to mark the 125th birth anniversary of noted painter Sobha Singh, following a gazette notification issued on November 25.The Sobha Singh Memorial Art Society (SSMAS) said the coin makes Sobha Singh the first Indian painter to be honoured with a commemorative coin, calling it a milestone for Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, and the wider art community.Born on November 29, 1901, at Shri Hargobindpur in Punjab, Sobha Singh served as a draughtsman in the British Indian Army in Iraq and ran studios in Amritsar, Lahore, and Delhi before settling in Andretta near Palampur in Himachal Pradesh’s Kangra Valley after the Partition in 1947. His portraits of Sikh Gurus, historical figures, and Himalayan subjects put the quiet hamlet on the cultural map, and he was earlier honoured with a commemorative postage stamp on his birth centenary in 2001.The coin will be released during year-long celebrations running from November 2026 to November 2027 under the theme Janambhoomi Se Karmabhoomi Tak, tracing his journey from his birthplace in Punjab to his studio base in Andretta.SSMAS secretary general Hirday Paul Singh, who is also the artist’s grandson, thanked the Union government, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, and culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, along with public representatives and supporters for backing the push. He said the coin will keep Sobha Singh’s humanist message and art before younger generations and international audiences.

headline: Jakhar targets Kejriwal, asks if the Constitution licenses ‘all tricks’ to win elections
content: Senior Punjab BJP leader and former state chief Sunil Jakhar today attacked Aam Aadmi Party national convener Arvind Kejriwal and asked if the Constitution licensed the deployment of all tricks to win elections."Today, as Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia celebrate Constitution Day, can they tell us where the Constitution says that to win elections, one is allowed to resort to conciliation, bribery, punishment, sowing discord, fighting, and lying?" asked Jakhar, who is in Delhi today.Jakhar questioned that now that Kejriwal and Sisodia were in Moga, would they also bring into the party that alleged supporter of the Khalistan Commando Force at whose home Kejriwal stayed in 2017."Will they also add him to that ‘army’ of gangsters and criminals they have already recruited in the party to spread chaos and unrest in Punjab? The people of Punjab see and suffer the consequences of this every day in the gunfire on their streets. As Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia celebrate Constitution Day today, can they point to where the Constitution allows to resort to all tricks of the trade to register poll victories?" he asked.Jakhar added that he would expose AAP and AAP government misdeeds as chairman of the BJP charge sheet committee that will highlight the "lapses under the ruling government."

headline: PNB 680-day FD rates: Calculate returns on ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh for regular and senior citizen investors in India
content: Punjab National Bank (PNB) is offering a special 680-day fixed deposit (FD) with interest rates of up to 7.65% per annum. The scheme has separate rates for regular and senior citizen investors, making it an option for those seeking fixed returns over a tenure of less than two years. But how much can an investor earn by putting ₹5 lakh or ₹10 lakh in this special FD? What are the rules, and how can it be booked? Here is a breakdown of the rates and estimated returns across customer categories. PNB offers regular customers 6.90% per annum on this scheme. Senior citizens get an additional 0.50%, while super senior citizens get a higher rate of 7.65%. The 680-day tenure works out to about 1 year, 10 months and 10 days, offering an alternative to conventional 1-year and 2-year FDs and more flexibility in choosing a tenure. Returns on this FD depend on the amount invested, the investor's category and the applicable interest rate. Below is an illustrative calculation, using quarterly compounding, of the interest earned on deposits of ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh over 680 days. These figures are indicative estimates based on a 680/365-year period and quarterly compounding. Actual maturity proceeds may vary depending on PNB's calculations and terms and conditions. Taxation and tax deducted at source (TDS) may also affect post-tax returns.

headline: SAD-BJP reunion signals retreat from BJP’s Punjab ambitions
content: NEWS ANALYSIS While return of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) may reassure the Bharatiya Janata Party, for the oldest ally is back in the fold, the occasion arrives on an ominous note: the BJP’s bid to dominate Punjab politics has vanished four months ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election. On Tuesday, Union Minister for Home Affairs Amit Shah shared a dais at the BJP headquarters to welcome Sukhbir Singh Badal, former Punjab Chief Minister and the SAD supremo, back into the NDA. Shah showed no hesitation in declaring that the SAD will be in the role of a “bade bhai” (big brother). Ironically, Badal had said they are “judwa bhai” (twin brothers) in response to a reporter’s question on who will be the lead partner for the Punjab polls. But Shah declared the SAD the big brother in the alliance. To leave no room for ambiguity, Shah also said on the question of who will be the Chief Minister if the alliance were to win the polls: “I’ve already said in Hindi. Bade bhai means the CM will be from the SAD only.” The BJP, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah at the helm of the party’s affairs, keeps symbolism high. The SAD returned on the day when Punjab and elsewhere Sikhs celebrated Guru Nanak Jayanti. Modi had earlier sported the traditional Punjabi headscarf, as he attended Shabad Kirtan at the Lok Bhavan in Delhi, organised by the city’s Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu. The SAD founder and former Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal had famously described ties with the BJP as “nau maas ka rishta” (nine-month bond). He had summed up BJP-SAD relations in an apparent emotional phrasing: a bond of blood and flesh. The BJP-SAD relations had ruptured when the Modi-led dispensation rushed with three contentious farm laws. Fresh with a mammoth majority win in the Lok Sabha in the 2019 general elections, the Modi government seemed sanguine to ideas circulating in the NITI Aayog of central legislations to open up the agriculture sector. Having won 303 Lok Sabha seats, the BJP approached Parliament with a newfound josh. Time to make big changes had arrived, the party seemed to suggest. In August 2019, Shah had shown that Article 370 could simply be abrogated with the passage of a Bill in Parliament. Next year, in 2020, the Modi-led government took the Presidential Ordinance route to unveil the three contentious farm laws. The urgency was such that the government didn’t even wait for the Monsoon session of Parliament in September. For at least three years leading to the promulgation of three contentious farm laws, Ramesh Chand, NITI Aayog Member (Agriculture), argued at any occasion that came his way that agriculture in India is deprived of high growth opportunity because States are not reforming mandis and not freeing land for ease of farming with suitable laws. On his watch, the NITI Aayog had come out with model Bills to reform agricultural mandis and also for contract farming—The State/UT Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2017, and a similar draft for contract farming, Model Contract Farming, in 2018. Chand travelled across the country to push the case for the States to adopt the model Bills. Within two years, he started sounding frustrated, as the States’ response didn’t match his josh. Even the BJP-ruled States dragged on committing to the ideas floated by Chand and the NITI Aayog. Chand began saying that India’s agriculture faced roadblocks because States were not pushing with reforms. But Chand carried weight within the Modi-led dispensation. His long tenure as a member of the NITI Aayog, over a decade, shows his proximity to the Prime Minister. Besides, he was a regular in meetings held by Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS) sympathiser groups. Harsimrat’s warning and farmers’ protest In the end, the Prime Minister decided for Central laws to adopt the ideas argued by Chand and the NITI Aayog. Three contentious farm laws first came out as Presidential Ordinances, and when legislative proposals were brought before Parliament, then Union Minister and SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal erupted in anger and anguish. She pleaded with the government to withdraw the Bills. Her speech amid the din in the Lok Sabha almost sounded hysterical, as she warned the government of backlashes. The government ignored her warnings. The SAD quit the NDA government at the Centre and also left the NDA in September 2020. The BJP-SAD relations showcased as brotherly Hindu and Sikh ties broke down. Soon, the Modi government understood the import of Harsimrat Kaur Badal’s warning, as farmers from Punjab launched an intense agitation. A year later, Modi realised the political cost of sticking to those farm laws, and appeared on DD News to announce their withdrawal. In 2022, the BJP contested on 73 Assembly seats. It won two seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP score chart read zero in Punjab. After the 2022 poor show, the BJP embarked on a journey to infuse flesh and blood into the party’s skeleton in Punjab by wholesome imports from the Congress. First, the BJP brought Captain Amarinder Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister. Afterwards, Sunil Jakhar also joined the saffron tent. In between the two prominent faces, the BJP showcased a large number of Sikh leaders joining the party at the national headquarters. https://frontline.thehindu.com/politics/punjab-congress-revival-assembly-election/article71733987.ece Shah held regular strategy meetings at his residence. Punjab was marked as a State where the BJP’s domination must be established. Punjab had defied Brand Modi. In Ferozepur in 2022, Modi had faced his most embarrassing moments when his cavalcade was stuck on a flyover as farmers blocked the pathway. He spent almost 15 minutes on the flyover. The Prime Minister abruptly returned to New Delhi without visiting Hussainiwala. He also didn’t attend functions organised for laying foundation stones for development projects in Ferozepur. Dominating Punjab politics for the BJP would, thus, have come as a balm to those embarrassing moments for the Prime Minister. Punjab is among those few States where Modi has gone the least as the Prime Minister of the country. Shah, as the political sherpa of Modi, had seemingly taken the task to win the Punjab turf for the BJP. Tarun Chugh, BJP leader from Amritsar in Punjab, emerged as Shah’s key aide. Chugh apparently embarked on engineering defections from the ranks of the Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab. The Congress imports into the BJP were not enough for the party to dominate Punjab politics. https://frontline.thehindu.com/politics/arvind-kejriwal-aap-punjab-crisis-india-bloc-political-future/article71665824.ece In April this year, seven Rajya Sabha MPs of the AAP joined the BJP. The saffron sentiment soared, for AAP’s former Punjab in-charge Raghav Chadha was now in the BJP. More importantly, the BJP seemed to have sensed that the party had grabbed the key to Punjab politics as Sandeep Pathak was part of the flock that joined the saffron outfit. For the AAP, the loss of Pathak was more painful than that of Chadha. Pathak had been AAP’s chief organisational strategist in Punjab. He knew AAP workers in Punjab by their names. The buzz in the BJP grew afterwards that the party alone is in a position to win Punjab Assembly elections. Arguments came in plenty: the AAP is facing major anti-incumbency, the infighting within the Congress is insurmountable, and many more. Believing that the BJP actually can write the script of Punjab politics, the BJP even sought to send a subtle message to the people in Punjab: the party has a Sikh face for the CM post. In July this year, Union Minister of State Ravneet Singh Bittu resigned from the government. He was sent to Punjab for full-time focus. Bittu, an import from the Congress, also carries legacy of late Beant Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister who was killed by terrorists. Bittu hit the deck hard. With Chugh, he began touring the length and breadth of the State. Together, they picked up the issue of drug abuse as the poll pivot. The issue is close to the heart of Chugh, who believes that it can pull away women and elder voters to the BJP from the AAP. A number of yatras were undertaken. The BJP leaders began noting that the strategy and their outcomes are not shifting from the paper to the ground. The yatras were taken, but the people were mostly onlookers. The AAP imports into the BJP failed to show their earlier skills in rallying the people to their new party. In the summer of this year, the BJP leaders argued that an alliance with the SAD will undo all the hard work done by the party so far. “The SAD is discredited in Punjab politics. The people associate this party with every menace in the State. The rise of the AAP in Punjab is solely because of the abject failure of the SAD in governance. An alliance with the SAD will automatically transfer the legacy of governance failure to the BJP,” a key BJP strategist engaged in Punjab works said. A few months later, the BJP leaders began sensing that an alliance with SAD is a necessity because the Jat Sikh in rural Punjab is refusing all outreach of the party. The agrarian Jat Sikh hasn’t yet forgotten those contentious farm laws. They have also not forgotten months spent at the Haryana border, where labels and insinuations were thrown at them as they held out for protests against the farm laws. Sooner, the buzz in the BJP spoke of a tactical alliance with the SAD: “The BJP will focus on 57 Assembly seats and leave rest for the SAD as a part of a tactical adjustment without a formal alliance.” Punjab has a total of 117 seats in the Assembly. The past two months have brought sombre notes to the BJP. The rural parts of the country, particularly in the western parts, are turning restive. In Gujarat, farmers held months-long agitation. In Maharashtra, farmers are regularly hitting the street. In Rajasthan, the BJP just suffered a major defeat in the Panchayat elections without a parallel for three decades. Punjab farmers already have an old battle to settle with the BJP: the pain and suffering on account of the contentious farm laws. The SAD in 2022 had faced its worst defeat in Punjab elections. In 2024, Bathinda saved blushes for the SAD as Harsimrat Kaur Badal retained the family bastion. The writing on the wall for the SAD also became clear that the 2027 Assembly elections’ key players are the AAP and the Congress. Joining hands with the BJP will help the SAD gain urban Hindu votes. But the BJP seems to have read the sign that the saffron season is waning and the party now needs more allies to meet the challenges. Manish Anand is a senior Delhi-based journalist, who for over two decades has covered the Indian politics for India’s leading English dailies. Strategic shift Strategic shift In a bid to win over the Sikh vote and Punjab single-handedly, the BJP is walking a tightrope, as it tries to condemn Operation Bluestar and soft-pedal Bhindranwale while still singing its signature tune of muscular nationalism.
