headline: BKU Doaba activists protest at Phagwara Sugar Mill over pending arrears
content: Activists of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU)/Doaba, began assembling at the main gate of Golden Sandhar Sugar Mill, Phagwara, on Thursday as part of their scheduled protest programme over the pending payment of sugarcane arrears.Around 20–25 BKU/Doaba activists have so far staged a sit-in protest near the mill’s main gate, demanding the clearance of outstanding sugarcane payments and fulfilment of other demands.The union’s major demands include the release of pending sugarcane arrears amounting to Rs. 28.74 crore for the 2021–22 season by Golden Sandhar Sugar Mill, Phagwara; payment of Rs. 18.93 crore by the Punjab Government towards the pending subsidy of Rs. 68.50 per quintal of sugarcane; and an increase in the sugarcane procurement price to Rs. 550 per quintal for the forthcoming 2026–27 season.Prominent BKU/Doaba leaders present at the protest included Kirpal Singh Mussapur, State Vice-President of the union; Gurpal Singh Pala, State Press Secretary; and Davinder Singh Sandhwa, District President, Nawanshahr.As of now, the protest has remained peaceful, with no blockade of National Highway-44 reported so far.

headline: Diversion of buses to Punjab Khushhaal Rally: High court refuses to pass interim order
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Thursday refused to pass interim order while hearing of a petition questioning Punjab Government’s legal authority to divert its buses from their designated routes to transport people to “Moga Maha Rally” or 'Punjab Khushhaal Rally'.The bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor while hearing the matter gave time to the petitioner to challenge the legality of the order by amending the petition.Yesterday, the state had produced an order dated November 24 issued by the Moga District Magistrate, vide which, the action has been taken.As the petitioner sought time to verify the document and respond, the matter was adjourned to November 26.In the petition, the petitioner sought directions to restrain the state from transporting supporters and workers of the ruling AAP to an event at Matwani village in Moga today. The petitioner alleged that the programme was a political event and sought directions to ensure that government buses were not diverted from regular public transport services at the cost of ordinary commuters.

headline: AAP’s Khushaal Punjab rally: Worker dies as coffee machine explodes at venue in Moga
content: A worker was killed after a coffee machine exploded at the venue of the Aam Aadmi Party’s state-level Khushaal Punjab rally in Moga on Thursday, triggering panic and chaos among those present.The incident took place at village Nathuwala Jadid on the Moga-Ludhiana national highway, where the rally was being held to mark the party’s foundation day under the leadership of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.According to information, the coffee machine was installed inside a marquee arranged for serving meals to mediapersons. It suddenly exploded, killing a worker deployed there.The explosion caused panic, with a large number of people rushing towards the spot.

headline: Punjab Khushaal Rally: Day after Kejriwal’s Ludhiana visit, AAP workers leave for Moga in large numbers
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers and leaders, in large numbers from Ludhiana, left for Moga today to participate in the party’s ‘Punjab Khushaal Rally’ to be addressed by national convener Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.Party leaders described the rally as an important political event and said workers from across Punjab were expected to attend.The mobilisation from Ludhiana assumed significance as Kejriwal and Mann had stayed in the city a day earlier and also met the family of Ludhiana West candidate Sanjeev Arora.Ashok Prashar Pappi, MLA, Central constituency, said the visit of the top leadership had infused fresh enthusiasm among the cadre and workers were eager to join the Moga rally in large numbers.He said that the Ludhiana unit was fully geared up for the programme.“Workers from Ludhiana have been leaving for Moga since morning. There is tremendous excitement among party supporters following the visit of Arvind Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann to Ludhiana,” added MLA Kulwant Singh Sidhu from Atam Nagar constituency.MLA (Ludhiana East) Daljit Singh Bhola Grewal said the rally would serve as an opportunity for workers from different districts to come together and strengthen the party’s grass-roots network.“The enthusiasm among workers is very high. The rally will showcase the support enjoyed by the AAP government among the people. Ludhiana workers are participating in large numbers and remain committed to carrying forward the party’s programmes and welfare initiatives,” Bhola said.With buses and private vehicles carrying supporters to Moga throughout the day, party leaders expressed confidence that the event would send a strong message of unity and public support for the party leadership.

headline: Punjab chemists threaten poll boycott over regulatory woes
content: Patiala: Punjab Chemists Association (PCA) on Wednesday said chemists would temporarily resume stocking and selling Pregabalin 75mg strictly against valid doctors’ prescriptions and patient identity verification, amid shortages affecting people requiring neurological and psychiatric medicines.The association also threatened a statewide boycott of upcoming elections by 34,000 chemists, their families, employees and dependants if Punjab health department failed to resolve their regulatory grievances.The decisions were taken at an emergency virtual meeting chaired by PCA state president Surinder Duggal and general secretary GS Chawla. Presidents, secretaries and executive members from all 23 districts participated. PCA is affiliated with All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists.Chemists had earlier returned stocks of neurological, psychotropic and antidepressant medicines to pharmaceutical companies, causing severe shortages for thousands of patients, office-bearers said.PCA accused the health department of failing to ensure availability of these medicines at govt hospitals and health centres. It said Pregabalin 75mg supplies would be temporarily restored following repeated requests from doctors and patients, particularly those with neurological disorders, diabetes and depression.The association alleged that authorities had not acted on repeated representations concerning six issues. These include failure to amend the existing drug policy, suspension of drug licences and sealing of shops over minor technical lapses, and inadequate action against restricted and banned medicines entering Punjab from neighbouring states.PCA also cited operational problems with Online National Drugs Licensing System (ONDLS), which Punjab has implemented for new licences. It demanded that glitches be removed before enforcement, saying several states had delayed its rollout.Other grievances include alleged delays by Punjab Pharmacy Council in renewing licences of pharmacists whose credentials had previously been renewed, failure to act against unauthorised online medicine sales and unwarranted police interference with chemists.The association will submit its demands to heads of political parties and urge them to include the grievances in their election manifestos. A statewide convention of chemists from all 23 districts will be held after 10 days to decide further action.Pregabalin, prescribed for neuropathic pain and other conditions, has faced regulatory and police scrutiny in Punjab amid alleged off-label abuse, particularly of 300mg capsules. Some district magistrates have imposed restrictions under Section 163 of BNSS on its stocking and sale without strict records. The issue of drug substance abuse witnessed a political turmoil in Punjab following broad day light murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh alias Jhota at chemist shop in Mansa.Fearing FIRs, shop closures and licence cancellations during police and health department raids, many chemists stopped stocking even 75mg capsules, affecting patients’ access. Punjab Assembly elections are scheduled for early 2027.

headline: Punjab farm fires 40% higher than last year; 2,184 FIRs registered
content: Bathinda: Punjab recorded 13 farm fire cases on Wednesday, taking the season’s tally to 7,159 — over 40% higher than the 5,114 cases reported during the corresponding period last year. Punjab’s share of the total cases across seven states has dropped to 39.2%, but it still has the lion’s share.The state has registered 2,184 FIRs, made 2,289 red entries in land records and initiated prosecution against 41 supervisory officers under Section 14 of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Act.Across seven states, 379 fresh cases took the cumulative count to 18,226, with Madhya Pradesh topping the chart with 231 new cases, taking its tally to 5,981 (33% of all cases). Uttar Pradesh followed with 105 cases (tally 2,613), Rajasthan with 20 (1,873), Haryana with eight (349) and Uttarakhand with two (244). Delhi has recorded seven cases.Four Punjab districts figure among the 10 worst-affected across these seven states — Ferozepur (918), Sangrur (810), Tarn Taran (711) and Bathinda (650). In penal action, 2,184 FIRs have been registered under Section 223 of BNS and red entries have been made in land records in 2,289 cases. An environmental compensation of over Rs 1.2 crore has been imposed, of which Rs 45 lakh has been recovered.Warning and showcause notices have been issued to 2,193 nodal and supervisory officers, while prosecution has been initiated against 41 of them. According to the Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modelling from Space (CREAMS), crop residue burning has been reported in 180 districts so far, including all 23 districts of Punjab.

headline: Tareekh pe tareekh, drugs sticks around as poll issue in Punjab
content: Chandigarh: In 2014, when Aam Aadmi Party found its foothold in Punjab, drugs became a major poll issue for the first time and worked against the Shiromani Akali Dal-BJP alliance govt. AAP leveraged the issue in a big way in the 2022 assembly election as well and set a deadline to end the drugs menace in Punjab.Ironically, ‘chitta’ has come full circle in 12 years.Announcing their alliance on Tuesday, BJP and SAD projected drugs as one of the biggest concerns for Punjab, tried to put AAP in the dock on the issue, and announced a deadline for ending the menace in Punjab.When the 2014 elections were over and AAP got its first four MPs from Punjab, the Parkash Singh Badal govt ordered a crackdown on drugs, leading to arrests in large numbers across the state.The 2016 Bollywood movie ‘Udta Punjab’ put the issue on the national centre stage and the state got an infamous tag that still sticks a decade later.SAD leaders had then said that the state was being defamed. Ahead of the 2017 polls, AAP aggressively used this issue and the tag in its campaigning. AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal had levelled serious allegations against then SAD minister Bikram Singh Majithia linking him to the narcotics trade but ended up tendering a written apology when Majithia sued him in a criminal defamation case.Drugs remained a major issue in subsequent elections. Four deadlines set by AAP, one before the 2022 polls and three later, to eradicate drugs in Punjab lapsed and the issue is back on the political centre stage.In the run-up to the 2022 polls, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal had given a deadline of six months for eliminating drugs in Punjab. In one TV interview, he even claimed he could eradicate drugs in three to four months.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann, while addressing the Independence Day function on Aug 15, 2023, at Patiala, announced that before next Aug 15, his govt would end the problem. During the 2024 Parliament elections, then Punjab minister and AAP’s candidate for Amritsar Lok Sabha seat, Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal, told people that Punjab CM had set the deadline of Dec 31, 2024, to make Punjab drug-free. And in the beginning of March 2025, CM gave another deadline of May 31, 2025, while launching a ‘war against drugs’.But ‘chitta’ never vanished from Punjab nor its political discourse. And it’s back on the poll platter.Addressing a rally at Jalandhar on Sept 30, Union home minister Amit Shah asked people of Punjab to give BJP ‘ek mauka’ (one chance) in the upcoming assembly election to make Punjab ‘chitta mukt’ (drug free) and announced a deadline of Dec 31, 2029, to achieve the target. He said that there were other important issues as well, but BJP would contest the election solely on the issue of making Punjab ‘chitta mukt’. He accused AAP of allowing open trading of drugs in Punjab.

headline: Amritsar: Ahead of  elections, BJP to focus on poll booths
content: The BJP on Wednesday stepped up its organisational preparations for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, focusing on strengthening its grassroots network.Addressing a meeting of party office-bearers at the BJP district office, Shaheed Harbans Lal Khanna Memorial, Punjab co-incharge Varinder Sachdeva projected the BJP-SAD alliance as a force for peace, security and development in the state.He said the NDA had united to secure a better future for Punjab and its people. The meeting, chaired by district president Salil Kapoor, focused on strengthening the party at the grassroots level and formulating election strategies.Sachdeva alleged that Punjab was passing through a difficult phase under the AAP government, with deteriorating law and order, drug abuse, extortion and gangsterism emerging as major concerns. He urged party workers to raise awareness about the Central government’s welfare schemes and strengthen the organisation at the booth level.The party also highlighted its public consultation campaign for the 2027 election manifesto launched on November 22.The party also highlighted its public consultation campaign for the 2027 election manifesto, launched on November 22. Residents can share their suggestions by calling 0797-194-3333, giving a missed call to 991-300-2027.

headline: A first: 4 Indian Army microlight aircraft land, take off from Amritsar-Jamnagar Economic Corridor
content: In a unique demonstration of civil-military coordination, four microlight aircraft of the Indian Army successfully landed and took off from a stretch of the Amritsar-Jamnagar Economic Corridor (NH-754A) in Gujarat, showcasing the potential of national highways to serve strategic and operational requirements of the Armed Forces, Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari said on Thursday.Gadkari shared a video of the take-off and landing of aircraft on his social media handle X.In his post he said the aircraft — belonging to the Indian Army's ‘Team Mountain Eagles’ and participating in the Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition — carried out the exercise between Chainage Km 946 and Km 949 of the economic corridor.Describing it as a historic demonstration of synergy between the Indian Army and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), the minister said the successful landing and take-off underscored the government's commitment to developing world-class highway infrastructure that caters not only to connectivity and economic growth, but also to the strategic and operational needs of the Armed Forces.In a historic demonstration of synergy between the Indian Army and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), 4️⃣ microlight aircraft of the Indian Army’s ‘Team Mountain Eagles’, participating in the Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition, successfully landed and took off from the Amritsar–Jamnagar Economic Corridor (NH-754A), between Chainage Km 946 and Km 949 in Gujarat.This remarkable feat underscores the commitment of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and NHAI to developing world-class highway infrastructure that strengthens connectivity, drives economic growth and meets the strategic and operational needs of our Armed Forces.It also highlights the potential of National Highways to facilitate aero-adventure, tourism and other emerging activities, wherever feasible, with appropriate safety measures and coordination.I congratulate the Indian Army’s ‘Team Mountain Eagles’, NHAI and all the concerned authorities for their exemplary coordination and successful execution of this historic endeavour.Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji, we remain committed to building a robust, resilient and future-ready National Highway network that goes beyond connectivity to serve the nation’s developmental, strategic and emergency-response needs.#PragatiKaHighway #AmritsarJamnagarEconomicCorridor#TeamMountainEagles— Nitin Gadkari (@nitin_gadkari) November 26, 2026As part of the Indian Army’s ongoing national flying expedition titled ‘Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition’, all four participating aircraft of the Army’s renowned aero-adventure team, ‘Team Mountain Eagles’—comprising two Fixed-Wing Microlights and two Flexible-Wing Powered Hang Gliders—executed precision landings and rapid ground refuelling on the designated highway stretch.Gadkari said the exercise also highlighted the potential of national highways to facilitate aero-adventure, tourism and other emerging activities, wherever feasible, subject to appropriate safety measures and coordination.Congratulating the Army's Team Mountain Eagles, NHAI and other agencies involved in the exercise, he lauded their coordination and successful execution of the endeavour.He said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government remained committed to building a robust, resilient and future-ready national highway network that goes beyond conventional connectivity to meet the country's developmental, strategic and emergency-response requirements.Working alongside Indian Army aviators, state police, and local district authorities, NHAI’s technical and incident management teams ensured that the selected stretch of NH-754A met all surface, geometric and safety requirements for light aircraft operations. NHAI field personnel managed corridor sanitisation, temporary traffic diversions and swift restoration of normal vehicular movement immediately after the drill, ensuring minimal inconvenience to highway commuters while Army ground support units carried out mobile refuelling and turnaround procedures, NHAI said.The successful touchdown of the expedition fleet—featuring the X-Air ‘Hanuman’ and Savannah MXP 740 Microlight aircraft alongside the Tanarg Bionix and Nuvix Skypper Powered Hang Gliders—demonstrated both the exceptional skill of Indian Army pilots and the world-class engineering standards of India’s modern National Highway network. Beyond accelerating regional connectivity and economic growth across Gujarat’s Kutch region, highways like NH-754K underscore the strategic versatility of national road infrastructure in supporting specialized aviation, emergency logistics, and national defence exercises.Organised by the Army Adventure Nodal Centre (AANC) (Microlight & PHG), Military College of Telecommunication Engineering (MCTE), Mhow, under the aegis of the Army Adventure Wing (AAW), DG IT, IHQ of MoD (Army), the ‘Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition’ was flagged off on 14 November and will conclude at Mhow on 28 November after traversing Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan.

headline: The show is on the road: How Punjab’s political parties are gearing up for elections
content: Chandigarh: For Punjab opposition parties that are yet to announce their door-to-door campaigners for next year’s polls, state roads and highways have turned into a political stage, with cycle rallies, roadshows, religious yatras and bus processions in full swing. While the Congress and BJP are already visible on the streets with their Jawani Sambhal Cycle Yatra and Samrasta Sankalp Yatra respectively, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) had planned a statewide bus yatra which was postponed in wake of the impending tie-up with the BJP (which was formally announced Tuesday). The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on the other hand is focusing on door-to-door campaigns and localised gatherings with candidates and ticket hopefuls. AAP has already announced candidates for 71 of Punjab’s 117 assembly constituencies. Tuesday’s announcement of the BJP-SAD alliance has added another dimension to these campaigns. With the two parties now set to contest the 2027 elections together after a six-year separation, the proposed statewide bus yatra is likely to be a combined affair. Beginning from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo, the bus campaign planned to cover all 117 assembly constituencies in three phases. The first phase was to run from 10 to 22 November, while subsequent phases were expected to begin from Sri Anandpur Sahib and Sri Akal Takht Sahib in Amritsar. “The objective is not necessarily to seek votes for individual candidates at this stage, but to ensure that the parties remain visible in political conversation, demonstrate organisational strength and build a perception of growing political momentum,” Dr Kanwalpreet Kaur, a political science professor at Chandigarh’s DAV College, told ThePrint. The Congress first launched the ‘Punjab Mangda Insaaf’ yatra on a bus on 4 November in the wake of Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Insaaf’ rally in Sangrur. But it was Congress’s Jawani Sambhal Cycle Yatra, led by former chief minister and Jalandhar MP Charanjit Singh Channi, that became the party’s most visible recent campaign. Launched from Chamkaur Sahib on 12 November in the presence of Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot, state president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, the first phase covered approximately 625 km across 27 constituencies before concluding at Khanna on 19 November. Around 2,000 bicycles were distributed for the campaign.

headline: HC seeks Punjab response on CBI probe into pharmacy exam cheating case
content: Bathinda: The Punjab and Haryana high court has asked the Punjab govt and the CBI to respond on transferring a probe into alleged cheating in the July 19 pharmacy officer examination conducted by Faridkot’s Baba Farid University of Health Sciences (BFUHS) for 454 posts to the central agency.Justice Sandeep Moudgil passed the order while hearing a petition by candidates alleging an inter-state cheating racket.The CBI’s counsel agreed to take over the probe, while Punjab’s counsel sought time to consult the state govt. The court, which had initially issued a notice to the CBI on Sept 24, listed the matter for Nov 30.On July 19, a total of 27 candidates were caught cheating while using high-tech Bluetooth-enabled gadgets in the examination. A number of candidates and opposition parties claimed it was a paper leak, but the state govt called it a cheating case busted by the police.Anil Mehta, the counsel for the petitioners, said, “We submitted that certain persons apprehended on July 19 were freed. They were nominated as accused at a later stage when the public raised a hue and cry. A status report filed by Punjab admitted that cheating has taken place with high-tech devices and 37 electronic devices seized and sent to Forensic Science Laboratory.”

headline: Farmers sell paddy stubble to biomass firms, cut farm fires in Punjab
content: For years, 60-year-old farmer Rajinder Singh burned his paddy stubble after the harvest, one of thousands of fires across India's Punjab state each ​autumn. Now, his crop waste is trucked to a biomass plant, generating power and ​village incomes instead of smoke.The shift offers a potential solution to stubble burning, which has persisted despite ‌years of government efforts to stamp it out. Such fires have contributed to the toxic smog that blankets the capital Delhi and much of northern India each winter, making it one of the most polluted areas in the world."Our earnings have improved considerably through this work," Singh said, speaking in his Sedha Singh Wala village in Punjab. "Earlier we used to burn the stubble. Now many families are getting employment from it."More Punjab farmers are finding that straw once treated as waste can generate income, reducing the incentive to burn it.Punjab recorded 5,114 farm fires during the 2025 paddy-harvesting season, down 53% from 2024 and 86% from 2023, according to government estimates.But the dramatic fall has yet to translate into noticeably cleaner air in Delhi. The capital's air quality again reached hazardous levels in ‌mid-November this year, underscoring both the multiple sources of its pollution and the limited scale of the biomass industry."Biomass-based projects are financially sound and genuinely effective," said Pratima Singh, a director at policy and research firm iFOREST."But right now they're operating at a fraction of the scale needed, so their impact isn't yet visible in Delhi's air."MORE INCOMES, JOBSIn Punjab's Faridkot district, a network of farmers, machinery operators and biomass power producers have emerged to collect paddy straw and turn it into fuel for electricity generation.Farmers and analysts say the business is also creating jobs, and boosting incomes, but ​government incentives are needed to expand it enough to make a meaningful dent.Amandeep Singh Gill, who processes paddy straw into feedstock ‌for power plants, provides work for tractor operators, drivers and labourers, providing livelihoods for as many as 70 families.The business requires substantial investment. Gill said his operation cost about 45 million rupees ($484,340) to set up and can ​generate annual turnover ‌of 70 million to 80 million rupees.The collected straw eventually reaches an 18-megawatt biomass power plant operated by SAEL Industries Ltd, ‌where agricultural waste is used to generate electricity.SAEL, the country's largest procurer of agricultural residue, is buying 2 million tonnes this year, a fraction of the roughly 750 million tonnes of agricultural waste generated in India each year.A ‌minimum support ​price for paddy ​straw and standardised procurement contracts could help expand the industry and meet the government's target of utilising 10 million tonnes of straw per year, iFOREST's Singh said.That, she said, could further reduce farm fires, ‌although a much larger expansion ​would be needed before the impact becomes visible in Delhi's air.

headline: Keeping it in the family | Male aspirants turn to wives as Chandigarh general wards become reserved for women
content: With 12 of the 35 wards in the municipal corporation (MC) reserved for women, sitting male councillors and ticket aspirants are turning to their wives to keep their political turf intact, as parties prepare to announce their candidates for the upcoming elections.The change in ward reservation, announced in September this year, has turned several previously general seats into women-reserved constituencies, triggering a fresh round of political hunt within families.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), which emerged as the single-largest party with 14 seats in the 2021 MC elections, has already announced candidates for 17 wards. Gurpreet Kaur Ladi, wife of sitting councillor Jasbir Singh Ladi, will contest from Ward 21, while Radhika Dhingra, wife of sitting councillor Yogesh Dhingra, has been fielded from Ward 25.Intense lobbying for tickets is underway in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which is expected to announce its candidates around November 28. Having managed to have its mayor in four of the five years of the previous MC term, the BJP is now in a majority in the outgoing House following defections from other parties over the five year term.Sitting BJP councillor Harjeet Singh, who represents Ward 8, comprising Mauli Jagran, Raipur Kalan, Makha Majra and Raipur Khurd, is eyeing a ticket for his wife, as the ward has now been reserved for women (general category).Similarly, in Ward 17, comprising Sectors 22 and 23, the BJP is likely to field the wife of Pankaj, owner of Nukkar Dhaba. The ward has also been reserved for women (general category). There are also reports that former BJP mayor and MC’s richest councillor in previous term, businessman Anup Gupta’s mother can also be fielded by the party from ward 17.The sitting Congress councillor from this ward, Damanpreet Singh is also eyeing a ticket for his wife. “I have worked for the overall development of ward 17 for the last five years and I am seeking a second term from here for my wife as this is now a woman ward. We serve as a family, so it doesn’t matter whether I am contesting or my wife as both work together,” said Damanpreet.In Ward 2, covering Sectors 1 to 10, the BJP is keen on fielding the wife of sitting councillor Maheshinder Singh Sidhu. Sidhu has been elected twice from here.Sitting Congress councillor Taruna Mehta, wife of Congress leader Yadwinder Singh, is likely to be considered for renomination from Ward 18. Yadwinder Singh had switched from the AAP to the Congress in 2023. The ward has now been declared a general ward.

headline: Chandigarh: ED raids SAD leader’s premises in money laundering case
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Wednesday searched the premises of a Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader based in Mohali as part of a money laundering investigation, officials said.The politician, Ravinder Singh Khera, is SAD’s constituency in-charge for the Mohali-Kharar assembly seat. Recent news reports suggest that he is a contender for the party ticket for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.The ED action comes a day after the SAD and BJP announced a pre-poll alliance for the elections expected early next year.Khera did not immediately comment on the ED raids. Officials said action was taken against Khera, a rice miller and proprietor of Guru Kripa Rice and Agro Industries in Kharar, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.The raids against the SAD leader stem from a January 2023 FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation on charges of criminal conspiracy with officials of the Food Corporation of India to obtain undue favours for procurement, storage and quality inspection of foodgrains, they said.The CBI later charge-sheeted Khera and other accused individuals.

headline: Chandigarh MC elections: Nomination process begins November 26
content: The nomination process for the municipal corporation elections begins Thursday, with candidates contesting from the city’s 35 wards required to file their papers at the offices of the respective returning officers (ROs) between 11 am and 3 pm.The last date for filing nominations is December 3, followed by scrutiny of papers on December 4. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until December 7, after which the final list of contesting candidates and their election symbols will be announced, according to the schedule issued by the State Election Commission (SEC).The SEC has appointed nine returning officers to oversee the nomination and election process across the wards. Each RO has been assigned a specific set of wards and will receive nomination papers at designated offices.To ensure transparency, the commission has ordered videography of all critical election-related activities, including filing of nominations, scrutiny of papers and allotment of election symbols. CCTV cameras will also monitor all RO offices, strongrooms and counting centres.Candidates can also file their nominations through an optional online facility available on the SEC website. However, the facility will remain open only until 24 hours before the deadline for offline filing of nominations.The expenditure limit for candidates has been fixed at ₹7.5 lakh per ward. They will have to maintain an account of their election expenses from the date of nomination until withdrawal, rejection of nomination or declaration of results, as applicable. The accounts must be submitted to the concerned RO within 15 days of the declaration of results.Four general observers, four expenditure observersThe SEC has appointed four general observers to monitor election-related activities and ensure free and fair polls. Candidates, political parties and other stakeholders can approach them with election-related complaints.Another four expenditure observers will monitor candidates’ spending and scrutinise their accounts. Candidates have been advised to obtain bills and vouchers from suppliers and maintain proper records of their campaign expenditure.The commission has also appointed 20 assistant returning officers, 96 sector officers and around 3,500 polling personnel. A special police observer has been assigned to oversee security arrangements.

headline: Chandigarh MC elections: Day before nominations, SC certificate rules spark row
content: A day before the nomination process for the municipal corporation (MC) elections begins, the state election commission’s clarification on the validity of Scheduled Caste (SC) certificates for reserved wards has triggered a political row, with Congress and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) questioning the timing and implications of the decision.The commission, in a clarification issued on Wednesday, reiterated its November 26, 2011, directions, stating that only SC certificates issued by the Chandigarh administration on a bona fide basis to residents belonging to the 36 castes notified for the Union Territory would be valid for contesting elections from SC-reserved wards. Certificates issued by the administration to residents who migrated from other states would not be accepted for this purpose.A bona fide SC certificate, in this context, refers to one issued to a Chandigarh resident whose family can establish its residence in the city before November 1, 1966, when Chandigarh became a Union Territory. This is distinct from a migration-based certificate issued to a person who moved to Chandigarh from another state and produced an SC certificate from their state of origin.The restriction applies to those contesting from SC-reserved seats; it does not, by itself, disqualify such individuals from contesting general wards. The UT has seven SC-reserved wards in the 35-member civic body, including three reserved for SC women.‘May affect candidatures’ Chandigarh Congress president HS Lucky said the clarification could affect three to four of the party’s prospective candidates. “We had three to four wards where our candidates belonged to the SC category and were bona fide residents. They will be affected by this clarification,” Lucky said.Former Union minister and senior Congress leader Pawan Kumar Bansal questioned the basis of the restriction, arguing that a person enrolled as a voter in the city should be entitled to contest an election. “One has to be a voter in the city to contest an election. If a person is enrolled as a voter here, why should they not be entitled to be a candidate?” he said.Will explore legal options: AAP AAP Chandigarh president Vijay Pal termed the clarification “unconstitutional” and said the party would explore legal options to challenge it. “People from other states have migrated to Chandigarh and are enrolled as voters in all wards. Who qualifies as a bona fide resident dating back to 1966? Who was living here at that time? This is worse than deleting voters and is an insult to the SC community. We will seek legal advice and challenge the decision,” he said.‘Timing questionable’AAP Chandigarh co-in-charge Prem Garg also criticised the clarification, calling it impractical and objecting to its timing.“This is neither possible nor practical. Either the administration should issue certificates to willing candidates on the basis of SC certificates issued by other states, after verifying their Aadhaar and voter cards, or it should accept the SC certificates issued by their respective states. Issuing clarifications at this belated stage does not augur well for the Election Commission,” said Garg.‘What about precedence’BJP leader Gopal Shukla, alias Pappu Shukla, whose wife Chanderwati Shukla was a former councillor, said the eligibility criteria should also be viewed in the context of Chandigarh’s electoral history. “Some past councillors, and even sitting ones, who contested from reserved wards belong to the SC category but are from other states. Such directives have never been passed in an arbitrary manner,” he said.He added that no person enrolled as a voter in Chandigarh and holding a valid SC certificate issued by a government authority should be denied the right to contest from a reserved seat.On being contacted, a state election commission official said the clarification reiterates the commission’s November 26, 2011, directions and does not constitute a new directive.

headline: AI conference brings industry leaders to Chandigarh
content: Exploring how artificial intelligence (AI) can transform sectors such as healthcare, education, finance, law and business, the inaugural AiXCon 2026 brought technology leaders, entrepreneurs, academicians and policymakers together at Tagore Theatre on Wednesday.The one-day conference focused on the practical applications of AI, emerging technologies and the challenges of integrating them into different industries. It featured expert talks, panel discussions, demonstrations and recognition awards, providing a platform for industry professionals, startups and researchers to exchange ideas and explore collaborations.The event was organised by Chandigarh-based AiX Foundation and Vascular Society for Limb Salvage (VSLS), with Shoolini University as the title sponsor. It was conceptualised by entrepreneur Adit Jindal, founder and president of AiX Foundation and founder and CEO of Callidora Technology. The initiative also aimed to establish the tricity as an emerging hub for AI innovation and encourage local talent to build technology-driven ventures.Sameep Shastri, chairman, BRICS Chamber of Commerce and Industry, attended as the chief guest. Punjab IT secretary Dhirendra Kumar Tiwari, Shoolini University pro-chancellor Vishal Anand and actor-comedian Gurpreet Ghuggi were the guests of honour.Shastri highlighted the need to bridge the gap between AI innovation and its practical implementation, particularly for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and startups.Fortis Hospital Mohali’s Dr Ravul Jindal discussed how AI can assist doctors with clinical documentation, data analysis and medical research. Shoolini University’s Nishtha Shukla Anand highlighted the potential of AI in making education more personalised while retaining human interaction.Brahm Alreja, president, TiE Chandigarh, called for the region to develop AI solutions rather than merely adopt them.

headline: Patient care hit at Aam Aadmi Clinics amid strike in Mohali
content: Patients visiting Aam Aadmi Clinics in Mohali were left without medical examinations and medicines on Wednesday as a staff strike disrupted healthcare services across the state.Although doctors were deployed at some clinics from the civil hospital in Phase 6 to minimise the impact, the absence of pharmacy officers and clinical assistants meant that essential services could not be maintained. Patients at the Phase 5 clinic also had to return without receiving the treatment or diagnostic facilities they had come for.The shortage of support staff affected the functioning of the clinics, where doctors alone could not ensure the delivery of all services. While medical officers attended to their duties, the absence of pharmacists disrupted medicine distribution, and diagnostic services were also affected.The strike was called by the Aam Aadmi Clinics Sanjha Front, whose members held a protest and hunger strike in Sangrur. The employees are seeking regularisation of their services, an increase in incentives and separate payments for work under national health programmes.Their other demands include full salary and incentives for duties performed on Sundays and public holidays, health and accident insurance for employees and their families, and payment equivalent to at least 75 patients a day irrespective of actual outpatient attendance.The employees said discussions had been held with government representatives and their demands had received in-principle approval, but no written orders had been issued so far.

headline: Two new borewells planned to tackle water shortage in Mohali
content: Residents of Sectors 88 and 89 are expected to get some relief from water supply constraints, with the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) planning to install two additional borewells in the area at a cost of ₹2 crore.The project will involve drilling both borewells to a depth of 250 metres. Separate rooms housing the tubewell equipment will also be constructed, along with toilets. Motors and pumping systems will be installed to draw water and connect the facilities to the supply network.The additional infrastructure is intended to strengthen supply in the sectors, where the existing arrangement is struggling to keep pace with growing demand. Four tubewells are currently being used to meet residents’ requirements, but the increase in population has added pressure on the available resources.According to the project details, the new facilities will include the necessary arrangements for operating and maintaining the pumping equipment. Pipelines will be laid to ensure that water drawn from the borewells can be fed into the distribution system.GMADA officials said the area was yet to receive water through the sewerage and water supply network. Although four tubewells were already supplying water, two more borewells were being planned to ensure that residents do not face shortages during the coming summer.The new installations are expected to provide additional capacity and help cater to the area’s increasing water needs. The project will also add supporting infrastructure for the operation of the tubewells.

headline: Punjab hikes sugarcane price to ₹431/quintal, highest in country | Hindustan Times
content: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday announced a ₹15 per quintal increase in the state advised price (SAP) of sugarcane to ₹431 for the 2026-27 crushing season, making it the highest sugarcane price in the country.The announcement comes at a time when sugarcane farmers in neighbouring Haryana are protesting for a higher procurement price of ₹600 per quintal, rejecting the state government’s recent hike to ₹430 per quintal.Chairing a high-level meeting here, Mann said the decision reflected the state government’s commitment to the welfare and economic prosperity of the farming community.In a post on X, the CM said, “Big news for sugarcane farmers in Punjab. Our government has increased the sugarcane price to ₹431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, the highest in the entire country.”He also announced that sugar mills across Punjab would commence operations from November 25 to facilitate the timely and convenient supply of sugarcane by farmers.Addressing the meeting, Mann described the increase as a significant initiative for the state’s sugarcane cultivators. He said farmers worked tirelessly to feed the nation and strengthen its economy, and it was the government’s responsibility to ensure that their hard work received its rightful value.“Farmers are the backbone of our economy, and their prosperity is essential for the overall progress and economic well-being of Punjab. Our government is fully committed to safeguarding their interests, strengthening their financial position and ensuring that they receive remunerative prices for their produce,” he said.The CM reiterated that providing remunerative prices for agricultural produce and extending all possible support to farmers remained among the foremost priorities of his government. He added that the state was consistently taking farmer-friendly decisions to strengthen the rural economy and secure a dignified and prosperous future for the farming community.Sugarcane farmers in Haryana have been protesting for the second consecutive week, demanding an SAP of ₹600 per quintal for the 2026-27 crushing season.The Haryana government has announced a price of ₹430 per quintal for the current season, followed by an increase to ₹450 per quintal in 2027-28. Farmers’ organisations have rejected the proposal, arguing that the increase of ₹35 over two years is inadequate in view of rising input and production costs.Sugarcane farmers in Haryana received ₹415 per quintal last year. They maintain that the proposed increase does not adequately address their financial concerns and have continued to press for a substantially higher price.

headline: Sangrur: 104 PRTC employees brought under contract
content: Punjab Finance and Transport Minister Harpal Singh Cheema on Wednesday handed over appointment letters to 104 employees of the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) as part of the state government’s initiative to bring 1,719 outsourced employees under contract.He formally launched the process at a special function held at the PRTC’s Sangrur depot. The appointment letters were distributed to employees from various depots across the state.Congratulating the employees, Cheema said the Punjab Government, led by CM Bhagwant Singh Mann, was committed to providing them with job security, dignity and better service conditions.Interacting with mediapersons, he said the government had enacted a legislation to fulfil the long-pending demand of outsourced employees. The process was initiated after completion of the mandatory 90-day period prescribed under the law.He said appointment letters were being prepared for eligible employees after completing departmental formalities.

headline: Anti-sacrilege law: Akal Takht panel calls Punjab govt committee for Nov 30 talks | Hindustan Times
content: The Akal Takht’s expert committee has invited the Punjab government’s seven-member coordination committee for talks at Anandpur Sahib on November 30 over the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026, notified in April, after skipping earlier meetings called by the state panel.After an internal meeting attended by Justice Rupinder Singh Sodhi (retd), Justice Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi (retd), senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, Kehar Singh, and Jagmohan Singh, coordinator Lakhvir Singh wrote to nodal officer Harjit Singh Sandhu, a PCS officer, urging the panel not to “mislead” the Sikh sangat on Akal Takht directives.Standoff over stay directivesIn the letter, the Takht panel said it reviewed statements around the coordination committee’s November 23 meeting at Amritsar’s Circuit House, which it again skipped. It called press remarks in Amritsar by two unnamed non-committee speakers “misleading” and accused the panel of ignoring earlier objections.Those speakers, the letter said, overlooked May 11 and June 29, 2026, Akal Takht directives staying the amendment Act pending consensus on clauses covering custodianship, saroops, and religious governance that distance the Sikh sangat from Guru Granth Sahib. It said that staying Amendment Act No. 7 of 2026 is legally distinct from the 2008 Satkar Act (Act No. 1 of 2008) on printing, so holding the amendment in abeyance would not freeze the 2008 law.Nearly all sitting Punjab MLAs and cabinet ministers, the letter said, had agreed unconditionally to remove the Akal Takht’s objections out of regard for the sanctity and maryada of Guru Granth Sahib.The Takht panel accused the coordination committee of ignoring letters dated November 7, 14, 17, and 21, 2026, without sharing them publicly or with the media. Regretting that the state panel treated the stay directive as disregarded for lacking stay powers, the letter said the government could have placed the directives before the cabinet, stated its position publicly, and replied in writing. Without a written reply—and amid conflicting reports over a proposed November 27 sitting—Takht members stayed away from earlier meetings.Govt panel’s positionFormed in September 2026, the seven-member coordination committee includes former Akal Takht jathedar Giani Raghbir Singh, Damdami Taksal head Sant Giani Harnam Singh Khalsa, Sant Baba Sewa Singh of Rampur Khera, former high court judges Jaspal Singh and Gurbir Singh, former IPS officer Jatinder Singh Aulakh, and law officer Preet Inder Paul Singh.After its November 18 and November 23 Amritsar meetings, the panel urged dialogue over confrontation and invited talks, including on November 27. It maintained that staying or amending a legislature-passed law carries legal and institutional implications beyond its mandate. While newspaper statements claimed objections were addressed according to Takht directives, the expert panel said it remained unclear whether the law is in force or held in abeyance, with repeated written queries unanswered.The expert committee invited the coordination committee to meet at 11am on November 30 at the Baldev Singh Mahilpuri Meeting Hall, Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, Anandpur Sahib, following Akal Takht directives. Only nominated members will be allowed to attend, and fresh copies of the May 11 and June 29 directives were enclosed.

headline: 25 IPS, 6 PPS officers transferred ahead of Punjab polls | Hindustan Times
content: Ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, the Punjab government on Wednesday ordered the immediate transfer of 25 Indian Police Service (IPS) and six Punjab Police Service (PPS) officers, including three commissioners of police and 11 senior superintendents of police.The move came in compliance with an October 27 directive by the Election Commission of India, asking the governments of Punjab and four other poll-bound states—Goa, Manipur, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand—to transfer all election-related officials posted in their home districts or those who have completed three years in the same district by November 30.As per the orders, Swapan Sharma, who was commissioner of police, Ludhiana, has been posted as deputy inspector general of police (DIG), Ropar Range. Satinder Singh, earlier the commissioner of police, Jalandhar, will take over as Ludhiana police chief.Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, who was inspector general of police (IGP), Border Range, Amritsar, has been appointed commissioner of police, Jalandhar. Kuldeep Singh, who was DIG, Technical Services, and was holding the additional charge of DIG, Patiala Range, has been moved as commissioner of police, Amritsar.Harmanbir Singh, the commissioner of police in Amritsar, will take charge as DIG, Border Range, Amritsar.Jagdale Nilambari Vijay, IGP, anti-narcotics task force, and holding the additional charge of IGP, Faridkot Range, has been transferred as IGP, Jalandhar Range.Naveen Singla, DIG, Jalandhar Range, and holding the additional charge of director, Vigilance Bureau, has been relocated to head the Faridkot Range as DIG.Harjeet Singh, DIG, Training, and holding the additional charge of DIG, Bathinda Range, has been deployed as DIG, Bathinda Range.Snehdeep Sharma, DIG, AGTF, with additional charge of DIG, Ferozepur Range, has been relieved of his AGTF duties and will now serve solely as DIG, Ferozepur Range.Amneet Kondal, who was DIG, Personnel, has been tasked with heading Patiala Range as DIG.Dr Nanak Singh, DIG, Internal Vigilance Cell, and holding the additional charge of DIG, Ropar Range, has been reassigned as DIG, Technical Services.Gurmeet Singh Chauhan and Vivek Sheel Soni, who were available for posting, have been given the charge of DIG, Provisioning; and AIG, Internal Vigilance Cell, respectively.11 SSPs shiftedAmong SSPs, at the district level, Surendra Lamba, SSP Tarn Taran, has been moved to Sangrur, replacing Ravjot Grewal, who will take over as SSP, Punjab Vigilance Bureau, Mohali.Charanjit Singh, AIG, Special Branch-1, Intelligence, has been posted as SSP Ludhiana Rural in place of Ankur Gupta, who has been relocated as SSP Faridkot.Ashwini Gotyal, AIG, ANTF, has been posted as SSP Ferozepur and Vatsala Gupta, AIG, Personnel-II, as SSP Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar.Dr Pragya Jain, AIG, ANTF, Ludhiana and holding the additional charge of AIG, Internal Security, will take over as SSP Amritsar Rural.Tushar Gupta, SSP SBS Nagar, has been shifted as SSP Gurdaspur and Ajay Gandhi, AIG, Provisioning, as SSP Tarn Taran.Aditya, SSP Gurdaspur, has been tasked with ANTF, Punjab, Mohali, as AIG.Maninder Singh, AIG, Welfare, and holding the additional charge of SSP Ropar, will now hold only the latter post.Bhupinder Singh, SSP Ferozepur, has been given the charge of SSP Malerkotla, replacing Harkamalpreet Singh Khakh, who has been shifted to Jalandhar Rural as SSP.Harvinder Singh Virk, SSP Jalandhar Rural, has been reassigned as AIG, Special Branch-1, Intelligence.Naunihal Singh, ADGP, Internal Vigilance Cell, will also hold the additional charge of ADGP, State Armed Police, Jalandhar Cantt.The services of three officers have been placed at the disposal of the Vigilance Bureau. These include Kanwalpreet Singh, SP Headquarters, Amritsar Rural, also holding the additional charge of SSP Amritsar Rural; Gurbans Singh Bains, SP, Punjab Bureau of Investigation, Faridkot, and holding the additional charge of SSP Faridkot; and Karamvir Singh, SP Operations, Barnala.

headline: Punjab hikes sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal, govt claims highest rate in country
content: Chandigarh: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday announced an increase in the state advised price (SAP) of sugarcane to Rs 431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, which the state govt claimed was the highest in the country.Chairing a high-level meeting, CM Mann said the decision reflected the govt’s commitment to the welfare and economic well-being of farmers. Mann posted on X: “Big news for sugarcane farmers in Punjab. Our govt has increased the sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, the highest in the entire country. To ensure convenience for farmers, sugar mills across the state will commence operations from Nov 25, 2026.”In a statement, Mann said the commencement of sugar mills from Nov 25 would enable sugarcane farmers to supply their produce in a timely and convenient manner. He added that the state govt was continuing to take farmer-friendly decisions aimed at strengthening the rural economy and ensuring a dignified and prosperous future for the farming community.Punjab had last revised its sugarcane price in 2025, when the state govt increased the State Agreed Price (SAP) from Rs 401 to Rs 416 per quintal for the 2025-26 crushing season, marking a hike of Rs 15 per quintal. For the 2026-27 season, neighbouring Haryana has fixed its sugarcane price at Rs 430 per quintal, an increase of Rs 15 over the previous season’s rate of Rs 415.Sugarcane farmers in the state have been demanding an increase in the sugarcane price to Rs 550 per quintal. Meanwhile, the area under sugarcane cultivation in Punjab has increased to 1.16 lakh hectares this year, compared with 1.12 lakh hectares last year. Sugarcane production during the current season is projected to reach around 700 lakh quintals.

headline: Drugs, ED, debt, ad expense: Ahead of Moga rally, Punjab BJP chief poses questions to Kejriwal, Mann
content: Chandigarh: Ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party’s rally in Moga on Thursday, Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Wednesday posed five questions to AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and chief minister Bhagwant Mann, seeking answers on drugs, law and order, corruption, rising debt and ad expenditure.Dhillon asked the AAP leadership to explain its performance before presenting a five-year report card at the rally. He alleged that the govt had failed to fulfil its promises while spending public money on publicity.Questioning the govt’s record on drugs, Dhillon recalled Kejriwal’s promise to eliminate the menace within three months and alleged that drug abuse and overdose deaths continued to claim young lives. On law and order, he cited gang violence, extortion and shootings, accusing the govt of failing to protect citizens.He also questioned the govt over ED proceedings involving Punjab officials and alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. On the state’s finances, he asked how Punjab’s debt had crossed Rs 4 lakh crore despite promises to curb illegal mining and generate revenue. He also flagged delays in financial assistance to women and implementation of the Seventh Punjab Pay Commission.Targeting advertisement expenditure, Dhillon alleged that crores were being spent on publicity in Gujarat and southern states instead of education, healthcare and agriculture.He also raised the shooting of Sukhbir Singh, husband of AAP sarpanch Manjit Kaur of Nawan Pind Daleke village in Tarn Taran. Dhillon alleged that drug peddlers targeted Sukhbir for opposing drug trafficking and informing police. Sukhbir was critically injured while travelling with his wife on a motorcycle. Dhillon demanded the accused be arrested and security provided to panchayat representatives opposing drug trafficking.

headline: Garbage crisis deepens in Patiala amid poll campaign
content: At a time when campaigning for the Municipal Corporation (MC) elections in 30 wards of Patiala is gathering momentum, the city’s worsening garbage management situation has emerged as a major issue, with Opposition parties targeting the civic body over its failure to ensure proper sanitation.The large heaps of garbage could be seen lying along roadsides and on the banks of the Badi Nadi, particularly on the stretch leading towards the landfill site near the Ghalori Gate area.The accumulated waste has not only become an eyesore but is also posing serious health hazards to local residents. The mosquitoes and flies are breeding around garbage heaps, while pigs, dogs and birds can be seen hovering over the accumulated waste.A visit to the landfill site revealed that garbage collectors were forced to dump waste along roadsides due to lack of space at the designated dumping area. The situation has further deteriorated following the breakdown of machinery deployed for waste processing.The poclain machine deployed at the site by Suntan Life Company, the agency hired for solid waste management, has developed a snag. A company employee at the site said the machine’s chain had broken, rendering it non-functional. Besides, the trommel machines installed for processing waste are also lying non-operational, resulting in accumulation of garbage into huge heaps.A senior MC official said the civic body had withheld payments of more than Rs 2.50 crore to Suntan Life Company over alleged inefficiency in carrying out its assigned work. The production of refuse-derived fuel (RDF) from fresh waste had almost come to a halt over the past few weeks, further aggravating the problem.The official said delays in payment of salaries to the company’s employees had also affected daily garbage collection in several areas of the city. Despite repeated warnings to the company, the situation had failed to improve.“The MC has issued several warnings to the company over its failure to perform the assigned work. If the situation continues to deteriorate, the civic body may be left with no option but to cancel its contract for solid waste management and daily garbage collection,” the official said.Interestingly, the deteriorating sanitation situation has provided ammunition to Opposition parties during the ongoing election campaign.BJP Punjab youth wing president Anuj Khosla, who is contesting from Ward No. 40, lashed out at the MC authorities over the mounting garbage problem. Khosla, a former Leader of the Opposition in the MC House, said the condition of the city had exposed the civic body’s failure to provide even basic civic amenities. He alleged that residents were being made to suffer because of administrative apathy and demanded immediate steps to clear the accumulated waste.Shiromani Akali Dal candidate Amarjit Singh Bathla, who is contesting from Ward No. 28 against former Senior Deputy Mayor Harinder Kohli, also criticised the civic body’s handling of sanitation.“The people of Patiala are being forced to live amid garbage heaps, foul smell and unhygienic conditions. The MC has failed to ensure even regular garbage collection, despite maintaining sanitation being one of its basic responsibilities. The residents need permanent solutions, not temporary cleaning drives,” Bathla said.With sanitation becoming a prominent campaign issue, the garbage crisis is likely to figure prominently in the electoral battle in the poll-bound wards.-----------------------MC allots 6 acres for biogas plantPatiala Mayor Kundan Gogia said the MC had signed a contract with the HPCL Renewable and Green Energy Limited to set-up a 100-tonnes-per-day compressed biogas (CBG) plant at the landfill site to process wet municipal waste. This plant would scientifically process wet waste, reduce burden on the landfill, curb methane emissions and generate renewable energy as well as organic manure. “We have also given six-acre of land to the HPCL to set-up the biogas plant, the construction work on which will begin soon,” he said.
