headline: Senu Duggal appointed observer for Patiala Municipal Corporation re-poll
content: The State Election Commission, Punjab, has appointed IAS officer Dr Senu Duggal as observer to ensure that the re-election in 30 wards of the Patiala Municipal Corporation, scheduled for November 28, is conducted in a free, fair and peaceful manner.Duggal today reviewed poll arrangements during a meeting with Additional Deputy Commissioner Kuldeep Bawa. She also publicised the contact details of the nodal officer (Complaints) for the convenience of voters and candidates in the 30 wards. Complaints related to the municipal re-election can be lodged on mobile number 96460-06027 or via email at patialazp@gmail.com.The observer said voters and candidates could contact the nodal officer at any time regarding the re-election process.ADC Kuldeep Bawa said Dr Senu Duggal would remain stationed in Patiala as observer till November 28. Polling would be held from 8 am to 4 pm on November 28. Besides Patiala, elections would also be conducted for seven seats in Dharamkot and 15 seats in Baghapurana.The re-elections follow a Supreme Court order directing fresh polls in wards where alleged irregularities were reported during the previous municipal elections. In compliance with the apex court’s directions, the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court constituted a judicial monitoring committee to oversee the election process conducted by the State Election Commission and ensure adherence to the safeguards laid down by the Supreme Court.

headline: Delhi High Court refuses to interfere with government’s decision to shut Kartarpur Sahib Corridor for pilgrims
content: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (November 26, 2026) refused to entertain a petition challenging the Centre’s decision to close the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor following the Pahalgam terror attack. https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/kartarpur-corridor-a-pilgrim-corridor-across-a-bleak-landscape/article37600761.ece Also read | Kartarpur Corridor will be reopened as soon as national security concerns are resolved, says Amit Shah https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kartarpur-corridor-will-be-reopened-as-soon-as-national-security-concerns-are-resolved-says-amit-shah/article71737824.ece The corridor links Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan, the final resting place of Sikhism's founder, Guru Nanak Dev, to the Dera Baba Nanak shrine in Gurdaspur district in Punjab. It has been shut since May 7, 2025. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said it cannot interfere with the government’s policy decision. Punjab Congress chief urges PM to reopen Kartarpur Corridor, resume Attari-Wagah trade Punjab Congress chief urges PM to reopen Kartarpur Corridor, resume Attari-Wagah trade In a letter to the PM on November 23, Pargat Singh said the Kartarpur Corridor represents the deepest spiritual sentiments of the Sikh community Punjab Congress chief urges PM to reopen Kartarpur Corridor, resume Attari-Wagah trade storyline 1 “It appears that the corridor was operational to secure and promote the religious sentiments of sikh pilgrims. However, the record reveals that after the Pahalgam terror attack, a policy decision was taken by the government of India to suspend the services of Shri Kartarpur Sahib corridor from May 7, 2025. Such decision is taken by the government of India in the interest of its citizens,” the bench noted. It added, “In view of the aforesaid policy decision, we see no reason for us to cause any interference in the same in extraordinary writ jurisdiction.” However, the bench expressed hope that the government will look into the petition pending before it. The court passed the order on a public interest litigation filed by the NGO Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation. The outfit sought the opening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor for Sikh pilgrims to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur in Pakistan.

headline: Tough job punjab
content: Whoever wins has a lot to fix, from debt to drugs, unemployment to crime. A frontier state can’t be allowed to fall behindNow that SAD and BJP have come together again, they may do better in Punjab’s elections early next year. This could upset the plans of Congress and AAP. But the election result is only part of the story. The bigger question is: what will the winning party do after taking power?Punjab has been struggling for many years. In the 1980s and early 1990s, it faced militancy. At least the enemy was easier to identify and fight back then. Today, the state faces several problems at once. Three different governments have failed to solve them over the past 20 years.Punjab’s problems are not easy to see at first. Its people are not especially poor, and its towns and villages do not look run-down. Very few people suffer from several forms of poverty at the same time, and the gap between rich and poor is smaller than in many other states. But this appearance of well-being comes mainly from the Green Revolution of 60 years ago. New seeds and guaranteed government purchases of crops made Punjab India's food bowl.By 1981, Punjab had the highest income per person in the country. It also managed to hold on to much of its wealth despite years of militancy. But today, it has fallen to 16th place. While other states built factories and developed service industries, Punjab remained too dependent on farming. It is a small state and cannot keep expanding agriculture forever. As a result, its farm growth and industrial growth are now slower than the national average.Worse, years of intensive farming have damaged the soil and used up groundwater. The government spends thousands of crores of rupees to provide farmers with free electricity to run their water pumps and grow rice and wheat. This adds to Punjab’s growing debt, which is close to ₹4.5 lakh crore, or 45% of the state's economy.After paying government employees and interest on its loans, the state has very little money left to build roads, improve infrastructure or create jobs. This is a serious problem because one in five young people in Punjab is unemployed.Young people without jobs can easily be drawn into criminal gangs or groups supported by Pakistan that want to break Punjab away from India. Drugs are another major problem. A 2018 estimate said that 67 lakh people, or about 22% of Punjab's population, used drugs such as cannabis, heroin and amphetamines. The problem shown in the film ‘Udta Punjab’ is very real.Now, gangs, demands for protection money and targeted killings have made life even more difficult. Even shopkeepers in Chandigarh, the Union Territory that serves as Punjab's capital, have not been spared.Businesses will not invest in a state where people fear for their safety. Without new industries, Punjab cannot create enough jobs or earn the money it needs to reduce its debt.Whoever wins the election will have a huge task ahead. Punjab needs a government that can tackle all these problems together. A border state that once led India's economic growth cannot be allowed to fall further behind.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

headline: Preparations for Khedan Watan Punjab Diyan finale underway
content: Additional Deputy Commissioner (Development) Amarjit Bains on Wednesday reviewed preparations for the state-level closing ceremony of Khedan Watan Punjab Diyan Season-4 at Lajwanti Stadium.The meeting was held on the directions of Deputy Commissioner Aashika Jain to ensure that all arrangements for the November 29 event were completed well in advance.Bains said Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann would attend the ceremony, while singer Mika Singh would give a special musical performance. A large gathering of players, sports enthusiasts and members of the public is expected at the event.The ADC reviewed arrangements relating to security, traffic management, parking, sanitation, drinking water, electricity supply, deployment of medical teams and cultural programmes. He directed officials of the concerned departments to discharge their assigned responsibilities with utmost seriousness and complete all arrangements within the stipulated timeframe.He emphasised that players, spectators and guests should not face any inconvenience during the ceremony. All departments were asked to work in close coordination and ensure regular monitoring of the arrangements.

headline: Buddha Nullah rejuvenation plan fails to show results despite Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s direction
content: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Punjab general secretary Anil Sarin on Wednesday criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and the Municipal Corporation (MC) over the delay in preparing depots for 100 electric buses sanctioned for Ludhiana under the Centre’s PM-eBus Sewa scheme. He said the project had missed its November 2026 deadline despite receiving approval three years ago.Sarin said the Central Government, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, had approved the budget to strengthen the city’s public transport system and reduce pollution. However, he alleged that the state government and the MC’s engineering branch had failed to complete even a single depot despite the availability of funds and the passage of three years.Under the project, two depots were planned for the 100 electric buses. A depot with a capacity of 70 buses was to be constructed at Ghora Road Colony at a cost of Rs 12.33 crore, while another, with a capacity of 30 buses, was planned on Hambran Road at a cost of Rs 5.82 crore. Both facilities, including sheds, charging stations, workshops and administrative infrastructure, were scheduled to be ready by November.“Surprisingly, barely 20 per cent of the work on the Ghora Road Colony depot has been completed, and construction has been lying completely stalled for the past several months. On the other hand, after missing the deadline for the Hambran Road depot, officials are now making hollow promises to complete the work by the end of December,” Sarin said.Drawing a comparison with Chandigarh, the BJP leader said electric buses were already operating in the city under the same Central scheme, while Ludhiana was yet to get its proposed fleet. He alleged that the delay had deprived residents of modern public transport facilities, leaving the industrial city to grapple with pollution and traffic congestion.Sarin also questioned the preparedness of the authorities for operating the buses. He claimed that no blueprint had been finalised for bus operations, routes, stoppages, timetables or coordination with e-rickshaws across the seven proposed routes spanning 152 km.He criticised the AAP government for failing to ensure timely completion of the infrastructure, saying the delay had held back the introduction of an improved public transport system in the city.

headline: ‘China-linked gang’ under lens in Rs 109-cr cyber fraud at PNB, where Haryana parked funds after IDFC scam
content: Chandigarh: Haryana Police is investigating the suspected role of an international cybercrime group in the alleged siphoning of over Rs 100 crore from the accounts of the state’s panchayati raj institutions (PRIs) in Punjab National Bank (PNB). This comes months after the department moved its accounts to the bank after a direction by the Haryana government to multiple departments to move their money to secure banks in light of the IDFC First Bank scam. Pankaj Nain, Panchkula’s Commissioner of Police, confirmed to ThePrint Thursday that the possibility of the role of an international cybercrime group was being considered. A preliminary probe points to a gang called ‘Crafty Falcon’, suspected to have links to China. Police have not named anyone from the group so far. The funds reported to be moved out of the accounts of gram panchayats, panchayat samitis and zila parishads amount to Rs 109 crore. The Panchkula office of the Development and Panchayat Department of Haryana was the first to report the fraud amounting to nearly Rs 75 lakh earlier this month. Later, it was found that the Panchayati Raj Institutions in multiple districts of Haryana lost their money in a similar manner. The case comes at a sensitive time for the Haryana government. After the IDFC First Bank fraud surfaced in Haryana, the state had asked its departments to keep public money in secure banks. The panchayati raj bodies had moved their funds accordingly, and many of its accounts were shifted to Punjab National Bank, one of the oldest nationalised banks. This cyber fraud has come to light within months of those transfers. Eight people have been arrested so far, including two from Bihar and one from Rajasthan. They were produced in the Panchkula court Wednesday, and sent to seven days of police remand. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has formed four teams, which will travel to other states to question account holders and raid the hideouts of the hackers. The money involved in the fraud was part of the State Finance Commission grant released in October to 6,230 panchayats, panchayat samitis and zila parishads.

headline: Gurugram's Property Market After the Price Rally and the Factors Driving the Next Investment Cycle
content: NewsVoirGurugram (Haryana) [India], November 26: Gurugram's residential real estate market has witnessed a significant appreciation in property values over the past few years, with average residential capital values rising from Rs. 6,150 per sq. ft. in 2019 to Rs. 13,350 per sq. ft. in Q2 2026, according to ANAROCK. While the price rally has strengthened the city's position as a leading real estate investment destination, it has also prompted buyers and investors to adopt a more selective approach. As several micro-markets mature, the next phase of growth is increasingly expected to be driven by infrastructure development, employment hubs, connectivity and the quality of residential developments.BK Malagi, Vice Chairman, Experion Developers, said, "Gurugram's next investment cycle will belong to corridors backed by hard infrastructure. An operational Dwarka Expressway, upgrades along the Southern Peripheral Road, and faster access to IGI Airport and commercial hubs have redrawn the city's commute map. We are seeing that buyers are willing to pay for time saved and daily convenience, which means sustained demand will follow micro-markets that pair reliable transit with schools, healthcare, and planned civic amenities."The growing preference for infrastructure-backed locations reflects a broader shift in buyer behaviour. With established residential corridors witnessing considerable price appreciation, homebuyers are increasingly evaluating the actual development status of emerging locations, their connectivity to employment centres and the availability of essential social infrastructure.Sandeep Chhillar, Founder and Chairman, Landmark Group, said, "Buyers are now comparing locations more carefully. A few years ago, the possibility of future infrastructure development was enough to attract interest in some emerging sectors. Today, they want to know how much of that development is actually in place. Access to workplaces, schools and healthcare, along with the scope for rental income, are all part of the investment decision."Employment continues to remain a key demand driver for Gurugram's residential market. The city has an office stock of over 100 million sq. ft., with established commercial districts such as Cyber City, Udyog Vihar and Golf Course Road supporting demand from professionals and corporate employees. The concentration of employment opportunities, coupled with improving connectivity across residential corridors, continues to influence both end-user demand and rental prospects."Gurugram's real estate market has witnessed significant price growth over the past few years, but the next phase will be about identifying the right investment opportunities rather than simply riding the price wave. Buyers today are looking beyond current property values, evaluating infrastructure growth, connectivity, proximity to business hubs and future appreciation potential. Homebuyers are also becoming more discerning, prioritising construction quality, spacious layouts, privacy and lifestyle amenities. While investors seek markets offering capital appreciation and rental potential, end-users are focused on the overall living experience. Ultimately, the next investment cycle will favour developments that combine the right location, quality and lifestyle with sustainable long-term value," said Sehaj Chawla, Managing Director, TREVOC Group.The variation in property values across micro-markets further highlights the importance of location-specific investment decisions. According to ANAROCK's Q3 2026 data, average quoted capital values stand at Rs 14,400 per sq. ft. along Dwarka Expressway and Rs 13,690 per sq. ft. in New Gurugram. These differences reflect the varying stages of development, infrastructure accessibility and residential demand across the city's key corridors.Changing household requirements are also influencing the premium housing segment, with buyers increasingly looking for homes that accommodate evolving family structures and lifestyle needs.Dr. Gautam Kanodia, Founder, KREEVA and Kanodia Group said, "Families are also looking at how a home can accommodate different generations. In many households, parents and adult children want to live close to each other but retain their independence. This is creating interest in larger homes, flexible layouts and developments that offer facilities for different age groups. It is a requirement that deserves more attention in the planning of luxury housing."On the infrastructure front, the proposed 28.5-km Gurugram Metro corridor connecting Millennium City Centre with Cyber City, along with a spur towards Dwarka Expressway, is expected to strengthen connectivity across key commercial and residential areas. The continued development of road networks and urban infrastructure is also reshaping the city's residential landscape. Dwarka Expressway offers connectivity towards Delhi and IGI Airport, New Gurugram benefits from access to NH-48 and the Manesar employment belt, while Southern Peripheral Road (SPR) connects several southern residential sectors with established parts of Gurugram.Alongside location and infrastructure, the balance between property pricing, rental potential and upcoming residential supply is becoming increasingly important in investment decisions. Investors are assessing not just the quoted capital value but also the potential for rental returns, the pace of surrounding development and the long-term demand outlook of a particular micro-market.Karan Malik, Regional Director, Realistic Realtors, said, "Buyers are comparing ready properties with new launches more carefully. They want to understand the rent a property can command, how much competing supply is coming into the area and how soon the surrounding sector will be occupied. A quoted price tells only part of the story. The condition of the property and the development around it also matter."As Gurugram moves beyond its recent phase of rapid price appreciation, the next investment cycle is likely to be shaped by a more discerning market. Infrastructure-led growth, employment-driven housing demand, evolving lifestyle preferences and the availability of quality residential developments will play an important role in determining which micro-markets sustain their growth momentum. For investors and end-users alike, the focus is gradually shifting from short-term price appreciation to long-term value, location fundamentals and the overall quality of development.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by NewsVoir. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: HTET 2026 registration ends tomorrow at bseh.org.in: Check key dates and direct link to apply
content: Candidates have one more day to apply for the Haryana Teacher Eligibility Test (HTET) 2026, as the online registration window will close on November 27. Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official website of the Board of School Education Haryana (BSEH) at bseh.org.in.According to the board, the application process began on November 18 and will remain open until 11:59 pm on November 27. Candidates who have already registered but have not paid the examination fee must also complete the payment process before the deadline.The HTET 2026 examination will be conducted on December 26 and 27 for all three levels. Dr Shankar Lal Dhoopar, chairperson of BSEH, Bhiwani, confirmed the examination schedule.Candidates are advised to complete their applications and download the confirmation page after submitting the form and examination fee. The board will not accept applications after the registration deadline.HTET 2026: How to applyCandidates who have not yet submitted their applications can follow these steps:Visit the official website at bseh.org.in.Open the HTET 2026 application link available on the homepage.Read the instructions and eligibility conditions mentioned in the Information Bulletin.Complete the online registration and fill in the required details.Upload the necessary documents and complete the application form.Pay the prescribed examination fee.Submit the application form and download the confirmation page.Take a printout of the confirmation page for future reference.Direct link here.Candidates should check all the details carefully before submitting their applications.HTET 2026 application correction windowThe board will open the application correction facility on November 28 and 29, 2026. Candidates will be able to make changes to certain details in their submitted application forms during this period.Permitted corrections will include details such as the candidate's name, father's name, mother's name, date of birth, photograph, identity proof, Aadhaar number and subject selection for Levels 2 and 3.However, candidates will not be allowed to make changes to certain other details, including their category, home state and physically challenged status. The board will not consider correction requests sent through email, letters or any other offline mode.Candidates should use the correction window carefully, as no further changes will be accepted after November 29.HTET 2026 examination scheduleThe BSEH will conduct the HTET 2026 examination on December 26 and 27. The examination will cover all three levels:Level 1: For candidates seeking eligibility to teach Classes 1 to 5.Level 2: For candidates seeking eligibility to teach Classes 6 to 8.Level 3: For candidates seeking eligibility to teach Classes 9 to 12.Candidates can check the detailed examination instructions, eligibility conditions and other important information in the HTET 2026 Information Bulletin available on the official website.Applicants are advised to complete the registration process before the deadline and regularly visit bseh.org.in for further updates.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM SH ANIL VIJ HARYANA MINISTER FOR ENERGY, TRANSPORT AND LABOUR
content: *Vij expresses gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Constitution Day; says the occasion provides an opportunity to reflect on the Constitution’s values, rights and duties* *“The Constitution provides a strong foundation for the country’s unity, integrity and equality. Despite our diversity, India remains united—unity in diversity is our greatest strength”: Anil Vij* *“Democratic rights were curtailed during the Emergency, the press was censored and opposition leaders were jailed”: Anil Vij* *“The Bharat Ratna was conferred on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar by a BJP-supported government, and his portrait was installed in Parliament in 1990”: Vij* *“Haryana’s progress is the result of the collective efforts of hardworking farmers, youth, teachers and an effective governance system”: Vij* Chandigarh, November 26: Haryana Energy, Transport and Labour Minister Sh. Anil Vij said that the essence of the Indian Constitution lies in the words “We, the People of India” and that the ultimate power in a democracy rests with the people. Expressing his gratitude to Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi for the initiative to celebrate Constitution Day, Vij said the occasion provides an opportunity to reflect on the values enshrined in the Constitution, as well as the rights and duties of citizens. He said that India, despite being home to people belonging to different religions, castes, languages and cultures, remains united, and that “unity in diversity” is the country's greatest strength. The Constitution has provided a strong foundation for India's unity, integrity and equality. He added that Haryana's development journey, too, is the outcome of the collective efforts of its hardworking farmers, talented youth, teachers and an effective governance system.

headline: Satin Finserv's SANKALP Grand Finale; 14 teams to compete for INR 30 lakh+ prize pool
content: VMPLGurugram (Haryana) [India], November 26: Satin Finserv Limited has announced the 14 finalists and an eminent six-member jury for the Grand Finale of SANKALP by Satin Finserv: The Climate Edition, bringing together emerging climate innovators and industry leaders to identify solutions to some of India's pressing environmental challenges.The Grand Finale, scheduled for 3rd December 2026 at The Leela Ambience, Gurugram, will see seven student teams and seven startups compete for a prize pool of over INR 30 lakh+, presenting solutions spanning clean energy, green mobility, water and waste management, sustainable agriculture and the circular economy.The six-member Grand Finale jury brings together leaders from business, sustainability, finance and green technology, including:- Ajay Jain, Chairman, IIM Calcutta Innovation Park- Malini Thadani, Environmental & Sustainability Expert- Piyush Gupta, CEO, Strategic Investments and Group CFO, HT Media Ltd.- Ram Gopal, CEO and Co-founder, Kaamyabi and Former CEO, Barclays India- Sandy Khera - CEO, Enel Green Power- Sulajja Motwani, Founder and CEO, Kinetic GreenThe jury will evaluate the finalists on the strength of their ideas, innovation, feasibility, scalability and potential environmental impact, with an emphasis on solutions that can move beyond concepts to real-world implementation.The finalists represent a diverse mix of emerging talent and entrepreneurial innovation. The student track features teams from IIT Patna, IIM Ahmedabad, XLRI Jamshedpur, Masters' Union, the Institute of Rural Management Anand and the National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management. The startup track brings together seven ventures developing solutions to environmental and climate-related challenges.The 14 teams were shortlisted following virtual jury presentations held between 2nd to 4th November 2026. At the Grand Finale, they will present their solutions, business models and plans for implementation before the jury.Speaking about the initiative, Pramod Marar, Managing Director and CEO, Satin Finserv Limited, said, "Climate change is one of the biggest challenges before us, but it also presents an opportunity for innovation and entrepreneurship. Through SANKALP, we want to create a platform where young minds and emerging businesses can bring forward solutions with the potential to make a meaningful difference. The quality and diversity of ideas we have seen are encouraging. With an experienced jury bringing perspectives from industry, sustainability and finance, we hope to help these innovators look beyond the idea itself and understand what it takes to build solutions that are practical, scalable and sustainable."He added, "The Grand Finale is not just about recognising the best ideas. It is about giving promising innovators the opportunity to engage with industry leaders, challenge their thinking and take their solutions closer to real-world implementation. SANKALP aims to spotlight innovative climate solutions and help accelerate their journey from concept to impact. Beyond the competition, eligible teams may also be considered for financing discussions, subject to further evaluation."Startup Track- BigsiBucks Innovation Pvt Ltd- Decorearth Private Limited- Levaebio Private Limited- Newcycl Clean Technologies Pvt Ltd- PREserwe- Udyom Eco Tech Private Limited- Yotuh Energy(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. headline: Gurgaon homebuyer wins refund battle: Builder ordered to return ₹1.35 lakh with interest, pay ₹52,000 compensation
content: A Gurgaon homebuyer who withdrew from an affordable housing project without receiving an allotment letter or signing a builder-buyer agreement has won a refund battle against the developer.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurgaon, has directed Czar Buildwell Pvt Ltd to refund ₹1.35 lakh deposited by the buyer, along with 9% annual interest from the date of payment. The builder has also been ordered to pay ₹52,000 towards compensation for mental harassment and litigation expenses.The order follows a complaint by Vrinda Thareja, who had applied for a flat in the developer's Mahira Homes 104 project in Sector 104, along the Dwarka Expressway, under Haryana's Affordable Housing Policy.According to a Times of India report, Thareja applied for the flat in February 2023 and deposited ₹1,35,298. Her name was subsequently selected in the draw, following which the developer informed her that unit T7-1704 in Tower T7 had been allotted to her through a welcome letter dated April 25, 2023.A day later, the developer raised a demand of ₹7,05,530, asking her to deposit the amount within 15 days.However, Thareja decided to withdraw from the project on May 15, 2023, and sought a refund of the money she had already paid.The builder promised a refund but failed to return the moneyThe developer acknowledged that Thareja had neither received a formal allotment letter nor signed a builder-buyer agreement. Its cancelled document receipt, issued on May 15, 2023, also recorded that the refund would be processed shortly.Despite this assurance, the money was not returned.Thareja subsequently made repeated requests for repayment and also sent a legal notice on January 7, 2025. However, these efforts did not result in a refund, prompting her to approach the consumer commission.Advocate Vaibhav Kaushik represented the complainant before the commission.Czar Buildwell did not appear before the commission despite being served notice and was proceeded against ex parte.What the consumer commission orderedThe commission, headed by President Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur, found that the documents submitted by Thareja supported her complaint.It observed that the developer's own records confirmed that no formal allotment letter had been issued and no builder-buyer agreement had been executed. The commission also noted that the buyer's evidence remained unrebutted because the developer did not contest the case.Holding the builder guilty of severe deficiency in service, the commission allowed the complaint and directed it to:Refund ₹1,35,298 deposited by the homebuyer.Pay 9% annual interest on the amount from the date of deposit until the refund is realised.Pay ₹30,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony.Pay ₹22,000 towards litigation expenses.The developer has been given 45 days to comply with the order. If it fails to make the payment within the stipulated period, the amount will accrue 12% annual interest for the period specified in the order until payment is made.The commission also said Thareja could initiate execution proceedings to enforce the order. The developer could additionally face prosecution under Section 72 of the Consumer Protection Act for failing to comply.

headline: Haryana minister Vipul Goel divested of civil aviation portfolio
content: Chandigarh: In a surprise move, cabinet minister Vipul Goel was on Wednesday night divested of the civil aviation portfolio by chief minister Nayab Singh Saini. Goel retains his other portfolios, revenue and disaster management, and urban local bodies.Saini will now hold the charge of the civil aviation department in addition to his existing ones with immediate effect. Orders to this effect were issued by chief secretary Anurag Rastogi and Vijay Kumar Bhavikatti, secretary to the governor.The reason Goel was removed from civil aviation was not immediately clear, and efforts are on to reach him for comment. The shift comes against the backdrop of a Hindustan Times investigation on July 7 that found Hisar airport handled only 9,559 passengers and recorded 474 aircraft movements between April 2025 and March 2026 despite a nearly ₹1,457-crore investment, according to Airports Authority of India data. The figures placed Hisar among the least-utilised commercial airports in the country.The statistics highlighted the gap between spending on the airport and its actual use. At present, the airport operates seven arrivals and seven departures a week, connecting Delhi, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Ayodhya, with Ayodhya accounting for nearly 47% of passenger traffic. A former IAS officer who once handled the civil aviation department told HT that Hisar airport is an expensive showpiece—a marquee project yet to justify its investment. “It is a case of dream selling backed by massive public investment but limited utilisation, a grand vision confronting ground realities,” the officer said.The airport did not handle any cargo during 2025–26, and passenger traffic declined by 8.3% during April and May 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. Hisar airport faces headwinds from a limited passenger catchment and proximity to Delhi airport, which offers wider connectivity.The scale of spending is also reflected in the state’s budget allocation. The ₹315-crore capital outlay for the integrated aviation hub accounts for about 63% of the civil aviation department’s ₹495-crore capital allocation for 2026–27.Responding to the July investigation, Goel—then civil aviation minister—had said the numbers reflected the early phase of commercial operations, which began in April 2025. He cited limits on daylight operations, terminal capacity constraints and the lack of instrument approach facilities as factors affecting flights.Goel had said the government was working to upgrade navigation and landing systems, expand flight routes and build passenger and cargo infrastructure, while engaging with airlines, maintenance firms and logistics operators to draw aviation-linked businesses to the airport.

headline: 28 shops, police post on Gohana school playground land; Haryana rights panel seeks report
content: The Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has taken a serious view of the lack of adequate and uninterrupted playground facilities for students of Government Senior Secondary School, Gohana.Chairperson Justice Lalit Batra observed that 27 Kanals and 10 Marlas (approximately 3.44 acres) of land situated near the school has been continuously recorded in the revenue records as being in the possession of the Education Department since 1976–77 under the entry ‘Makbuja Mahkama Taleem’. However, despite this, the students have not been able to avail themselves of adequate and uninterrupted sports facilities on the said land.The commission has directed the Principal Secretary, School Education Department, Government of Haryana, to coordinate with the Deputy Commissioner (DC), and the District Education Officer (DEO), Sonepat, to examine the entire matter and specifically clarify why the land recorded in the possession of the Education Department has not been made fully available for the benefit of the school students.The authorities concerned have been directed to submit a detailed report at least one week before the next date of hearing.During the hearing, DEO Naveen Gulia, appeared through video conferencing. He informed the commission that, in compliance with its earlier directions, he had personally inspected the school and that a four-member committee had conducted physical verification of its infrastructure. The DEO submitted a detailed report dated November 2, 2026, along with photographs, a site map and relevant records. The report submitted by the DC, Sonepat, was also placed before the Commission.Edu Dept's possession recorded in revenue records since 1976–77According to the report of the District Revenue Officer submitted by the DC the Jamabandi for the year 2020–21 records the ownership of the 27 Kanals and 10 Marlas of land falling under Khewat no 6199 and Khatauni no 6713, comprising Rectangles and Killa Nos 1347 to 1352, in the name of the ‘Provincial Government’, while the column relating to possession/cultivation records the entry ‘Makbuja Mahkama Taleem’. This entry has continued uninterrupted since the Jamabandi for the year 1976–77. The nature of the land has consistently been recorded as ‘Gair Mumkin Maidan’ (non-cultivable land/playground) in all the relevant Jamabandis. Thus, prima facie, the revenue records indicate that the land had been earmarked and placed at the disposal of the Education Department for educational and allied purposes.School operates in 2 separate campuses with 862 studentsAccording to the report of the DEO, the Government Senior Secondary School, Gohana, has been functioning since 1905 and is presently operating from two separate campuses. The distance between the two campuses is approximately 170 feet, with a public street passing through a market area in between.The Senior Secondary wing of the school, catering to classes IX to XII, has an enrolment of 581 students. This campus has an area of approximately 1,464 square metres. The Middle wing, catering to classes VI to VIII, has 281 enrolled students and occupies an area of approximately 669 square metres. Thus, the two wings together cater to approximately 862 students. The report stated that no apparent encroachment was noticed within the two campuses currently being used by the school.28 shops, a police post and a primary school operating on land recorded as a playgroundThe physical inspection report submitted by the DEO revealed that 28 shops, a police post and Government Primary School, Mughalpura, are presently situated on different portions of the land recorded in the Jamabandi as a playground. The primary school is functioning on approximately 430 square yards of land. During inquiries at the site, the shopkeepers informed the inspection team that the rent collected from the 28 shops is deposited in the office of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), Gohana. The report further stated that the key to the entrance gate of the playground is in the custody of the Municipal Committee, Gohana. In addition, the SDM, Gohana, periodically grants permission for organising circuses, religious functions, jagrans and other public activities on the said ground. The DEO, in his report, stated that the playground could be utilised by school students for sports and other outdoor activities after obtaining the requisite permissions and coordinating with the authorities concerned.Question of sports facilities despite availability of land as per prescribed normsAccording to the DEO's report, under the provisions of the Haryana School Education Rules, 2003, and the notification dated April 16, 2021, a land requirement of 2,000 square metres has been prescribed for senior secondary schools established in urban and controlled areas before the applicability of the relevant provisions. The combined area of the two school campuses has been reported to be approximately 2,133 square metres. The report also mentioned that a playground should be available within a distance of 500 metres from the school. In this regard, Shaheed Madan Lal Dhingra stadium, near Shani Mandir, Gohana, has been stated to be situated at a distance of approximately 350 to 400 metres from the school premises.The Commission observed in its order that when the land has been recorded in the revenue records as being in the possession of the Education Department since 1976–77, it is incomprehensible why the students are still not being provided with proper, adequate and uninterrupted playground facilities.The Commission emphasised that merely recording the name of the Education Department in the revenue records serves no meaningful purpose if the very students, for whose educational interests and conducive learning environment the land was earmarked, are unable to derive any benefit from it.Directions for demarcation of land, examination of encroachmentsIn its report, the DEO recommended a joint inspection and demarcation of the playground land, along with an examination of the status of the 28 shops and the police post situated there.The report further recommended that, if any unauthorised occupation or encroachment is established, appropriate action should be taken by the competent authority in accordance with law.The Commission directed the authorities concerned to make coordinated efforts in this direction and undertake a comprehensive assessment of the school's infrastructure to ensure that the necessary measures are taken.Assistant Registrar Puneet Arora informed that the next hearing in the matter has been scheduled for February 10, 2027.It is pertinent to mention that the Commission has also directed that a copy of its order be placed on the records of all 133 connected complaints relating to the matter. All these children sent their complaints to commission separately through individual postcards.

headline: Tiger Shroff shooting case: Special court orders minor accused to be produced in juvenile court
content: Mumbai: A special court here has ordered that an accused in the actor Tiger Shroff attack case be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) after it was confirmed that he was 17 years old..The accused, who was one of the shooters, will be produced before the JJB and be sent to a correctional home instead of jail..Earlier this month, the boy’s father filed an application stating that his son was a minor and should therefore not be produced before the regular court..The special court had then ordered the police to verify the claims..The city police had sent a team to Haryana to verify the boy’s school records..Tiger Shroff returns to stage, performs in Mumbai weeks after shooting incident.On Wednesday, the prosecution submitted his documents, including the school leaving certificate and birth certificate, showing that the boy was born on November 30, 2008..The boy was 17 years, 10 months and 18 days old at the time of the attack on the actor, making him a minor..The court then ordered that he be produced before the JJB..“From the inquiry conducted, the accused is found to be a ‘child’ on the date of the incident. Therefore, it is necessary to produce him before the Juvenile Justice Board,” Special Judge S R Navander said..Two shooters fired five rounds at Shroff’s car as he was leaving a football ground in Mumbai’s Juhu on October 18. While the 36-year-old actor escaped largely unhurt, his car driver and a bystander, who is a vlogger, were injured..Members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang had claimed responsibility for the firing..Police have named jailed gangster Bishnoi’s aide Anil Pandit as a wanted accused in the case..The minor accused was arrested the next day in Rajasthan.

headline: GAIL plans data centre foray with 5 MW facility in Faridabad, eyes expansion across four states
content: Eligibility for partners includes experience in operating data centres.GAIL, India's biggest gas transporter and marketer, plans to enter the booming data centre industry in partnership with an established operator, leveraging its nationwide optical fibre network and land banks for building facilities across the country.GAIL is proposing to forge an equal joint venture with a strategic partner for developing its first data centre, with a minimum capacity of 5 MW, at Faridabad in Haryana, where it owns a land parcel, according to an expression of interest floated by the state-run company, seen by ET.Depending on the facility's performance and techno-economic assessments of other sites, the alliance may develop additional data centres at multiple locations across Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra, per the document.GAIL's entry into the business is underpinned by three existing assets-a nationwide optical data fibre network running alongside its gas pipelines, land parcels at several pipeline terminals and compressor stations, and access to natural gas that can fuel power generators supplying electricity to energy-intensive data centres.The company has land parcels in many states that could be considered for developing such facilities. It owns around 15,800 km of optical fibre cable network along its cross-country natural gas and LPG pipelines, connecting more than 100 towns and cities across India.GAIL's plans underscore an unprecedented investment boom in the global data centre industry, driven primarily by AI, cloud computing and growing volume of digital information. Beyond technology companies, infrastructure and energy firms are also entering the space, attracted by the growing demand for infrastructure and enormous amounts of electricity they consume.For the proposed Faridabad unit, GAIL will provide the land parcel and access to its optical fibre network. The joint venture will be responsible for arranging power and water, as well as establishing, operating and commercialising the facility.GAIL wants its prospective partner to own at least one operational data centre with 1 MW capacity to qualify for the bid. The selection criteria assigns different weightages to the number of data centres owned or operated by applicants, the capacity of their largest facility, their commitment to book capacity in the proposed Faridabad data centre, and revenues over the last three financial years.

headline: Power bill only at approved rate if upkeep bill separate: Haryana power regulator
content: Gurgaon: A housing society cannot charge residents more than the approved tariff for grid electricity after collecting maintenance charges separately, Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) has ruled. It directed New Shivani CGH Society in Sector 56 to recalculate the electricity bills of 82-year-old resident Sudarshan Kumar Ahuja from Jan 2024 until its unified billing software was implemented in March 2026. The society must use HERC-approved tariffs and adjust any excess payments already made by him.The dispute began in Jan 2024, when the society increased monthly maintenance charges from Rs 2,300 to Rs 3,000 and separated maintenance expenses from electricity bills. Ahuja alleged that the society continued charging him Rs 10 per unit of electricity, higher than the applicable DHBVN tariff. It also imposed a Rs 500 monthly penalty for the difference in payments.The society said its general body had approved the Rs 10 per unit rate in 2016. It comprised Rs 5.93 for grid electricity and Rs 4.07 towards diesel generator (DG) running costs, fuel and maintenance. The society also pointed out that Ahuja had served as its president from Feb 2018 to Nov 2022. Advocate Pankaj Maini represented the society, while advocate Akshay Gupta assisted the commission as amicus curiae.HERC said the society could not continue charging an inflated rate for grid electricity after collecting maintenance charges separately. However, it could recover generator backup costs through a clear, itemised bill showing these expenses separately.The commission said it could not decide disputes over maintenance charges, generator expenses or late-payment penalties. It directed DHBVN to continue checking the society’s billing software and common-area meters. It also said electricity could be disconnected only in accordance with Section 56 of the Electricity Act and applicable regulations.HERC rejected Ahuja’s claim for Rs 50,000 in compensation.

headline: Haryana assembly session set to be stormy
content: Chandigarh: Haryana’s special assembly session on Thursday is set to see the opposition target the BJP govt over electoral rights, unemployment and farmers’ issues, even as speaker Harvinder Kalyan has urged legislators to rise above party politics and make the discussion meaningful.The Congress is preparing for an aggressive intervention, with leader of opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda, AICC in charge Sanjay Dutt and HPCC president Rao Narender Singh scheduled to chair the Congress Legislature Party meeting ahead of the session. The meeting is expected to finalise the party’s strategy on alleged electoral irregularities, unemployment, farmers’ problems and other public issues.The party has also announced a Samvidhan Raksha March in Panchkula on Nov 26 under its Vote Bachao–Desh Bachao campaign. It plans to link alleged voter deletions and concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to what it calls a wider fight to protect constitutional institutions and democratic rights. Its Vote Rakshak Abhiyan is aimed at identifying and verifying cases of alleged wrongful deletion.The INLD, which has two members in the House, is also expected to raise farmers’ concerns and unemployment, adding to the Opposition’s focus on agrarian distress and jobs.Kalyan, meanwhile, has called for constructive discussion on Haryana’s 60-year journey since its formation and the contribution of political leaders, public representatives and institutions to the state’s development. He has urged members to participate actively, uphold parliamentary traditions and reinforce public faith in democratic institutions.The schedule provides for obituary references at 11am, followed by a 75-minute adjournment for a special Constitution Day programme. The House will reconvene at 12.30pm. No separate item-wise debate schedule has been publicly detailed.The programme will include tributes to Dr BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, screening of a documentary on the making of the Constitution and presentation of Hindi and English copies of the Constitution to legislators.With the Congress planning a parallel march in Panchkula and the INLD preparing to flag farmers’ and employment concerns, the Speaker faces the task of maintaining the commemorative character of the sitting while allowing the House to address public issues.

headline: Delhi's poor air streak continues, AQI at 226; no immediate relief in sight
content: Delhi's air quality remained firmly in the poor category on Thursday, with the city-wide AQI at 226 at 7 am, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. While the reading was marginally lower than Wednesday's 228, pollution levels remained elevated across several parts of the capital, with three locations recording air quality in the very poor category. Of the 59 monitoring stations in the capital, 56 had valid readings. Thirty-seven recorded AQI levels above 200, while three crossed 300 and entered the 'very poor' category. PM2.5 was the prominent pollutant in the city's average reading. Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 327, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 308 and North Campus, Delhi University, at 302. Pusa recorded 298, while ITO reported 296 and Burari Crossing 289. At the other end, Sri Aurobindo Marg recorded the lowest AQI at 139, followed by Jharoda Kalan at 146 and Pusa (DPCC) at 147. IMD Lodhi Road reported 148, while Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium recorded 153. These locations were in the 'moderate' category. NCR cities continue to report poor air Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained uneven, with several cities reporting readings in the poor category. Meerut in Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest AQI in the region at 276, followed by Ghaziabad and Greater Noida at 264 each. Panchgaon in Haryana reported an AQI of 261, while Bhiwadi in Rajasthan recorded 246. Dharuhera and Manesar in Haryana reported readings of 238 and 233, respectively. Gurugram also recorded 233, while Noida stood at 228 and Delhi at 226. Bahadurgarh reported an AQI of 217, followed by Rohtak at 211. Baghpat recorded 193, Bharatpur 192 and Sonipat 184. Faridabad reported an AQI of 172, while Hapur stood at 162. Among the better-performing cities in the region, Palwal recorded the lowest AQI at 87, followed by Alwar at 112 and Panipat at 142. Sirsa records India's highest AQI Among the 286 cities with valid readings in the CPCB's 7 am dataset, Sirsa in Haryana recorded the highest AQI at 368, placing it in the 'very poor' category. Anpara in Uttar Pradesh followed at 307, while Darbhanga in Bihar reported 290. Ballabgarh in Haryana recorded an AQI of 289, followed by Gajraula in Uttar Pradesh at 287. Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan and Meerut in Uttar Pradesh both reported 276, while Kaithal in Haryana recorded 273. At the other end, Chikkaballapur in Karnataka recorded the lowest AQI at 19, followed by Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 25 and Ramanagara in Karnataka at 26. Gangtok in Sikkim reported 27, while Eloor in Kerala and Madikeri in Karnataka recorded 30 each. Under the CPCB's National Air Quality Index classification, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'. Grap Stage II remains in force Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) remains in force across Delhi-NCR, according to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM). The measures include intensified mechanised road sweeping, dust suppression and water sprinkling, stricter enforcement of dust-control norms at construction sites, and steps to encourage the use of public transport. The CAQM dashboard lists Stage II as active, with the order effective from November 2. The measures are intended to prevent further deterioration in air quality across the region.

headline: ‘Stone crusher dust chokes wheat fields’: NGT seeks Haryana govt reply; Mahendergarh farmer seeks environ
content: Gurgaon: National Green Tribunal (NGT) has sought responses from Haryana govt and others after a farmer in Mahendergarh alleged that the dust from a stone crusher operating next to an agricultural field has affected his wheat cultivation. A joint inspection committee found that excessive accumulation of crusher dust was preventing the soil from absorbing irrigation water. The committee had concluded that the crusher dust was adversely affecting the farmer’s crops and that agricultural production was likely to decline.The applicant — Khyali Ram — had initially approached the Punjab and Haryana high court through a petition. However, through an order dated May 6, the HC directed him to pursue the remedy before NGT. Ram placed the observations before NGT, having relied on photographs showing dust settling on the adjoining field and the joint committee’s inspection report to substantiate his claims. He alleged that the stone crusher operating adjacent to his agricultural field was damaging the soil and crops. The farmer also raised questions over the regulatory permissions of the crusher, submitting that its consent to establish and consent to operate were valid only until March 2026 and that he had no information about their renewal thereafter.A bench headed by NGT chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr Afroz Ahmad, while hearing the matter on Nov 18, issued notices to the respondents — Haryana govt, Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB), block agricultural officer, district collector and Shree Ram Stone Crusher Company — and directed them to file their replies through affidavits at least a week before the next hearing. The tribunal has listed the matter for Feb 24, 2027.Seeking action against the crusher for alleged environmental violations, the applicant also sought environmental damage compensation for the loss caused to his agricultural land and crops. In its inspection, the joint committee found that dust accumulating on the surface of the wheat field had affected the land’s ability to absorb water even after irrigation, leaving the crop without adequate water. The case highlights how pollution from stone crusher operations can extend beyond air quality concerns to affect agricultural land and farmers’ livelihoods.

headline: BJP govt working tirelessly to translate Guru Ravidas vision of Begumpura into reality: Saini
content: KURUKSHETRA, Nov 25: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Wednesday said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the 'double-engine' government of the BJP is working tirelessly and with unwavering commitment to translate Guru Ravidas' vision of 'Begumpura' into reality.Saini was addressing a ceremony organised at Umri in Kurukshetra to welcome the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra being undertaken to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas.Earlier, the Chief Minister welcomed the Yatra upon its arrival at Umri."The prime minister's guiding mantra of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas' is, in essence, a modern and practical manifestation of Guru Ravidas' philosophy of social harmony and equality," he said.Saini said the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra aims to take Guru Ravidas' message of equality, social harmony, service, social justice and humanity to the last person in society and unite different sections of society in the spirit of social unity.He said the yatra, which commenced from Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Jalandhar on November 18, will cover approximately 2,402 kilometres over 16 days.Passing through eight districts of Haryana, it will culminate on December 3 at Seer Govardhanpur in Varanasi, the birthplace of Guru Ravidas.At Umri here, Saini said the yatra embodies Guru Ravidas' timeless message of equality, brotherhood, social justice and 'Sarvajan Hitaya, Sarvajan Sukhaya' (the welfare and happiness of all)." Nearly 650 years ago, when society was shackled by social evils, hierarchical divisions, discrimination and ritualism, a divine light emerged from the sacred land of 'Kashi', illuminating the world with wisdom and devotion," he said.Saini said Sant Guru Ravidas occupies a unique place in India's Bhakti tradition. Besides being a revered saint, he was a great social reformer, a visionary and a true guiding light for humanity."Guru Ravidas accorded supreme importance to righteous action. His celebrated saying, 'Maan Changa To Kathoti Mein Ganga', continues to remind us that divinity resides not in outward rituals but in the purity of our conscience, honesty and noble deeds," Saini said. Saini said the Haryana government is consistently working to preserve and disseminate the teachings and ideals of saints and great personalities for future generations.With this objective, the government is implementing the 'Sant-Mahapurush Vichar Samman Evam Prasar Yojana', he said.As part of this initiative, a grand Guru Ravidas Dham is being developed at Umri village at a cost of Rs 124 crore. A 125-foot-high statue of Sant Guru Ravidas will be installed at the Dham, which will emerge as a major centre of faith, devotion and social harmony in northern India, he said.On December 15, the Haryana government will organise a free four-day pilgrimage to Varanasi for senior citizens of the state under the Chief Minister's Teerth Yatra Scheme.Saini will flag off the special train carrying the pilgrims. The portal has been opened to invite applications from eligible devotees for the pilgrimage, Director General of the Department of Information, Public Relations and Languages, Aditya Dahiya said in Chandigarh.He said that each pilgrim would also be provided with a tourist kit during the train journey. Senior citizens aged 60 years and above will be eligible to avail themselves of the benefits of this scheme. The annual family income of the devotee must not exceed Rs 1.80 lakh.Under the Chief Minister's Teerth Yatra Scheme, devotees from Haryana have previously been provided free pilgrimage facilities to Ayodhya and Shri Hazur Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra. (PTI)

headline: Rs 300 cr spent on drains, Gurugram to now use parks to check flooding
content: After spending hundreds of crores on building drains that still fail every monsoon, Haryana is now turning to Gurugram’s parks to keep water out of its homes and streets.The government has directed the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) and the Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) to build water bodies and retention ponds across 247 acres of city-level parks and open spaces before the next monsoon. Rainwater harvesting structures will also come up across the green spaces to recharge groundwater.The plan marks a shift in approach, from carrying water away through drains to letting the land hold it. Stormwater will be stored in the parks, the idea being that it does not spill into residential areas. The parks, in effect, are being asked to come to the city’s rescue.DS Dhesi, Principal Adviser to the Government of Haryana for urban development, gave the directions at a review meeting on Wednesday. He stressed that the parks must include sustainable water management alongside landscaping, so that the city was better able to withstand monsoon waterlogging.GMDA CEO Dushmanta Kumar Behera, HSIIDC Managing Director Vinay Pratap Singh and GMDA Chief Town Planner Sanjeev Maan attended the meeting.The need is plain. This monsoon, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) had 155 waterlogging hotspots under round-the-clock watch. A single day of nearly 97 mm rain left large parts of the city waterlogged for a second consecutive day and forced a work-from-home advisory. The MCG has spent over Rs 300 crore on drainage and stormwater projects in the past three years.A major part of the problem is the loss of natural drainage. A 2022 state government survey found Gurugram had lost nearly 75 per cent of its natural stormwater drains to the real estate boom that followed the last master plan. Restoring that capacity inside parks could offer a cheaper and greener cushion than more pipes and channels, said an official.

headline: IIT Mandi Postdoctoral Fellow Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
content: The Indian Institute of Technology Mandi has invited applications for Postdoctoral Fellow positions at its C3DAR centre, open to PhD holders in Meteorology, Atmospheric Modeling, Weather Forecasting or Climate Modeling within five years of completing the PhD. The consolidated fellowship runs from ₹80,000 for a fresh PhD to ₹95,000 for PhD plus 3 years or more of relevant experience. Applications go by email, with a CV and cover letter, to [email protected] with the subject "PDF C3DAR", before 10/12/2026 (Advertisement No. IIT Mandi/PDF/2026/C3DAR/). The official notification does not specify the number of vacancies, the age limit or the application fee. The Indian Institute of Technology Mandi is located at Kamand Campus, Distt. Mandi, Himachal Pradesh. In this notice it invites applications from candidates with an outstanding track record for positions at the level of Postdoctoral Fellow for the C3DAR centre. The Chairperson's contact details are on the C3DAR website, https://c3dar.iitmandi.ac.in/. The notice sets two eligibility conditions for the Postdoctoral Fellow position: IIT Mandi PhD scholars are not eligible to apply for the Institute PDF. The minimum qualification and/or experience may be relaxed for candidates with outstanding credentials. Otherwise, HRA will be paid at the prevailing rates of the fellowship amount for off-campus housing.

headline: Family pension denied to disabled son over missing records: How he won relief from Armed Forces Tribunal after 9 years
content: Can an adult child with a lifelong disability claim family pension after the death of a parent who served in the armed forces? A case before the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT), Chandigarh, has brought this question into focus.Family pension is a regular payment made by the government to eligible family members of a deceased employee or pensioner to provide financial support after their death. It is generally paid first to the surviving spouse. After the spouse's death, the pension will pass to children.Children with disabilities that prevent them from earning a livelihood may qualify for lifelong family pension, subject to the applicable rules.The Chandigarh case concerns a 68-year-old man with a lifelong physical disability who sought his late soldier father's family pension. His claim faced objections from the authorities, including over the absence of his name from his father's Army service records. Here's what happened and how he won the case.What was the case?According to a Times of India report, the applicant, Anil Kumar, lives in Palampur, Himachal Pradesh, with his wife. His father served in the Indian Army from 1940 to 1957 and died in 1975.After his father's death, Kumar's mother, Guffi Devi, received a family pension from 1988 until her death in 2016. Kumar subsequently applied to have the pension transferred to his name, but the Army's Record Office rejected his requests in 2017 and 2019.The authorities cited the absence of his name in his father's service records. They also argued that the documents had been destroyed after the mandatory 50-year retention period and that his claim was time-barred, meaning it had been filed beyond the prescribed legal period.Kumar has a congenital deformity affecting his right leg. Medical certificates from Civil Hospital, Palampur, and Zonal Hospital, Dharamshala, assessed his disability at 45% for life and established that he could not earn his livelihood. He approached the AFT in 2021, seeking lifelong family pension and arrears.What did the AFT rule?The tribunal rejected the government's objections and relied on Army Instruction No. 51 of 1980, which provides for lifelong family pension to disabled children who cannot support themselves after attaining 25 years of age.It clarified that a physically disabled son who cannot earn a livelihood because of his disability does not lose eligibility for ordinary family pension merely on turning 25, provided he fulfils the prescribed conditions.The tribunal also held that the absence of Kumar's name in his father's service records could not override his pension entitlement, particularly when the authorities themselves no longer possessed those records.The order was passed by a bench comprising Justice Umesh Chandra Sharma and Air Marshal Manavendra Singh. The pension will be payable from 17 January 2016, the day after his mother's death.The bench directed the Centre to issue the Pension Payment Order (PPO) within three months and pay the pending arrears with 6% annual interest.Disclaimer: This is for informational purposes only. Please consult a legal adviser for specific guidance.

headline: Woman killed, two injured as burning tree falls on car amid forest fire in Himachal’s Kinnaur
content: Shimla, Nov 26 (PTI) A woman was killed and two others injured after a burning tree fell on the car they were travelling in amid a forest fire in Himachal Pradesh’s Kinnaur district, police said on Thursday. The deceased was identified as Sanjoki Kumari (57), while the injured were identified as Virender Singh (43) and Abhishek Kumar (36). All three were residents of Chagaon village in Kinnaur. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening near Chagaon, where a forest fire was raging. A burning tree suddenly fell on the car, leaving its occupants seriously injured, police said. Locals spotted the accident and alerted the police, following which a team reached the spot and rescued the occupants. They were taken to Jindal Sanjeevni Hospital in Sholtu, where Kumari succumbed to her injuries during treatment. The two injured men are undergoing treatment at the hospital. Superintendent of Police, Kinnaur, Sushil Sharma confirmed the incident and said a case had been registered and an investigation was underway.
