headline: Delhi Police denies permission for SKM's march to Jantar Mantar on farmers' protest anniversary | India News
content: The Delhi Police has denied permission to the Samyukta Kisan Morcha’s (SKM) proposed protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar, scheduled for Thursday. The farmers’ organisation had planned the march to mark six years since the beginning of the farmers’ protest.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, is currently in force in the New Delhi district, prohibiting unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas.“Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on November 26. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march,” DCP (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said.He urged people to comply with the prohibitory orders and cooperate with the police, warning that violations would invite legal action.Farmers' fresh demands The SKM said its current demands include an end to what it termed the “MSP loot”, opposition to the India-US trade deal, scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The SKM said the march would begin at Kali Bari on Mandir Marg at 1pm. The farmers’ body said the protest would mark the sixth anniversary of the beginning of the year-long farmers’ agitation, which began in Delhi before moving to the Singhu, Tikri and Ghazipur borders of the city.The farmers had opposed the three agricultural laws passed by Parliament in September 2020 and demanded a legal guarantee for the minimum support price (MSP). In November 2021, the Centre agreed to their demands and repealed the laws.

headline: Delhi records first single-digit temperature of the season; air stays 'poor'
content: Delhi recorded its first single-digit minimum temperature of the season on Thursday, with the mercury falling to 9°C at the Safdarjung weather station, even as the air quality stayed in the "poor" category.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the minimum temperature fell 2.3 degrees Celsius below normal. This temperature was one degree Celsius lower than Wednesday's 10 degrees Celsius. Palam recorded a minimum of 9.9 degrees Celsius, while Lodhi Road saw the mercury dip to 9.4 degrees Celsius. The Ridge and Ayanagar stations recorded minimum temperatures of 11.4 degrees Celsius and 10.5 degrees Celsius, respectively.At Safdarjung, the maximum temperature stood at 28 degrees Celsius, 1.3 degrees Celsius above normal. There was no rainfall recorded at any of the five stations.The air quality, on the other hand, was again recorded in the “poor” category as weak winds and a strong temperature inversion limited the dispersal of pollutants. The AQI at 7.05 am was 226, while it was 220 on Wednesday. According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), 13 of Delhi's 56 monitoring stations recorded air quality in the “very poor” category, 25 in the “poor” category and 18 in the “moderate” category. Anand Vihar recorded the city's worst AQI at 355, while Sri Aurobindo Marg had the lowest at 131.The CPCB classifies AQI into six categories: good (0-50), satisfactory (51-100), moderate (101-200), poor (201-300), very poor (301-400) and severe (401-500).Of the 56 stations reporting data at 6am, PM2.5 was the predominant pollutant at 46 stations, while PM10 was the main pollutant at the remaining 10. A day earlier, PM2.5 was the leading pollutant at 44 stations and PM10 at 12.Meteorological conditions continued to lead to accumulation of pollutants near the surface. At 4.30am, a layer of air about 150 metres above Delhi was 10°C warmer than the air at the ground. This temperature inversion tends to act as a lid, preventing pollutants from rising and dispersing.Winds beneath this layer averaged just 5 kmph from the north-north-west, significantly weaker than the 15 kmph recorded at the same time a day earlier. The inversion layer was also lower, at 150 metres compared with 300 metres on Wednesday, further limiting vertical mixing.Meanwhile, NASA's satellite data recorded 5,480 farm fires in Punjab and Haryana. It recorded 4,864 cases in Punjab and 616 in Haryana.However, the actual number of fires could be higher as the satellite passes over the region at around 1.45pm, while an increasing number of farmers are reportedly burning crop residue later in the day to avoid detection.

headline: Passport row: CJP leader asked to explain birthplace discrepancy, says MEA
content: New Delhi: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das has been asked to explain discrepancies regarding the place of birth in his passport and advised not to use the travel document until he submits his response, the external affairs ministry said on Wednesday amid a controversy over his being stopped from travelling to the United Kingdom.Das, who was set to take a flight to London early on Tuesday, approached the Delhi high court on Wednesday to challenge the decision to prevent him from travelling. He was scheduled to attend an event at the Oxford Union on December 1 and said he was invited to speak about the “Cockroach Movement”.“Based on reports that we received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, a show-cause notice was issued by RPO [Regional Passport Office] Chennai to Saurav Das on November 23, 2026, seeking his clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at a regular media briefing when asked about the issue.“He was also advised not to use the passport until submission of [his] response,” he said.Elaborating on the show-cause notice, Jaiswal said the passport application “provides for declaration of correct information by the applicant”. He added, “If at any stage, a discrepancy is noted or reported by authorities, which amounts to suppression of facts, then we issue a show-cause notice to the applicant to explain his or her point of view.”The RPO in Chennai issued the notice to Das late on Monday, and he has alleged that he received the notice “just five hours before my flight, and its sole purpose was to harass me and send a message to other young people: look, this could happen to you too”.Das’s passport was issued by RPO Chennai. He said he was stopped by immigration authorities at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport and was not shown any order or Look Out Circular. The Delhi high court is set to hear the matter on Thursday.

headline: Govt to redesign, beautify 13 roundabouts in Delhi
content: New DelhiThe Delhi government will redesign and beautify 13 roundabouts and traffic islands across south Delhi, covering installations at Nehru Place, Kalkaji, Andrews Ganj and Eros hotel, among others, officials with the Public Works Department (PWD) said.The exercise is aimed at improving traffic flow and increasing pedestrian safety, for which footpaths near Hansraj Sethi marg near GK1 market will also be redeveloped, officials said.A senior PWD official, asking not to be named, said that the project will cover two rotaries located on Hansraj Sethi Marg, two traffic islands near Nehru Place and Kalkaji T-Point, and those at Andrews Ganj Flyover, R-Block, Nehru Place, Eros Hotel, BRT Road and Raja Dheer Sen Marg.“Besides redesigning the rotaries and traffic islands based on inputs from traffic police, we will also undertake illumination work and addition of greenery at all these spaces,” the official said, with the department having invited bids with a timeline to complete works in six months.Last month, PWD minister Parvesh Verma said that the government has begun theme-based beautification work to efficiently utilise space beneath flyovers. From a wildlife trail under the Chirag Dilli flyover to a science corner at the IIT Flyover and a Yogshala at Punjabi Bagh, specific themes have been selected for each flyover.Officials said that “nature and wildlife” has been selected as the theme for Chirag Delhi Flyover, “Indian classical dance in modern art” for Panchsheel Flyover, “science and technology” for IIT Delhi Flyover, “transit hub” for Mukarba Chowk Flyover and “multi-hued expression of space” for Aurobindo Marg.Delhi government has announced a series of projects to upgrade and revamp public spaces and areas under the flyovers over the past year. PWD previously stated that it would convert 41 major roundabouts across the city into themed spaces representing different states, Union territories (UTs) and the armed forces. PWD has already begun similar projects at Madhuban Chowk, Azadpur intersection, Anukampa Chowk, Deepali Chowk, Sant Nagar intersection, and Ambedkar X-Ring.Parallelly, PWD is building over 400 police booths for Delhi Police beneath flyovers to improve public safety and bring a visible police presence to busy junctions and corridors.

headline: Delhi records seasons lowest minimum at 10°C
content: New Delhi: Delhi recorded its lowest minimum temperature of the season at 10 degrees Celsius (°C) on Wednesday, 1.3 degrees below normal, as the city continued to experience cool nights.The Safdarjung station recorded the lowest minimum among the five weather stations. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast minimum temperatures of 9°C and 11°C over the next few days.Delhi’s air quality improved slightly, with the average air quality index (AQI) falling to 220 on Wednesday, from 227 on Tuesday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 4pm bulletin. It remained in the ‘poor’ category.Weather conditions remained unfavourable for dispersing pollutants. Weaker winds and a lower mixing height restricted the movement of polluted air. According to an HT analysis of IMD weather-balloon readings from Safdarjung showed that by 4.30pm on Wednesday, sunlight had helped mix pollutants up to around 1,100 metres, below the usual 1,300 metres for late November. Winds through this layer averaged 10 km/h, compared with the seasonal average of around 15 km/h.The lower mixing height and slower winds gave pollutants less opportunity to disperse, keeping concentrations high near the surface.Lodhi Road recorded a minimum of 10.1°C, Ayanagar 10.4°C, Palam 11°C and the Ridge 11.7°C.Last year, Delhi recorded minimum temperatures of 9.7°C on November 15 and 9°C on November 16.

headline: Delhi road rage: Two thrashed with bats, hammer near Sarai Kale Khan flyover
content: New DelhiTwo persons on a motorbike were assaulted with baseball bats and a hammer, and left bleeding by two occupants of a car in an altercation over the two-wheeler brushing against the car on Wednesday evening near the Sarai Kale Khan flyover in south Delhi, police said.Police identified the victims as Vikram, 39, and Arun, 22, contractual employees with the Safdarjung Hospital. They were returning home at around 4pm, when the incident took place. They have both been admitted to AIIMS for treatment, officers said.“On the way, a white Hyundai Creta bearing Delhi registration number allegedly touched their motorcycle. Following this, two occupants of the Creta got out of the vehicle and entered into a scuffle with the motorcycle riders. The accused persons allegedly assaulted Vikram and Arun with a baseball bat and a hammer, striking them on the head and causing injuries, before fleeing the scene,” said deputy commissioner of police (southeast) Vineet Kumar.A case on charges of attempt to murder, robbery and common intention has been registered under sections 109, 309 and 3 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Sunlight Colony police station. Multiple teams have been formed to identify and nab the suspects, a senior police officer aware of the case said.DCP Kumar said that the police control room was informed of the incident at 4.10pm on Wednesday by a passerby named Ankit Mavi. A police team reached the scene and learnt that two men were injured in the incident.Police said the injured persons were immediately shifted to the AIIMS Trauma Centre for medical treatment. Based on the PCR call, a daily diary (DD) entry was made at the Sunlight Colony police station. While Vikram is a resident of Shastri Nagar in Ghaziabad, Arun is a resident of Govindpuram, in Ghaziabad as well.The officer cited above said that the exact sequence of events leading to the alleged road rage, the role of each accused, the nature of injuries and the motive behind the crime are being probed. Investigators are scanning CCTV cameras installed around the scene and the routes that the suspects may have taken after the crime to identify the vehicle and nab the suspects.“Further investigations are on,” he said.

headline: Delhi to operationalise 2 new government hospitals next year: CM Rekha Gupta
content: Two new government hospitals at Siraspur and Hastal are set to become operational next year, which will strengthen healthcare in the Capital by adding 1,815 beds for medical treatment, chief minister Rekha Gupta said on Wednesday.Besides, the government will also open 40 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month as part of the healthcare expansion plans, CM Gupta said.“The opening of both hospitals will improve access to healthcare in the surrounding areas and help reduce the patient load on existing hospitals,” she said.At present, there are 40 government-run hospitals in the Capital, with a bed count of 15,659. The two new hospitals will also fall under the jurisdiction of the Delhi government, officials said.Siraspur hospital to have 1,164 beds, Hastal facility 651Officials aware of the matter said that procurement of medical equipment for the Siraspur hospital, which will have 1,164 beds, is expected to be completed by January 2027. Construction of the 651-bed Hastal hospital is nearing completion, Gupta said after reviewing health infrastructure projects at the Delhi Secretariat.Officials said that of the government’s plan to open 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs across Delhi, 415 have been opened and 40 more will be opened next month on the occasion of the 102nd birth anniversary of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.The government is also considering running centres in two shifts in areas with high patient footfall.Gupta directed officials to meet project deadlines, warning that negligence would not be tolerated. The meeting was attended by health minister Pankaj Kumar Singh and senior officials of the health department and the Public Works Department (PWD).Singh said the health department was monitoring construction, equipment procurement and other arrangements to ensure projects were completed on schedule.In the pipelineAs per the government’s plans, two more 691-bed hospitals are being built in Madipur and Jwalapuri, with both scheduled for completion by 2028. The Madipur project is estimated to cost ₹466.50 crore and the Jwalapuri facility, ₹484.04 crore.The government is also expanding maternal and child healthcare facilities, with a 463-bed block under development at the Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini. Its out-patient department (OPD) block is ready for inauguration, officials said.Also, a 270-bed block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are nearing completion, they said.Medical colleges and specialised healthcare services in expansion planMedical colleges are proposed at Indira Gandhi Hospital in Dwarka and Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital, each with 150 MBBS seats. The government also plans to increase MBBS seats at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and dental seats at Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70.The integrated redevelopment of Lok Nayak Hospital and the Maulana Azad Medical College campus is also being planned, with a timeline of around 30 months.Separately, the government is working to bring GTB Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi State Cancer Institute and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences under a common institutional framework to strengthen specialised healthcare services.

headline: Delhi district court lawyers to march to MHA office, press for pecuniary jurisdiction hike
content: NEW DELHILawyers across Delhi’s district courts plan to take out a “mass peaceful march” from the Patiala House Courts to the office of the ministry of home affairs (MHA) at Kartavya Bhavan on Thursday, demanding an increase in the pecuniary jurisdiction of district courts from ₹2 crore at present to at least ₹20 crore.To be sure, pecuniary jurisdiction is a court’s legal authority to hear and decide a case based on the monetary value of the claim. Enhancing the pecuniary jurisdiction has been a long-standing demand of the district court bar associations. As far back as April 2015, lawyers went on a 15-day strike, demanding an increase in the then-existing limit from ₹20 lakh to ₹2 crore. The strike was called off after the passage of the Delhi High Court (Amendment) Bill, 2015, which paved the way for the enhancement.Lawyers have since renewed their demand for a further increase to ₹20 crore, and the march has been called by the Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi.The bar committee is also demanding amendments to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, to ensure that contested traffic challans and penalties are adjudicated by regular courts rather than executive authorities. This issue had also triggered a strike by district court lawyers in September, protesting changes that transferred the adjudication of contested traffic challans from judicial magistrates to designated executive authorities.The Delhi government subsequently put the proposed mechanism on hold following the lawyers’ protests.The committee has also called for amendments to the Jan Vishwas Act, 2026, and related laws to protect judicial adjudication and citizens’ legal rights.Advocate Dhir Singh Kasana, former secretary of the Saket Bar Association, said, “Several states adjoining Delhi have much higher pecuniary jurisdiction. The increase will help litigants and give civil courts greater power to adjudicate monetary disputes of a higher value with ease”.The bar association said, “We have also requested all Hon’ble Judicial Officers to kindly consider the difficulties faced by advocates and litigants and refrain from passing adverse orders on account of non-appearance arising out of participation in the march”.

headline: Polluted air may add to diabetes burden, overall risk remains unclear: AIIMS director
content: Air pollution may contribute to the rising burden of diabetes, but its share in the overall risk remains unclear, said All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) director Dr Nikhil Tandon, adding that more evidence was needed to establish pollution as a dominant risk factor for the disease.“The question is not only whether something is related, but, if there are many factors, we need to know how much of the risk can be attributed to air pollution?” Dr Tandon said, stressing the need to distinguish between an association and the extent to which a particular factor contributes to the disease burden.“So if you look, there may be a contribution to overall diabetes risk, but whether that’s a dominant one or not, I don’t think we have data to support that,” he said, at a press conference at AIIMS on World Diabetes Day.Also read: The AQI paradox: Why the official count may be downplaying the pollution problemHe maintained that the immediate impact of air pollution would primarily be on the pulmonary and cardiovascular systems.Evidence linking air pollution to diabetes has, however, been emerging. A 2023 study published in the BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care, which included researchers from AIIMS and other institutions, examined the association between exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5), blood glucose levels and the incidence of type 2 diabetes in Delhi and Chennai.The study stated that it analysed data from 12,064 participants and found that every 10 micrograms per cubic metre increase in monthly average PM2.5 exposure was associated with a 0.40 mg/dL increase in fasting plasma glucose and a 0.021-unit increase in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). It also found that a 10 micrograms per cubic metre increase in annual average PM2.5 exposure was associated with a 22% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes.Also read: CPCB’s AQI method understates severity of Delhi’s worst pollution daysThe researchers observed an association between air pollution exposure and higher blood glucose levels and the incidence of type 2 diabetes in both cities.Meanwhile, speaking about the treatment of people with type 1 diabetes at AIIMS, Tandon said the institute has put in place a structured system to ensure continuity of care as patients move from paediatric to adult services.“A structured transition of care from a paediatric to an adult care provider is very important. And we have actually worked on that, created a model, we have tested that model and now at least within this institution we have formalised a process by which a paediatric to adult transition happens,” he said.He added that the institute has also devised a referral framework to facilitate the transfer of patients between paediatric and adult care providers across institutions.

headline: Delhi college students flag unsafe last-mile stretches despite safety upgrades near campuses
content: Weeks of student-led protests across educational institutions seeking women’s safety around colleges led to a string of measures introduced by authorities – installation of streetlights, CCTV cameras, and police pickets outside college gates. But an HT ground check at four major campuses revealed an unmistakable pattern — while authorities have secured the optics, real issues remain unaddressed. Women’s safety effectively ends a few metres away from the college gate, the moment students step onto the last-mile stretches leading to metro stations, bus stops, and paying guest (PG) hubs.Outside the back gate of Lady Shri Ram (LSR) College for Women, a 350-metre stretch now boasts additional streetlights, CCTV cameras, and a permanently deployed PCR van. The upgrades followed protests triggered by the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old schoolgirl inside Aastha Kunj Park near Kalkaji in September -- similar demonstrations were also reported in Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) and Dr BR Ambedkar University Delhi (AUD).Also read: Women’s safety is still an unfulfilled promiseHowever, the improved stretch — located less than two kilometres from the Aastha Kunj Park — is part of a larger road network connecting Amar Colony on one end and Moolchand Metro Station on the other. These adjoining stretches remain poorly lit, with streetlights covered by dense tree cover on both sides, and passing vehicles largely serving as the only source of illumination, LSR students said.“Beyond installing a few streetlights, I don’t think much of our demands has translated into action on the ground. The main road that leads to the front gate remains dark after 6pm, and the back gate is used by students to go to Amar Colony where many live in PGs, whereas day scholars use Moolchand Metro station—the stretch to both these areas remains dark,” said Evia, 21, an LSR undergraduate.She added that police presence at the nearest pink booth remains irregular. “Certain days, you will find two personnel; other days, you will find one who is also occupied on the desktop.”Also read: Nearly 9 in 10 women, girls feel unsafe walking to metro, bus stops in Delhi: StudyNorth Campus: Main stretches lit, lanes darkSimilar concerns were raised by students of DU’s North Campus. A spot check of surrounding lanes between 5pm and 7pm on Saturday found that while main stretches near college gates were well lit, roads leading to hostels near the DU Sports Complex and Cavalry Lane, which connects to Vishwavidyalaya Metro Station, remained shrouded in darkness. The eerie silence along these stretches was broken only by the occasional headlights and honking of passing two-wheelers.“Even if there are four of us walking, there’s a different sense of safety when the group is joined by a male. If we stay late after classes for society events, there’s an unsaid rule that a male friend would accompany us back. We still turn our heads back when we walk, especially if we leave college after 5 or 6pm, to ensure we aren’t being followed,” said Pallavi Singh, 23, who stays in Hudson Lane.She highlighted that catcalling and stalking remain persistent concerns for students living in Hudson Lane, Vijay Nagar, and Kamla Nagar.Also read: Policing, when women’s safety becomes the metricThese concerns have added to teachers’ responsibilities. Latika Gupta, a DU professor, said, “Whenever there’s a field visit or a seminar after routine classes, male students are excited to join, and the reaction I get from female students is different. Their parents would ask for my number, and hours after the trip, I have to ensure they have reached home safely.”Officials of the Delhi University did not respond to requests for comment.A senior Delhi Police officer from the southern range denied the allegations. “Our staff is regularly sensitised and conduct patrolling in the morning and night outside colleges and at parks, especially after the Aastha Kunj Park incident. If something happens inside, we keep in touch with the college administration and their private security for prompt action.”The Public Works Department (PWD) said it is equipping stretches between campuses, hostels and metro stations with smart LED streetlights. “PWD is integrating these stretches with the ongoing Smart LED Street Lighting project. The work is being expedited and is expected to be completed shortly, with the objective of improving visibility and safety for students and other commuters,” an official said.Also read: Women safety: NHRC recommends sensitisation of police personnel to avoid victim-shaming of survivorsAUD and JMI: Concerns continueWomen’s safety isn’t an isolated DU issue. Students of AUD had staged an indefinite 17-day protest over infrastructure concerns, which included demanding access to the university’s front gate, citing safety issues. “The main gate on Lothiyan Marg has been inaccessible for nearly one-and-a-half years. The back gate is near lanes with godowns and a residential area. Catcalling is common, and there have been instances where students reported being inappropriately touched,” said a 19-year-old UG student, who sought to remain anonymous.Officials of AUD did not provide a response until the time of going to print.At Jamia Millia Islamia, the issue became a key demand for students seeking restoration of the students’ union.Shifa Ali, 20, said bus stops near the campus—Batla House, Gafar Manjil, and Tikona Park next to the JMI Metro station—are particularly unsafe. “After 6 or 7 pm, groups of intoxicated men loitering around the campus are a common sight, while women students routinely encounter men on bikes following them and asking for names and phone numbers.”A JMI spokesperson said in-campus safety, particularly around women’s hostels, is tight with layers of checks at multiple entry points. “There is a main entrance gate, followed by separate entry points to hostels and academic buildings. The hostel premises are well-guarded and adequately lit. The university is situated in one of south Delhi’s busiest localities, ensuring steady movement of people and vehicles. We have not received any complaints of Eve-teasing or misbehaviour towards female students on campus,” said chief PRO Saima Saeed.

headline: Man held for murdering wife in Delhi’s Mangolpuri
content: New DelhiA 46-year-old man was arrested for allegedly strangling his 42-year-old wife to death over a domestic dispute at their house in Mangolpuri on Monday, police said on Wednesday.The accused worked as a cashier at a private multi-specialty hospital in Rohini. He and his wife had not been on speaking terms for the past nine years, despite living together, police said.During the altercation on Monday, the accused allegedly repeatedly insisted that she speak to him, but when she refused, he strangled her. “Her reluctance enraged the man, who allegedly strangled her to death with his bare hands”, said deputy commissioner of police (outer) Vikram Singh.According to the DCP, the accused panicked after seeing that his wife had died. He left the house, leaving her body inside and informed no one about the incident. When the couple’s three children returned home, they found their mother lying unconscious in a room.“The man returned home and pretended to be in shock as if he did not know what had happened to his wife. He rushed his wife to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital for medical attention in an auto-rickshaw. The attending doctors declared her dead on arrival. The hospital staff became suspicious when they found ligature marks around the woman’s neck and informed the police,” DCP Singh said.A police officer aware of the entire incident said that the hospital authorities suspected the involvement of the woman’s family members in her death by alleged strangulation. A team from the Raj Park police station questioned the family members. The woman’s husband objected and accused the personnel of harassing the family at the time of death.“The husband became the prime suspect after the personnel learnt about the couple’s domestic disputes and also found some abrasions on his body. He was interrogated and confronted with technical evidence, after which he confessed to strangling his wife,” the officer said.A case of murder was registered under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Raj Park police station, and the husband was arrested, the police said.

headline: IMD weather update: Chennai faces lightning warning, rain in Bengaluru, Delhi gets colder; check full forecast
content: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of thunderstorms and lightning in Chennai on Thursday, November 26. Bengaluru can expect light rain under mostly cloudy skies. Delhi is likely to see mist and a minimum temperature of 9°C. Hyderabad could see thunder and lightning, with the highest forecast temperature among metro cities. Delhi’s Safdarjung station is forecast to record a maximum of 27°C on Thursday. Friday could bring shallow fog and a lower high of 25°C. The minimum is expected to stay at 9°C on Friday. On November 25, the lowest temperature in the national capital was 10°C. The IMD forecasts moderate fog in the capital on Saturday and Sunday.Kolkata’s Alipore station can expect mainly clear skies, with temperatures between 17°C and 26°C. Friday’s forecast keeps both temperatures at the same levels. The city could warm on Saturday, with a high of 27°C and a low of 18°C. Those temperatures are expected to hold through Monday.Southern metrosAt Chennai’s Meenambakkam station, the temperature is forecast to range from 25°C to 31°C. Skies will be partly cloudy, with one or two spells of rain or thundershowers likely.The station recorded 4 mm of rain in the 24 hours ending Wednesday morning. The thunderstorm and lightning warning also applies on Friday. Light rain is forecast for Saturday.Bengaluru is likely to record a high of 27°C and a low of 20°C. The city’s forecast high is four degrees lower than Chennai’s. The city station recorded 9 mm of rain in the 24 hours ending Wednesday morning. Light rain could continue on Friday, with the maximum temperature reaching 28°C. The IMD expects partly-cloudy skies over the weekend.In Hyderabad, the temperature could reach 33°C and drop to 23°C on Thursday. The IMD expects partly cloudy skies and says thunder and lightning could develop. The city has no weather warning for Thursday. Similar conditions are forecast for Friday, before haze returns on Saturday.Western metrosMumbai and Pune will both see mainly clear skies and highs of 32°C on Thursday. Mumbai’s Santacruz station could record a low of 19°C. At Pune’s Shivajinagar station, the minimum could dip to 16°C.Both western cities recorded zero rainfall by Wednesday morning. Mumbai’s daytime high may climb to 34°C by Sunday. Pune’s maximum could fall to 30°C by then, with skies remaining mainly clear.Ahmedabad can expect mainly clear skies, with temperatures ranging from 16°C to 31°C on Thursday. The high is expected to reach 32°C on Friday and remain at that level through Monday. The IMD expects skies to remain mainly clear through December 1. The maximum could ease to 30°C that day.

headline: Delhi gives one-time age relief to TGT aspirants
content: New Delhi: Delhi govt has implemented a one-time relaxation in the upper age limit for recruitment of trained graduate teachers (TGTs), raising it from 30 to 32 years for male candidates and 40 years for female candidates. The directorate of education has sought the reopening of the online application portal to enable eligible candidates to apply.The decision pertains to the recruitment of TGTs under an advertisement issued by Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) on Oct 3, 2025. The proposal for relaxing the upper age limit was approved by the lieutenant governor and examined in consultation with Union Public Service Commission.The relaxation will be applicable to teaching posts in eight subjects — mathematics, English, social science, natural science, Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu and Punjabi — covering 16 post codes for male and female candidates.The decision follows months of representations by teaching aspirants seeking restoration of the earlier upper age limits of 32 years for men and 40 years for women. The age ceiling of 30 years prescribed in the Oct 2025 recruitment advertisement had rendered several aspirants ineligible.Candidates had been approaching various govt departments and public representatives since Jan 2025, seeking changes in the recruitment rules. In Jan, education minister Ashish Sood had assured aspirants of a one-time age relaxation. However, with the proposal awaiting approval, candidates continued to raise concerns over the delay. In April, aspirants wrote to Sood again, seeking restoration of the previous age limits and reopening of the DSSSB application portal, a report stated.“We took up the matter on priority as several aspirants were losing an opportunity to appear for recruitment examinations because these had not been conducted regularly,” Sood told TOI, adding “If recruitment examinations are not conducted regularly and vacancies are not advertised, candidates could cross the upper age limit without getting adequate opportunities to appear for examinations. It becomes even more difficult for women.”He added that the govt would work towards ensuring that recruitment was conducted regularly in the future, while the one-time relaxation was intended to address the grievances of aspirants affected by earlier delays. “The revision of recruitment rules dates back to 2023. And after that, the exams were not conducted regularly due to which many aspirants were left out. When we assumed office, we had decided we will solve this problem.”In a communication to DSSSB, director (education) clarified that the exercise would exclusively be for extending the benefit of the approved one-time age relaxation and would not be treated as an extension of the original application period. The age of candidates will be calculated with reference to Nov 7, 2025, the original closing date for applications, after allowing the approved relaxation.All other eligibility conditions, including those relating to educational qualifications, Central Teacher Eligibility Test and category or community certificates, will remain unchanged. Candidates will have to meet these requirements in accordance with the cut-off dates prescribed in the original advertisement.Union ministry of education has also conveyed its approval to the proposal submitted by the department on July 27. It has advised Delhi govt to consider revising the upper age limit for all teaching posts in its schools in line with the recruitment rules for corresponding positions in Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Delhi to get 40 more arogya mandirs next month, 2 new hospitals in 2027: CM
content: New Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that 40 more Ayushman Arogya Mandirs will become operational next month and two new hospitals with a total of over 1,800 beds in North and West Delhi will be operational next year. Rekha Gupta: From the wings to the centre storyline 1 Also read | Over 6,500 lung cancer cases reported in prominent Delhi hospitals in six years; one death every three days https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/over-6500-lung-cancer-cases-reported-in-prominent-delhi-hospitals-in-six-years-one-death-every-three-days/article71741262.ece The two hospitals are under construction, and one is likely to be operational in the first half of the year and the second later on, according to officials. The CM said that the government is undertaking extensive efforts to expand healthcare infrastructure and improve access to medical treatment in the capital, ranging from the construction of major hospitals to strengthening primary healthcare services. Working towards enhancing quality of healthcare services in Delhi govt. hospitals: CM Working towards enhancing quality of healthcare services in Delhi govt. hospitals: CM Gupta unveils new facilities at G.B. Pant Hospital, says they will benefit patients from Delhi and other States Working towards enhancing quality of healthcare services in Delhi govt. hospitals: CM storyline 1 Earlier in the day, Ms. Gupta reviewed various projects of the Health Department at the Delhi Secretariat on Wednesday and directed officials to ensure that all projects related to hospitals and healthcare facilities are completed within the stipulated timelines. “The Delhi Government aims to ensure accessible, quality and timely healthcare services for every citizen of the capital. Expanding healthcare infrastructure is not limited to building new hospitals; it also means ensuring that patients receive better treatment, modern medical equipment, adequate doctors and other healthcare personnel at hospitals. The government is also strengthening primary healthcare services so that people do not have to travel long distances for treatment of common illnesses,” the Chief Minister said. She also directed officials to ensure that there are no unnecessary delays at any level in healthcare projects and that all public welfare works are carried out with full responsibility, promptness and sensitivity. AAP accuses Delhi govt. of giving hospitals’ construction work to private companies AAP accuses Delhi govt. of giving hospitals’ construction work to private companies AAP accuses Delhi govt. of giving hospitals’ construction work to private companies storyline 1 Hospitals in Siraspur, Hastal The Chief Minister said that the 1,164-bed hospital in Siraspur of north Delhi is ready and the procurement of medical equipment for the hospital is underway and is targeted for completion by the end of January. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal is also nearing completion and it, too, will become operational next year, she added. “The opening of both hospitals will improve access to healthcare in the surrounding areas and help reduce the patient load on existing hospitals,” she said. The CM said that a total of 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are being developed across Delhi, of which 415 are currently operational. “The government aims to open another 40 centres next month. Plans are also underway to introduce services in two shifts at Arogya Mandirs receiving a higher number of patients, ensuring timely treatment at the local level,” she said. The government is also targeting the opening of 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on December 25. Madipur, Jwalapuri hospitals by 2028 Ms. Gupta said the government is also developing hospitals with 691 beds each in Madipur and Jwalapuri to be completed by 2028. The Madipur hospital is being built at a cost of Rs 466.50 crore, while the Jwalapuri hospital has an estimated cost of Rs 484.04 crore. In addition, maternal and child healthcare facilities are being expanded at existing hospitals. A 463-bed maternal and child healthcare block is being developed at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini. Its OPD block is ready for inauguration. “A 270-bed maternal and child healthcare block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are also nearing completion. The process of making these facilities operational shortly is underway,” an official statement said.

headline: Two hospitals with 1,815 beds to become operational next year: Delhi CM
content: Two major hospitals in Siraspur and Hastal, together adding 1,815 beds, are expected to become operational next year, while the Delhi Government plans to open 40 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month to strengthen healthcare services across the Capital, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said on Wednesday.Reviewing Health Department projects at the Delhi Secretariat, the Chief Minister directed officials to ensure timely completion of hospital projects and warned that negligence and unnecessary delays would not be tolerated.Gupta said the 1,164-bed hospital in Siraspur was ready, with procurement of medical equipment underway and scheduled to be completed by the end of January. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal was also nearing completion. Both facilities are expected to improve access to healthcare in their respective areas and reduce the burden on existing hospitals.The government is also aiming to open 40 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, coinciding with the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Of the 1,139 centres being developed across Delhi, 415 are currently operational. The government is also considering running two shifts at centres witnessing a high patient footfall.The Chief Minister said the government was simultaneously expanding hospital infrastructure and medical education facilities. Hospitals with 691 beds each are being developed in Madipur and Jwalapuri, with both projects scheduled for completion by 2028. The Madipur project has an estimated cost of Rs 466.50 crore, while the Jwalapuri hospital is being built at a cost of Rs 484.04 crore.Maternal and child healthcare facilities are also being expanded. A 463-bed block is being developed at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini, where the OPD block is ready for inauguration. A 270-bed maternal and child healthcare block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are also nearing completion.On medical education, Gupta said the government planned to establish medical colleges at Indira Gandhi Hospital in Dwarka and Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital, each with 150 MBBS seats.The government is also working to increase MBBS seats at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and seats at the Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70.PWD plans Rs 73L upgrades at five Arogya MandirsAlongside the new developments, the Delhi Government has also proposed civil, electrical and mechanical upgrades at five Ayushman Arogya Mandir sites, with the Public Works Department inviting bids for works worth a combined Rs 73.07 lakh.Four centres - Bamnoli, Jhatikara, Polyclinic Najafgarh and Rangpuri Pahadi Milkpur - are covered under a Rs 27.13-lakh package, with a 60-day work period. A separate Rs 45.94-lakh project covers civil and electrical renovation at Baraat Ghar in Badarpur Khaddar, with a 90-day work period.The tender for the four-centre package has been invited again after an earlier procurement exercise was issued on November 3, whose deadline was extended to November 18. The fresh invitation, published on November 23 and marked as a recall, sets December 3 as the new deadline.

headline: Indigenous Drone-Swarm Killer 'Bhargavastra' Passes Pokaran Trials
content: New Delhi:Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) has successfully designed, developed and integrated Bhargavastra, a Vehicle-Mounted Counter Swarm Drone System (VMCSDS), and completed its in-house development trials at Pokaran field firing ranges from November 20 to 24. The system offers an effective, two-layer defence against enemy drone swarms, with the capability to engage multiple drones simultaneously. Bhargavastra is India's first indigenously designed and developed two-layer vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system, combining air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to provide an integrated solution against this emerging threat. VMCSDS has been developed indigenously on specific qualitative requirements given by the Indian Army through a PSO from the MoD (Defence Production) issued on July 09, 2024, with PDC of March 31, 2027, to a number of private sector companies for developing VMCSDS under Make II (Buy Indian IDDM) as version-1 using rockets. The PSO specifies realisation of 01 set as prototype and 12 sets of deliverables after successful completion of prototype demonstration. Going beyond the Indian Army's initial requirement of a rocket-based Version-I system, SDAL has independently developed an advanced Version-II featuring guided micro-missiles. These missiles use autonomous guidance and an infrared (IR) seeker for precise target engagement. headline: Ludhiana: Couple booked for duping man of nearly  ₹15 lakh on pretext of govt job
content: The Moti Nagar police have booked a husband-wife duo for cheating a man of ₹14.98 lakh on the pretext of securing him a government job.The accused have been identified as Gagandeep Kaur and her husband, Pankaj Kumar, residents of Mansa.The case was registered following a complaint by Raman Kumar, a resident of Sartaj Nagar on Noorwala Road. In his complaint to senior police officials, Raman alleged that the couple had lured him with the promise of arranging a government job and collected ₹14.98 lakh from him in instalments on different occasions.However, despite receiving the entire amount, the accused allegedly failed to arrange the promised employment and refused to return the money even after a considerable period.Raman lodged a complaint with the police on July 27 After conducting an inquiry into the allegations, the Moti Nagar police registered an FIR under Sections 316(2), 318(4) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the couple.ASI Sethi Kumar stated that efforts are on for the arrest of the accused.The complainant added that the accused allegedly called him to a hotel parking area on Chandigarh Road, where they assured him of arranging a government job and initially took ₹9.50 lakh from him. They later sent him a fake appointment letter and collected the remaining amount in installments on different dates, taking the total sum to ₹14.98 lakh. The complainant alleged that whenever he enquired about the status of the job, the accused kept putting him off with one excuse or another. Eventually, they refused to return the money as well, leaving him with no option but to approach the police and lodge a complaint.

headline: Ludhiana: Agri varsity experts call for intensified efforts to achieve zero stubble burning
content: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) has called for intensified research and farmer outreach to promote scientific crop residue management and achieve zero stubble burning across Punjab. The issue took centre stage during the biannual Research and Extension Council meeting chaired by director of extension education MS Bhullar in Ludhiana on Thursday, with around 130 senior officials and scientists in attendance.Expressing concern over persistent farm fires and depleting groundwater levels, Bhullar urged scientists to step up field-level interventions. He noted that while stubble burning incidents have declined, achieving complete elimination requires sustained efforts. He also stressed curbing the indiscriminate use of water, promoting sustainable farming practices, and encouraging kitchen gardening—cultivating fruits, vegetables, and oilseeds—as a supplementary income source.Plant Clinic in-charge and meeting coordinator GS Makkar said the biannual council evaluates newly introduced crop varieties and technologies to offer practical solutions to farmers. During the session, school of organic farming director SS Walia and additional director of extension education PS Sandhu reviewed minutes from the previous meeting, while additional director Rajinder Singh presented the action-taken report. Additional director of communication KS Sangha added that feedback shared by participating farmers from across the state would help strengthen PAU’s research and extension programmes.Home science meet on turning research into social impact organisedThe 36th Biennial Conference of the Home Science Association of India (HSAI) commenced at PAU on Thursday on the theme “Innovation to Impact: Harnessing the Potential of Home and Community Sciences for Social Transformation”. Over 250 academicians and scientists are participating in the three-day conclave covering textile innovations, nutritional security, community engagement, family well-being, and resource efficiency. Inaugurating the event, PAU vice-chancellor Harvinder Singh Dhaliwal stressed inter-university collaboration, while guest of honour Padma Shri Rajni Bector encouraged youth entrepreneurship. Keynote speaker Anupa Siddhu urged translating academic research into practical community solutions, alongside addresses by college of community science dean Kiran Bains, postgraduate studies dean VS Hans, HSAI president Madhu Sharan, and ICAR emeritus professor Suman Singh.PAU student bags best thesis awardJaspreet Singh, an MSc student in PAU’s department of climate change and agricultural meteorology, has won the Prof PSN Sastry Best MSc Thesis Award from the Association of Agrometeorologists (AAM), Anand. Conferred during the International Conference on Agrometeorological Intelligence for Digital Agriculture (INAGMET-2026) at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, the award recognises his thesis on spatio-temporal projections of temperature and rainfall across Punjab using CMIP6 climate models. Conducted at PAU’s Regional Research Station, Ballowal Saunkhri, under the guidance of agrometeorologist Navneet Kaur, the study provides key insights into future climate risks to support sustainable, climate-resilient agricultural planning in the state.

headline: Grit on display: Para athletes shine on Day 2 of state-level games in Ludhiana
content: State-level Para Khedan Watan Punjab Diyan entered its second day in Ludhiana on Thursday, with athletes from across Punjab competing in track-and-field events including discus throw, shot put, club throw, and javelin. Cabinet minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian attended the meet and interacted with participants, lauding their determination and urging them to pursue sporting excellence despite physical challenges.District sports officer Mandeep Kaushal, Punjab Para Sports Association general secretary Jaspreet Singh, association coach Gagandeep Singh, and athletics coach Sanjeev Sharma were also present on the occasion.In the under-19 boys’ discus throw event, Avtar Singh of Fatehgarh Sahib secured first place in the F51 category, followed by Rambir Singh of SAS Nagar in second place and Kirandeep Singh of Faridkot in third. In the F54 category, Baljinder Singh of Muktsar Sahib won the first position, while Surinder Singh of Ludhiana finished second and Salinder Singh of Muktsar Sahib came third.In the F56 category, Bikramjit Singh of Amritsar claimed the top position, Ravi Dutt of Rupnagar finished second and Sarabjit Singh of Ludhiana secured third place.The under-19 boys’ shot put competition in the F52 category saw Sanjay Kumar Sharma and Shashi Kumar, both from SAS Nagar, finish first and second, respectively. Rajinder Kumar of Rupnagar secured third place. In the F54 category, Malwinder Singh of Muktsar Sahib won first place, while Gurdeep Singh of Jalandhar finished second.In the club throw event in the F51 category, Avtar Singh of Fatehgarh Sahib secured the first position, Rambir Singh of SAS Nagar came second and Harpreet Singh of Gurdaspur finished third.The women’s competitions also saw athletes deliver strong performances. In the above-19 age group, Mandeep Kaur of Amritsar won the discus throw event in the F55 and F56 categories. Amandeep Kaur of Barnala secured second place, while Harsimrat Kaur of Ludhiana finished third.In the shot put event across the F55, F56 and F57 categories, Lovepreet Kaur of Patiala won first place, Darshana Devi of Rupnagar came second and Charanjit Kaur of Moga finished third.In the javelin throw event in the same categories, Amandeep Kaur of Barnala secured the top position, followed by Rajwant Kaur of Ludhiana in second place and Labh Kaur of Fatehgarh Sahib in third.

headline: Ludhiana: Residents cry foul as garbage piles up in Model Town, Dugri
content: Towering heaps of garbage dumped in the open across several stretches of Model Town and Dugri have left residents battling severe unhygienic conditions, foul stench, and recurring health scares, with locals alleging persistent civic apathy despite repeated complaints.Residents stated that key residential and institutional areas have turned into dumping grounds.Social activist Arvind Sharma said, “Residents of Model Town Extension D Block, near the cremation ground, have been suffering due to heaps of garbage lying there for several years. The situation is equally alarming near the municipal corporation’s garbage compactor alongside Dugri Canal, where employees allegedly dump waste in the open.”Highlighting similar situation in Dugri Phase-2 behind a private school, Model Town market welfare society secretary Jaswinder Singh Shammi said his young children frequently fall ill due to the stench and unhygienic surroundings, adding that a dead cow was also recently found dumped at the spot.Locals alleged that neither the municipal corporation (MC) nor the health department has initiated permanent waste-management measures, even after residents approached the human rights commission.The open dumping continues just days after the civic body launched a special garbage-lifting drive to curb illegal waste disposal, during which several private collectors were allegedly caught dumping refuse in the open.The campaign also ran into resistance in Sherpur Kalan on November 24, where an MC sanitary inspector and his team were allegedly assaulted and threatened during a waste-lifting operation on 100-foot Road.MC health officer Dr Vipal Malhotra said, “The private garbage collectors working in these areas dump their waste in the open at night. We will get these spots cleared and try to catch those dumping waste.”

headline: Structural failure fears: Railways alerts MC over ‘aging’ Jagraon Bridge
content: Slug: Unsafe for heavy vehicular trafficBQ: The work on strengthening the bridge is a priority and will be done as soon as possible – Damanjit Singh Mann, MC commissionerThe Railways has alerted the Municipal Corporation Ludhiana (MCL) that the 51-year-old Jagraon Bridge is unsafe for heavy vehicular traffic, warning that continued movement of heavy vehicles could trigger a structural failure.In a “most urgent” communication on November 7 to the MCL commissioner, the assistant divisional engineer (ADEN), Northern Railway, Ludhiana, Manoj Kumar Meena, flagged serious structural defects in the road over bridge (ROB) in front of Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib.According to the letter to the MCL chief, a railway inspection found wide cracks have developed in the lower portions of several bridge piers, while minor cracks have appeared at the top where the bridge bearings rest. Officials also noted that reinforcement steel in the abutments has become exposed at the base, and the foundation and substructure—including some piers—are showing signs of deterioration.The letter noted that the ROB was constructed in 1975, and has now deteriorated considerably due to ageing and continuous vehicular loading, urging the civic body to take immediate precautionary measures to avert a risk to public safety.Built with an estimated service life of 40 to 50 years, the bridge handled around 20,000 vehicles daily in 1975—a load that has now surged exponentially. Concerns over the key corridor have been mounting since a retaining wall of the bridge ramp collapsed during last year’s monsoon.Uncontrolled vegetation on the retaining walls, bird feeding, rodent activity, and issues linked to the nearby fish market have further compounded maintenance challenges.“We already witnessed the collapse of a retaining wall on the bridge ramp last year during the rainy season. Uncontrolled vegetation growing on retaining walls, along with issues arising from bird feeding, the fish market and rodent activity, further add to the maintenance concerns. The MCL and the concerned authorities must treat this as a priority infrastructure and public safety issue,” said member, Punjab State Road Safety Council, Rahul Verma.He stressed that rather than opting for temporary repairs, the MCL should engage reputed technical institutions such as RITES or IIT Roorkee to conduct a comprehensive structural assessment and prepare a long-term plan for the strengthening, rehabilitating, and widening of the bridge.“The involvement of the Punjab government and the department of local government is essential to ensure the necessary technical guidance, interdepartmental coordination and financial support. We must act today to secure this vital infrastructure for Ludhiana’s future, rather than wait for another major incident,” he cautioned.Following the railway alert, social activist Arvind Sharma, filed an urgent complaint with the Punjab State Human Rights Commission (PSHRC) chairperson on Thursday, alleging administrative negligence.Pointing out that active railway lines run directly beneath the bridge and Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib is located nearby, Sharma warned that any collapse could lead to a catastrophic accident endangering thousands of commuters and train passengers. He alleged that authorities were delaying concrete safety measures in the name of expert consultations.Sharma urged the commission to seek an immediate action-taken report from the MCL commissioner, order an independent safety audit, restrict or suspend heavy traffic if warranted, and fix responsibility for any delay. Copies of the complaint have also been sent to the Punjab governor, the local government minister, and senior officials of the local government department.Municipal Corporation (MC) commissioner Damanjit Singh Mann inspected the bridge on Wednesday and issued orders to expedite the overall project for adding strength to the existing structure.The civic body is working on a project for strengthening retaining walls, drainage, removal of wild growth and deep-rooted trees and Guru Nanak Dev Engineering College has been roped in for consultancy.The MC commissioner said, “The work on strengthening the bridge is a priority and will be done as soon as possible”.

headline: Ludhiana civic body likely to miss Nov deadline for central e-bus project
content: The Municipal Corporation Ludhiana (MCL) is likely to miss the November deadline for completing one of the two proposed e-bus depots, as a 3.5-acre plot at Ghora Colony remains partially occupied by the police, which has parked seized vehicles on the land.Despite repeated requests to the police to vacate the site, the civic body is yet to get possession of the entire plot. The MCL, however, has started construction on the available portion, with around 20% of the work completed so far.Superintending engineer Sham Lal Gupta, who is overseeing the project, said the civic body was in touch with the police authorities to get the land vacated.The two depots are being developed under the Centre’s PM-eBus Sewa scheme to support a planned fleet of 100 electric buses for Ludhiana. The Ghora Colony depot, which will accommodate 70 buses, has an estimated cost of ₹12.33 crore, while the 30-bus-capacity depot on Hambran Road is being developed at a cost of ₹5.82 crore.Both facilities are to be equipped with bus sheds, charging stations, maintenance workshops and administrative buildings. Each depot will have a charging station capable of charging 30 buses at a time. The Hambran Road depot is scheduled to be completed by November 30, said SE Sham Lal Gupta.Reacting to the delay, BJP state general secretary Anil Sarin criticised the AAP government and the MC, alleging that the project had suffered due to administrative apathy. He said the Ghora Colony depot, being built at a cost of ₹12.33 crore, was only 20% complete, with work stalled for months. The Hambran Road depot, costing ₹5.82 crore, had also missed its November deadline. Sarin further claimed that the civic body is yet to finalise bus routes, stoppages and timetables for the seven proposed routes spanning 152 km.Gupta said that the Union government had already selected a contractor for the buses and the civic body will start receiving the buses by next year.DCP (rural) Gursewak Singh said, “We will talk to the municipal corporation and find out a solution.”

headline: AAP puts women voters at centre with ‘Maawan Dheeyan da Maan’ pitch for 2027 Punjab polls
content: The Aam Aadmi Party on Thursday sounded the bugle for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, putting women voters at the centre of its campaign while projecting Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann as “Maawan Dheeyan da Maan” — the pride and respect of mothers and daughters. The slogan is a play on the word “Maan”, which in Punjabi means pride and also respect, and sounds same as the CM's surname. The messaging was hard to miss as it was splashed across multiple hoarding and banners put up on highways and roads leading to Moga where the party held its Khushhaal Punjab rally. Many billboards that until a few days ago carried Mann's photo with slogans of “Lokan da CM (people's chief minister)” and “Imaandaar CM (honest CM)” were replaced with the new slogan, signalling party's sharper focus on woman voters ahead of the polls. The slogan was also the dominant feature on the main stage at the rally. With more than 97 lakh women voters in Punjab, the rally was built around the AAP’s outreach to the 'aadhi abaadi' (the woman voters who make for half the population). Woman beneficiaries of government's flagship Maawan Dheeyan Satkaar Yojana, under which they receive Rs 1,000 a month, shared the stage with Mann and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal. Woman beneficiaries of newly issued Smart Ration Cards too shared the stage and narrated how the government’s schemes were helping their families. Mann and Kejriwal distributed Rasoi kits to some of the beneficiaries selected from among 10 lakh new Smart Ration Card holders. The kits, having Mann's photo on the bag and distributed under the Punjab Smart Ration Card scheme, contain mustard oil, pulses, sugar, turmeric and salt, besides monthly wheat for eligible families under the National Food Security Act. Kejriwal made it clear that Mann would be the face of the AAP’s 2027 campaign and appealed to women to vote for him. He also asked them to persuade the men in their families to back the AAP. “You (women) should tell your husbands, fathers, sons, brothers and even men in in-laws' family to vote for Mann. Tell them that Mann also gave you free 300 units of power, water for irrigating fields and good schools which are benefitting entire family. Tell your son that he gave 71,000 government jobs. The vote of every Punjab woman should go to Mann,” he said. “Mann’s government has touched the dreams of every common household in Punjab, especially women. Grandmothers who wanted to visit Vrindavan are being taken on free Tirath Yatra in AC buses. Majority women are getting Rs 1,000 a month in their accounts,” Kejriwal said. He acknowledged that the women’s scheme had been delayed, attributing it to the financial condition of the state when the AAP came to power. “People say we delayed implementing Maawan Dheeyan Scheme, and I admit it is true. But that is because previous government handed us empty coffers. We had to fill them again to give promised money to our sisters and mothers,” he said. He said, "Five years ago, when I came asking for votes, I gave you some guarantees. They were called 'Kejriwal ki guarantee'. Today I am here because my younger brother Bhagwant Mann has fulfilled all of Kejriwal ki guarantees”. Kejriwal also alleged that the BJP-led Centre had tried to obstruct the scheme by withholding Punjab’s funds. "They tried in various ways to stop the scheme, but Mann Sahib is very strong. He did not let it stop," he said The AAP chief also slammed the Centre, alleging inflation made everything in the country expensive. "At a time when the Modi government has made life so expensive, Mann has provided women of Punjab with Rs 1,000 to give them some relief," he said. He linked the AAP’s women-focused pitch to its other welfare measures, asking women to tell their families about 300 units of free power, irrigation water, schools and the 71,000 jobs claimed by the government. Mann, too, cast his relationship with woman voters in familial terms, saying he was the “brother of lakhs of sisters and son of lakhs of mothers”. “My alliance is with the mothers and sisters of Punjab, and with 3 crore people of Punjab,” Mann said. He added that he could have pursued a lucrative career in films in Mumbai but chose public life, saying money was not everything. Kejriwal said Opposition leaders had called the Maawan Dheeyan scheme a “wastage of money”, and warned voters against the Congress, Akali Dal and BJP, claiming that these parties would discontinue the Mann government's existing schemes if voted to power. He said people in Delhi were "regretting" voting for the BJP after it "shut down" all schemes introduced by the AAP government. At the rally, which AAP claimed was attended by over 2 lakh people, the AAP leaders presented the state government's five-year report card, highlighting its achievements.
