headline: DIG Bhullar bribery case: Former hockey Olympian Gagan Ajit Singh appears before ED in Chandigarh
content: Former hockey Olympian and Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh appeared before the Enforcement Directorate (ED) at its Sector 17 office in Chandigarh on Thursday in connection with its investigation into suspended DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar and alleged intermediary Krishanu Sharda.Singh reached the ED office at 2.30 pm and left at 6.30 pm. Speaking to media persons after the questioning, Singh said he had arrived during lunchtime and was later called to join the investigation, during which officials asked him some basic questions.“The ED officials asked me about my relationship with Krishanu Sharda. We have a common sporting background. I told them that Sharda was also a hockey player and I have played hockey as well. A couple of other questions were also asked. If they summon me again, I will appear,” he said.Several serving and retired Punjab bureaucrats and police officers have also been summoned by the ED in connection with the investigation. These include IAS officers Kumar Rahul and Neeru Katyal Gupta, IPS officer Swapan Sharma, PCS officer Anand Sagar Sharma, and retired bureaucrats Gurpreet Sapra and Arun Sekhri.

headline: Record turnout endorsement of honest govt, says Punjab CM at Moga rally
content: Moga (Punjab), Nov 26 (IANS) Declaring the record-breaking turnout at the ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ Maha Rally of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government here, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday said that when intentions “are honest and promises translate into tangible results, people do not need to be mobilised through hollow slogans”. “From zero electricity bills and over 77,000 government jobs secured without bribes to canal water reaching the tail ends, free healthcare cover of up to Rs 10 lakh and financial assistance for women,” he said, “the government’s work has given people a reason to rally behind its vision”. The gathering, the Chief Minister asserted, “sends an unmistakable political message: Punjab has moved beyond the empty promises of the past and is choosing development, progress and prosperity”. With the 2027 Assembly elections on the horizon, the rally also saw CM Mann sounding the poll bugle, thanking the people of Punjab for their overwhelming love and trust. Addressing the rally, CM Mann said, “Today, I want to speak directly to the people of Punjab about the work we have done and the promises we have fulfilled. Those who ruled this state for decades must also tell the people what they did for Punjab. They had years in power, but the state continued to face problems. Our government is presenting its report card before the people because we believe that a government must be answerable to the public.” Launching a sharp attack on the Shiromani Akali Dal, the Congress and BJP, the Chief Minister said they have ruled Punjab for years and have taken turns in power. “They blamed one another, made promises and then forgot the people after elections. Now they are coming together because they are worried about the work being done by the Aam Aadmi Party government. The people of Punjab know their history and will not be misled by their new political arrangements.”

headline: AIL Mohali Celebrates Constitution Day with Legal Awareness Session at Gurukul World School
content: AIL Mohali Celebrates Constitution Day with Legal Awareness Session at Gurukul World School Mohali, 26 November 2026: To commemorate Constitution Day, the Legal Aid Cell of the Army Institute of Law (AIL), Mohali, under the guidance of Principal Prof. (Dr.) Rashmi Khorana Nagpal and Registrar Col. Gurdev Singh (Retd.), organised a special legal awareness session for students of Gurukul World School, Mohali. The interactive session focused on the foundational principles of Indian democracy, introducing students to the significance of the Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties enshrined in the Constitution of India. The AIL team encouraged young learners to understand their constitutional rights and responsibilities and appreciate their role as informed and responsible citizens. Bridging constitutional principles with contemporary challenges, AIL students also highlighted important aspects of cybersecurity and digital awareness. The discussion covered online safety, responsible digital expression and data protection, explaining their relevance to the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19 and the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, including the Right to Privacy, under Article 21 of the Constitution. To foster active learning, the discussion was followed by a spirited constitutional quiz competition, where top-performing students were awarded gift hampers for their sharp legal acumen. The event concluded with the presentation of a memento to the school Principal- Ms. Poonamjit kaur as a token of gratitude, marking a successful collaboration coordinated by AIL Faculty Coordinators Dr. Deepinder Kaur Gill, Dr. Manveer Kaur, and Ms. Arshpreet Kaur in nurturing constitutional and digital awareness among the nation's future citizens.

headline: Ahead of 2027 poll, Punjab sees major police reshuffle: 305 officers transferred in 5 days
content: Amid a crackdown and drive against gangsters and drug peddlers, the past five days have witnessed a major reshuffle in the police department ahead of the 2027 Assembly election.Barring a few district heads, over 305 officers, including 274 ASPs and DSPs and 31 IPS and PPS officers, were transferred in two major exercises within five days.The major reshuffle in the police department was not a routine exercise. Rather, the transfers followed directions issued by the Election Commission (EC) on October 27 to five poll-bound states, including Punjab, to reorganise the deployment of officers associated with election management.The first major exercise was carried out on November 21, when 274 DSP-level officers were transferred. This was followed by the transfer of 25 IPS and six PPS officers on November 25, including three Police Commissioners and 11 SSPs.EC had asked Punjab, Goa, Manipur, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand to complete the transfer exercise and submit compliance reports by November 30.Under the guidelines, officers directly connected with election-related duties cannot be posted in their home districts. Those who have completed three years in a district during the preceding four years, or would complete the prescribed tenure by March 31, 2027, were also required to be shifted, subject to the applicable provisions.The latest instructions have also widened the scope of the exercise by covering officers who were deployed in the same Assembly constituency or district during the 2022 Assembly election or a subsequent bypolls. The restriction applies to specified election officials and police personnel from the rank of inspector and sub-inspector upwards.This is a significant departure from the earlier practice, under which the transfer restrictions largely covered officers deployed during the preceding Lok Sabha election or subsequent bypolls. The revised guidelines have consequently brought a much larger section of the civil and police administration under scrutiny.The November 25 reshuffle brought substantial changes at the senior level. Swapan Sharma, who was Police Commissioner, Ludhiana, was posted as DIG, Ropar Range, while Satinder Singh, earlier Police Commissioner, Jalandhar, was moved to Ludhiana. Gurpreet Singh Bhullar was appointed Police Commissioner, Jalandhar, and Kuldeep Singh Chahal took over as Police Commissioner, Amritsar.Several range-level postings were also changed, including those of DIGs in Patiala, Ferozepur, Faridkot, Bathinda and the Border Range. Eleven SSP-level postings were part of the exercise.Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar had recently urged EC to keep officers summoned by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in corruption-related cases away from the election process. He also demanded that officers whose names had surfaced in such investigations be removed from posts involving direct public dealing.

headline: AAP kicks off Punjab poll campaign; Kejriwal says fulfilled every single promise
content: Moga, Nov 26 (PTI) Launching his party’s campaign here for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday said the Bhagwant Mann government fulfilled every single promise it made and urged people to vote for AAP to make Mann chief minister again. He warned voters against the Congress, Akali Dal and BJP and claimed that these parties would discontinue the Mann government’s existing schemes if voted to power, saying people in Delhi were “regretting” voting for the BJP after it “shut down” all schemes introduced by the AAP government. Kejriwal was addressing AAP’s ‘Punjab Kushhaal Rally’ where other party leaders presented the state government’s five-year report card, highlighting its achievements. On the occasion, Chief Minister Mann, his cabinet colleagues and party MLAs were also present. Talking about the ‘Mawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojna’ scheme, he urged women voters to persuade the men in their families to vote for AAP. Looking at the gathering, Kejriwal claimed that there must be over two lakh people. “I think such a big rally has never happened in Punjab’s history,” he said. “Five years ago, when I came asking for votes, I gave you some guarantees. They were called ‘Kejriwal ki guarantee’. Today I am here because my younger brother Bhagwant Mann has fulfilled all of ‘Kejriwal ki guarantees’. We have fulfilled every single promise,” he said.

headline: AAP sounds poll bugle in Moga, Kejriwal-Mann promise all welfare schemes will continue
content: The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Wednesday sounded the poll bugle for the upcoming Assembly election with its ‘Khushhaal Punjab Rally’ at Matwani village on the Moga-Ludhiana highway in Moga district. The event was officially billed as a “Smart Ration Card Distribution Function” organised by the state government, where Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann launched the scheme and distributed smart cards and free ration kits to a few beneficiaries.The rally witnessed a massive turnout, with the AAP leadership attacking political opponents, particularly the revived SAD-BJP alliance, while projecting the Mann government’s welfare schemes as its principal electoral plank. The party has already announced 71 of the 117 candidates, much ahead of other parties.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, who addressed a gathering in Punjab after a gap of five months, appealed to women voters and guaranteed that all existing welfare schemes would continue if the party returned to power. He accused the BJP-led Central Government of attempting to stop the monthly financial assistance of Rs 1,000 and Rs 1,500 to women under ‘Maawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana’.Addressing Mann as his “younger brother”, Kejriwal claimed that more than two lakh people had attended the rally. Invoking the significance of November 26, he said it was the day Dr BR Ambedkar’s Constitution was adopted and AAP was formed in 2012. “The Constitution is being crushed today. It is an indication from God that this responsibility has been given to the AAP,” he said.Recalling the 2022 Assembly election, Kejriwal said he had sought votes by giving guarantees rather than making false promises and credited Mann with fulfilling those commitments. Blaming the Modi government for inflation, he said the monthly assistance was providing women financial independence and helping them manage household expenses.Two women beneficiaries were also invited to the stage to share their experiences of the scheme and explain how the assistance helped them meet household and medical expenses.Kejriwal alleged that the Congress intended to discontinue the scheme, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi had described welfare benefits as ‘free revadis’. Referring to the AAP government’s initiatives in Delhi, he alleged that BJP had stopped schemes such as free pilgrimage facilities and mohalla clinics after coming to power there.“No one has the courage to stop any scheme. All schemes will continue,” he said, assuring women that all welfare schemes would continue if AAP returned to power. He urged them to vote for the party and persuade men in their families to support it. He cited free electricity, improved canal water supply, daytime power supply for agriculture, free treatment and more than 70,000 merit-based government jobs as achievements of the Mann government.Later, Mann launched a scathing attack on the revived SAD-BJP alliance, accusing the two parties of betraying Punjab’s interests and joining hands again for political gains. He said the Akalis formed the alliance just to secure a Cabinet berth in the Central Government for Harsimrat Kaur Badal and to pass the three farm laws.He also targeted Congress leaders over their alleged infighting.Referring to the farmers’ agitation against the three farm laws, Mann accused the Badal family of initially supporting the legislation and changing its stand only after protests intensified. He also questioned the SAD leadership’s alleged silence on Chandigarh, river waters, Bandi Singhs and the Anandpur Sahib Resolution after renewing its alliance with BJP.Targeting SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, Mann recalled the party’s earlier allegations against BJP over interference in Sikh religious institutions and questioned its decision to share a political platform with the same party. He also took a dig at BJP’s anti-drug campaign and made remarks about Sukhbir Badal’s late mother, his wife Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal and brother-in-law Bikram Singh Majithia.Without making any fresh announcement, Mann listed the government’s achievements, including free electricity, improved canal water supply, Aam Aadmi Clinics (renamed Ayushman Arogya Kendras), merit-based government jobs and financial assistance to women. He claimed that more than 70,000 government jobs had been provided without bribes and that his government had curbed corruption.AAP Punjab affairs in-charge Manish Sisodia and state president Aman Arora also addressed the gathering. No AAP leader targeted Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) in his speech.The pandal was packed and the public cheered during Bhagwant Mann’s speech. Moga MLA Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora and Dharamkot MLA Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose, who have been summoned by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on November 26 and 27 respectively, were also present.Meanwhile, a worker manning the coffee machine at the press gallery allegedly died after the machine exploded before the start of the rally. However, neither AAP nor the district administration or the police officially confirmed the death. AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said one person had been injured, but some eyewitnesses claimed that the worker had died on the spot due to a severe head injury. None of the speakers on the stage mentioned him in their speeches.Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, who has not been fielded from Lambi this time, was sitting in the front row on the stage. AAP’s Bathinda Mayor Padamjeet Singh Mehta had put up hoardings all the way to the rally venue, located about 80 km from Bathinda. The rally led to a huge traffic jam lasting over two hours on the Moga-Ludhiana highway.Famous Punjabi singer Kulwinder Billa enthralled the audience.

headline: Moga becomes Punjab's election launchpad as AAP takes on SAD-BJP alliance
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday formally launched its campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections with a mega 'Khushhaal Punjab' rally in Moga, where national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, and Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann sought another term for the party by highlighting the state government's performance and welfare initiatives.Organised on the party's 14th foundation day across nearly 116 acres, the rally witnessed what AAP claimed was a gathering of 1.5 lakh to two lakh people, with Kejriwal describing it as an unprecedented congregation in Punjab's history.The rally, held at Matwani village, also served as a platform for the Mann government to present its 5-year report card and launch the distribution of smart ration cards to nearly six lakh beneficiaries.Food and Civil Supplies Minister Lal Chand Kataruchakk said the initiative would ensure transparent and corruption-free delivery of ration to eligible families.While the government described the programme as an official state-level function, its political messaging was unmistakable, with both Kejriwal and Mann making a direct pitch for the 2027 elections.The event also came amid preparations for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed visit to Moga on December 8, when he is expected to share the platform with leaders associated with the BJP-SAD alliance.MANN ATTACKS TEAM BJP-SADMann used the occasion to target the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP combine, recalling the 2007-2017 period of their governments and accusing them of allowing drugs and gangsterism to flourish in Punjab.He said people had experienced the alliance's "goondagardi" and contrasted it with what he described as AAP's clean governance.Taking aim at the December 8 gathering, Mann questioned the political understanding between leaders who had previously criticised one another.He referred to Bikram Majithia, Sukhbir Badal, Ravneet Bittu and Sunil Jakhar, accusing them of changing positions for political convenience.He also raised the issue of the 750 farmers who died during the farmers' protest against the now-repealed farm laws and alleged that the BJP wanted to turn Chandigarh into a Union Territory, which would undermine Punjab's rights.Mann further questioned the BJP's position on drugs, alleging that its leaders were sharing platforms with Majithia despite the allegations against him in a drug-related case. "For six years they abuse each other, then they come together," he said.KEJRIWAL SPEAKS ON SCHEMESKejriwal, meanwhile, focused on welfare schemes, inflation and the Centre's policies. He accused the BJP-led government of stopping several free-scheme programmes introduced by AAP in Delhi and urged voters to support Mann if they wanted such initiatives to continue.Acknowledging the delay in providing the promised Rs 1,000 monthly assistance to women, he attributed it to the financial condition inherited by the government.He also appealed to women to use the assistance as they wished, including buying a new suit, while asking them to ensure their families voted for AAP.ON MANN GOVT'S PERFORMANCEOn the government's performance, Kejriwal cited action against drug trafficking, claiming that around 77,000 FIRs had been registered and 70,000 arrests made, besides the demolition of properties belonging to alleged drug traffickers.Marking the party's foundation day, Kejriwal also recalled AAP's journey since its formation in 2012, saying it had overcome initial scepticism and established governments in Delhi and Punjab."Politics could not change us; instead, we changed politics," he said in a message marking the occasion.With PM Modi's proposed December 8 visit bringing the rival political camps to Moga within days of each other, the district is set to remain at the centre of Punjab's emerging electoral contest as parties step up preparations for the 2027 Assembly polls.- EndsMust Watch

headline: AAP kicks off 2027 Punjab poll campaign with Moga rally, promises continuation of welfare schemes
content: CHANDIGARH:The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday formally sounded the poll bugle for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections by organising a 'Khushhaal Punjab Maha Rally' in Matwani village, Moga, where it began distributing smart ration cards. The rally marked the party's foundation day and Constitution Day.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann sought a second term, claiming that the government had fulfilled its promises and would continue all welfare schemes if re-elected. Mann targeted the SAD-BJP alliance, describing it as an “unholy” tie-up driven by vested interests.Addressing the rally, Mann blamed the alliance for the drug menace during its 2007-2017 tenure and questioned how leaders who had accused each other of links to drugs would now share a stage.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed rally at the same Moga ground on December 8, Mann said, “The same people who have been criticising one another for years are now preparing to share a platform. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ravneet Singh Bittu, Sunil Jakhar, Kewal Singh Dhillon, Ashwani Kumar and Tarun Chugh are among those whose politics the people of Punjab have watched closely. They should explain what they have done for Punjab.”“Remember, Ravneet Singh Bittu used to say, how can we join hands with those who are into drugs, pointing towards Majithia. Now, how will Modi, Shah, Capt Amarinder Singh, Sukhbir Badal, Bikram Majithia and Bittu share the stage?” he said.Mann accused Sukhbir Badal of initially supporting the farm laws and opposing them only after the farmers' agitation gained ground. He alleged that the BJP wanted to bring back the laws with the SAD's support and accused Badal of compromising Punjab's rights for political power.Referring to the December 2, 2024, edict, Mann said Badal had initially accepted it but later called the jathedars who pronounced it “tools of BJP and RSS”.“You had also said that anyone who wants to join the BJP should have their DNA tested. Now that you have joined hands with the BJP and RSS, your DNA should be tested,” he said..Referring to the Akali Dal leadership, he said, “The people of Punjab know who has been running the Akali Dal and what the party has done during its years in power. Sukhbir Singh Badal, Bikram Singh Majithia and other Akali leaders must answer to the people. The party cannot escape accountability by changing its slogans or making new political arrangements.”Taking a swipe at the party's internal affairs and leadership, Mann also referred to Prem Singh Chandumajra and Bibi Jagir Kaur, saying, “The people have seen how leaders have been treated and how the party has functioned. Those who could not keep their own house in order are now trying to lecture Punjab.”Launching a sharp attack on the Shiromani Akali Dal, Congress and BJP, Mann said, “These parties have ruled Punjab for years and have taken turns in power. They blamed one another, made promises and then forgot the people after elections. Now they are coming together because they are worried about the work being done by the Aam Aadmi Party government. The people of Punjab know their history and will not be misled by their new political arrangements.”“Whether they belong to the Akali Dal, Congress or BJP, the people of Punjab have seen their governments. They had opportunities to work for the state. Today, they are joining hands not because they have suddenly developed love for Punjab, but because they want to stop the work of the Aam Aadmi Party government. The people will give their answer in 2027,” he said.Arvind Kejriwal said the AAP was formed 14 years ago to protect the Constitution and ensure equality. Claiming that the Mann government had fulfilled its five-year guarantees, he cited free electricity, healthcare, education and financial assistance for women..“Now all guarantees have been fulfilled despite the central government having stopped Punjab government funds and the state government having to move the court,” he said, promising that all schemes would continue if AAP retained power.Kejriwal urged voters to give every vote to AAP, saying a change of government could lead to the discontinuation of welfare schemes. He also asked women to use their cash assistance to buy new clothes and wear them while voting for the party.Highlighting the government's employment record, Mann said, “We have provided 77,182 government jobs to the youth of Punjab. These jobs have been given on merit and through a transparent process. Our young people are getting government employment on the basis of their qualifications. They do not have to approach a minister, a political leader or anyone else to get a job, and they do not have to pay bribes.”Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia and state president Aman Arora also addressed the rally..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 'Aam Aadmi will run country, not politicians': Arvind Kejriwal claims over 2 lakh people attend ‘Khushhal
content: MOGA: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday claimed that more than two lakh people attended the party's ‘Khushhal Punjab Rally’ in Moga, asserting that the gathering was never seen in the history of Punjab.He also linked Constitution Day with the foundation day of the AAP, saying the responsibility of protecting the Constitution had been entrusted to the common man.Addressing the rally in the presence of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann, Kejriwal said the Constitution was adopted on November 26, the same day the Aam Aadmi Party was formed, describing the coincidence as a sign of the responsibility entrusted to ordinary citizens."More than 200,000 people are present at this rally—a gathering of a scale never before seen in the history of Punjab. The Constitution was adopted on November 26th, and the Aam Aadmi Party was also formed on November 26th. It seems that the Almighty has entrusted the responsibility of safeguarding the Constitution to the 'Aam Aadmi' (the common man). From now on, the country will not be run by politicians, but by the common man,” he said.Recalling the promises made by the AAP ahead of the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, Kejriwal said the party had outlined several commitments under what he described as 'Kejriwal's Guarantees', including free electricity, healthcare and education, along with a monthly payment of Rs 1,000 to women.“Before the 2022 elections, when I came to seek your votes, I made several promises—promises that came to be known as 'Kejriwal’s Guarantees.' We pledged to provide free electricity, free healthcare, and free education. We also guaranteed a monthly payment of Rs 1,000 to women—a promise we have since fulfilled. It took some time to implement the Rs 1,000 monthly payment because previous governments had left the state treasury completely empty. It took four years to replenish that treasury; yet, throughout this process, we ensured that the coffers never ran dry,” he said.Kejriwal further said the Punjab government had implemented its final guarantee, the Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, despite alleged hurdles created by the Centre.He said, “We did all the work, and now we have also implemented our final guarantee, the Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana. They also created a lot of hurdles in implementing this scheme. The Modi government stopped Punjab's money. Took the support of the court. They tried in various ways to stop the scheme, but we are strong too. Maan Sahab is very strong, he didn't let it stop. Now Mama Dhiya's money is coming every month.”Clarifying the payment structure under the scheme, the AAP National Convenor said women were entitled to Rs 1,000 per month, while women from the Scheduled Caste community would receive Rs 1,500 per month.“Some people are confused. Three thousand has arrived in some people's accounts. Some got it once. Some got it twice. Let me clarify for you what this scheme is. Every woman is supposed to get one thousand rupees every month. They are deposited into their accounts all at once for three months. So three thousand for three months, and for the women of the SC community, four and a half thousand, calculated at one and a half thousand rupees per month,” Kejriwal said.Highlighting the impact of the financial assistance on women, Kejriwal said the monthly amount was intended to help families cope with rising prices.He said, “Modi Ji has caused so much inflation. But Bhagwant Mann has given you a thousand rupees to help support your family. I met many women. Everyone has such emotional stories about how women are being used. And how they are spending the money. There is a woman, the poor thing is very poor. Her father is often sick at home. She goes to the pharmacy to get medicine for his illness. The pharmacist is also a good man. He gives it to her on credit and writes it down in a notebook in her name—how much the medicine costs. When she gets the money, she pays it off in full.”Sharing another instance of how women were using the assistance, Kejriwal said some beneficiaries had used the money to purchase clothes and earrings.“Just a few days ago when she went to get the medicine, the shopkeeper gave it to her and took out the notebook to write. She quickly took money out of her pocket, said there's no need to write it down now, take this money for your medicine. He said, you've become very rich. Where did you get the money? She said Bhagwant Mann sent it. Many women have bought new clothes for themselves. Several women have bought earrings. Today we have about seven such women here,” Kejriwal added.The rally comes ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The state has 117 Assembly seats, with the majority mark at 59.In the previous Assembly elections, held on February 20, 2022, with results declared on March 10, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) won 92 seats, securing a clear majority and forming the government under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Chandigarh court rejects Punjab CM Mann’s wife’s defamation suit against retired Justice Ranjit Singh
content: In a significant development in the defamation proceedings instituted by Gurpreet Kaur, wife of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Chandigarh, has rejected her suit against retired Justice Ranjit Singh, holding that no cause of action for defamation was disclosed against him.Dr Gurpreet Kaur had filed a suit seeking damages against Justice Ranjit Singh, SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia, Congress leader Sukhpal Singh Khaira and Bhawna Nair.In her suit, she alleged that the defendant had made defamatory allegations against her on August 20, 2026, which were false, baseless and highly defamatory. She claimed that he had specifically stated that she had demanded Rs 5 crore from an accused in a rape case.The statement was posted on the social media handle of DD News Live on X (formerly Twitter) with the intention of tarnishing her image in the eyes of the public.Advocate Charanjit Singh Bakhshi, appearing for Justice Ranjit Singh, argued that the plaintiff had approached the court by relying on an incomplete and selectively reproduced version of his press conference, without disclosing the crucial background of the statement and the judicial proceedings to which it related.After hearing the arguments, the court observed that, from the plaintiff's own statement, it was prima facie evident that she had admitted that she was unaware of the complete statement at the time of filing the suit.She had also raised no objection to deleting the name of defendant No. 2 (Justice Ranjit Singh) from the array of parties, subject to the conditions mentioned in the statement made by her counsel.The court said this clearly showed that the plaintiff had admitted that, in the absence of the complete video of Justice Ranjit Singh's press conference, the suit was not maintainable against him, as no cause of action could be established on the basis of an incomplete video extract.The court held that the plaintiff had miserably failed to disclose a cause of action against Justice Ranjit Singh and that the plaint was liable to be rejected qua him.

headline: All election guarantees fulfilled, says Arvind Kejriwal; Opp. slams AAP of misusing public resources
content: CHANDIGARH: Ahead of the Assembly elections in Punjab, due in early 2027, Aam Aadmi Party’s national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) urged women to persuade the men in their families to vote for the AAP. He was speaking at a rally in Moga on the party’s foundation day, where he highlighted the ₹1,000 financial assistance provided by the AAP Government to help women deal with inflation, taking a dig at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Government at the Centre. The Opposition parties, meanwhile, targeted the AAP, accusing it of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis. Mr. Kejriwal claimed that the AAP had fulfilled all its election guarantees within five years, adding that the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP had announced that they would discontinue the AAP Government’s existing schemes if voted to power. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement Former State Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring accuses SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, and his wife, former Union Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal, of misleading people by publicly distancing themselves from the BJP while supporting it on key issues in Parliament Three AAP leaders join BJP ahead of Punjab Assembly election Three AAP leaders join BJP ahead of Punjab Assembly election Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap, Sanour MLA Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Samana MLA Chetan Singh Jauramajra join the BJP in Delhi; State BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon says it indicates the impending end of the party’s regime in Punjab “I am standing before people of Punjab today because my ‘Chota Bhai’, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, has fulfilled all of Kejriwal’s guarantees. We promised free electricity and people are getting free electricity. We promised to organise ‘tirth yatra,’ and now devotees are going on the ‘yatra.’ We promised to open Aam Aadmi Clinics and now people are receiving great treatment. We promised free treatment, and everyone has been provided with a health insurance card worth ₹10 lakh,” he said. The Smart Ration Card Scheme to extend food security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries was also launched at the event. Leader of the Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa alleged that the Government machinery, including State-owned buses, administrative resources and police personnel were deployed for a political function at the expense of the public exchequer. ‘Financial mismanagement’ “Before calling it a ‘Khushhaal Rally’, the AAP must answer a fundamental question: has Punjab actually become prosperous under its rule? When the State is drowning in debt, why is public money being spent on a party celebration? Punjabis are already bearing the brunt of financial mismanagement, and this event has added to their inconvenience,” Mr. Bajwa said. Hitting out at the AAP, State BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon questioned what had happened to the promise of making Punjab drug-free within three weeks. “The Government’s war is not against drugs, but against Punjab itself,” he said in a statement. headline: SKM holds rally in Patiala, slams Centre, Punjab for failing to fulfil accepted demands
content: In response to a national call by the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), its Punjab chapter organised a rally at the PUDA Ground in Patiala on Thursday. Farmers from seven districts of the Malwa region—Patiala, Sangrur, Mohali, Ludhiana, Ropar, Fatehgarh Sahib and Malerkotla—participated in the event.Leaders of 15 farmer organisations affiliated with the Samyukt Kisan Morcha took part in the rally. It is noteworthy that, on the occasion of the sixth anniversary of the historic 'Delhi Morcha' (farmers' protest), four rallies were held across Punjab—in Patiala, Bathinda, Jalandhar and Amritsar—following a call by the SKM.Addressing the gatherings, the speakers urged the public to question political parties during the upcoming elections about their plans to resolve the deepening crisis affecting Punjab's water resources and agricultural sector.The leaders strongly criticised both the BJP-led central government and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab for failing to implement farmers' demands that had earlier been accepted.They pointed out that the BJP had initially agreed to the demand for a law guaranteeing the procurement of crops at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) but subsequently backtracked."On the other hand, the Punjab Government has avoided tabling resolutions in the Legislative Assembly on several agreed-upon demands. These include repealing Sections 78, 79 and 80 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, which symbolise the injustice inflicted upon Punjab by the Centre over its river waters, and implementing a one-time settlement scheme for loans taken from cooperative institutions," said senior leaders Balbir Rajewal and Dr Darshan Pal.They said a strategy would be formulated at a future meeting of the SKM to hold the parties running both the state and central governments accountable.SKM leaders termed the Rs 15 increase in sugarcane prices "negligible". They said that by announcing such a meagre hike, despite rising input costs and soaring sugar prices, the Punjab Government had played a cruel joke on sugarcane farmers."The price of sugarcane should be fixed at Rs 500 per quintal, and all outstanding dues should be cleared immediately through the implementation of a 'single-window, single-payment' scheme," they said.Another SKM leader, Jagmohan Singh Patiala, issued a stern warning to the BJP-led central government, asserting that any anti-national, duty-free agreement entered into under American pressure would not be tolerated. Describing the US government's policy of imposing a 25 per cent tariff on India as "imperialist bullying", he said the people of the country would not forgive the Modi government for its policy of kowtowing to the United States.The rally was presided over by Jagmohan Singh, Jarnail Singh Jahangir, Manjit Singh Dhaner, Parminder Singh Palmajra, Kulwant Singh Maulviwala, Harbhajan Singh Dhuhar and others.

headline: RBI accepts ₹8,003 crore of state bonds in its first switch auction
content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Thursday accepted Rs 8,002.80 crore of state government securities in its first switch auction, allowing states to replace bonds maturing in 2027-2029 with longer-dated securities maturing between 2034 and 2044. The central bank issued destination securities worth Rs 8,261.55 crore in face value against the accepted bonds. It had notified Rs 10,800 crore across 10 securities and received 81 offers worth Rs 11,188.66 crore, of which it accepted 50. Tamil Nadu accounted for the largest share of accepted securities at Rs 2,222 crore, followed by Rajasthan at Rs 1,950 crore, Madhya Pradesh at Rs 1,844.80 crore, Uttar Pradesh at Rs 1,381 crore and Punjab at Rs 605 crore. The offers were below the notified amount for three of the 10 securities, while one security received offers worth Rs 775 crore but saw no acceptance. The availability of eligible securities with banks was a constraint in the auction, market participants said. Cut-off yields on the longer-dated securities ranged between 7.89 per cent and 8.08 per cent, depending on the state and maturity. The securities issued under the switch had maturities ranging from 2034 to 2044. "This is a very small amount. It will not affect much. The availability of securities with banks and whether they were trading at favourable prices to be offered in the switch were key constraints. Unlike switches of central government securities, availability of state government bonds was a bigger challenge," a dealer at a private bank said.

headline: Punjab notifies PhysicsWallah Digital University: When will first session begin, which courses will be offered?
content: Edtech company PhysicsWallah (PW), founded by Alakh Pandey, is expanding beyond school education and competitive exam preparation, entering the formal higher education sector with a digital university in Punjab.The state government has notified the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, paving the way for the institution to offer undergraduate, postgraduate and career-oriented programmes through online and distance learning.The university is expected to begin its first academic session in July 2027, with admissions targeted for the same month, according to The Economic Times. Its proposed academic portfolio will span more than 16 undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and certificate programmes, subject to recognition by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and other applicable regulatory approvals.The company said in its investor presentation filed with stock exchanges that the proposed university would build on its existing education platform by expanding into formal degree programmes and career-focused learning. PhysicsWallah's wholly owned subsidiary, Nextseed Foundation, will sponsor the institution, which will function as a self-financed university.Which courses will PhysicsWallah Digital University offer?The university plans to organise its academic programmes across five schools:1. Business and Management2. Computer and Information Technology3. Humanities and Social Sciences4. Journalism and Media Communication5. Skills and Vocational StudiesAccording to the company's investor presentation, its proposed degree offerings include Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA), Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), Bachelor of Commerce (BCom), Bachelor of Arts (BA), Master of Commerce (MCom), Master of Computer Applications (MCA) and Master of Business Administration (MBA).The portfolio will also include programmes incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) and data science. Career-oriented certifications are proposed in Banking and Financial Services, Digital Marketing with AI and Social Media Marketing.The company has also outlined programmes combining academic degrees with competitive examination preparation, including BCom with Chartered Accountancy (CA) preparation and BA with Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) preparation. Its MBA offering is aimed at CAT aspirants, while skills diplomas are expected to incorporate apprenticeship opportunities.How will the digital university operate?PhysicsWallah plans to adopt an AI-enabled learning framework, integrating technology into teaching, assessments, student engagement and academic support.The proposed model will combine live online classes, faculty mentoring and global faculty interaction sessions. Its digital infrastructure will prioritise mobile-first access and low-bandwidth connectivity to reach students in smaller towns and remote locations.The company also intends to bring faculty from IITs, IIMs and industry into its academic ecosystem, according to its investor presentation.What did Alakh Pandey say?Pandey stated the initiative would extend the company's focus on making education affordable and accessible into formal higher education.“Since its inception, PW has been focused on providing students across the country with accessible quality learning at affordable costs and equal opportunity for all students irrespective of geography or economic status. The Digital University will help us take this vision into formal higher education. We want students to access good teachers, the right guidance, and learning opportunities that prepare them for robust careers,” he said, according to a release.The university has been established under the Punjab Private Digital Open Universities Policy, 2026. Its programmes will need to comply with applicable UGC regulations governing online and open and distance learning. The framework also provides for credit mobility through online and distance courses and micro-credentials, as well as an independent ombudsman to address student grievances.

headline: Record Crowd Of 2 Lakh At ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ Moga Rally; CM Bhagwant Singh Mann Sounds Poll Bugle
content: CHANDIGARH / MOGA | A sea of two lakh people converging in Moga, turned the ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ Maha Rally into a powerful show of public support for Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government’s politics of performance. Declaring the record-breaking turnout a historic endorsement of ‘Kaam Di Rajneeti’, the Chief Minister said that when intentions are honest and promises translate into tangible results, people do not need to be mobilised through hollow slogans. From zero electricity bills and over 77,000 government jobs secured without bribes to canal water reaching the tail ends, free healthcare cover of up to ₹10 lakh and financial assistance for women, he said, the government’s work has given people a reason to rally behind its vision. The massive gathering, the Chief Minister asserted, sends an unmistakable political message: Punjab has moved beyond the empty promises of the past and is choosing development, progress and prosperity. With the 2027 Assembly elections on the horizon, the rally also saw CM Bhagwant Singh Mann sound the poll bugle, thanking the people of Punjab for their overwhelming love and trust. Sharing a few snippets from this historic gathering, CM Bhagwant Singh Mann stated on X, “The massive sea of humanity that gathered on the soil of Moga today, with lakhs of Punjabis turning up, was no ordinary gathering. It was a historic endorsement of the politics of performance. When intentions are honest and people witness tangible results such as zero electricity bills, over 77,000 government jobs provided without bribery, canal water reaching the tail ends, free healthcare coverage of up to ₹10 lakh, and dignity and respect for mothers and daughters, they come forward in overwhelming numbers. This record-breaking historic gathering is proof that Punjab no longer believes in the empty promises of the past. It chooses progress, development and prosperity. Heartfelt gratitude to every Punjabi for this immense love, faith and support.” Addressing the mega rally, CM Bhagwant Singh Mann said, “Today, I want to speak directly to the people of Punjab about the work we have done and the promises we have fulfilled. Those who ruled this state for decades must also tell the people what they did for Punjab. They had years in power, but the state continued to face problems. Our government is presenting its report card before the people because we believe that a government must be answerable to the public.” Launching a sharp attack on the Shiromani Akali Dal, Congress and BJP, the Chief Minister said, “These parties have ruled Punjab for years and have taken turns in power. They blamed one another, made promises and then forgot the people after elections. Now they are coming together because they are worried about the work being done by the Aam Aadmi Party government. The people of Punjab know their history and will not be misled by their new political arrangements.” Referring to the Akali Dal leadership, he said, “The people of Punjab know who has been running the Akali Dal and what the party has done during its years in power. Sukhbir Singh Badal, Bikram Singh Majithia, and other Akali leaders must answer to the people. The party cannot escape accountability by changing its slogans or making new political arrangements.”

headline: BJP holds programme on Constitution Day in Punjab’s Sangrur
content: Sangrur, Nov 26 (PTI) The Punjab BJP organised a state-level programme on Constitution Day on Thursday, with party leaders saying the BJP-led Centre truly safeguarded Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar’s legacy, while the Congress always disrespected it. Lok Sabha MP Bhola Singh and Rajya Sabha MP Satnam Singh Sandhu paid floral tributes to the chief architect of the Constitution, Ambedkar. The BJP leaders asserted that the central government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has fulfilled the vision of social justice and equality by developing five historic sites associated with Babasaheb as “Panchteerth” and giving rights to weaker and underprivileged sections through constitutional amendments. Bhola Singh said the sole objective of constitutional amendments must always be national interest and public welfare. He said during the Congress regime, the majority of constitutional amendments were enacted solely to serve the party’s narrow political interests and lust for power. “In stark contrast, all constitutional amendments implemented under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership since 2014 have been dedicated to strengthening national security, economic resilience, and citizen welfare,” Bhola Singh said. The MP said the BJP has consistently worked to translate Ambedkar’s teachings and constitutional ideals into ground reality to achieve genuine social equality.

headline: 3 killed as overloaded gravel truck overturns on car on Ropar-Manali highway
content: Three persons travelling in a Delhi-registered car were killed on the spot after an overloaded multi-axle truck carrying gravel overturned on their car near Bharatgarh on the Ropar-Manali national highway on Thursday afternoon.The truck allegedly went out of control, hit around eight vehicles before overturning on the car, crushing all three occupants under its massive load. A newlywed couple travelling on the road had a narrow escape as their car was buried under gravel when the multi-axle vehicle overturned.Tribune photoUntil the filing of this report, the police had not identified the deceased. Ropar SSP Maninder Singh, when contacted, said details of the deceased would be shared later as the police were busy clearing the traffic jam on the highway caused by the accident.The accident triggered chaos on the busy highway, bringing traffic to a virtual standstill and leaving thousands of commuters stranded for several hours.According to sources, the truck driver lost control of the vehicle before it rammed into several vehicles moving along the highway. The truck subsequently overturned on the car, completely crushing it under its weight.Tribune photoThe accident also exposed the difficulties faced by commuters due to the alleged absence of adequate police personnel to regulate traffic. Interestingly, a large number of police personnel had reportedly been deputed at Nangal for the AAP government's ‘Ek Sham Shiv Ke Naam’ programme, which was also scheduled to be attended by Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann later in the evening.With police personnel engaged in arrangements for the event, commuters caught in the traffic snarl faced considerable inconvenience. The congestion was so severe that several ambulances travelling towards Chandigarh from different parts of Ropar district and neighbouring Himachal Pradesh also got stuck on the highway.The tragedy has once again brought the spotlight on the unchecked movement of overloaded tippers and multi-axle trucks, particularly those allegedly transporting illegally mined material in Ropar district.Congress leader and former president of Ropar Bar Association, Paramjit Singh Pamma, criticised the state government over its failure to check the movement of overloaded vehicles.He said the Chief Minister was visiting Ropar district, yet there had been no let-up in the movement of overloaded tippers and trucks allegedly carrying illegally mined material. He alleged that such vehicles had already claimed several lives, but the authorities continued to turn a blind eye to blatant violations.Holding the government responsible for failing to enforce traffic and mining regulations, Pamma said the loss of three precious lives in the accident also raised questions about the accountability of the authorities concerned.BJP state vice-president Subhash Sharma also targeted the AAP government, alleging that it had failed to curb illegal mining and the movement of overloaded vehicles on roads in the district. He said the continued operation of such vehicles reflected the failure of the government to enforce its own rules.As per the existing provisions, police and mining department officials can impose fines of up to Rs 2 lakh on overloaded tippers and trucks. However, despite widespread complaints about overloading, action against violators has reportedly remained limited to a small number of vehicles.

headline: No tie-up with AAP in Punjab, Congress open to INDIA bloc partners: Partap Bajwa
content: On Constitution Day, the Punjab Congress held a ‘Samvidhan Bachao Rally’ on Thursday as part of the party’s nationwide campaign to safeguard constitutional values, oppose alleged electoral irregularities and highlight the drug menace in Punjab.Addressing mediapersons on the sidelines of the rally, Leader of Opposition Partap Bajwa ruled out any alliance with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Punjab, but said the Congress is open to joining hands with like-minded parties within the INDIA bloc. He added that candidates for the upcoming Assembly poll would be declared by the start of next month, after a meeting of the selection committee.On the alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP, Bajwa dismissed its political significance, saying, “Zero plus zero equals to zero.”The SAD returned to the NDA and revived its alliance with the BJP on Wednesday, nearly six years after it walked out over the farmers’ agitation against the controversial farm laws.Bajwa took a dig at the SAD, saying Sukhbir Badal should clarify whether the BJP had given any assurances to them on the farm laws, release of Bandi Sikhs and scrapping of the Agniveer scheme, which were the main issues concerning Punjab.The rally, held at a resort near India Gate, was also attended by Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and other senior party leaders, including Rajkumar Verka, Gurjeet Aujla, Danny Bandala, Jasbir Dimpa, Sunil Datti and Harpartap Ajnala.The speakers targeted the BJP-led Central Government and the AAP government in Punjab over the drug menace and gangsterism, claiming Punjab needed an alternative government capable of delivering effective governance and restoring law and order. They asserted that only the Congress could provide an efficient government to rid the state of drugs and gangsterism.Pargat accused the BJP of trying to undermine the country’s secular and democratic character. He alleged that the BJP is seeking to expand its political influence in Punjab with the help of the Akali Dal.The leaders also emphasised the importance of the INDIA bloc, saying secular and like-minded parties, including Left organisations, needed to work together to protect the country’s democratic and secular fabric.The rally also provided the Congress an opportunity to mobilise its cadre ahead of the next Assembly election.

headline: Ex-Congress MP Pawan Bansal says he ‘wasn’t consulted’ on Chandigarh poll picks
content: Unease appears to be brewing in the Chandigarh Congress as former Union minister and four-time MP Pawan Kumar Bansal finds himself on the margins of the party's preparations for the December 2026 municipal corporation elections. While the party has included him in its Political Affairs Committee, Bansal's remarks about the committee, his absence from its lone meeting, and exclusion from the Election Committee point to his displeasure. When asked if he was consulted on the selection of candidates, Bansal told The Indian Express, "No, I was not consulted.” “I was put in some Political Affairs Committee. There is no meaning of political affairs in Chandigarh. There was one meeting of it, and I did not attend,” he said. Asked whether he was part of the Election Committee, Bansal replied, “I wasn't put in any Election Committee.” “All I can say is that I have always wished—and will always wish—the best for Congressmen,” he replied when asked if he was satisfied with the candidate selection process. Though Bansal stopped short of openly criticising the way the Congress functions in the city, his statement brought attention to the apparent distance between the veteran leader and the ongoing election preparations. "For a leader who represented Chandigarh in Parliament four times and remained the Congress's principal face in the city for years, his absence from the committee handling ticket selection will not go down well for the party. Even though the party's internal equations changed a lot after Tewari's candidature, those who have seen the city grow can't be sidelined," a Bansal loyalist said. Bansal’s ‘blessings’ for candidate selection: Chandigarh Congress chief Asked whether Bansal had been consulted on candidate selection, Chandigarh Congress president H S Lucky said, “His blessings are there.” "The election committee comprises party in-charge Rajni Patil, MP Manish Tewari, myself, and several other senior leaders, including ward in-charges. All of them are actively involved in the process of assessing candidates and finalising the list," he added. Lucky also said the Congress would announce its candidates before Sunday. While Tewari is part of both the Political Affairs Committee and the Election Committee, Bansal has been included only in the former. The developments also bring back the rift post 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Bansal, a former Union railways minister, had represented the Chandigarh constituency for several terms, but the Congress opted to field Tewari, who went on to defeat BJP candidate Sanjay Tandon. The decision had triggered discontent among a section of Bansal's supporters. Tewari's victory subsequently strengthened his position in Chandigarh's Congress politics. Nominations open Ahead of the civic polls, the party has constituted 12 ward-level committees, comprising three experienced leaders each, to assess prospective candidates and gather feedback on their winnability. Their recommendations are being examined by the Election Committee, with the final list to be cleared by the party leadership. With nominations for the 35 municipal wards opening Thursday, the Congress is now engaged in the crucial exercise of balancing organisational considerations and competing claims for tickets. Whether Bansal's supporters will find adequate representation in the final list and whether the veteran leader will have any say in the process are still unclear.
