headline: 8th Pay Commission update: With DA hiked under 7th CPC, what central and state govt employees can expect next
content: The Centre and several state governments have announced increases in Dearness Allowance (DA) for serving government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners in recent weeks, offering some relief amid rising living costs.However, these periodic revisions are separate from the much-awaited 8th Pay Commission, which is expected to recommend a broader overhaul of salaries, allowances and pensions.Government employees and pensioners are still awaiting clarity on the proposed fitment factor, revised minimum basic pay and other benefits.Centre raises DA and DR to 63%The Union Cabinet on October 28 approved a 3 percentage point increase in DA and DR for central government employees and pensioners, taking the rates from 60% to 63% of basic pay and pension, respectively.The revision is effective from July 1, 2026, and follows the established formula under the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC).According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the increase is expected to benefit around 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners. It will entail an annual financial implication of approximately ₹10,016.10 crore for the government.Several state governments have also announced DA and DR revisions. According to CNBC TV18, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Gujarat have raised DA by 3 percentage points to 63%. Punjab has increased DA from 50% to 53%, effective November 1. Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh also announced DA hikes ahead of Diwali, although the revised rates and effective dates vary. These increases, however, do not constitute a revision of the basic salary structure. They are periodic adjustments linked to inflation and remain separate from the recommendations expected under the 8th Pay Commission. What is the latest status of the 8th Pay Commission? The 8th Central Pay Commission was constituted on November 3, 2025, and has been given 18 months from its formation to submit its recommendations. This puts the expected deadline around May 2027. The Commission is responsible for reviewing and recommending changes to the pay, allowances and other benefits of specified categories of central government employees. Its mandate also covers pension and retirement-related benefits. While examining the proposed revisions, the Commission has been asked to consider several factors, including the country's economic conditions, fiscal prudence and the potential impact of its recommendations on state government finances. However, no final decision has been announced on the fitment factor, revised minimum basic salary or the new pay structure. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on August 10, 2026, the Finance Ministry said that the 8th Pay Commission had not yet submitted its recommendations to the government, as per CNBC TV18 report. What are employees demanding under the 8th Pay Commission? Employee organisations have submitted several proposals to the Commission, seeking a higher minimum basic salary, a revised fitment factor, changes in allowances and improved pension benefits. The National Council-Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM), which represents the staff side of the consultative mechanism for central government employees, has sought a minimum basic salary of ₹69,000 and a fitment factor of 3.833 in its memorandum to the Commission.The proposed fitment factor is particularly significant because it is used to calculate the revised basic pay by multiplying the existing basic salary by the prescribed factor. However, these figures represent demands made by employee organisations and should not be treated as approved revisions. The Commission will examine the submissions and other representations before finalising its recommendations. Will state govt employees also get 8th Pay Commission salary hike? The 8th Pay Commission is a Central Pay Commission, and its terms of reference cover specified categories of central government employees and other listed personnel. State government employees are not automatically covered by its recommendations. However, state governments have traditionally adopted the recommendations of Central Pay Commissions. The Union Cabinet's October 2025 announcement on the Commission's terms of reference also acknowledged the likely impact of its recommendations on state government finances, given that states generally consider adopting the revised pay structure. Each state government will have to take an independent decision on whether to adopt the recommendations, what modifications to make and when to implement the revised pay structure.

headline: Cooking with firewood, dung cakes top PM2.5 source in Indo-Gangetic Plain
content: A new study has revealed that cooking with firewood, dung cakes and coal, among others, is the single largest source of PM2.5 emissions in the most polluted areas of the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP). It added that cooking through such methods contributes 36-49 per cent of the total primary PM2.5 emissions in the IGP's most polluted parts, stretching from Punjab in the west through Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to West Bengal in the east. The study, released by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW) on Thursday, comes at a time when Delhi-NCR continues to witness bad air quality, and much of the focus is on how stubble burning and Diwali firecrackers drive spikes in pollution. Cooking's contribution to PM2.5 emissions remains high despite the progress made by the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) in recent years. The scheme was launched in May 2016 to provide economically weaker households with free LPG connections. According to the study, the PMUY helped avert 15 per cent of India's household PM2.5 emissions in financial year 2025-2026.In a statement, Abhishek Kar, a fellow at the CEEW, said, "Many families still cook with firewood alongside LPG because the next refill is hard to afford, and in the Indo-Gangetic Plain's most polluted areas, cooking is the single largest source of PM2.5 emissions." The study highlighted that residential combustion takes place year-round and increases every winter, as households also burn fuel for heating. Cooking accounts for about 80 per cent of household energy use, so transitioning from polluting to cleaner cooking fuels is the only way to cut most of the residential emissions, according to the study. It recommended a winter top-up under the PMUY that would make the next LPG refill affordable when pollution is at its worst. The study also suggested that India's 25,000-plus LPG distributors sell certified induction cooktops and electric pressure cookers at a discount to households that give up two of their four subsidised cylinders

headline: Punjab court sets deadline for cops to file report on ED’s charges against real estate firms
content: New Delhi: A Punjab court has ordered the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Mohali, to ensure the filing of a final report after examination of materials and records submitted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) with regard to alleged fraudulent practices of real estate firms, including one run by a friend of Punjab Cabinet minister Aman Arora. Making it clear that no further adjournment would be granted for this purpose, the court gave the Mohali SSP till 2 December to ensure that the final report is submitted to it. The magistrate asked the ED to file a response to the police challenge on the maintainability of its petition seeking the court’s go-ahead for registering a First Information Report (FIR). The development comes a couple of months after the ED approached the court under Section 175(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita(BNSS), which empowers a magistrate to order a police investigation into a cognisable offence after reviewing an application supported by an affidavit under Section 173(4), conducting necessary inquiry, and hearing the police officer. In its plea, the ED informed the court that it sent the Mohali SSP materials under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act on 1 July, following up with as many as four reminders via email, but there was no response from the SSP office. The ED had asked the SSP to register an FIR against Altus Space Builders, its managing directors Harpreet Singh and Mohinder Singh, Dhir Construction and its owner Gaurav Dhir, a long-time associate of Arora. It alleged that they cheated several plot buyers by fraudulently obtaining Change of Land Use (CLU) certificates and layout plan approvals while bypassing mandatory procedures set by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), the Punjab Urban Planning & Development Authority (PUDA), and the Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP).

headline: Punjab Police, Rail Coach Factory Register Wins; Eight Teams Qualify For QFs
content: In three-key matches of the 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament played last evening at Jalandhar, Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala) secured a commanding 4-1 victory over BSF Jalandhar, while the match between Bharat Petroleum and the Army (Delhi) ended in a 0-0 draw. Punjab Police team defeated Indian Navy (Mumbai) by 4-1. So far in the tournament, teams of Indian Oil, Punjab Police, Punjab National Bank (Delhi), Indian Air Force, Bharat Petroleum, Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala), Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi), and CAG (Delhi) have secured their spots in the quarter-finals. In today’s 4 quarter-final matches, Indian Oil (Mumbai) will play with Punjab National Bank (Delhi) at 12:00 PM. Indian Air Force will take on CAG (Delhi) at 2:00 PM. Bharat Petroleum (Mumbai) will face Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala) at 3:30 PM and Punjab Police will dribble with Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi) at 5:30 PM.

headline: Punjab farmers announce November 26 protest over Rs 27.84 crore Phagwara mill dues
content: The Bharatiya Kisan Union has called a protest at Mill Chowk on November 26, demanding the release of Rs 27.84 crore in outstanding sugarcane payments owed by Phagwara Sugar Mill to farmers, The Tribune reported. Several farmer organisations are expected to participate in the agitation, which will also involve a blockade of the national highway. Farmer leader Manjit Singh Rai said farmers would gather outside the sugar mill at 10 am before moving to Mill Chowk for a sit-in protest. He said the delay in clearing sugarcane dues had left farmers with no option but to launch an agitation. Rai said that, in addition to the Rs 27.84 crore owed by the mill, the state government had pending payments of around Rs 18.93 crore to farmers. He demanded the immediate clearance of all outstanding dues and an increase in the sugarcane procurement price. Meanwhile, farmer representatives visited Mill Chowk to assess the protest venue and review arrangements ahead of the agitation.

headline: 253 teachers’ termination: Protesters warn to gherao CM’s residence on Dec 6
content: Teachers, employees and farmer organisations on Wednesday staged a protest outside the SDM office here against the termination of 253 teachers recruited under the 4161 recruitment process.The protesters burnt an effigy of the Punjab government and demanded the withdrawal of the termination orders, restoration of the teachers’ services and protection of their future. A memorandum highlighting their demands was also submitted to the state government.The protest was organised by the Democratic Teachers’ Front (DTF), 253 Victim Teachers’ Union, Government Teachers’ Union, Democratic Pensioners’ Front, 4161 Master Cadre Union, Old Pension Restoration Front, Kirti Kisan Union and the All India Kisan Sabha, among others.Addressing the gathering, DTF leaders Mukesh Kumar and Sukhdev Dansiwal, 253 Victim Teachers’ Union representatives Balkar Singh Maghania, Harwinder Kaur and Chanda Rani, and Government Teachers’ Union leader Naresh Kumar said the decision to terminate 253 teachers who had been serving in the Education Department for the past three to three-and-a-half years was unjustified.They alleged that the termination action had been initiated on the basis of the cancellation of an answer key prepared by expert professors from universities in accordance with the High Court’s directions. They urged the government to withdraw the decision and reinstate all 253 teachers to safeguard their careers.State president of the 4161 Master Cadre Union Sandeep Gill and Bagga Singh, All India Kisan Sabha leader Gurnek Singh Bhajjal, Vikas Manch Garhshankar representatives Kulwinder Singh Sangha and Avtar Singh, and Old Pension Restoration Front leader Iqbal Singh Sapra warned that if the government failed to resolve the issue, the organisations would gherao the Chief Minister’s residence in Sangrur on December 6. They said other mass organisations would also join the agitation in support of the teachers.

headline: Hoshiarpur to get Rs 276-cr medical college by 2028
content: MLA Brahm Shankar Jimpa performed the ground-breaking ceremony (bhoomi pujan) for the proposed medical college on the Civil Hospital premises here on Wednesday. The project, estimated to cost Rs 276 crore, is expected to be completed by 2028.Speaking to mediapersons, Jimpa said the medical college had been a long-pending demand of the people of Hoshiarpur. He said the project would benefit not only residents of the district but also people from neighbouring districts and Himachal Pradesh.He said around Rs 146 crore would be spent on constructing a modern 350-bed hospital, while the remaining amount would be utilised for the medical college building, students’ hostels and other essential infrastructure. Jimpa said the proposed hospital would provide specialised medical services and reduce the need for patients to travel to other districts and major cities for treatment of serious ailments. The project would also create opportunities for students to pursue MBBS education in Hoshiarpur. He said strengthening healthcare and education infrastructure was among the priorities of the Punjab government led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann.

headline: Congress reaches out to Left for 2027 Punjab polls
content: The Punjab Congress on Wednesday said it was in talks with the CPI and CPI(M) for an electoral tie-up in the state with party chief Pargat Singh saying they want to bring the Left parties together as part of a broader alliance of parties in the INDIA bloc. “All of us have a thinking that the CPI, CPM and other Communist parties be taken together. We are in talks with the CPI and CPI-M. Comrades are part of the INDIA bloc,” Pargat told reporters in Patiala. He said the Congress had constituted a team to hold discussions on seat-sharing with the Left parties. Leader of Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa, speaking separately, said the Congress was open to alliances with parties that had a presence in the state. “Leaders of INDIA bloc members — CPI, CPM and other parties — are sitting in Delhi. The thing is that we should be seen together. Seats can be given only where they have a presence,” Bajwa said. The Congress’s outreach to the Left comes a day after the Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP announced the revival of their alliance, ending their six-year separation. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the SAD would be the “big brother” in the alliance and would get the Chief Minister’s post. Pargat, meanwhile, stepped up his attack on SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal over his past remarks about those joining the BJP. Referring to Badal’s comment during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign that “jehda apna Khalsa BJP join karda hai, usda DNA test hona chahida hai (those who joined the BJP after being Khalsa should undergo a DNA test)”, Pargat asked whether SAD chief would now agree to undergo a DNA test himself. Calling the revived alliance an example of “opportunistic politics”, Pargat said it was neither based on a common ideology nor formed in Punjab’s interest, but was aimed at protecting the political fortunes of the two parties. “Both parties have lost the trust of the people of Punjab,” he said, asserting that their return to an alliance would not help them regain lost ground. Comparing the SAD and BJP to the East India Company, Pargat alleged that the two parties were seeking to gain control over Punjab’s resources and rights. Congress manifesto committee chairman and MP Amar Singh also criticised the alliance, calling it an “opportunistic political arrangement aimed solely at polarising Sikh and Hindu votes”. Amar Singh questioned the SAD’s position on issues including the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), Punjab’s claim over Chandigarh and implementation of the Swaminathan Commission report. He alleged that by joining hands with the BJP, the Akali Dal had compromised Punjab’s interests. Pargat also targeted the Aam Aadmi Party government, alleging that it had lost public trust and lacked a concrete agenda beyond publicity and political theatrics. Speaking after attending a workers’ meeting organised by the District Congress Committee in Patiala, he alleged that the government was using publicity to conceal its failures and expressed concern over corruption, drugs and administrative lapses. He demanded an impartial investigation into the medical drugs trade and the alleged involvement of individuals in it. He also urged government officials not to function as political workers and to discharge their constitutional and legal responsibilities impartially. On the Congress’s preparations for the 2027 elections, Pargat said the party had begun its candidate-selection process and held its first round of meetings. The Central Election Committee would deliberate on candidates in the coming days, and decisions on nearly half of the Assembly constituencies could be taken within the next 10 to 15 days, he said. Pargat also announced the induction of Paramjit Singh Sidhwan, a former political adviser to Sukhbir Singh Badal, and Roop Kaur, who was associated with the AAP, into the Congress. He expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power with a full majority in 2027, saying the party would remain united in raising issues concerning Punjab’s rights, farmers, labourers, youth and other sections of society.

headline: Haryana Cong hits Panchkula roads over constitutional rights
content: The Haryana Congress on Thursday organised a 'Save the Constitution' march in Panchkula, accusing the BJP of undermining democratic institutions and electoral integrity.The march, held in response to a call by the Congress, began at Maharana Pratap Bhawan in Sector 26 and was attended by Haryana Congress in-charge Sanjay Dutt, Leader of the Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda, state party president Rao Narender Singh and MP Deepender Hooda, besides several sitting and former legislators, MPs and party functionaries.Raising slogans against the BJP government and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the protesters accused the ruling party of electoral malpractice and demanded accountability from the Election Commission. They also pledged to protect the Constitution and the right to vote.Addressing the gathering, Sanjay Dutt said protecting the spirit of the Constitution, the independence of democratic institutions and citizens' constitutional rights was the biggest challenge facing the country. He called upon people to uphold the ideals of Dr BR Ambedkar and the vision of the Constitution's framers.Hooda alleged that instances of vote theft by the BJP had come to light in Haryana and other parts of the country. He said voters would not allow electoral manipulation in future elections.Rao Narender Singh said safeguarding the electoral rolls was essential to ensure that every eligible citizen could exercise the right to vote. He urged people to raise their voices against any attempt to deprive voters of this constitutional right.Deepender Hooda accused the BJP of weakening democratic institutions and said the Congress, under Rahul Gandhi's leadership, would continue its fight to protect the Constitution and democracy.He also criticised the state government's handling of law and order, citing the recent killing of four persons in Rohtak. Alleging that Haryana was witnessing rising extortion, gang violence and shootings, he questioned Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini's focus on the state's security situation while campaigning in Punjab.The Congress leaders reiterated their resolve to continue raising issues concerning electoral transparency, constitutional rights and public safety.

headline: Haryana CM Saini, LoP Hooda participate in Constitution Day event
content: Chandigarh, Nov 26 (PTI) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Assembly Speaker Harvinder Kalyan, ministers and MLAs took part in a special programme to mark Constitution Day here. The programme, held on the library premises near the ceremonial gate of the Vidhan Sabha, commenced with the offering of floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi. The central theme of the programme was “Haryana’s 60-year journey of glorious development, public participation in realising the goal of a Viksit Haryana, and the role of elected representatives in raising awareness of constitutional values among citizens”, a statement said. At the culmination of the programme, Speaker Kalyan led the reading of the Preamble to the Constitution, with the chief minister, elected representatives and distinguished guests joining the recitation. They also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding constitutional ideals, democratic values and citizens’ duties. A documentary highlighting the significance of the Constitution, its fundamental spirit and democratic values was also screened. The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949. It came into force on January 26, 1950, when India became a Republic.

headline: 10 former CJIs inaugurate India's first Chief Justices of India Museum in JGU University, Sonipat
content: Ten former Chief Justices of India (CJIs), attending in person or virtually, inaugurated India's first Chief Justices of India Museum at the O P Jindal Global University (JGU) in Haryana's Sonipat a day before Constitution Day on Wednesday, a release said.Also Read | Lok Sabha Speaker & Law Minister launches JGU's 3 master's degree coursesIt said the former CJIs were M N Venkatachaliah, B N Kirpal, S Rajendra Babu, K G Balakrishnan, P Sathasivam, R M Lodha, Dipak Misra, S A Bobde, U U Lalit and B R Gavai.Titled "Guardians of the Republic", the release said the museum has five galleries and features more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 high courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive pillars on the lives of chief justices and 20 landmark judgments. It also has a holographic courtroom, artwork, sculptures, and an oral-history project with former chief justices and judges, the release added.Also Read | Public confidence in judicial authority must be continuously earned through independence: CJIAccording to the release, Justice Gavai congratulated the university and spoke about his own journey. "I am humbled that I got an opportunity to be the chief justice of India, specifically coming from a simple background," he said. He added that during his tenure, the court worked to give representation to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, minorities and women.Also Read | CJI Surya Kant calls for greater representation of women in legal professionJustice Lalit, according to the release, said the museum traces the growth of law alongside the growth of the country. "At the time of independence, India did not have food security, and literacy was 18 per cent. Today we are self-sufficient in all areas," he said.

headline: Asian Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad Ranked No. 3 Among Best Private Multispeciality Hospitals in Delhi NCR at THE WEEK Best Hospital Awards 2026
content: PNNFaridabad (Haryana) [India], November 26: Asian Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad, has been honored at THE WEEK Health Summit 2026 & Best Hospital Awards Ceremony, securing the prestigious No. 3 rank under the category of Best Multispeciality Hospitals in Delhi NCR (Private) in THE WEEK-Hansa Research Best Hospitals Survey 2026.The grand award ceremony took place at The Ambassador Hotel, New Delhi. The honor was conferred in recognition of the institution's sustained excellence, clinical innovation, and significant contributions to the Indian healthcare sector.Widely regarded as one of India's most credible healthcare benchmarks, THE WEEK-Hansa Research Best Hospitals Survey evaluates top medical institutions across 19 major cities and the National Capital Region through an extensive nationwide survey of general physicians and specialists, followed by rigorous factual validation. Being ranked among the top three private multispeciality hospitals in the fiercely competitive Delhi NCR region underscores Asian Hospital's steadfast commitment to clinical quality, patient safety, and compassionate care.Over the years, the NABH- and NABL-accredited super-specialty tertiary care hospital in Faridabad has established itself as a premier healthcare destination, offering comprehensive services across key centers of excellence including Cardiology, Oncology and Bone Marrow Transplant, Neurology and Neurosurgery, Orthopaedics and Joint Replacement, Urology and Kidney Transplant, Gastroenterology, and Mother and Child Care. By seamlessly integrating cutting-edge medical technology with patient-centric protocols, the hospital continues to deliver world-class clinical outcomes to patients from across India and abroad.Speaking on the milestone, Dr. N. K. Pandey, Chairman of Asian Hospital, said,"We are immensely delighted and humbled to receive this prestigious recognition from THE WEEK-Hansa Research Survey. Being ranked among the top three private multispeciality hospitals in Delhi NCR is a proud milestone that validates the relentless dedication of our doctors, nurses, and frontline staff, as well as the unwavering trust our patients place in us. Looking ahead, this honor inspires us to further expand our clinical capabilities, integrate next-generation medical technologies, and strengthen preventive and accessible healthcare initiatives so we can serve the broader public health needs of the community in the years to come."About Asian Institute of Medical Sciences, FaridabadEstablished in 2010 in Sector 21A, Faridabad, Asian Institute of Medical Sciences is a leading super-specialty tertiary care hospital providing preventive, diagnostic, therapeutic, rehabilitative, and palliative support under one roof.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by PNN. headline: Haryana Assembly marks Constitution Day, calls for focus on citizens’ duties
content: imes News NetworkCHANDIGARH: The Haryana Legislative Assembly on Thursday marked Constitution Day with a special session, reaffirming its commitment to constitutional values, democratic traditions and citizens’ duties, even as the state completed 60 years of its formation.Speaker Harvinder Kalyan called upon legislators to rise above party politics and engage in constructive discussions on Haryana’s development, stressing that the Assembly must serve as a forum for articulating people’s aspirations and shaping the vision of a developed state.Addressing the House, Kalyan said the Constitution was the country’s greatest strength, holding India together despite its diversity and guiding its democratic journey. He said Haryana’s six-decade journey was not merely about economic and infrastructure growth but also reflected the strengthening of democratic institutions, public participation and civic consciousness.The special programme was attended by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Mahipal Dhanda, Deputy Speaker Krishan Lal Middha, ministers and MLAs.Professor Dinesh Kumar of Panjab University, Chandigarh, delivered a special lecture, underlining the need to create greater awareness about Fundamental Duties alongside Fundamental Rights. He said elected representatives had an important responsibility in educating citizens about their constitutional obligations.Protecting public property, safeguarding national sovereignty and integrity, preventing violence and preserving the environment were among the duties that needed greater public awareness, he said. Emphasising fraternity and social harmony, he added that discrimination on the basis of religion, language or region had no place in a constitutional democracy.The programme also featured a documentary on the Constitution, followed by a collective reading of its Preamble led by Kalyan.Earlier, Saini, Kalyan, Hooda and other dignitaries paid floral tributes to Dr BR Ambedkar’s statue on the Assembly premises and Mahatma Gandhi’s statue near the Assembly Library.The House proceedings began at 11 am and were adjourned after obituary references, ahead of the special programme centred on Haryana’s development journey and the role of elected representatives and public participation in building a developed state.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: From filling quilts at flour mill to AICC secretary: Tracing Yogender Yogi’s rise
content: Yogender Yogi, a grassroots leader from Haryana’s Hisar district who has been appointed secretary of the All India Congress Committee (AICC), recalls how he spent his boyhood days filling cotton quilts and mattresses at his family’s village flour mill. Yogi has been appointed AICC secretary in the recent organisational reshuffle announced by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. His appointment is among five from Haryana to the party's national secretarial team, giving the state greater representation in the Congress's central organisation. Alongside his appointment as AICC secretary, he has been assigned the responsibility of co-in charge of Maharashtra party affairs. “When I was in Class VII at a government school in my village, Mujadpur (Hansi), my father asked me to fill quilts and mattresses for villagers,” recalls Yogi. His family ran a local chakki (flour mill) where residents brought wheat to be ground into flour and cotton to be processed into binola (cottonseed cake) for livestock—leaving soft cotton that young Yogender helped stuff into quilts and mattresses. “Yogi is a number-one person in the village who has contributed to its development since his young age. The news of his elevation has spread across the village,” said Satish Jangra, husband of the Mujadpur village sarpanch. Belonging to the Nai community, which falls under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category, Yogi is the son of Dharampal, who worked as a postman rather than pursuing the community's traditional occupation of hairdressing. After completing his schooling in the village, Yogi enrolled in a vocational course at a government Industrial Training Institute (ITI) in neighbouring Nalwa village. Years later, he earned a bachelor’s degree in commerce from a university in Tamil Nadu in 2012. Early activism days His first brush with activism came in 1999, when, as a 19-year-old pursuing a vocational course in two- and three-wheeler mechanics, he joined a movement involving 62 villages demanding adequate water for irrigation and drinking purposes. Around the same time, he began working for the Congress at the grassroots level and later associated with the Nehru Yuva Kendra in Hisar, spearheading campaigns on drug de-addiction, environmental conservation, and social awareness. On the social and political front, Yogi emerged as a voice for the political and socio-economic representation of extremely backward communities within the OBC category. He argued that many communities were unable to secure a fair share of political representation, government jobs, and admissions to educational institutions. According to Yogi, Haryana has 78 OBC communities, of which 72 fall under the BC-A category and six under BC-B. He alleged that only four communities among the 72 in the BC-A category had largely cornered the benefits of government schemes and opportunities, leaving the remaining 68 at a disadvantage. “Among the 68 communities that remain disadvantaged are the dhobhi, Teli, Maniyar, Sunar, Lohar, Nai, Chhimpa, and Jogi communities. They have not received their fair share of the benefits of government schemes and representation,” Yogi said. To mobilise these communities, he organised a mahapanchayat in Meham, Rohtak, in 2022 and led a foot march from Rohtak to Chandigarh in 2023 to highlight their demands. A phone call from Rahul Gandhi One of the most memorable moments in his political journey came in 2012, when he received a telephone call from Rahul Gandhi after sending him an invitation to his sister's wedding. “I went to the roof of my house to hear his voice clearly. Rahul Gandhi conveyed his wishes for the wedding but expressed his inability to attend, citing a programme in Shimla that day,” Yogi told The Indian Express. He added that the then Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda attended the wedding despite scepticism among villagers. “People had joked before the wedding that how could a Chief Minister come to the house of a Nai family and that perhaps only an MLA would attend. But Hooda came,” Yogi recalled. As part of the Congress's OBC outreach initiatives, Yogi has also served as the party's national coordinator for OBC affairs in Jharkhand. Recalling a meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Yogi said he had highlighted the lack of adequate political representation for extremely backward communities within the OBC category. “I told him that these extremely backward communities have traditionally been with the Congress. However, even among the 72 backward communities, only four have received political representation most of the time, leaving the remaining 68 largely unrepresented. This aspect needs to be looked into,” he said. “I am happy that, coming from such a humble background, I have been given such a significant responsibility in the party,” he said. Yogi's appointment is being seen in the context of the Congress's efforts to strengthen its outreach among weaker sections and backward communities by promoting grassroots workers and leaders without established political backgrounds. Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh said the appointments reflected Rahul Gandhi’s push to elevate non-dynastic grassroots cadres based on merit rather than political patronage. “The party, especially Rahul ji, has a mindset that people should not be appointed based on recommendations. Secondly, Rahul ji personally interviewed all the aspirants. Priyanka ji and K C Venugopal ji also attended these interviews,” he said.

headline: Flagged illegal tree felling, then faced suspension: The case of IFS officer Jhalkar Uyake
content: Just four years into his career in the Indian Forest Service (IFS), 2022-batch officer Jhalkar Uyake faces possible termination after the Haryana Forest Department recommended his removal over the alleged illegal felling of 2,585 trees in the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserved Forest in Faridabad. Uyake, who has served as Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) in Haryana for less than two years, was suspended on November 18 amid allegations of negligence and alleged involvement in the felling, even as he himself had flagged the large-scale tree cutting and alleged collusion by field staff. Born on August 28, 1991, Uyake holds a Bachelor of Technology (BTech) degree and belongs to the 2022 batch of the Indian Forest Service. Before joining the civil services, he worked as a patent examiner in the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry for seven years, holding a Class-I (Group A) position. After clearing the UPSC examination and joining the IFS on December 13, 2022, Uyake underwent training, including at the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy (IGNFA) in Dehradun. As part of his state-specific training, he completed field training in Morni and Pinjore, Haryana, in 2024. He was posted as DCF, Faridabad, on December 2, 2024, before being transferred to Jhajjar. He returned to Faridabad in February 2026 and remained posted there until November 18, when he was suspended. Illegal felling of trees As DCF, Faridabad, Uyake oversaw nearly 7,000 hectares of forest area in the district, covering different categories of land, including areas under the Punjab Land Preservation Act (PLPA), Reserved Forests (RF) and Protected Forests (PF). An official said nearly 11 per cent of Faridabad district's geographical area was under forest cover. However, the department had only 19 field personnel, including forest guards and foresters, to protect the area. "There is no regular system of nakas to prevent tree theft. Normally, the Forest Department acts after receiving complaints from citizens or information through government channels," the official said. Official sources said the illegal felling was suspected to have begun in September this year in the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserved Forest under the pretext of preparing ridges for compensatory afforestation under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) scheme. Contractors were engaged to undertake preliminary plantation work in the forest area. Sources said senior forest officers remained unaware of the alleged large-scale felling for nearly two months. Instead of restricting the work to removing invasive vegetation, particularly vilayati kikar (mesquite), and clearing undergrowth, the contractors allegedly resorted to selectively felling fully grown trees belonging to Classes I, II, and III. "The trees cut included mature mesquite and eucalyptus, with the felled timber subsequently transported out of the reserved forest," an official said. The extent of the alleged operation came to light during raids in Punhana, Nuh district, where forest officials seized 19 truckloads of timber suspected to have originated from the Alipur Reserved Forest. The official said the seized timber was later transported back to the Faridabad Forest Division. An inspection and a letter According to official records, Uyake inspected the site on the morning of November 11 and found extensive felling at a location where CAMPA-funded plantation work was underway across approximately 19 hectares, involving the proposed planting of nearly 64,000 saplings. The following day, he wrote to Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF)-cum-Head of Forest Force K C Meena, flagging the alleged illegal felling of mature green kikar trees in the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserved Forest. He suspected that the plantation work was a pretext for commercial timber extraction and said the activity could have continued for nearly two months, or even before the tender was awarded. In his communication, Uyake also alleged gross negligence and possible connivance by field staff, including Range Forest Officer Afzal Khan and forest personnel Ankit Kumar and Sandeep Kumar, for failing to prevent or report the felling despite clear instructions that no standing tree was to be cut. On November 12, he also lodged a complaint with Rajesh Mohan, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Central, Faridabad, seeking registration of a First Information Report (FIR) and action against the contractor. He further sought the suspension of the three forest officials pending an investigation, citing serious supervisory lapses and possible collusion. Acting on the allegations, the Haryana Forest Department suspended Afzal Khan, Range Forest Officer, Faridabad, and two other field officials — Ankit Kumar, a forest guard, and Sandeep Kumar, a forester — on November 12. The state subsequently dismissed all three from service on November 20, 2026, without a regular departmental inquiry. However, the state government also placed Uyake under suspension on November 18, following reports from Subhash Yadav, Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF), Gurugram, who flagged the alleged involvement of field-level forest staff Yadav also said Uyake was aware of the felling of mature trees and the transportation of timber to different locations. Another senior IFS officer had also flagged allegations against Uyake. Uyake was not available for comment.

headline: 805 Haryana development announcements pending, 339 declared unfeasible
content: Chandigarh: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini’s directive to officials to expedite development announcements has brought the govt’s backlog of unfulfilled political promises into focus. As many as 805 announcements remain pending, while another 339 have been declared unfeasible, despite claims that departmental feasibility is assessed before such commitments are made.Of the 7,988 announcements made by successive governments during visits to assembly constituencies, 5,743 have been completed and work on 1,101 is in progress. The remaining 1,144 are either pending or have been abandoned as unfeasible. The backlog includes announcements dating back to the tenure of former chief minister and now Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar.At a review meeting at Sant Kabir Kutir on Wednesday, Saini directed officers to prioritise announcements made during rallies and public programmes and complete them within stipulated timelines. He warned that laxity would not be tolerated and asked MLAs to coordinate with departments to resolve bottlenecks.The chief minister acknowledged that announcements cleared as feasible sometimes become unviable later because of non-availability of land or other reasons.

headline: Haryana to hold special session to mark Constitution Day today | Hindustan Times
content: The Haryana vidhan sabha will hold a special session to mark Constitution Day on Thursday.The vidhan sabha secretariat spokesperson said the House proceedings will begin at 11am with obituary references, followed by an adjournment at 11.15am. A special programme will be organised during the break, featuring a documentary on the making of the Constitution.Speaker Harvinder Kalyan said the special session aims to strengthen the commitment of elected representatives to constitutional principles, parliamentary traditions and democratic values.

headline: Saini to visit UK, Germany from November 28 to December 5 to woo investors | Hindustan Times
content: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini will lead a high-level delegation to the United Kingdom and Germany from November 28 to December 5, aiming to attract foreign investment and establish industrial partnerships.Amit Kumar Agrawal, commissioner and secretary, industries and commerce, said the delegation will hold extensive deliberations with leading global companies, investors, universities, research and technology institutions, and representatives from various sectors.He said the visit is the state’s investment outreach to key European markets. Delegations led by the CM visited Japan, Singapore, and Sweden recently.During these visits, memoranda of understanding (MoUs) were signed with various companies for investment, industrial cooperation, and partnerships, and agreements were reached on significant investment proposals worth over ₹10,000 crore. The upcoming visit to the United Kingdom and Germany is another step in this direction, Agrawal said.He said during the UK visit, the delegation will interact with business leaders, global investors and industry representatives. Discussions will also be held with a delegation of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on investment opportunities in Haryana.The CM will also interact with members of the Indian diaspora from Haryana and will invite them to invest in the state. He said that on November 30 and December 1, the Saini will hold one-to-one meetings with representatives of leading industries, companies and educational institutions.Special roundtable meetings will also be organised to explore trade and investment opportunities across various sectors under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). Detailed discussions and dedicated sessions will be held on key areas, including education, skill development and vocational training.The CM will invite UK Members of Parliament and other prominent representatives to visit Haryana and participate in the Global Investors Summit proposed to be held in April 2027.During the visit, Saini will also interact with representatives of the Centre for Science and Policy at the University of Cambridge. He will meet Indian students studying at the University of Oxford to discuss their experiences, ideas and potential role in Haryana’s development.The CM will also visit Queen Elizabeth’s School, Barnet, where discussions will focus on cooperation in the education sector and the possibility of establishing an educational campus in Haryana. Agrawal said a special celebration of the International Gita Jayanti Mahotsav will also be organised in London, in which the CM will participate.He said the Haryana state roadshow will be organised in Germany on December 2. The roadshow will showcase Haryana’s industrial infrastructure, investor friendly policies, connectivity and investment opportunities. Agrawal said that on December 3, the CM will hold a meeting with representatives of Fraunhofer, Germany’s prestigious research and technology institution. Detailed discussions will be held on the proposed establishment of a Centre of Excellence in Haryana, and a MoU will also be signed in this regard.The proposed Centre will focus on cutting-edge and strategically important areas such as microelectronics and energy storage. The initiative is expected to give fresh impetus to research, innovation, technological development and industrial collaboration in Haryana. On December 4 and 5, the CM will hold one-to-one meetings with representatives of leading German companies, industrialists and potential investors. These meetings will explore investment opportunities in Haryana, industrial cooperation and new avenues for long-term business partnerships.

headline: Govt nod to issue commemorative coin to mark 125th birth anniv of Sobha Singh: Ex-RS member
content: New Delhi, Nov 26 (PTI) The government has approved the issuance of a commemorative coin of Rs 125 denomination to mark the 125th birth anniversary of noted painter Sobha Singh, former Rajya Sabha member Tarlochan Singh said on Thursday. Sobha Singh was born in Punjab in 1901, and later had his studio base in Andretta in today’s Himachal Pradesh. Tarlochan Singh, 93, said he had written to the Centre on May 30 this year, requesting the issuance of a commemorative coin to mark the 125th birth anniversary. “Now, the government has approved the decision to issue a Rs 125 commemorative coin in his honour,” he said. Tarlochan Singh also issued a statement thanking the government for the decision. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) on November 19 had issued a profile of the artist on its website.

headline: NGT flags high pollution levels in two locations at Ashwani Khad in Shimla
content: Shimla, Nov 26 (PTI) The National Green Tribunal has found high levels of organic pollution at two locations in Ashwani Khad near Shimla and directed the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board to continue investigating the sources of pollution. A principal bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) comprising its chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Afroz Ahmad heard the matter on Wednesday. The order was made available on Thursday. The case relates to pollution in Ashwani Khad and its connected streams and drains. It was taken up following a News Himachal report titled ‘Ashwani Khad: The Most Polluted River in Himachal Pradesh’ published on December 4, 2023. On November 16, the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) shared results of water samples collected from 25 locations, which were tested at the State Board Laboratory in Shimla, a NABL-accredited facility. The samples recorded biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) levels of 16 mg/L and 22.4 mg/L, with the higher level found in the Lift Nullah at Combermere. The BOD levels were within the prescribed limit of 3 mg/L at 23 locations. However, the Lift Nullah near a waste processing site recorded 16 mg/L, while the Lift Nullah at Combermere recorded 22.4 mg/L.

headline: How Sanju Samson’s selfless act helped Azharuddeen score a 57-ball 101
content: Mohammed Azharuddeen woke up on Thursday feeling unwell. "I had all sorts of problems," the Keralam wicketkeeper-batter tells The Indian Express from New Chandigarh. The ailments have yet to loosen their grip. There was medicine to be taken in the evening, as there had been in the morning. Between the two doses came a 57-ball 101 against Himachal Pradesh that won Keralam a must-win Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match. "I was under the weather. I had fever, headache, sore throat, runny nose, all kinds, basically," the opener says. Keralam went into the game four points adrift of Himachal, and a defeat would have called curtains to their dream of a maiden SMAT title. Azharuddeen's innings kept that dream alive, and Keralam won by 67 runs. "This was a very crucial match. It was a do-or-die game that we had to win at any cost. I was not doing well, but I knew that I was in form. I have scored runs in the last two matches (an unbeaten 93 against Assam and 78 against Puducherry). So, I told my team, 'Regardless of what happens to me, please let me play this match and take my team to the next stage.' Fortunately, we have a very good medical team in Keralam, so they guided me on what medication to take before the game." Nothing in the way he batted gave away his health. The first five overs yielded 76 runs, among them five consecutive boundaries off Harshit Sandal, four fours and then a six. His opening partner, Rohan Kunnummal, fell in the last over of the powerplay, but Azharuddeen put on another stand, this time with his idol, Sanju Samson: 77 runs in 40 deliveries. Samson was gone before Azharuddeen reached his hundred. When he got there, he showed the dugout the sticker on his bat that read "Samson". The assumption since has been simple: that the gesture acknowledged a bat Samson had gifted him. He had gifted it, but that was not why Azharuddeen pointed it out. "Everyone thinks I pointed out Sanju bhai's name because I played with his bat. It is true that I played with his bat, but it is not why I did that gesture," he says. "Ever since my Under-19 days, I have played with the bats that Sanju bhai has gifted me. This is not something new. But he actually gave up his batting position just for me." The explanation follows. "You see, Sanju bhai is a world-class opener. We all know that. He won India a T20 World Cup while opening the innings. But I have also been in good form as an opener. I scored plenty of runs in the Kerala Cricket League (596, he finished as the leading run-scorer). Before SMAT, he called me and said: 'Be ready to open the innings, because you've been doing well there. I will drop down to number three instead.' I was waiting for my hundred to point his name out on my bat today, because of what he has done for me." Azharuddeen believes that Samson's presence lifts the dressing room and has a direct bearing on his own batting. "Batting with Sanju bhai is always special. He has known me for the last 15 years and has guided me at every step. It is the same when we bat together. He guides me on which bowlers to go after, when to take singles and when to play big shots. It makes my life easier." Five years have passed since Royal Challengers Bengaluru signed him, and an Indian Premier League appearance has eluded him since. He is 32 now and trying to find his way back. "A lot of things were not working for me at the time. I kept constantly thinking about what was going wrong. But what I never stopped was putting in the hard work. I spotted mistakes in my game and rectified those. I am 32 now, but the dream of playing for India is still alive. For now, though, the focus only is on scoring runs consistently so that I can win matches for my team." Over the past week he has done exactly that: 272 runs from 142 deliveries, at a strike rate of 191.55. Those numbers have been enough to carry Keralam into the Super League of SMAT, where Baroda, Delhi and Vidarbha await. Brief Scores: Keralam 268/4 (Mohammed Azharuddeen 101; Mridul Surroch 2/33) beat Himachal Pradesh 201/6 (Vaibhav Kalta 57 not out; Vaisakh Chandran 2/33) by 67 runs.)

headline: Call for stronger inter-State coordination to combat spurious, adulterated drugs
content: Bengaluru Drug regulators across States need to strengthen inter-State coordination, intelligence sharing and joint enforcement mechanisms to effectively combat the growing menace of spurious, adulterated and not-of-standard-quality (NSQ) drugs, Manish Kapoor, Drugs Controller and State Licensing Authority, Himachal Pradesh, has said. Read | Karnataka can independently benchmark drug regulatory system against WHO standards: Union Health Secretary https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/karnataka-can-independently-benchmark-drug-regulatory-system-against-who-standards-union-health-secretary/article71746745.ece At the conference, Mr. Kapoor stressed that the fight against spurious drugs and the illegal diversion of pharmaceutical products cannot be confined to individual States and requires close coordination between State drug regulatory authorities, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), police and other enforcement agencies. He said delays in intelligence sharing, jurisdictional limitations, inadequate manpower and logistical constraints often hamper timely action. He pointed out that investigations frequently involve multiple states, making it essential for regulatory authorities to establish a coordinated mechanism for sharing intelligence and conducting joint operations.

headline: Himachal: Workshop stresses community action to curb drug demand
content: Shimla, Nov 26 (PTI) Importance of community action and institutional coordination in reducing drug demand was highlighted during a one-day orientation workshop on ‘Drug Demand Reduction, Prevention and Community Action’ organised by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department here on Thursday. The workshop aimed to develop a shared understanding and strengthen a coordinated, prevention-oriented and community-based framework for drug demand reduction in Himachal Pradesh, while motivating all stakeholders towards collective action for a drug-free society, a statement issued here said. General Secretary, Bharat Gyan Vigyan Samiti O P Bhureta stressed the importance of community action and institutional coordination in reducing drug demand. He highlighted the need for active participation of local communities, organisations and various government departments to develop effective prevention and support mechanisms. Director of the Social Justice and Empowerment Department Sumit Khimta said that the deliberations focused on the prevailing substance use scenario in the state, its social and public health implications and comprehensive strategies for reducing drug demand. Director of Gunjan Organisation Vijay Kumar discussed the drug use scenario in Himachal Pradesh and highlighted the need for an integrated approach encompassing prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.

headline: Himachal Police marks Constitution Day with pledge ceremony
content: Shimla, Nov 26 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh Police observed Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) on Thursday with a ceremony at the state Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau headquarters in Shimla, commemorating the adoption of the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949. Police officers and personnel representing various ranks from the police headquarters, state Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau headquarters and Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters participated in the ceremony, a statement issued here said. Director General of Police, Himachal Pradesh, Ashok Tewari, IPS, administered the Constitution Day pledge to the assembled officers and personnel through the collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution. Police personnel reaffirmed their commitment to the foundational constitutional principles of Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, and pledged to uphold the dignity of every citizen while discharging their official responsibilities with honesty, integrity, impartiality and professionalism. The observance highlighted the Constitution’s significance as the supreme guiding framework for governance, democratic institutions and the functioning of law enforcement agencies. It also served as a reminder of the police force’s responsibility to protect the constitutional rights of citizens, maintain the rule of law and ensure that public service remains guided by constitutional morality and accountability.

headline: Himachal Anti-Conversion Law: 19 Arrests, Six FIRs, No Convictions in Four Years
content: SHIMLA, November 26, 2026: Nearly four years after Himachal Pradesh strengthened its anti-conversion law, none of the six cases registered under the legislation has resulted in a conviction, although 19 people have been arrested, according to figures disclosed by the state government in the Legislative Assembly. Between 2023 and November 1, 2026, the state received 15 complaints under the Himachal Pradesh Freedom of Religion Act, 2019, as amended in 2022. Six of these complaints resulted in the registration of First Information Reports (FIRs), leading to 19 arrests. The figures were provided in a written reply during the Assembly's winter session. Kangra district accounted for the highest number of complaints, with eight cases. However, none resulted in an FIR, and all eight were disposed of by the police. Kullu received two complaints, one of which led to an FIR, while the other remains under preliminary inquiry. Dehra, Hamirpur, Mandi, Shimla and Una each recorded one FIR. No complaints were reported from the remaining police districts. The annual breakdown shows that eight complaints were received in 2023, three in 2024, one in 2025 and three up to November 1, 2026.

headline: Himachal to supply surplus water to neighbouring states, govt agencies at uniform rates
content: The Himachal Pradesh Government will provide surplus raw water to neighbouring states and various government agencies at uniform rates under a state policy formulated to ensure transparent and economically rational valuation of water resources while safeguarding the state's financial interests.A benchmark rate of Rs 100 per 1,000 cubic feet has been approved under the state policy, with periodic revisions linked to the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) to ensure that the economic value of water is protected against changes in prevailing price levels. However, this framework will not apply to water utilised for domestic purposes within the state.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the state government was committed to protecting Himachal Pradesh's natural resources and ensuring that the state received appropriate economic returns from its valuable water resources.“Water is one of the most important assets of the state, and its economic value must be recognised while entering into any arrangement for supplying surplus water to other states or agencies. The policy would establish a transparent and uniform mechanism for determining water rates and their periodic revision, thereby protecting the long-term financial interests of the state,” he said.The policy also covers all existing and future projects in Himachal Pradesh from which surplus raw water is supplied to other states or eligible agencies. It envisages a standard pricing framework for inter-state multipurpose and water-storage projects, including the proposed Kishau Multipurpose Project and Renuka Ji Dam Project. The framework will ensure that the water requirements of Himachal Pradesh remain the foremost priority.The policy aims to establish a uniform mechanism for determining rates for surplus raw water supplied to neighbouring states, government agencies and industries, wherever permissible, after meeting the state's present and future requirements.The Chief Minister said the government would ensure that the state's interests and requirements were fully safeguarded before making any surplus water available to other states. The state's drinking water, irrigation, agricultural, environmental and developmental needs would remain paramount, he added.The matter assumes significance in the context of the Kishau Multipurpose Project, under which Himachal Pradesh has been allocated a share equivalent to 3.154 per cent of the dam's live storage, amounting to approximately 42 million cubic metres.The state also has an allocated share of Yamuna waters under the MoU signed among the Upper Yamuna Basin states. The MoU envisages the development of the Lakhwar, Kishau and Renuka Ji Dam projects for the optimum utilisation of the basin's water resources.

headline: 75-year-old groom, 63-year-old bride tie the knot in Himachal: Sabina from Bengal marries Kanhaiya in Mandi...
content: A 75-year-old groom married a 63-year-old bride in Himachal Pradesh. The groom is from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, and was so devastated after his wife's death that he began living in a cave in the forest. When his condition deteriorated, an organisation brought him to an old-age home. Meanwhile, Sabina from West Bengal reached Shimla by train after her mental condition deteriorated following her husband's death. The organisation also admitted her to its old-age home. The two met there and have now got married. The two will now live as husband and wife in a new old-age home. This was made possible with the support of Prakash Bansal, founder and chairman of Himachal's Manav Seva organisation, who arranged their wedding according to all the traditional rituals. After his wife's death, Kanhaiya left home and began living in the forest Prakash Bansal, founder and chairman of Manav Seva Sanstha, said Kanhaiya Lal, a resident of Mandi, lost his wife in 2021. So devastated was he by the shock that he left his home and family and began living in the forest. He spent around seven months in a cave. The trust rescued him in 2022. During that period, his mental health had also deteriorated, and he had lost hope in life.

headline: 75-year-old Bilaspur man abandoned by family finds love at Himachal old-age home, marries 63-year-old woma
content: Age did not come in the way of finding love for a 75-year-old man from Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district. After spending years at an old-age home without family support, Kanhaiya Lal has found a companion for the rest of his life. He married 63-year-old Sabina, whom he met at the same facility, in a traditional wedding ceremony on Wednesday, a PTI report stated. The wedding took place at the 'Apna Ghar' old-age home in Dayoli, where the two had gradually developed a close bond. What started as an acquaintance eventually turned into a relationship, with both deciding to spend their remaining years together.The ceremony was held around 11.30 am. Kanhaiya Lal and Sabina exchanged garlands as residents and staff members celebrated their union with traditional songs and wedding rituals. The occasion brought a festive atmosphere to the old-age home.How Kanhaiya Lal ended up at an old-age homeKanhaiya Lal originally belongs to the Janjehli area of Mandi district in Himachal Pradesh. He had worked in the Public Works Department (PWD) and retired from government service in 2000. He once owned around two to two-and-a-half bighas of agricultural land and a two-room house. However, he transferred these properties to his brothers. He later alleged that they did not take care of him, leaving him without family support.With no wife or children, Kanhaiya Lal eventually found shelter at the Apna Ghar old-age home in Dayoli. He had been living there for approximately three-and-a-half years before his marriage.Sabina also found companionship at the old-age homeSabina, a 63-year-old woman originally from Kolkata, had also become separated from her loved ones due to circumstances in her life. She came to the Dayoli facility, where she met Kanhaiya Lal. Their conversations and growing familiarity gradually developed into a relationship based on trust and companionship. After spending time together, the two decided to get married rather than spend their remaining years alone.Traditional wedding celebrations at the ashramThe celebrations started on Tuesday evening, a day before the wedding. Women at the facility applied haldi to the bride and groom, following traditional Indian wedding customs. Mangalgeet, or auspicious wedding songs, filled the premises, while the beats of a dholki added to the celebrations.The couple had initially considered registering their marriage through a court ceremony. However, the old-age home management decided to organise a traditional wedding for them instead. A few people from Kanhaiya Lal's native village also attended the occasion. Among them were individuals who had helped rescue him and brought him to the old-age home.Neither Kanhaiya Lal nor Sabina was expected to have family members attending the wedding.Where will the couple live after marriage?The couple's new life together will begin at another old-age home operated by the Manav Seva Trust in Nalagarh. The management has arranged accommodation for both so they can stay together after their marriage. Preparations for their departure from Dayoli began around 3 pm on Wednesday.Prakash Chand Bansal, manager of the Apna Ghar old-age home, confirmed that the wedding had taken place and said arrangements were ready for the couple at the Nalagarh facility.

headline: Congress removes two PCC vice-presidents for organisational ‘inactivity’
content: Shimla: In a major organisational shake-up ahead of next year’s Himachal Pradesh assembly elections, the Congress has removed two Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) vice-presidents, Rajneesh Kimta and Mohinder Chauhan, from their posts with immediate effect for alleged organisational inactivity.Both functionaries were under scrutiny during an assessment of office-bearers’ performance. A party official said their prolonged absence from important party meetings and organisational programmes reportedly prompted the action.Kimta’s removal attracted attention because he had contested legislative assembly elections from the Chopal constituency in Shimla district and also served as the PCC general secretary (organisation).The party assessed office-bearers on the basis of attendance at meetings, participation in organisational activities and discharge of assigned responsibilities.State Congress president Vinay Kumar said the repeated absence of the two functionaries was taken seriously. The matter was discussed with the chairperson and members of the PCC disciplinary committee. Following the committee’s recommendation and approval from AICC in charge for Himachal, Rajani Patil, the decision was taken.The state party president made it clear that all office-bearers must ensure regular attendance and active participation in party programmes, adding that negligence would not be tolerated at any cost.

headline: Chandigarh professor appointed chairman of Centre’s scientific terminology commission
content: A Chandigarh-based academician has been appointed chairman of the Centre’s Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT), which standardises scientific and technical terms in Indian languages.Prof Sunil Kumar Singh, who was serving as Professor and Head of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Chandigarh College of Engineering and Technology (CCET), Degree Wing, has formally assumed charge of the post in the Union Ministry of Education in New Delhi for a three-year deputation.His appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on the recommendation of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). The Ministry of Education issued the appointment order on October 30.Singh has been associated with the CSTT for nearly two decades, contributing to its Expert Advisory Committee, multilingual terminology development, academic programmes and initiatives to promote scientific and technical education through Indian languages.An expert in artificial intelligence, natural language processing and technology-enabled education, he has published more than 260 research papers, authored and edited at least eight books and journals, and holds seven granted patents, besides two published patents.He has guided three PhD scholars and is currently supervising five others under Panjab University. He has also reviewed more than 770 research papers for over 145 international journals and received around 27 awards and appreciation certificates.His appointment comes amid the Centre’s push under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to expand access to higher and technical education in Indian languages.The CSTT is expected to strengthen the development and standardisation of technical vocabulary, educational resources and reference material in Indian languages, making contemporary knowledge in science and technology more accessible.Singh joined CCET through the UPSC in December 2014. He originally hails from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh.

headline: Chandigarh’s Group Home Exposes Gaps in Disability Care
content: Concerns raised by families and mental-health professionals about Chandigarh’s Group Home in Sector 32 have highlighted wider gaps in community-based care for persons with mental disabilities, including inadequate activities, shortages of trained staff and potentially restrictive access requirements. Nearly 40 persons with mental disabilities, family members, mental-health professionals, students and research scholars shared their experiences at an interaction organised by the Centre for Human Rights & Duties at Panjab University on Wednesday. The discussion included the experience of Rita Sharma, a single mother caring for her adult son, Rajat. Sharma said she had hoped the Sector 32 facility would provide longer-term support, but her son stopped attending after three weeks because he found the activities unengaging and the staff insufficiently trained, according to the report. The case illustrates the difference between creating a facility and providing the specialised support needed to make community-based care workable. Families require services that can respond to varied conditions, support daily living and offer continuity of care when family members are no longer able to provide it. Dr Upneet Kaur Mangat, chairperson of the Centre for Human Rights & Duties, said the ground situation remained difficult despite India’s obligations under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. She attributed continuing difficulties in accessing appropriate services to a shortage of rehabilitation facilities. Dr Adarsh Kohli, a retired professor of clinical psychology at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, said awareness of mental-health issues had improved but that government officials still showed insufficient understanding of group homes and assisted-living facilities. She also expressed concern about what she described as the UT administration’s reluctance to appoint professional staff at the Sector 32 home, despite qualified professionals being available in the city.

headline: Robotic surgery: How much will your health insurance policy actually pay?
content: The Delhi National Capital Region is emerging as India’s largest hub for robotic-assisted heart surgery, with around 1,800 procedures performed in 2025. Cardiac surgeons at the recently held 10th annual conference of the Society of Minimally Invasive Cardiovascular and Thoracic Surgeons of India said they expect that number to rise by around 40 per cent in 2026. Bengaluru is the second-most important centre. With more patients set to undergo these procedures, policyholders need to check whether their health insurance covers robotic-assisted surgery. “Robotic surgeries offer better patient outcomes in terms of a sho­rter hospital stay and faster recovery. They carry reduced risk of complications as well,” says Hari Radhakrishnan, expert, Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI). How widely it is covered Regulations bar insurers from excluding robotic surgery when doctors deem it necessary, so most policies cover it under modern treatments. The real question is how much they will pay. “An estimated 60-70 per cent of policies apply a sub-limit because robotic surgery falls under modern treatments, which can have their own limits,” says Kapil Mehta, co-founder, SecureNow. Check the fine print Read the modern treatments section of the policy wording and search for ‘robotic surgery’ or ‘modern treatment’ to understand whether these surgeries are covered. Next, check for sub-limits. On a hypothetical robotic surgery bill of ₹6 lakh, a procedure-specific sub-limit of ₹3 lakh could leave the policyholder paying the remaining ₹3 lakh, subject to other admissible expenses and deductions. Look at deductibles and room-rent restrictions too. “Check whether robotic instruments, consumables and associated technology charges are covered or restricted,” says Arun Ramamurthy, chief executive officer and co-founder, Staywell.Health. The usual waiting periods for pre-existing diseases apply to robotic surgeries as well. Check for exclusions too. Another important consideration is whether the procedure has been recommended by the treating specialist as medically necessary. “If a patient chooses robotic surgery purely as a preferred or premium alternative when a conventional procedure is equally suitable, the insurer may scrutinise the additional costs, depending on the policy wording,” says Shilpa Arora,co-founder and chief operating officer, Insurance Samadhan. Full cover costs more While robotic surgeries cost more up front, a shorter hospital stay, which translates into lower room rent and nursing charges, offsets a considerable portion of that cost. “It is therefore not always the case that robotic surgery is so expensive that insurers have to charge an additional premium to cover it,” says Radhakrishnan. Nonetheless, expect to pay more for a comprehensive policy. “Comprehensive policies typically cost about 20-30 per cent more than policies with sub-limits,” says Mehta. Only part of that gap reflects robotic surgery, as these plans offer better features in other areas. “Most plans launched in the past two to three years cover rob­otic surgery up to the full sum insured,” says Siddharth Singhal, head of health insurance, Policybazaar. Everyone should consider buying a comprehensive policy that covers robotic surgery up to the full sum insured, since no one can predict future illness. “It mat­ters most for people with a family history of heart disease, older buyers and those who may need a complex surgery,” says Arora. What to confirm before surgery Inform the insurer in advance, submit your doctor’s documents and seek written pre-authorisation. “Confirm whether robotic equipment and consumables are covered and whether any sub-limit or co-payment applies, and verify the cashless amount approved and your likely out-of-pocket cost,” says Ramamurthy. If your claim gets rejected or partly paid, approach the intermediary that sold you the policy to present your case to the insurer. “If the issue remains unresolved, escalate it through the insurer’s grievance redressal mechanism. The next step is to approach the insurance ombudsman. A court of law is a further option,” says Singhal. Tips for switching health plans Switch if better policy eases restrictive sub-limits or co-payments for robotic surgeryCompare overall cover, cashless network and long-term affordabilityCheck pre-existing disease terms, age-related underwriting and exclusions Consider switching if younger, healthy and underinsuredIf older, explore upgrades, add-ons and migration options with existing insurer Consider porting if migration is unavailableKeep existing cover until new insurer accepts and starts coverage

headline: Central government holiday 2027: 17 days off, 4 long weekends, optional leaves and more, check full list
content: The holiday list for 2027 has been unveiled by the central government for its offices across India. The list of holidays for the upcoming year includes four three-day-long weekends when a holiday falls on a Friday or Monday. It also has compulsory holidays, optional holidays and restricted holidays for the employees. Central government holiday list for 2027 According to a July 2026 Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) memorandum, central government offices in Delhi and New Delhi will have 17 compulsory holidays. Apart from this, employees can also opt for two additional holidays from the restricted holiday list. Offices outside this region will observe 14 compulsory holidays, along with three optional days which can be selected from a list of 12 optional holidays.
