headline: Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ to open for public tours as ‘example of corruption’: Delhi govt
content: New Delhi, Nov 26 (PTI) Public Works Department Minister Parvesh Verma announced on Thursday that the Delhi government will open former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ residence for a media tour initially, and later to the public. The minister said a ticketing system will be set up for reservation of visits for the public by this week. “The doors of Sheesh Mahal will open from tomorrow. We will show it to the media,” Verma said in a post on X in Hindi, along with a video attached of Kejriwal’s first oath-taking ceremony as chief minister of Delhi. “Looking at public demand, we will open ‘Sheesh Mahal’ for public tour. We will show the biggest example of corruption to people, that how one person who said he will not even use a government vehicle, had built the lavish residence for himself by demolishing several other houses,” the minister had said. Initially, media tours will be organised; later on, the public can buy tickets and see the interiors of the residence, he added. According to officials, the ticket price is likely to be around Rs 20 and for senior citizens and college students, the entry would be free.

headline: ‘Can’t stop us’: Amit Shah attacks Rahul Gandhi over women’s reservation, UCC
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday accused the Congress of disrespecting Constitutional institutions by imposing Emergency in 1975 as he reiterated the BJP-led NDA government's commitment to implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) and 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures. Addressing the Delhi unit of BJP to mark ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’ in the Capital, Shah stated that India's democratic journey began with the adoption of the Constitution on November 26, 1949. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he said, the poor had received rights, dignity and essential facilities. “Although the Constitution may appear to be merely a black-and-white written document, it embodies the aspirations and heartfelt wishes of all freedom fighters. It cannot be understood merely as a book. To understand its principles and underlying spirit, one must delve deep into it,” he said. Shah added, “The BJP government introduced Goods and Services Tax (GST) through the 101st Constitutional Amendment, thereby integrating the country's tax system, and provided for 33% reservation for women in Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies, which the Congress continues to block. I want to tell Rahul Gandhi that women will certainly get 33% reservation. You cannot stop us.” While the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha constantly speaks about the Constitution on one hand, he “ridicules constitutional institutions on the other”, Shah alleged. “Whenever a court verdict is not favourable to him, he questions the judiciary. Instead of engaging in discussions in Parliament, he talks about holding discussions on the streets. He maligns the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and travels abroad to tarnish India's image,” Shah alleged. “We too remained in the Opposition for a long time, but we never refused to participate in discussions in Parliament, nor did we disrespect the courts, the Election Commission or the electoral process. Rahul Gandhi's problem is that he has been continuously losing elections for 20 years, but blaming elections for his defeats is akin to the saying, 'A bad dancer blames the floor’,” he added. Shah said that while the nation was scaling new heights in every field, the Opposition was “spreading misconceptions about the Constitution.” “Our Constitution makers had included the UCC among the Directive Principles of State Policy so that every citizen, irrespective of religion, would be governed by a uniform law. Rahul Gandhi's party opposes it, but he wanted to make it clear that in the coming days, we are going to implement the UCC in all the BJP-ruled states,” he said.

headline: 164 Indonesian, Malaysian nationals rescued from ‘cyber slavery’ racket in Delhi
content: Lured to India with promises of lucrative jobs, 164 foreign nationals from Indonesia and Malaysia allegedly found themselves trapped in a network of cyber slavery, with their passports seized upon arrival, movement restricted, and lives reduced to making fraudulent calls to people back home, the Delhi Police said on Thursday.Kept in paying guest (PG) accommodations, allegedly served substandard food and subjected to physical assault if they refused to work, the foreign nationals were forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in their own countries through fraudulent investment platforms, police said.Also read: CBI nabs Hisar man for ‘cyber slavery’, trafficking of Indians to Southeast AsiaIn a major crackdown in southwest Delhi's Dwarka on an alleged international human trafficking and cyber fraud network, the Crime Branch of the Delhi Police has rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from premises allegedly being used to operate the racket. A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, has been arrested in connection with the case.According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India, promising attractive salaries and better career prospects. However, their ordeal allegedly began soon after they landed in the country.Also read: ₹14L with fake ₹6-crore lottery claim">Five held for duping Rohtak woman of ₹14L with fake ₹6-crore lottery claimTheir passports were taken away upon arrival, leaving them without control over their identity documents and restricting their ability to leave, police said. They were subsequently shifted to PG accommodations and allegedly forced to work as cyber slaves.Those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities were allegedly thrashed by members of the network to ensure compliance, a senior police officer said, adding that so far they have learned that around two people were thrashed.The living conditions at the accommodations were also allegedly poor, with the foreign nationals being provided substandard food. Despite a fleet of around 40 cabs being used to ferry them between the PG accommodations and the cyber fraud call centre, they were not allowed to venture out independently or move around as they wished, the officer said.Also read: Baghpat man trafficked to Cambodia for cyber fraud repatriated safely"The cabs were allegedly deployed to transport them to the call centre and bring them back to their accommodations, ensuring that their movement remained under the control of the handlers," the officer said.The foreign nationals were not merely made to operate computers and mobile phones but were allegedly trained to execute a specific pattern of cyber fraud. They were provided written scripts containing conversations that they had to follow while approaching prospective victims.The targets were primarily people in Malaysia and Indonesia. The operators allegedly created fictitious female identities and social media profiles to establish contact with unsuspecting individuals.Also read: ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad">Mohali: Haryana govt employee duped of ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad"Using these profiles, the foreign nationals were instructed to initiate conversations, develop online relationships and gradually gain the confidence of their targets. Once trust was established, the victims were persuaded to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms," the officer added.The syndicate allegedly used websites and APK-based applications to lure people with promises of high returns. The victims were made to believe that they were investing in legitimate financial opportunities, while the money was allegedly siphoned off through the fraudulent network."We got to know about the fraud after the crime branch received an email alert about the alleged cyber slavery racket around a week ago, following which its officers began developing intelligence about the network," the officer said.Initial information suggested that around 60 to 70 foreign nationals were being held and forced to work in the cyber fraud operation. However, when the police team conducted the operation at the suspected premises, the actual number turned out to be significantly higher. The operation led to the rescue of 164 foreign nationals, exposing the scale of the alleged racket.Also read: ₹55 lakh in cryptocurrency investment fraud in Delhi">5 held for cheating man of ₹55 lakh in cryptocurrency investment fraud in DelhiThe police are now investigating how the foreign nationals were recruited, who facilitated their travel to India, and how their passports were taken away. "During the entire investigation, two names -- Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati -- cropped up. Bhati used to arrange the PG accommodations and transportation facilities. Both are absconding, both will be arrested soon," the officer said.Certain bank accounts allegedly maintained by Kumar and Bhati have been identified as being used to meet rental and other operational expenses of the network. The financial trail is being examined to establish the flow of money, identify the beneficiaries and trace the proceeds generated through the alleged cyber fraud. The arrested Malaysian national, Tan Guan Wei, a resident of Negeri Sembilan, is being questioned about his alleged role in the network, his association with other members and the extent of his involvement in operating the fraudulent platforms.The police have seized a substantial digital infrastructure allegedly used to run the operation. The recoveries include 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports. Of the 355 mobile phones, 335 were old or used handsets, and 20 were new phones in sealed packaging. The 53 SIM cards include 31 international and 22 Indian connections. The recovered passports comprise 95 Indonesian and 79 Malaysian documents.Servers and other electronic material have also been seized. Investigators are examining the devices to identify the victims, establish the communication channels used by the syndicate and trace financial transactions linked to the fraudulent platforms.Also read: ₹25 crore">Gurugram: 2 arrested in PayU's cloud servers breach, siphoning over ₹25 croreA case has been registered at the Crime Branch police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway to identify other members of the international network and establish the extent of the alleged human trafficking and cyber fraud operation.

headline: Gen Z seeks jobs, AI-ready education and better sports infrastructure in budget consultations
content: New Delhi: Young people want the government to put job creation, industry-relevant skills and emerging technologies at the heart of the Union Budget 2027-28, pressing for an education system that keeps pace with a changing job market.The demands emerged at the finance ministry’s final pre-budget consultation on Thursday, where participants also called for better-paid internships, closer coordination between industry and educational institutions, and greater investment in sports infrastructure, two people familiar with the discussions told Mint.Chaired by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, the meeting was the 13th and final round of stakeholder consultations for the upcoming budget. Representatives from leading educational institutions and organisations across the country took part, with women accounting for around 40% of participants, the two people said.“The distinctive feature of this round of consultations was the participation of young people from different parts of the country, including remote regions, who shared suggestions on making education more skill-oriented and strengthening internship programmes through better stipends to provide students with practical exposure,” said the first person.Participants also called for closer coordination between industry and educational institutions to ensure that academic curricula better reflect industry requirements. They stressed the need to align education with artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies to prepare young people for changes in the job market.The finance ministry said in a post on X that Sitharaman had chaired the 13th and final pre-budget consultation with Yuva for the Union Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi on Thursday. The meeting was attended by the secretaries of the Department of Economic Affairs, the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.A separate consultation with experts and bureaucrats, also scheduled for Thursday, was cancelled. Neither of the two people cited above explained the reasons for the cancellation.The finance ministry spokesperson did not immediately respond to Mint’s request for comment.From classrooms to jobsThe emphasis on employability comes as the government continues to prioritize education, employment and skill development in its budgets.In the Union Budget 2026-27, the government allocated ₹1.39 trillion to the Ministry of Education, an increase of 8.27% over the previous year’s budget estimates. It also proposed a high-powered Education to Employment and Enterprise committee to recommend measures to strengthen the services sector and examine how emerging technologies, including AI, could affect jobs and skill requirements.The upcoming budget offers another opportunity to address the concerns raised by young people.Participants welcomed the finance ministry’s initiative to engage directly with young people and give them an opportunity to share their expectations and policy priorities ahead of the budget, the two people said.“Engaging young people in the budget-making process is important as they are among the most affected by decisions on education, employment and skills. The key challenge is to translate their suggestions into concrete policy measures, particularly by aligning education with changing industry needs, expanding quality apprenticeships and internships, and equipping young people with skills relevant to emerging technologies,” said D.P. Majhi, former director of Dr Ambedkar Foundation, an autonomous body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.“Greater coordination between the government, educational institutions and industry will be essential to improve employability,” said Majhi.“India’s demographic dividend will translate into an economic advantage only if young people have the skills that the job market demands. The focus should be on moving beyond classroom-based learning to industry-linked training, meaningful internships and greater exposure to emerging technologies,” said Arvind Mohan, former political researcher at Lokniti, the research programme of the Delhi-based Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.Sports and other prioritiesBeyond education and employment, participants called for greater support for sports. They suggested introducing more incentive-based programmes to encourage students to take up sports, alongside improving infrastructure and creating better opportunities for young talent, the second person said.The government had announced the Khelo India Mission to strengthen the country’s sports ecosystem in the 2026-27 budget. It also increased the allocation to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to ₹4,479.88 crore for 2026-27, from ₹3,346 crore in the previous year’s revised estimates.The youth consultation was part of a wider exercise that the finance ministry said it had concluded on Thursday. The consultations for the Union Budget 2027-28, held between 16 and 26 November, brought together more than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and groups in discussions chaired by Sitharaman, according to a statement from the finance ministry.The consultations covered industry, manufacturing, MSMEs, banking and financial services, information technology, infrastructure, employment, agriculture, education, skilling and youth affairs, among other areas.Suggestions included promoting domestic manufacturing of bio-fertilizers and advanced agricultural inputs, developing sector-specific artificial intelligence models suited to locally available hardware, and strengthening cyber-hygiene awareness among MSMEs and smaller financial institutions. Participants also called for measures to help rural youth and workers move into non-farm employment and sustainable enterprises.Other recommendations included promoting rental housing to expand affordable urban housing options, accelerating the development of tier-2 and tier-3 cities to support the transition from education to employment, and launching a nationwide reading movement to ensure every child can read and understand a newspaper by the end of Grade 5.

headline: Ministers scramble to return to Delhi as govt calls special Cabinet meet
content: Soon after parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had moved to reconvene Parliament, the government called a special Cabinet meeting on Friday, prompting several ministers to scramble to book flights to be in the Capital by 1pm, people aware of the matter said on Thursday.While some ministers were still in Delhi after Wednesday's meeting, others had to rearrange their travel plans at short notice, the people added. The meeting would mark a rare instance of the Union Cabinet convening twice in the same week, a rare departure from its usual weekly schedule.Follow live updates on Parliament special sitting here. The hurried arrangements came hours after ministers and lawmakers of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) put their travel plans on hold, with a leader telling HT that there was an “understanding” that a session could be announced at short notice and lawmakers should therefore remain prepared.“There are indications that the session may be convened in the first week of December…” the lawmaker had said.Rijiju later said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business.Leading up to Thursday, the Opposition questioned the delay in proroguing the monsoon session, with the government not offering an explanation. Rijiju has maintained that there is nothing unconstitutional about the delay.Also Read | As Parliament reconvenes, a look back at what parties said when women's quota bill failed in AprilThe developments come against the backdrop of the government's keenness to pass the delimitation and Constitution amendment bills to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies by 2029. The government has also been pushing to convene a special session to take up the proposed legislation.The Union government has reached out to Opposition parties, urging them to set aside political differences and support the bills, which seek to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50%. It has assured them that the proportional representation of states will be maintained.Also Read | NDA lawmakers put travel on hold hours before govt moved to reconvene ParliamentThe proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The bills are a prerequisite for implementing 33% reservation for women.The Opposition, however, has stuck to its demand that the government's assurances be incorporated into the bills. Some parties have also suggested that the government implement the reservation using the existing strength of the Lok Sabha.

headline: Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days
content: New Delhi, Nov 26 (PTI) Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026. Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor. "Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI. The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days. In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days. In 2023, the city recorded one satisfactory day, 12 moderate days, 16 poor days, 17 very poor days and 10 severe days. In 2022, there were two good days, four satisfactory days, eight moderate days, 22 poor days, 17 very poor days and three severe days. In 2021, Delhi recorded one good day, three satisfactory days, 19 moderate days, 10 poor days, 15 very poor days and eight severe days during the same period. The average PM2.5 concentration in Delhi declined to 113 micrograms per cubic metre this year from 158 in 2025 and 179 in 2024. The average PM10 concentration also fell to 221 micrograms per cubic metre from 287 last year and 320 in 2024. PM2.5 refers to fine particles with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or smaller, which can penetrate deep into the lungs, while PM10 includes particles with a diameter of 10 micrometres or smaller, including dust. Despite the decline in both pollutants, their average concentrations during the period remained considerably above the national annual standards of 40 micrograms per cubic metre for PM2.5 and 60 for PM10. They were also higher than the World Health Organisation's annual guidelines of 5 micrograms per cubic metre for PM2.5 and 15 for PM10.

headline: Delhi invites NGOs to rehabilitate beggars in 6 additional districts
content: New Delhi, Nov 26 (PTI) The Delhi government has invited applications from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to rehabilitate people engaged in begging in six additional districts and an existing hotspot under the Centre’s SMILE scheme, with an annual allocation of Rs 55.80 lakh for each district. The Department of Social Welfare has issued an Expression of Interest (EOI) for empanelling voluntary organisations, trusts and societies to implement the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) scheme, aimed at making India free of begging. The six additional districts identified for the programme are North-East, North, North-West, Central, East and South Delhi, while Rohini has been included as an existing hotspot, according to the EOI. The selected organisations may be assigned an entire district, a part of it or specific locations, including traffic intersections, railway stations, bus terminals, religious places, tourist spots and marketplaces, it stated. The scheme will cover surveys and identification of people engaged in begging, counselling, rescue and voluntary mobilisation to shelter homes, healthcare, skill development and livelihood support. It further mentioned that NGOs will also be responsible for helping beneficiaries obtain Aadhaar cards, voter identity cards, ration cards and bank accounts, besides linking them with government welfare schemes, health insurance, pensions and employment opportunities.

headline: Bengaluru overtakes Delhi as India's top domestic flight destination for year-end travel
content: Bengaluru: Domestic travel has witnessed a significant uptick this year, with travel agents and tour operators reporting increased enquiries and bookings, particularly for shorter holidays and long weekends.Improved connectivity, rising disposable incomes and a preference for exploring domestic destinations have contributed to sustained demand, they say.Bengaluru has overtaken Delhi as the country's most popular domestic flight destination for the 2026 year-end travel period, with bookings up 6.2% year-on-year. The city is also seeing increased demand across other modes of transport, with bus, train and hotel bookings showing significant growth, according to a report by online booking platform Cleartrip."Bengaluru is increasingly becoming a popular leisure destination among North Indians, especially during this time of the year, when the air pollution chokes other major cities. Apart from this, compared to cities like Delhi and Mumbai, weekend bookings at luxury hotels in Bengaluru are at least 25-30% cheaper," said Rohit Hangal, director, Sphere Travelmedia and Exhibitions..From Nov 27, Bengaluru will become second airport to introduce simultaneous runway ops.Hotel bookings in Bengaluru recorded an 88.1% year-on-year increase, placing it among the country's top 10 domestic hotel destinations.He added that the city has become a popular 'meeting point'. "With the uptick in migration, it has become the norm for friends and family to fly down into the city to meet people who've moved to the city. It's become popular for reunions. Plus, the fact that Bengaluru airport is one of the most well-connected in the country also helps," he explained.Among those travelling outside Bengaluru, Himachal Pradesh, Goa, Rajasthan and Sikkim remain popular domestic destinations despite the high airfare, said travel agents."With the increasing spending power, people don't mind spending extra if they can shorten the travel time. They want to spend on leisure travel. For the year-end, travel to the lesser-explored destinations has been popular. Rajasthan, too, is a fan favourite due to the good weather now," said Mohan Hegde, manager at Nesara Tours, adding that domestic travel had seen a 40% hike in demand this year.Bus bookings to Bengaluru grew 253.8% year-on-year, while several routes connecting the city to popular destinations recorded sharp increases.The Bengaluru-Chennai route saw a 466.7% rise, followed by Bengaluru-Ernakulam at 650%, Bengaluru-Munnar at 1,100% and Bengaluru-Goa at 257.1%. Bookings on the return Goa-Bengaluru route increased 220%, while the Bengaluru-Hyderabad corridor recorded a 170% rise. These trends are part of the platform's PeekABoo Trends Tracker, which analysed travel demand for the year-end period between November 20 and December 31."There is such a demand that the number of buses on the ground has increased by about 40%. This includes both new operators and additional fleets by existing operators," said an official from SRS Travels.The tracker also found that travellers aged 15-34 accounted for 57.6% of air bookings, 51.4% of hotel bookings, 50% of bus bookings and 66.2% of train bookings nationally. Bengaluru featured among the preferred domestic destinations for both Gen Z and millennial travellers.

headline: Delhi-NCR, Ahmedabad see highest housing inventory overhang: Knight Frank
content: Housing markets in Delhi-NCR and Ahmedabad are witnessing higher levels of inventory overhang, or unsold units, compared with other leading residential markets, according to real estate consultancy Knight Frank's Quarters to Sell (QTS) metric. The metric, which measures the time required to absorb existing inventory at the average sales rate of the last eight quarters, showed that the time required to sell existing inventory has reached two years in both markets. Delhi-NCR's QTS climbed from 7.3 quarters (equivalent to 1.8 years) to 8.0 quarters (equivalent to two years). Ahmedabad recorded the highest inventory overhang among all major cities in Q3 2026, with its QTS rising from 7.8 quarters, equivalent to 1.95 years, in Q3 2025 to 8.2 quarters, equivalent to 2.05 years, in Q3 2026. The absorption period in NCR has lengthened as average sales eased by 8 per cent, primarily owing to demand moderation in the luxury housing category of ₹5-10 crore. In Ahmedabad, strong new project launches have kept supply ahead of sales-driven absorption, lifting unsold inventory by 9 per cent compared with a modest 3 per cent increase in average sales. Overall, across the country's eight leading residential markets, the average Quarters to Sell (QTS) edged up to 6.1 quarters, or 1.52 years, in Q3 2026 from an eight-year low of 5.8 quarters, or 1.45 years, recorded during the same period last year (Q3 2025). At 6.1 quarters, QTS remains significantly lower than the seven to eleven quarters recorded between 2018 and 2021. Commenting on the trend, Gulam Zia, International Partner and Senior Executive Director – Research, Advisory, Infrastructure and Valuation, Knight Frank India, said, “Despite a marginal increase in Quarters to Sell, the Indian residential market, with an average QTS of 6.1 quarters, continues to demonstrate resilience. While NCR and Ahmedabad are witnessing longer absorption periods, QTS across the other six markets ranges from 4.3 to 6.4 quarters, signalling that the Indian residential market's fundamentals remain sound.” Among other major cities, Bengaluru recorded the sharpest rise in inventory overhang, with its QTS increasing from 4.6 quarters in Q3 2025 to 5.5 quarters in Q3 2026. Hyderabad and Pune also witnessed an increase in inventory overhang, with their QTS rising to 6.1 quarters and 4.7 quarters, respectively. Meanwhile, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata recorded an improvement in their inventory absorption cycles. Kolkata had the lowest QTS among the eight markets at 4.3 quarters, down from 4.7 quarters a year ago, as sales outpaced new launches, reducing unsold inventory by 10 per cent. Mumbai's QTS declined from 6.6 quarters to 6.4 quarters, while Chennai recorded a marginal improvement from 4.5 quarters to 4.4 quarters.

headline: 'Misconceived, untenable': Delhi High Court sets aside Centre's order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
content: New Delhi: The Delhi High Court on Thursday set aside the Centre's order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), saying the allegation that it has indulged in "aggressive anti-government political activism" was not based on any material..The high court said the government's cancellation order was misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact.."Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant's (SLIC) activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest..Order cancelling UK-based journalist's OCI card lacks specific reasons: Delhi High Court."The respondent’s (Centre) allegation that the appellant has indulged in 'aggressive anti-government political activism', is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation," Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani said..The court, in its 69-page judgement, said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in "political activity" or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains.."In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant's activities amount to an attempt to portray a 'wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community'. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light," it said..The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate..The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country..The high court said since the cancellation order was issued after the term of the FCRA registration certificate had already expired, the NGO is at liberty to file its renewal application, which would be decided by the authorities expeditiously without reference to the violations that were subject of the earlier cancellation order..The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.."However, upon examining the use to which foreign contributions have been put by the appellant, it is seen that such funds have been utilised and deployed for activities that are perfectly in line with the stated objectives of the appellant, namely, of providing legal-aid and engaging in social welfare activities," Justice Bhambhani said..The court said the MHA has not offered any justification or reason as to why it was necessary to adopt the drastic measure of cancelling the NGO's FCRA registration..Excise case: Trial court's order discharging Arvind Kejriwal suffers palpable errors, CBI tells Delhi HC.The NGO submitted that to undertake activities to benefit adivasis, Dalits, poor, women and children, acid attack victims, and child abuse victims can never amount to indulging in political activity or to portraying a poor image of the country to outsiders..It referred to a Supreme Court's decision in which it has been held that political activity must relate to active or party politics; and also that even habitual holding of bandhs or hartals in support of public causes does not make an organisation political..The court also noted that the government's allegation that the NGO has indulged in "aggressive anti-government political activism" does not find mention either in the show-cause notice or in the cancellation order and has only come in the reply filed by it in this appeal..It said on the point of law, an order must sustain on the reasons that are stated in it and they cannot be supplemented by way of a reply or an affidavit filed subsequently in the course of court proceedings.."While the respondent contends that the violations on the appellant’s part were brought to its notice through 'security inputs', which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs," the court said.

headline: Excise case: Trial court's order discharging Arvind Kejriwal suffers palpable errors, CBI tells Delhi HC
content: New Delhi: The CBI on Thursday contended before the Delhi High Court that the trial court's order discharging AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia and others in the excise policy case suffered from palpable errors and ignored material evidence..Seeking to set aside the trial court's February 27 discharge order, the probe agency said this was a case which could not be thrown at the threshold..The counsel for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) submitted before Justice Sachin Datta that there were several glaring defects in the trial court's decision and the order should be set aside..Delhi High Court gives 3 weeks to Arvind Kejriwal, other Aam Aadmi Party leaders to respond to criminal contempt case."The trial court judge travelled beyond the scope of its powers. It was not supposed to conduct a mini trial at the stage of charge. The trial court judge conducted a mini trial which was not permissible," Additional Solicitor General S V Raju argued..He contended that the trial court's order was patently illegal, perverse and suffered from errors apparent on the face..There were palpable errors on the face of it and material evidence was ignored and not considered by the trial court, Raju argued..He further said there was a lot of evidence on record to show that criminal conspiracy existed but the trial court judge failed to appreciate that conspiracy existed in the case..The trial court has erred by commenting on the evidentiary value of the material at the stage of charge, he said while concluding his submissions..The high court listed the matter for December 9 and 10 to hear the submissions of respondents, including the AAP leaders, on the aspect of maintainability of CBI's revision petition..The respondents have raised objections over maintainability of CBI's revision petition..The high court was hearing arguments on CBI's plea challenging the discharge of Kejriwal, Sisodia and others in the excise policy case..On February 27, the trial court discharged Kejriwal, Sisodia and 21 others in the liquor policy case, ruling that it was wholly unable to survive judicial scrutiny and stood discredited in its entirety..In its revision petition, the CBI has said that the discharge order was patently illegal, perverse and suffered from errors apparent on the face..The petition has contended that the trial court conducted a mini-trial at the stage of framing of charges and passed the discharge order on a "selective reading of the prosecution case"..IRCTC hotel 'scam': Delhi HC seeks ED stand on Lalu Yadav's plea against money laundering charges.Not only did the trial court fail to appreciate the facts of the case but it also passed unwarranted adverse remarks against the investigating agency and the investigating officer, the plea has claimed..According to the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate, irregularities were allegedly committed while modifying the excise policy and undue favours were extended to the licence holders..The previous government in Delhi implemented the policy on November 17, 2021, and scrapped it by the end of September 2022 amid allegations of corruption..The ED's money laundering case stems from a CBI case lodged after the then Delhi lieutenant governor recommended a probe into the alleged irregularities in the implementation of the excise policy.

headline: Delhi most polluted city in NCR for PM2.5, PM10, says Delhi-based think tank
content: New Delhi: Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026.

headline: Saket Court Acquits Former My FM CEO Harish Bhatia Of Sexual Harassment Charges, Finds Testimony Unreliable
content: A Saket court has acquitted former My FM CEO Harish M. Bhatia of sexual harassment charges, holding that the complainant’s sole testimony, marked by contradictions and improvements, did not prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. New Delhi: Harish M. Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, was acquitted by a court at Saket in Delhi on Monday, November 23, 2026, of charges under Sections 354 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code, the court holding that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt [State v. Harish M. Bhatia]. The judgment was delivered by Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of the Saket courts. The Court reiterated the standard for convicting on the complainant’s word alone: “The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence.” Where a case rests mainly on that testimony, the Court said, it must be scrutinised with greater care to ensure it is free of material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities.

headline: Delhi High Court strikes down ASI’s 65-year age limit for Taj Mahal photographers
content: Observing that self-employed professionals should not be barred from earning a livelihood merely because of their age, the Delhi High Court has struck down the Archaeological Survey of India's (ASI) decision to fix 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers working at the Taj Mahal. Justices Prathiba M Singh and Dinesh Bhatt were hearing the plea filed by 37 ASI-licensed photographers who provided photography services to tourists visiting the Taj Mahal, challenging the ASI’s 2017 policy that fixed 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers. "With the increase in life expectancy levels, even at the age of 65, professionals are physically and mentally equipped to render their services. Sometimes it is even a necessity or compulsion for such senior citizens who are self-dependent. Skills such as photography do not require enormous physical labour, and in fact their experience of being at the monument for so long may act as an advantage to tourists and visitors," the November 23 order read. The high court stated that the photographers were self-employed persons, who must be allowed to work as long as their "physical and mental faculties permit" and further observed that even in the field of business and politics, people much older than 65 continued to work and their age was not a problem but a positive feature. The photographers were opposing clauses 9 and 9.3 of the ASI's policy dated May 24, 2017, which introduced an age limit for licensed photographers. According to clause 9.1, photographers above 60 years must undergo a medical fitness test and get a certificate from a registered medical practitioner confirming that they are physically and mentally fit. Clause 9.2 makes the certificate mandatory for licence renewal. Clause 9.3 states 65 years as the maximum retirement age, which would mean that photographers could not continue working after that. As per clause 9.4, licences renewed after the age of 64 will be valid only until the photographer turns 65. The photographers alleged that the ASI had given them licences only after conducting tests and checking their eligibility and that they had been working as licensed photographers at the Taj Mahal for many years and their licences had been regularly renewed. The photographers contended that, as per an ASI advertisement dated August 24, 2000, their licence applications were evaluated and then renewed in 2003, and they had been providing photography services at the Taj Mahal without any interruption since then. The photographers stated that the newly introduced retirement age would force them to stop working and seriously affect their livelihood, as photography was their only source of income. 'Only source of livelihood' Advocate Anjana Gosain, appearing for the photographers, argued that setting a retirement age would deprive the photographers of their only source of livelihood and adversely affect their families, who were dependent upon their earnings. The counsel submitted that setting a retirement age affected the photographers' right to life under Article 21 as their livelihood would be "jeopardised". The counsel urged that photography was a professional service for which the ASI made no payment to the photographers and the restriction would not allow them to give their services as photographers at the monument. The counsel stated that fixing an age limit for photographers, who did not need any particular physical fitness, was "discriminatory and arbitrary". Advocate Vikrant Nilesh Goyal and Rakesh Kumar appearing for the ASI and the government, argued that if a retirement age was not given, then younger photographers would not get an opportunity to work at the Taj Mahal, which would result in overcrowding and a lack of space for tourists. The counsel contended that many licensed photographers also sent their "nominees" to render photography services, instead of working themselves, and these photographers were not fully aware of the "technological advancements" and were not able to provide service in an "efficient and modernised" manner. 'Self-employed professionals' The high court noted that the Supreme Court had observed in a judgment that "the nature of the licence granted by the ASI is merely one of access to the monument. Beyond that, the professionals have to compete amongst themselves, and show their technical competence and fitness to the tourists, who wish to avail of their services." The bench noted that as per the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, both photographers and tourist guides were "similarly placed" as both were licensed by the ASI, and the retirement age of tourist guides, which was set at 65 years, was struck down by the Supreme Court in one of its judgments, even though the job of tourist guides might involve "considerable physical exertion" The high court said that mostly the photographers remained "stationed" at a particular place within the monument and "the level of physical fitness required for performing such services would, therefore, not be equivalent to that required of tourist guides and may, in fact, be considerably lesser." The court was of the view that if an age restriction of 65 years was not held fair for tourist guides, then there was "no justification for imposing a similar restriction on the petitioners (photographers)". Calling it discriminatory, the high court struck down Clause 9.3, which fixed 65 years as the retirement age, and held that since the photographers were self-employed professionals, they could continue working for as long as their health allowed, but held that they would still have to undergo medical fitness tests and submit certificates from registered medical practitioners. The high court also ordered that the photographers couldn't allow others to use their licences or sub-license them, and if they did so, then their licences would be cancelled immediately. The court also stated that they might also need to attend refresher courses and clear any tests conducted by the ASI. Additionally, the court said that the nominees of photographers would be allowed to work only when the licensed photographer had disabilities, and the ASI could conduct medical or physical fitness tests even after they turn 65.

headline: After Delhi, I.N.D.I.A. bloc to hold major anti-SIR/CEC rallies in BJP-ruled Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and West Bengal
content: New Delhi: After the Ramlila Maidan rally in Delhi, I.N.D.I.A parties are heading to Bhopal and Ahmedabad next month and Kolkata in January, as the Opposition bloc plans to mount pressure on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Modi government over ‘vote chori’.The Bhopal rally is scheduled for December 12 while the one in Ahmedabad will be held on December 19. The rally in Kolkata is likely to be held only after January 15 next year.Sources said the I.N.D.I.A bloc is looking at BJP-ruled states as their protest destinations. A senior Opposition leader did not rule out holding one in Uttar Pradesh provided Samajwadi Party and Congress manage to stitch an electoral alliance for Assembly elections on time..“There is no point in holding anti-CEC rallies in states where the Opposition parties are in power. Our target is the BJP-ruled states,” the leader said. Following intense street protests in October, the Opposition parties had held a rally in Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, which saw top leaders participating. The Opposition parties have already restarted their protest on Thursday, celebrating the Constitution Day while protesting against the Modi government and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which they claimed was aimed at disenfranchising voters.“The SIR issue is not dying down,” the leader said. The Opposition is also alleging that the CEC was helping the BJP to steal elections.The decision to hold rallies in five cities was taken at a meeting of the I.N.D.I.A bloc in September. In October, the Opposition bloc along with students and youth activists had marched to Election Commission, Jantar Mantar, Supreme Court and Rashtrapati Bhavan demanding Kumar’s resignation..Supreme Court directs Election Commission to increase strength of West Bengal SIR tribunals, prioritise pleas against deletions.Sources said the Opposition is also looking at another opportunity to meet President Droupadi Murmu to share “proof” of ‘vote chori’ with her. The suggestion for seeking an appointment to meet the President came, citing Murmu’s suggestion to the I.N.D.I.A delegation on October 9 to provide her with proof, sources said. If this materialises, the Opposition leaders are likely to provide proof of voters who were “wrongly” deleted from electoral rolls.Rahul had then claimed he was “shocked and stunned” to see that the President in “no way denied, questioned or argued” with what they said about ‘vote chori’ though she asked them to provide her proof to substantiate their claims.

headline: Delhi govt tightens attendance watch: Daily biometric reports by 11 am mandatory after suspected tampering
content: From suspected tampering with biometric machines to attendance reports reaching headquarters after 11 am, the Delhi Government is tightening its watch on employee attendance, with Social Welfare Department introducing a daily verification mechanism across its offices, homes and institutions.In a circular dated November 25, the department directed all Heads of Offices, institutions and district offices to submit biometric attendance reports for every staff member under their jurisdiction to its Administration Branch every day. The reports must be sent in both hard and soft copies, with the digital version emailed by 11 am. Each report must be verified by the head of the establishment concerned, and delays will be taken seriously.The latest instruction follows a series of measures to make attendance monitoring more accountable. In July, the department ordered centralisation of biometric attendance devices at its headquarters, requiring functional internet connectivity, an inventory of machines and daily, weekly and monthly reports. It also said attendance records would be cross-checked for administrative and salary-related purposes.The issue took a sharper turn in August, when service engineers reportedly found water inside several biometric machines during an inspection. The circumstances raised suspicion of deliberate damage, after which the department decided to bring the devices under CCTV surveillance. It also examined the possibility of a mobile-based Aadhaar-enabled attendance system with face authentication and real-time geolocation for field staff.The attendance push is part of a wider government effort to regulate the availability of officials. In April, following a surprise inspection by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta at the State GST office, departments were directed to ensure biometric attendance across cadres. The Chief Secretary subsequently warned of action for non-compliance.Separately, in October, senior officers were directed to inform the Chief Minister and the minister concerned before taking leave. This followed earlier instructions on leave intimation, including the use of WhatsApp for communication.The November circular does not announce fresh disciplinary penalties or establish that employees have manipulated attendance records. It does, however, make daily reporting and verification compulsory, placing responsibility on institutional heads to ensure that attendance data reaches headquarters on time.

headline: Spotlight Promotions: Delhi-Based Digital Marketing and Social Media Marketing Agency Led by Brijesh Dhingra and Sugandha Aneja Dhingra
content: New Delhi [India], November 26: Spotlight Promotions, a Delhi-based digital marketing agency and social media marketing agency specialising in the restaurant, hospitality and food and beverage (F&B) industry, is strengthening its presence in India’s growing digital marketing landscape under the leadership of Founder Brijesh Dhingra and Co-Founder Sugandha Aneja Dhingra. With expertise in restaurant marketing, hospitality branding and digital brand development, Spotlight Promotions has successfully handled more than 300 projects and currently manages approximately 100 active clients. Positioned as a specialised hospitality marketing agency, the company provides a comprehensive range of services, including social media management, digital marketing, brand strategy, restaurant branding, creative campaign development, professional food photography, videography, influencer marketing coordination, digital promotions and restaurant launch marketing. Founded with the vision of helping businesses build distinctive brand identities, Spotlight Promotions focuses on delivering integrated digital marketing solutions for restaurants, cafés, lounges, clubs, premium dining destinations and hospitality businesses. The agency has worked with several recognised names in the hospitality and entertainment industry, including Studio XO, Molecule and Cafe Delhi Heights. Its approach combines creative storytelling, strategic social media marketing and professional visual content to help brands establish a stronger digital presence. Brijesh Dhingra, Founder of Spotlight Promotions, has been instrumental in shaping the company’s business vision, client relationships and expansion within the digital marketing and hospitality sectors. His approach focuses on understanding the unique positioning of each business and developing customised marketing strategies that support brand awareness, customer engagement and business growth.

headline: Ghaziabad couple thought they made crores, but couldn’t withdraw even Re 1
content: It took just over a month for a fake share trading scheme, advertised on Instagram, to wipe out a Ghaziabad couple’s savings. By the time they realised they had been cheated of Rs 75.13 lakh, their trading account was showing a fortune of Rs 4.75 crore – money they could neither touch nor withdraw. Five months later, they sold their home of nearly three decades. Today, the couple, aged 54 and 64, lives in a rented house in a village in Greater Noida's Jewar, paying a rent of Rs 10,000 a month. As the husband, a civil engineer who once worked for a private firm, looks for a job, the woman, who has battled cancer for years, is struggling to come to terms with how an Instagram advertisement turned their lives upside down. They are not alone. Their story is among hundreds of share trading scams reported in Ghaziabad, where such frauds have emerged as the largest category of cybercrime cases. Between January 1, 2024, and October 31, 2026, the Ghaziabad cyber police station registered 390 share trading fraud cases involving Rs 145.65 crore. These accounted for nearly 46% of the 849 cyber fraud cases registered during the period. For the couple, it began in January 2024, when the woman came across an Instagram advertisement purportedly linked to an American investment firm. It promised high returns from share trading. She clicked on it and was added to a WhatsApp group. “The group had the photograph of a member of the company’s board of directors as its icon. I even checked it on the company’s website,” she recalled. On January 18, the couple emailed the company through its official website, informing it that they had joined its online trading group. Over the next month, they invested in stocks recommended by people running the WhatsApp group. Among the investments were Rs 33 lakh from the husband’s retirement savings. The balance displayed on their trading account kept growing. At one point, it showed Rs 4.75 crore. For a couple who had spent years battling financial and medical crises, the prospect of earning such money seemed like a way out. The woman had worked in office administration until 2015, when she quit her job to spend more time with her daughter, who had started college. Around the same time, she was diagnosed with stage three ovarian cancer. “My cancer relapsed four times. It spread from my ovaries to my uterus, pancreas, liver and then to my right breast. The treatment was costing us a lot, so I started investing in shares to earn some money,” she said. Her husband, meanwhile, would privately message other members of the WhatsApp group to ask about their experience. “I’m getting rich,” he used to get a reply. Then came the promise of an even bigger windfall. The group administrators told them an initial public offering (IPO) was coming up and promised returns of Rs 1 crore. “We had only Rs 11 lakh at the time. They said they would give us a loan of Rs 41 lakh, which we could repay later. We agreed,” the woman said. On February 24, the couple finally received a response from the investment firm. It said there was no such WhatsApp group or share trading operation associated with it. “We froze. My husband tried calling all the numbers on the group but they were switched off. When he checked the numbers on Truecaller, they appeared to be linked to Bihar, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh,” said the woman. They found that they could not withdraw the amount displayed on their trading account. When the couple refused to invest further and demanded their money back, the people they were talking to allegedly began threatening them over the purported loan and asked for the money back. “They started calling and abusing us,” the woman said. In February 2024, the couple approached the Ghaziabad cyber police station, alleging that they had been cheated of Rs 75.13 lakh. What followed were months of visits to the police station. “We would sit there from 11 in the morning until 5 in the evening, almost every day, for months,” the woman recalled. On July 24, 2024, the couple sold their flat in Ghaziabad to repay the Rs 41 lakh being demanded by the alleged fraudsters. It was the same flat they had bought for around Rs 13 lakh after moving from Bengaluru to Delhi-NCR in the late 1990s, hoping for better jobs and opportunities. The couple alleged their daughter and son-in-law abandoned them during the crisis. According to the woman, police have so far recovered around Rs 11 lakh of their money. Their ordeal reflects a wider pattern of cyber fraud in Ghaziabad. While share trading fraud cases fell from 203 in 2024 to 126 in 2025, the amount lost increased by Rs 1.95 crore. Another 61 cases were registered in the first 10 months of 2026. A police officer investigating such cases said fraudsters often lure people through social media advertisements before adding them to WhatsApp groups where fake profits are displayed to encourage further investments. “They target rich and high-profile people by running AI generated videos in which known faces such as that of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and industrialists, to make their schemes appear genuine. They then add people to online groups,” the officer added. The officer further said the money is often routed through multiple accounts and, in some cases, transferred abroad, including to Cambodia and China. In another case registered in March 2024, a retired general manager of a central public sector enterprise, based in Ghaziabad, alleged that he was cheated of Rs 1.38 crore after joining a WhatsApp group offering a six-month stock market training programme. According to the FIR lodged under the Information Technology (Amendment) Act, the group conducted online classes, sometimes throughout the day, with people posing as market experts offering investment advice. The organisers allegedly claimed that the firm was registered with SEBI. It added that during the sessions, they were taught how to apply for IPOs, “through what they described as a foreign institutional investor account”. However, when he was unable to withdraw his money, he approached the police. So far, police have recovered around Rs 98 lakh in the case.
