headline: CJP's Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being stopped from travelling to London over passport row
content: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London over alleged discrepancies in his passport details, particularly his place of birth.Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union on December 1. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.The development followed a show-cause notice issued to Das by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, on Monday evening, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his birth-related documents within seven days. The notice warned that his passport could be impounded under the Passports Act, 1967, if he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation.According to government sources, inconsistencies in details such as his date of birth and father's name were flagged across documents, including his Aadhaar card, passport and school certificate. The authorities initiated a fresh verification of his documents and information recorded in his passport application.The passport was originally issued to Das on August 21, 2019, following the verification process.Why was Saurav Das stopped from travelling?According to government officials, a passport holder issued a show-cause notice over allegedly incorrect particulars cannot use the passport for international travel until the matter is resolved.An official told TOI, "As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of."Another government officer said Das had time until November 30 to respond to the notice. The official added that he could resume international travel using the same passport once the RPO completed its re-verification and cleared the documents.However, Das said he became aware of the notice only after reaching the airport, claiming that it had been issued just hours before his scheduled departure.Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Das questioned the timing of the notice and the discrepancies flagged by the authorities, pointing out that his passport had been issued in 2019 after police verification and that he had undertaken several international trips since then.“How was I issued the passport which was given after police verification?” he asked.Alleging that the action was linked to his association with the CJP, Das said, “I was scheduled to talk in various prestigious universities in London on their invitation. That trip couldn’t be completed because the coward govt has flagged my passport citing some discrepancies...”UK engagements cancelled amid controversyApart from the Oxford Union panel discussion, Das said he was scheduled to participate in engagements involving Cambridge University, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.The Oxford Union event was scheduled for December 1, with Das and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke listed as key panellists on the organisation's website.Explaining the purpose of his proposed engagements, Das said he intended to discuss the growth of the CJP movement and its use of non-violent methods.“The Indian students studying there wanted to understand what CJP movement is and how it grew. I would have spoken about how this movement without violence could become successful. How the world’s Gen Z could learn from us,” he said.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh, who was also scheduled to travel to the UK, said her visa had been rejected a few days earlier. Dipke said he had also received an invitation but was scheduled to attend a CJP programme in Nagpur on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.The London School of Economics Students' Union Amnesty International Society subsequently announced that its event featuring Das had been indefinitely postponed. In a statement, it condemned what it described as an “arbitrary obstruction” and the “apparent targeting of an individual seeking to engage in academic dialogue and public discussion”.The society expressed solidarity with Das and said it would share updates if the event could be rescheduled.CJP questions action against DasCJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the decision to stop Das from travelling, drawing comparisons with the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi.“Is he (Das) a terrorist, a criminal? Why was he stopped?” Dipke asked at a separate press conference.Meanwhile, a public interest litigation has also been filed in the Madras High Court concerning alleged inconsistencies in Das's birth and parentage documents, while also questioning his citizenship.The passport authorities' re-verification process is pending, with Das required to respond to the show-cause notice by November 30.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Miranda House introduces professional certificate courses for the AI, creator economy
content: Miranda House, University of Delhi (DU), has launched a portfolio of professional certificate courses to equip university students with practical, industry-oriented skills for the evolving creative, media, and technology economy. This initiative, introduced in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Eros AIVidya, is aimed at helping participants understand how they can integrate creative technology and AI skills into practical learning opportunities. The initial portfolio offers University of Delhi students 15 six-month professional certificate courses, co-certified by the collaborating partners. The list of programmes includes AI Filmmaking, Influencer and Creator Business, Avatar and Digital Human Creation, Animation, Video Blogging, AR/VR Production, VFX Editing, Script Writing, Acting, Music Production, Music Composition and Direction, Sound Editing, Editing and Art Direction. Also Read | No relief for Delhi University's first 4-yr UG batch as HC refuses to intervene, directs UGC to decide The launch of these professional certificate courses on AI and the creator economy follows India's increased emphasis on skills and infrastructure for its creative and digital economy, as stated by the institute. Admission process and fees structure Admissions for these programmes are currently open to eligible DU students, irrespective of their gender. Candidates applying for the courses are required to possess a valid Class 12 pass certificate or mark sheet, while the selection process is strictly based on merit. The course fees range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,50,000 depending on the programme chosen by the candidate. As notified by the institute, a loan facility is available for interested students, subject to valid documentation and applicable terms and conditions. What will participants get? Through the AI Filmmaking course, participants will be introduced to emerging AI-enabled approaches to content creation, while the Influencer and Creator Business course will help them learn the professional and commercial skills relevant to the creator economy. Avatar and Digital Human Creation programme will take students through the emerging forms of virtual identity and digital media. These courses are offered alongside creative disciplines such as animation, VFX, acting, script writing, editing, music and sound, enabling students to develop capabilities across both creative craft and emerging technologies. Also Read | 400 marks for research: Why DU teachers want fresh evaluation guidelines On completion of these courses, 15 high-performing students will receive support through the collaboration to start their own businesses, as announced by the institute. The opportunity will also be extended to students who demonstrate noteworthy performance during their courses.

headline: Building materials lie in open, anti-smog guns don’t work: Noida builders fined Rs 2.33 cr
content: Construction material left lying in the open. Sprinklers that barely wet the ground. Anti-smog guns that did not work. Excavated soil left uncovered, and trucks entering and leaving construction sites without having their tyres washed. In one case, construction continued even after a complete ban on the activity had come into force. For these lapses, builders in Noida have been fined a total of nearly Rs 2.33 crore, as authorities crack down on construction and demolition waste, a key source of pollution in the National Capital Region, which is currently grappling with its worst air quality of the season. Official data also shows that around 60 fines, amounting to more than Rs 1.5 crore, have been recommended in Greater Noida. An analysis of official records shows that around 75 penalties were imposed in Noida between September 30 and November 12. In October alone, the government issued challans worth Rs 1.3 crore against 47 construction projects. The data also shows that most of the fines were relatively small, with many below Rs 50,000. They also included penalties against the Noida Authority's own construction projects. Across the seven air quality monitoring stations in Noida, the 24-hour average PM2.5 over the last 30 days ranged from 104 to 206 µg/m³, against the 60 µg/m³ national 24-hour standard. The worst was Sector-62 (IITM), at an average of 206 and a peak of 365, CPCB data showed. The PM10 average noted here was 315 µg/m³ and highest peaks noted at 496 µg Sector-110 had the second-highest PM10 peak, at 393 µg Such elevated PM 10 level values is a clear indicator of coarse dust due to construction, road and other dust-generating works. The violators Noida and Greater Noida have been under GRAP Stage I since October 21, Stage II since November 2 and Stage III since November 6. During the first two stages, builders are required to transport waste in covered vehicles, deploy anti-smog guns and sprinkle water at construction sites, with these measures intensified as air quality deteriorates. Under GRAP Stage III, most construction activity is prohibited, with exceptions limited to projects of national importance. The October data covers three zones in Noida, excluding areas falling under the Greater Noida jurisdiction. Zone I recorded the highest penalties against 22 construction activities. The zone covers sectors 1 to 62. Zone II imposed against 16 such works, the area falling under the zone includes Sector 63 to 124. Meanwhile in Zone III, 9 fine recommendations were imposed, with areas from Sector 125-168. According to official records, the largest penalty, Rs 50 lakh, was imposed on October 5 on the Ivory County project in Sector 115, weeks before the strictest restrictions came into force. “Construction material was lying in the open, putting dust into the air, and the water sprinkling on site was ineffective,” a senior officer said. On November 12, the same penalty was imposed on Mahagun Infratech for a project in Sector 107. “By then, a complete ban on most construction activity was in force under GRAP Stage III. Work was still going on,” the officer said. Four other projects — Godrej Palm Retreat, Triune Global Solutions, Krescent Homes in Jaypee Greens Wishtown — were each recommended for penalties of Rs 10 lakh. “At the Godrej site, inspectors found four anti-smog guns that were not working, along with construction material lying in the open. At the Triune site, excavated soil was left uncovered and there was no tyre-washing system, among other violations,” the officer said. The pattern extends to Greater Noida, where an official said a penalty of Rs 50 lakh had been recommended against Avaada Electro Private Limited after a field inspection found violations of prescribed norms. Around 60 fines, totalling more than Rs 1.5 crore, were recommended in Greater Noida between August 1 and November 14, according to official data. Enforcement on the ground At 11 am on Monday, two Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) officials sat down at their office in Sector 1, Noida, with a list of registered construction sites spread across the table. On one computer screen, a team member pulled up live camera feeds from construction sites across the city. On the printed sheet, another began checking addresses and recording observations from the camera footage. This is how Chudamani Nimbark, an Assistant Environmental Engineer with the UPPCB, begins her day monitoring construction activity in Noida. As pollution levels rise, she is responsible for overseeing 45 sectors, from Sector 125 to Sector 168, an area the department identifies as Zone III. Her team aims to inspect roughly one sector each day. The monitoring begins online. Under the UPPCB's dust-control requirements, construction sites must register on the dust control portal and install Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras. These cameras allow officials to monitor construction activity remotely and identify sites that may be violating pollution-control norms. “When a site gets permission to carry out construction, it needs to register on the dust control portal and follow several standard operating procedures (SOPs). One of these is to install a PTZ camera. This allows us to monitor their activities online,” Nimbark says. The printed sheet before her is divided into columns for the sector number, site address, camera link and latest observation. The remarks are brief: ‘link did not open’, ‘no construction’ and ‘ongoing construction found’. The team, which usually comprises Nimbark and a Junior Engineer, sometimes accompanied by a Junior or Senior Research Fellow, uses these observations to decide where to go next. By identifying the addresses of suspected violators, the officials narrow down their daily inspection area to a single sector. They then head out to verify what the cameras have recorded, usually spending until 2 or 3 pm covering the area.

headline: Months of unexplained sickness, a daughter’s warning: Wife poisons Ghaziabad man, son at home
content: It began with a sudden illness last August. Then came repeated visits to doctors, a stay in the ICU and months of unexplained sickness. All this while, a 12-year-old girl had been trying to tell her father something disturbing: she had seen her mother spraying something on the food. But Sushil Bhatnagar, a Ghaziabad-based businessman in his 40s, brushed aside his daughter’s warnings, police said. It was only a year later, after another round of blood tests revealed chronic lead poisoning, that he began to suspect his wife. On November 23, Ghaziabad Police arrested the woman, Renu Bhatnagar (42), from her maternal home for allegedly poisoning him, their 16-year-old son and his nephew over a year. Investigators suspect she wanted to kill Sushil to claim his Rs 2-crore life insurance policy and take control of his travel business, estimated to be worth Rs 5-6 crore. For the family living in Ghaziabad’s Vasundhara, the ordeal began on August 21, last year. Bhatnagar complained of feeling unwell and went to a hospital for a check-up. His condition soon deteriorated. He was admitted to the ICU at Max Hospital and put on life-saving treatment. Blood tests showed unusually high levels of lead in his body, he said in his complaint to the police. He eventually returned home, but his health did not improve. Sushil continued to fall sick, with no clear explanation for his recurring illness. According to police, it was during this period that his daughter allegedly told him she had seen her mother spraying something on the food. “His daughter told him that she had seen her mother spraying something on the food several times, but he did not pay attention to it and dismissed it,” a senior officer said. Nearly a year after his first hospitalisation, Sushil consulted a doctor again. This time, a blood test revealed chronic lead poisoning. According to the FIR, the doctor immediately advised him to call the police helpline, 112, from the hospital. “A very high level of lead was found, which confirms poisoning. This act was done with the intention of killing me, which I came to know from the doctor after I was discharged from the hospital. For a year, I did not know what kind of treatment was being done to me,” Bhatnagar alleged in his complaint to the police. When Sushil confronted Renu, she allegedly fled the house, said police. On September 24, police registered an FIR based on Sushil's complaint, against Renu, her mother and a few other family members. According to Assistant Commissioner of Police (Indirapuram) Abhay Rajendra Daga, Renu allegedly told investigators that her husband owned a travel agency worth several crores and had a life insurance policy of Rs 2 crore, of which she was a nominee. “She thought that all his money would go to her after her husband’s death, and with this intention she committed this act,” Daga said. “The woman allegedly used to add poison (lead) in the food and serve it to family members. We are still investigating the matter,” another officer said. On Monday, police traced Renu to her maternal home in Delhi’s Vivek Vihar and arrested her. She has been booked for attempt to murder and causing hurt by means of poison.

headline: 2 hospitals with 1,815 beds to open next year, 40 more Arogya Mandirs next month: CM Rekha Gupta
content: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Wednesday announced that two new government hospitals in North West Delhi’s Siraspur and West Delhi’s Hastal, with a combined capacity of 1,815 beds, will become operational next year. At Siraspur, the hospital has 1,164 beds and the building is ready, Gupta said. Procurement of medical equipment is under way and is targeted for completion by January-end next year. The 651-bed hospital at Hastal is also nearing completion, said Gupta. The Chief Minister, who reviewed various Health department projects at a meeting at the Delhi Secretariat Wednesday, directed officials to finish all projects within the stipulated timelines. Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh and senior Health and PWD officials attended the meeting. The government also plans to open 40 more Ayushman Arogya Mandirs on the 102nd birth anniversary of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee in December, Gupta said. Of the 1,139 centres being developed across Delhi, 415 are currently operational. At centres with high footfall, the government plans to run services in two shifts. Two more hospitals at Madipur and Jwalapuri, with 691 beds each, built at estimated costs of Rs 466.50 crore and Rs 484.04 crore, respectively, are scheduled for completion by 2028, the Chief Minister added. The government said in a statement that maternal and child healthcare blocks are also coming up at existing hospitals. A 463-bed OPD block at Dr Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital is ready for inauguration, while a 270-bed block at Rao Tularam Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital are nearing completion, it said. On medical education, the government said it is planning to build medical colleges at Indira Gandhi Hospital and Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital, with 150 MBBS seats each. It is also working to raise seats at Dr Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and at the Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70. According to officials, work on an integrated redevelopment plan for Lok Nayak Hospital and the Maulana Azad Medical College campus, with a stipulated timeline of around 30 months, including planning and construction, is underway. Besides, Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, the Delhi State Cancer Institute and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences will be brought under a common institutional framework, the government said. Construction of the hospitals at Siraspur, Hastal, Madipur and Jwalapuri began between 2019 and 2021, during the regime of the previous AAP government. Initially planned as smaller facilities, the decision on the expansion of their capacities were taken later. All four, however, missed their original deadlines.

headline: Delhi govt to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ from September 17
content: The Delhi government will launch a month-long public service campaign, ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Monday. The campaign will feature a range of public welfare and outreach initiatives, including blood donation drives, health camps for senior citizens, worker registration, cleanliness campaigns and plantation programmes. Addressing a press conference, Gupta said development projects worth around ₹13,820 crore would also be inaugurated or have their foundation stones laid during the campaign. She said the initiative was aimed at turning the Prime Minister’s birthday into a month dedicated to public service and outreach, with the spirit of service placed at the centre of governance. The campaign will begin on September 17 with a mega blood donation camp organised by the Health Department, with a target of collecting 2,500 units of blood in a single day. Health check-up camps will also be organised for around 25,000 senior citizens across Delhi in coordination with the Health and Social Welfare departments.
